13. Learned Assistant Judge while dismissing the suit holding inter alia that gift in favour of Bazaler Rahman by his mother Arafatunnessa in 1935 with deliver of possession has been proved by exhibits 2 (Chha) and admitted by defendant Nos. 8-10 and plaintiff; plaintiff also proved that Bazaler Rahman is the owner of 26.5 decimals of land which is also admitted; on consideration of exhibit (Ga) learned Judge found that there was mutual settlement about the land between Bazaler Rahman and Abul Hasim by partition deed dated 10-5-1937, where it was amicably settled that Bazaler Rahman will got 10 annas, Abul Hasim will get 6 annas which is also an admitted position; by registered kabala dated 28-4-1944 exhibit (Ga) to (Ga) 15, Bazaler Rahman purchased 6 annas share from Abul Hasim. Learned Judge also considered the deposition of PW 2, Ali Ahmed and held that it is admitted position that Bazaler Rahman become 16 annas title holder of suit khatian. Learned Judge also considered that at the time of MRR survey the other daughters and sons of Arafatunnessa were alive but they did not raise any objection against 16 annas ownership of the suit land in favour of Bazaler Rahman. Defendant Nos. 8,9 and 10, it is found by the learned Judge that by document, proved oral gift in favour of Bazaler Rahman which has been supported by exhibits 2(Cha) to 2(Jha) to Neo that plaintiffs purchased suit land from the successive heirs of Arafatunnessa. Thereafter, learned Judge discussed oral evidence of the witnesses and found that DWs 2, 3 and 4 proved Bazaler Rahman had 4 other brothers and one sister and also learned Judge considered the deposition of PWs 1 and 2 who admitted that the name of husband of Arafatunnessa and father of Bazaler Rahman was Ayub Ali, which is the case of defendant Nos. 8, 9 and 10. Defendant No.9 as sharer, title holder, by exhibit 2 Chha, sold 6 decimals of land, which plaintiffs purchased from Anwara Khatun. Defendant Nos. 8, 9 and 10 claimed this deed as false, fabricated and not-binding upon, and in their depositions and written statements demand from plaintiffs to produce original deed but plaintiff did not produced and plaintiff did not give any explanation either orally or in the plaint as to why they did not produce this deed in evidence. Plaintiff also did not produce the deeds dated 7-6-1944 and 9-6-1944 in its original and it is also found by the learned Judge that by the deed dated 7-6-1944, and 9-6-1944, the predecessor of plaintiff exhausted his title of the exchange land and thereby from purchase from Anwara Khatun plaintiff did not acquire any title. Learned Judge also considered the depositions of the witnesses and found that neither PW 1 nor PWs 2 and 3 in their earlier depositions did properly describe the scheduled land and also found that PW 3 is the neighbor of the suit property. Learned Judge found witnesses of defendant Nos. 8-10 reliable. Learned Judge also found plaintiffs did not prove the PS khatian which was prepared wrongly and not created which has presumptive value. Learned Judge also found that plaintiff did not prove title of i.e. 4 sons and daughter of Amjad Khalasi and by deed plaintiff admitted PS Jorip. Learned Judge also found that plaintiff did not prove MRR khatian as wrongly recorded. Learned Judge also considered that plaintiff raised objection against Mutation Case and separated joma as a whole on 27-7-1983 but failed to prove that said recording was wrong and illegal and PW 1 did not state anything about their said mutation and separation of joma. Learned Judge also found that plaintiff although demanded but did not pay advelorem court fees as such the suit is not maintainable as per Order VII, rule 11 (c) read with section 149C of the Code of Civil Procedure. Learned Judge on consideration of depositions of witnesses ultimately held as:-

"তাহার কতেক নিঃস্বত্ববান ব্যক্তিগণের নিকট হইতে কতেক ভুয়া দলিলাত সৃজন করতঃ নাঃ বিবাদী ভূমিতে তাহাদের ভূয়া স্বত্বের দাবী করিয়াছে মাত্র। তাহা ছাড়া অত্র মোকাদ্দমায় বাদীপক্ষ তাহার কজ অব একশান প্রমান করিতে পারেন নাই। অধিকন্তু বাদী বন্টনের প্রার্থনা করিলেও কোন তারিখে বাদী শরিফ বিবাদিগনকে তলব তাগাদা করিয়াছেন তাহার বিন্দু মাত্রই তিনি আরজীতে উল্লেখ করেন নাই। তাহাছাড়া বাদী নালিশী ভূমির পি,এস,ও আর, আর, জরিপের বিষয় জানিয়া শুনিয়া কতেক দলিলাত সৃজনে ভূয়া স্বত্বের দাবী উখ্যাপনে অত্র মোকাদ্দমাটি দায়ের করিয়াছেন বলিয়া আমি মনে করি যে উপরোক্ত সুদীর্ঘ আলোচনার ভিত্তিতে-(৩)-(৫) বিচার্য্য বিষয়ের সিদ্ধান্ত বাদী পক্ষ ও ১১/১২ নং বিবাদিগনের প্রতিকূলে এবং ৮-১০ নং বিবাদীগণের অনুকুলে গৃহীত হইল।"

14. Plaintiff and Abdul Barek alias Manik Mea filed Title Appeal Nos. SO of 1997 and 21 of 1997. Both these appeals were heard analogously by the learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Laxmipur who by judgment and decree allowed both the appeals and decreed the suit. Learned Judge in the body of the judgment found that it is admitted fact that 29 decimals of land of District Survey Khatian No. 458, plot No. 3246 originally belonged to Amzad Khalasi. Learned Judge on consideration of exhibit 2-2(Ka) decided the share of Sabina Khatoon at 4 decimals of land. Learned Judge thereafter considered the case of defendant Nos. 8-10 that they claimed that Arfatunnessa orally gifted her 4 decimals of land to Bazaler Rahman but that oral gift was not at all proved. Learned Judge in support of such findings held that, principle of law that to prove gift, 3 essential ingredients must be proved, i.e. (i) there must have a declaration, (ii). acceptance of said declaration or offer and (iii) delivery of possession. It is settled principle of law that without delivery of possession no gift has been proved. Learned Judge found gift was executed in 1935 and Bazaler Rahman sold it by exhibit 2 Cha in 1944 but Bazaler Rahman did not make any respectful ground in exhibit 2 Cha that he got suit land by oral gift. Learned Judge also considered that bantaknama dated 10-5-1937 also did not mention in the recital of oral gift. Learned Judge considered that learned Judge of trial court committed gross illegality in not considering certified copy, exhibit 2 Cha dated 17-4-1944, in absence of original or in absence any explanation is in admissible, reversing that such finding of trial court as perverse as plaintiff stated that the said deed is aged about 50 years and the validity of said deed has not been challenged by Bazaler Rahman or his heirs as such at present, the validity of the deed cannot be questioned. Learned Assistant Judge took exhibit 2 Chha as illegal and on consideration exhibit 2 Cha dated 17-4-1944 learned Judge of the appellate court found that Abdul Aziz got 6 decimals of land and plaintiff purchased said 6 decimals of land from the heirs of Abdul Aziz, which plaintiff clearly proved and also proved possession of the plaintiff. Learned Judge also considered that defendant Nos. 8-10 claimed that Arafatunnessa had two other sons which had not been proved. Learned Judge thereafter found all the witnesses of plaintiff reside in and around of the suit land and witnesses of defendants are not adjacent to the suit land and people of suit property. Learned Judge also considered that Anwara Khatoon, daughter of Arafatunnessa, got 1 decimals of land through pre-emption case No. 147 of 1963 which was allowed on 8-6-1963, exhibit Chao. On these findings learned Judge found title of plaintiff and decreed the suit.

15. Learned Judge also found that plaintiff did not pay any court fees as required under Order VII, rule 11 (c) of the Code of Civil Procedure but the court fees can be submitted at any time.

16. Mr AKM Nazrul Islam, learned Advocate, appearing for the defendant, submits that, the defendant-respondent-petitioners are owner of the suit land measuring 14.5 decimals of land on the basis of deed of exchange from the rightful owners and they also claim separate saham in the suit land, since in a suit for partition the defendant having status of plaintiff and the plaintiff having  status of defendant vice versa and accordingly, when the trial court dismissed the suit, the appellate court cannot decree the suit for partition without ascertaining the respective share of the parties, the judgment and decree passed in the appeal is highly erroneous and bad in law and it is an error apparent on the face of the record occasioning failure of justice and, as such, the judgment and decree passed by the appellate court is liable to be set aside. Learned Advocate further submits that trial court found the plaintiff is out of possession of the suit property and also found that on the basis of the purchase he cannot get any share in the suit land measuring 10 decimals without any prayer for recovery of possession and partition without payment of advelorem court-fees is not maintainable and referred to the decision reported in 16 DLR 195 and the appellate court without ascertaining the share of the respective parties cannot pass the decree for partition and before realization of the advelorem court fees, the impugned decree is void ab-initio and, as such, cannot be given effect. Learned Advocate further submits that the appellate court hopelessly failed to consider genealogy of the transfer of the documents and illegally held that plaintiffs claim for partition is legal without ascertaining the title and possession of the plaintiff and in view of the fact that the trial court held that plaintiff has no title and possession and the suit is not maintainable without any prayer for khas possession on payment of advelorem court fees and, as such, the appellate court has not legally set aside the finding of facts arrived by the trial court.

17. Mr. Khair Ezaz Masood, learned Advocate, appeared for the opposite parties on both the rules, on the other hand, submits that, Abdul Aziz had one son, Serajul Islam and three daughters, Parul Begum, Minara Begum and Shamsunnahar and wife, Fatema Bibi and Amzad Khalasi had one son Abdul Haque, 4 daughters, Halima Khhatoon, Solema Khatoon, Chaiera Khatoon and wife, Fatema Khatoon who by exhibit 2 Kha dated 14-7-1930 transferred 14 decimals of land to Jabed Ullah. Abdul Huq, his son, sold 10 decimals of land to Jabed Ullah. The learned Judge of appellate court considered exhibit 2 (Kha) to 2 (Chha) and thereafter, passed judgment rightly and legally. Learned Advocate further submits that defendant Bazaler Rahman did not have 4 brothers and one sister and it is the case of plaintiff that Bazaler Rahman had 3 brothers and one sister which the learned Judge of appellate court having found, defendant could not prove, that Bazaler Rahman had 4 brothers legally justified in allowing appeal. Learned Advocate further submits that court of appeal below rightly held that exhibit 2 Chha, a basic deed dated 17-4-1944 is of certified copy but this deed being 30 years old has a legal foundation which confer title over the suit property: Plaintiff in order to prove their title produced in court certified copy of the deed dated 7-6-1944 and 9-6-1944 and this being deed for more than 30 years old has presumptive value. Learned Advocate further submits that appellate court in fact did not feel it necessary to find as to whether Bazaler Rahman had 4 brothers or 3 brothers as it is not necessary for deciding the suit.

18. On the submissions of the learned Advocates and on consideration of the plaint case with amendment, and case make out in written statements, depositions of the witnesses and exhibits filed by the parties, four questions calls for determination as (i) whether Arafatunnessa gifted 2 anna share orally to Bazaler Rahman in exclusion of other sharers legally, (ii)" whether exhibit 2 Cha to 2 Chha, deed dated 17-4-1944 and 9-6-1944 in absence of original deed can be said to be good deed of title and (iii) whether Bazaler Rahman had 4 brothers and one sister or 3 brothers and one sister (iv).whether the suit can be maintainable in absence of payment of advelorem court fee after demanded by court.

19. Mr. Khair Ezaz Masood, learned Advocate relied on the case of Abani Mohan Saha vs Assistant Custodian (SDO) Vested Property, Chand pur; 39 DLR (AD) 223 where it is held by the Appellate Division that "The plaintiff is claiming his title to the suit land on the basis of a deed of gift. I have got no doubt in my mind that the initial onus was on him to prove his title. The observation made in 32 DLR (AD) 29 would be of no avail to the appellant, as he failed to discharge his initial onus by proving his document of title. Had he succeeded to do so then the onus would have shifted on the enemy property authority to prove that the executants of the plaintiff's document, the sons of Surendra Mohan Saha, were residing in the enemy country at the relevant time," That means plaintiff is to prove his case.

20. Let us take first point at first i.e. whether oral gift is maintainable in law. DF Mulla defined hiba or gift is "a transfer of property, made immediately, and without any exhance," by one person to another, and accepted by or on behalf of the latter. It further been defined that "Every Mohammadan of sound mind and not a minor may dispose of his property by gift". Ingredience gift are (i) offer, (ii) acceptance and (iii) delivery of possession. Delivery of possession may either be actual or constructive. Mr Khair Ezaz Masood, learned Advocate, submits. that, of the three conditions there might be offer and acceptance but there is no sufficient evidence of taking physical possession. It may be true but at the same time it is seen that gift was between mother and son live in the same premises, in same mess. As per section 152(3) of Mulla's, Principles of Moharnmadan law when donor and donee both reside in same premises in that case. "No physical departure or formal entry is necessary in the case of immovable property in which the donor and the donee are both residing at the time of the gift. In such a case the gift may be completed by some overt act by the donor indicating a clear intention. on his part to transfer possession and to divest himself of all control over the subject of the gift. The principle for the determination of questions of this nature was thus stated by West, J., in the case of Sheikh Ibrahim vs Sheikh Suleman, 9 Born 146 followed by other Courts of the sub-continent that "When a person is present .on the premises proposed to be delivered to him, a declaration of the person previously possessed puts him into possession without any physical departure or formal entry." In the case of Abdul Sattar Ostragarvs Abu Bakkar Ostagar AIR 1977 Cal. 132 it is held that "When a father makes a gift of the dwelling house to his sons, and both the father and the donees (sons) are residing in the house, there is no need for delivery of possession." In the case of Ghulam Hassan vs Mumtaz Khan, 1956 PLD (WP) 1909 it is held that "In case of gift by father or guardian in favour of a minor, if a real and bonafide intention to make a gift is prove, law will be satisfied without a change of possession." In the case of Aurangzeb vs Daud Khan, PLD 195785 it is held that "No change of possession is necessary in the case of a gift by a grand-father to his minor grandson if the father is dead, for the grandfather is the person to take delivery on behalf of his grandson as his guardian." In the case of Natho vs Headyat Begum PLD 1952 Lahore 545 it is held that "It was entirely unnecessary for the mother to depart from the gifted premises in order to show the possession of the daughter, but, on the other hand, it was quite sufficient that it should be agreed between them that whereas previously the mother was the owner of the premises and the daughter was living with her, after the death, the daughter was the owner and mother was living with her." In the case of Zeenat Bibi vs Zaman Mehedi 1956 PLD 760 = 8 DLR 93 it is held that "It is unnecessary to point out that if the actual possession cannot be given by the donor to the donee, but the donor has done all that he could do to divest himself of the gifted property the gift would be considered to be complete and effective according to law."

21. Judicial decisions settled that when change of possession is unnecessary in the valid gift by a father to his minor child or by a guardian to his ward, all that is necessary is to establish a bonafide intention not more when donee lives in loco parentis with another, when donor and donee lived in the same house, subject of gift.

22. The authority opined that if gift is made to the donee who is not living with the donor or if the subject matter of the gift is in possession of a third party then delivery of possession is a must to be given in presence of witnesses. If it is challenged then it required to be proved as per law. But if gift is made in favour of donor's wife, or husband or daughter or son or ward who reside in the same house, such delivery of possession is not required, only evidence of the donor and donee is enough. Defendant's case is that Arafatunnessa orally gifted her entire share to Bazaler Rahman who is son as formal proof of delivery of possession is enough. In Gift propositor can exclude any one but in will or osiyatnama propositors has limitation. In gift donor could divest his entire property which immune from challenge. Court of appeal below did not consider the relationship in between donor and donee. It is admitted fact that Arafatunnessa lived with Bazaler Rahman in the same house in the same mess as such onus shifted upon the plaintiff, it also lies on plaintiff, to prove it otherwise but plaintiff did not adduce any such evidence. So, first question decided against plaintiff.

23. Now to the second point i.e. producing of certified copy of the title deeds by the plaintiff, exhibits 2 Cha to 2 Chha. Defendants challenge these deeds as false, fabricated, illegal and not acted upon. Section 65 of the Evidence Act permit to produce certified copy but for that, an explanation is required, certified copy is not photo copy. When the documents have been challenged as false, forged and fabricated, then, it is incumbent upon the plaintiff to produce the original. Naturally, when original document is lost, there is other method to prove it. Original is required to produce to find whether the signature and left thump impression appeared there in is of the person who executed the same. In certified copy, signature or left thump impression of the executants do not appear. In photo copy it does. Defendants in their written statement as well as in their depositions challenge the basic documents of title of plaintiff as false and for non production of originals but the plaintiffs goes to show the apprehension of defendants in respect of falsity of claim of the plaintiff on false document is true, legal and genuine.

<u>24. Mr. Khair Ezaz Masood, learned Advocate, on reference to the depositions, submits that PW 1 stated that he produced certified copy which is permissible in law but on a reading of the plaint or depositions of plaintiff we do not find any explanation as to why the originals have not been produced. Khair Ezaz Masood, learned Advocate further submits that executants as well as the scribe and witnesses died but there are other methods of proving the deeds, plaintiffs could call for the volume from Sub-Registry office. Certified copy of these two kabalas were produced and marked as exhibits 2 Cha to 2 Chha by the trial court. Learned Advocate submits that these documents being 30 years old has a presumptive value. Section 90 of the Evidence Act speak so, 30 years old document goes into evidence readily but the contents of it must prove to the hilt and that too, when the original produced, not certified copy.</u>

25. On consideration of entire matter, we are of the view that plaintiff did not take any proper step to discharge the onus and failed to prove the kabalas are not forged or in personation. It appears that plaintiff suppressed the documents from producing in court which infer a negative inference from court. Thus we are of the view that plaintiff cannot drive any benefit from exhibits 2 Cha to 2 Chha.

<u>26. When plaintiff instituted the suit it is desirable that plaintiff has all the arms under his belt to have a decree. It is also desirable that plaintiff 'shall' satisfy the court with fact, evidence of both kinds, oral or documentary for the decree prayed for. Weakness of defendant does not give decree to the plaintiff as it is not defendant who invoke the jurisdiction of court but is an invitee, his failure no way spoil plaintiff's claim. Plaintiff in all count must satisfy the court for the decree prayed for. A suit is decreed or dismissed at first on plaintiffs materials as such when we find plaintiff failed to make out a case for decree then naturally the suit would be dismissed.</u>

27. On the question of possession, it appears that trial court on consideration of a number of exhibits, held that plaintiff purchased the suit land from Ali Ahmed and Lutfunnessa but it appears that by this exhibit Ga series, title of Lutfunnessa has been extinguished, as such by purchase from titleless person plaintiff did not drive any title. On the question of possession the finding of trial court has not properly reversed by the appellate court but in cursory manner which is not lawful as such finding of the trial court stand.

<u>28. Above all, we find that trial court directed the plaintiffs to pay advelorem court fees, but plaintiff did not and without depositing advelorem court fees plaintiff filed the suit and also appeal. Learned Judge of the trial court could have dismissed the suit on this ground alone as under section 7 (lV)(c) of the Court fees Act unless court fees be paid even after demand by the court, suit cannot proceed. Plaintiff even in revisional stage and not even today, deposit the wanting court fees as such suit is barred under Order VII, rule 11(c) of the Code of Civil Procedure. We do not, either from order sheet of trial court or appellate court or High Court Division find plaintiff paid the advolerum court fees which is an added ground for dismissing the suit.</u>

29. We find substance in these two rules.

30. In the result, the rule of Civil Revision No. 1148 of 2001 and Civil Revision No. 4016 of 2009 are made absolute without any order as to costs.

31. The judgment and decree complained is set aside. Title Suit No. 56 of 1991 is dismissed.

Send down the lower court records.

Communicate this judgment at once.

End.

caseno:
Civil Revision No. 784 of 2007 
with 
Civil Rule No. 364 (R) of 2007 (Violation)
lawyer:
Abu Yahia Dulal, Advocate -----For the Plaintiff-Respondent-Petitioners. 
Shihab Uddin Ahmed, Advocate ----- For the Proforma-Defendant-Appellant-Opposite Parties.
parties:
Chowdhury Mia and others--------Plaintiff-Respondent-Petitioners
Vs.
Superintendent, Primary Teacher Institution and others-----Proforma-Defendant-Appellant-Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
Sharif Uddin Chaklader J: These two rules, one under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure being Civil Revision No. 784 of 2007, another filed under Order XXXIX, Rule 2(3) of the Code of Civil Procedure being Civil Rule No. 364 (R) of 2007 (Violation) for violation of order of this Court arising out from the aforesaid Civil Revision No. 784 of 2008 are taken up together and this judgment would govern both these rules.

2. Petitioners as plaintiffs instituted the aforesaid Title Suit No. 137 of 1995 for permanent injunction. It is the case of plaintiffs that suit land originally belonged in 2 annas share to Hafiz Khatoon, wife of, Alimuddin, predecessor of plaintiffs. Fazil Mia is the son of Jorina Khatoon, sister of Hafiza Khatoon. Homestead of Fazil Mia was in south of Noakhali town. In 1919-20, Dhumchar was totally deluvated in the river. Hafiza Khatoon gifted 73 decimals of land to Fazil Mia in 1920 orally and delivered possession. Fazil Mia after constructing homestead, pond, latrine etc. possessing the same. Leter on, the land was reformed in situ. Defendant No. 3 through LA Case No. 2/1920-21, for constructing infrastructure of District Headquarters, Noakhali acquired the land, took possession of acquired land excepting the land of Fazil Mia as there was no registered deed of gift and there was homestead. Later on, Government did not evict the plaintiff from the suit land. Subsequently, Government decided not to transfer District Head quarters of Noakhali in the land acquired and land remain unused. Fazil Mia having no other land continued to stay on the gifted land from 1920 and excavated a pond at south west and another at north, constructed homestead on 8 decimals of land, to the south of the said pond is the road. With the earth of the said pond some other constructions were made by Fazil Mia. Fazil Mia along with family lived in the said homestead. Fazil Mia died, leaving 4 sons, plaintiff Nos. 1-4, 5-6 as daughters and 7 as wife. Later on, Pourashava holding was opened in the name of plaintiff Nos. 1-4 and 5-7. They regularly paid taxes and got receipts and also became voters and casted votes. Defendant No. I tried to construct boundary wall, whereupon plaintiffs filed application before the Government. District Kanango Investigated the matter and submitted report mentioning that there is homestead of plaintiffs but the matter was still under consideration before defendant No.3. Defendant No.3 by memo dated 15- 12-1993 directed defendant No. 1 to take step in the matter. On 28-4-1995 defendant No.1 came to the door of plaintiffs and tried to erect pucca wall, hence the suit.

3. The case make out by defendant No. 1 in its written statement is that the land was acquired in 1920 for defendant No. 2 for installing PTI. Public Works Department of Government constructed a building and the same was handed over to Primary Teacher Institution, PTI, on 28-1-1975 as per Government rules and regulation. In LA Case No. 2/1920-21 Government acquired 339 acres of land put since 1963 there having no development work, taking advantage of such situation, plaintiffs went into possession forcefully on the land of dag No. 108 which is totally illegal. Plaintiffs after getting forceful possession, digged ponds and filled some portion of the land of the aforesaid dag, constructed homestead. PTI went to evict the illegal occupant, tried but could not. Plaintiffs being illegal occupant, the suit should be dismissed with cost.

4. In the suit, plaintiff examined 4 witnesses and defendant examined 1 witness, beside plaintiff exhibited some documents.

5. Learned Judge of the trial court decreed the suit. Learned Judge of the appellate court dismissed the suit in allowing the appeal.

6. In decreeing the suit, learned Judge of the trial court found that, plaintiffs are in possession for more than 70 years. In dismissing the suit the learned Judge of the appellate court relied on the case of Belayet Hossain vs Nurul Alam, 42 DLR (AD) 20, where it is held that "A person in wrongful possession of property is not entitled to be protected against the lawful owner by an order of injunction and a trespasser is not entitled to perpetual injunction' against the owner of property," and, subsequently dismissed the suit.

7. Mr Abu Yahia Dulal, learned Advocate, appeared for the plaintiffs-petitioners, submits that, in a case of permanent injunction the court cannot decide title of the parties, possession is prime consideration that having not been denied by defendant as well as both the courts below having found possession of plaintiffs, the suit for permanent injunction ought to be decreed by the court of appeal below. Learned Advocate further submits that, plaintiffs cannot be said to be unauthorized occupant as Government after finding plaintiffs are in possession and constructed homestead, did not evict the plaintiffs in 1920, such possession of the plaintiffs being more than 70 years; they can maintain such possession till plaintiffs evicted by due process of law.

8. Learned Advocate in support of his submissions, relied on the case of Kaimuddin Shaikh alias Kaimu Shaikh vs Bangladesh, represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Rajshahi, 3 BLC 410, the case of Jobayer Hossain vs Noor Hafez, 56 DLR (AD) 22, the case of Rafizuddin Ahmed vs Mongla Barman, 43 DLR (AD) 215, the case of Waziul Bashar (Md) vs Khaja Ahmed, 6 BLC 124, the case of Jabed Ali vs Abu Sheikh, being dead, his heirs Md Naimuddin, 1983 BLD (AD) 1=35 DLR (AD) 31, the case of Tajuddin vs Moktar Ahmed, 1991 BLD (AD) 144, the case of Farhaduzzaman vs Abdul Hasem Hawlader, 2 XP 81.

9. Mr Shihab Uddin Ahmed, learned Advocate, appearing for the defendant-appellant opposite parties, on the other hand, submits that, it is an admitted position that plaintiffs are in possession but their such possession being illegal, unauthorized cannot get any protection of law which having found by the court of appeal below committed no illegality in dismissing the suit while allowing the appeal.

10. Learned Advocate relied on the case of Administrative Officer, Housing Settlement, Chittagong vs Abdur Rashid Chowdhury, 63 DLR 479, the case of Abdul Kader Bhuiyan and 17 others vs Secretary, Ministry of Land, Government of the People s Republic of Bangladesh, 61 DLR (AD) 28, Rafizuddin Ahmed vs J. Mongla Barman, 43 DLR (AD) 215, the case of Dewan Shamsul Abedin, Mutwalli of Dewan Aftebur Reza Chowdhury Waqf Estate, of Village Tegharia, Police Station: Sunamgonj Sadar, District Sunamgonj, 13 MLR (AD) 163 = 13 DLR (AD) 118, the case. of Abdul Karim vs Bangladesh 51 DLR 447, the case of Belayet Hossain vs Nurul Alam Mir, 42 DLR (AD) 20, a case of granting of temporary injunction and also relied on section 16 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894. We will refer the decisions after consideration of materials before us.

11. It is admitted position that plaintiffs are in possession from 1920 which is supported by the finding of the trial court but appellate court did not pass any reverse finding of the trial court on this score, but dismissed the suit holding that plaintiffs are in unauthorized possession. From written statement it appears defendant admitted possession of plaintiffs from 1962. In the written statement defendant stated that plaintiffs surreptitiously entered into possession taking advantage of the situation that no development work has been done in the acquired land and after acquiring the land in 1920, defendant goes as to show that plaintiffs are in possession to the very knowledge and notice of defendants. It is stated in written statement that that plaintiffs digged ponds, made homestead, filled earth and also dispossessed defendant PTI and make boundary wall. It is also the case of defendant that they tried to evict the plaintiffs but they did not proceed, further. The aforesaid facts i.e. digging of ponds, construction of homestead and filling of earth cannot be done in hiding and cannot be done hurriedly behind the back of defendant as all these work are time consuming. All these admitted facts established that plaintiffs, possession is hostile, notorious, actual, visible and exclusive.

12. Learned Judge of the appellate court took the view that unauthorized occupant cannot get any protection of law. Unauthorized occupant is a person who by force entered into possession and to maintain his possession, hasitly filed the suit for permanent injunction so that original owner may not evict him. In the case in hand the plaintiffs cannot be said to be unauthorized occupant or may not be said to be lawful occupant but they are in possession from 1920, this finding of trial court has not been reversed by the appellate court, by which the plaintiffs acquired at least possessory right which by lapse of time conferred them a kind of legality to maintain possession. In such admitted position, we are of the view that court of appeal below was not legal in not granting permanent injunction. Granting of injunction is a judicial process, by which one who has invaded or is threatening to invade the rights, legal or equitable, of another, is restrained from continuing or commencing such wrongful acts.

13. Decision cited by petitioners, particularly the cases of 56 DLR (AD) 22, 43 DLR (AD) 215, 1983 BLD (AD) 144, speaks that 'Even a trespasser's possession is good and valid against the entire world except the true owner and such possession is entitled to protection until he is evicted by due process of law.' We have also seen that long user of the suit land plaintiffs acquired a right of possession as such, he cannot to be thrown out of possession until and unless defendant could prove that they have better title over the land of plaintiffs by instituting properly constituted suit.

<u>14. Decision cited by the learned Advocate Mr Shihab Uddin Ahmed, accepting the case of Rafizuddin Ahmed vs Mongla Barman, 43 DLR (AD) 215, the case of Dewan Shamsul Abedin, Mutwalli of Dewan Aftebur Reza Chowdhury Waqf Estate, 13 MLR (AD) 163, the case of Belayet Hossain vs Nurul Alam Mir; 42 DLR (AD) 20, other decisions cited are not to be considered as in front of the Hon'ble Appellate Division's decision, the decisions of High Court Division should not be required to be looked into. The decisions as cited by the learned Advocate for the defendant if we consider in particular perspective then also these decisions support plaint case as in all these decisions it is held that for permanent injunction as regard dispute landed property the relief is available to a person who is in possession. The court may inquire incidentally into the respective claims of the parties to the suit for determining whether the plaintiff is in possession of the disputed property and are entitled to the specific relief of permanent injunction. 42 DLR (AD) case is a case on granting temporary injunction. Article 144 of Limitation Act provides 60 years possession to give title, over the land of Government. We have seen that Appellate Court did not disturb the finding of trial court's finding of plaintiffs' possession for 70 years. We find merit in the rule.</u>

15. In the result, the rule is made absolute without any order as to cost.

16. The judgment and decree dated 20-2-2007 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 200 Court, Noakhali in Title Appeal No. 212 of 2000 is set-aside and those of the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Noakhali in Title Suit No. 137 of 1995 is restored.

<u>17. Now to the second one. It is the case of plaintiffs petitioners that, while Rule was issued and injunction was granted, the violator, Superintendent of Primary Training Institute on taking advantage of the decision of the Appellate Court, dispossessed plaintiff on 14-5-2007. We find that violator Superintendent without any order from any court dismantled the property of plaintiffs. It is a heinous offence and should not go without any punishment but Mr Shihab Uddin Ahmed, learned Advocate, submits that, this woman, did it on the instruction of her superior authority against whom no Rule was issued. We do no understand how a superior authority could act in such a manner taking law in his own hand. The suit is filed by plaintiffs not by the defendants. The suit may be dismissed or may be decreed which cannot in any way prompt the defendant to evict the plaintiffs or dismantle the property taking recourse to force. When law is there, until and unless the law is invoked no one can evict from the suit property by administrative order, but since it is submitted on reference to the records that when dismantle was done violator was not in knowledge about pendency of the proceeding before the High Court Division. We exonerate her from charge but we are directing defendant to restore possession of the plaintiffs within 30 days from today. It has been submitted that the violator has already retired. In that case we direct the present Superintendent of PTI that he shall restore possession of the plaintiffs within 30 days from today, not from the date of receipt of this order. We further direct the Superintendent of PTI that if possession be not restored to the plaintiffs within 30 days then he shall pay as compensation, Taka 50,000 to the plaintiffs per day till Superintendent restore possession of the plaintiffs.</u>

18. With these observations the Rule being Civil Rule No. 364(R) of 2007 (Violation) is disposed of.

Send down the lower court records. Communicate this order at once.

End.

parties:
Nur Hossain (Md) and others ------ Petitioners
Vs.
Bangladesh and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Md Badruzzaman J : Initially, rule nisi was issued on 18-8-2015 in the following terms; "Let a rule nisi be issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why they should not be directed to pay salary of Taka 14,540 (Fourteen Thousand Five Hundred and Forty) to the petitioners for the post of Sub-Assistant Engineer, Drafts Men (Sub-assistant Engineer) fixed by the National Pay Scale-2009 (BDT 8.000.00-14,540,00) for 2nd Class Gazetted Officer and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper."

2. Thereafter, vide order dated 19-1-2016, supplementary rule nisi was issued in the following terms: "Let a supplementary rule nisi be issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the Circular dated 19-11-1994 bearing Memo No. সম(বিধি-২) পদোন্নতি-২৭/৯৪-১৬৪ published in the Establishment Manual (Vol-2) (Annexure-H) and Circular issued by the respondent No.1 dated 3-12-1994 bearing Memo No. অনু/অবি/(বাস্ত-৪)ডিপ্লো-২০/৯২(অংশ)/৬৯ Annexure-H-1 of the writ petition) shall not be declared ultra vires and without lawful authority for being discriminatory and mala fide and is of no legal effect."

3. The case of the petitioners in brief, is that, the petitioners are government servants. Initially, they joined in the post of Work Assistant, Estimator and Surveyor in different offices under Local Government Engineering Department (LGED) under the Ministry of Local Government, Rural Development and Co-operatives. After completion of at least 15 years of their service and having been successful in departmental promotion examinations, they were promoted to the post of Sub-Assistant Engineer (SAE) between 2003-2009. By an office order dated 24-9-2006 (Annexure-C), respondent No. 3 (Ministry of Local Government, Rural Development and Co-operatives) fixed salary of Taka 5100-280-760, EB 30-10360 as per National Pay Scale 2005 for the Sub-Assistant Engineers who have been promoted to the said post from the post of Surveyor, Work-Assistant and Estimator. But said decision of Respondent No. 3 could not be implemented for the petitioners because of the barrier made in the impugned Circular dated 26-8-1995 (Annexure-H) issued by the Ministry of Establishment in which the post of Sub-Assistant Engineers having diploma in engineering degree have been upgraded to 2nd Class post followed by another impugned Circular dated 3-12-1994 (Annexure-H-1) issued by the Ministry of Finance (respondent No. 1) re-fixing pay scale of Taka 2300-4480 from Taka 1725-3725 as per National Pay Scale 1991, corresponding to Taka 5100-10360 as per National Pay Scale 2005.

4. Since the petitioners have been serving as Sub-Assistant Engineers, it is stated, they are entitled to the same status and pay scale which have been given to the Sub-Assistant Engineers having diploma in engineering degree but they are not getting the equivalent scale which was accorded by Circular dated 19-11-1994 and Circular dated 3-12-1994 for the Sub-Assistant Engineers. Therefore, it is stated, the decisions of the respondents in giving higher pay scale and status to SAOs having diploma-in-engineering degree depriving other Sub-Assistant Engineers of getting such status and benefit are discriminatory and ultra vires to Articles 27, 29 and 31 of the Constitution. The petitioners, being Sub-Assistant Engineers, agitated their grievance to the respondents by several representations in particular representation dated 18-1-2015 followed by a notice demanding justice dated 1-2-2015 praying for granting equal pay scale and status at par with Sub-Assistant Engineers having diploma-in-engineering degree and to do justice to them but the respondents did not pay any heed to their grievances.

5. In the above factual background, the petitioners have come up with this writ petition and obtained the rule and supplementary rule as quoted above.

6. The rule is opposed by respondent No. 2, the Secretary, Ministry of Public Administration and respondent No. 5, Chief Engineer Local Government Engineering Directorate by filing separate affidavits-in-opposition. The case of respondent No. 2 is that, initially the petitioners were appointed as Work Assistant, Estimator and Surveyor having no diploma-in-engineering degree and through departmental examinations they were promoted to the post of Sub-Assistant Engineer. Before joining in the post of Sub-Assistant Engineer, the petitioners were well aware about the impugned Circulars dated 19-11-1994 and 3-12-1994 and their service conditions as Sub-Assistant Engineer and accordingly they joined in their respective posts and, as such, they cannot claim service benefit now equivalent to the service benefit and status at par with Sub-Assistant Engineers who possess diploma-in-engineering degree in accordance with the provision of the impugned circulars. It is further stated that since the petitioners are government servants and they have come before this Court in respect of their terms and conditions of their service, this writ petition is not maintainable in view of the provisions under Article 117 of the Constitution and their proper forum lies with the Administrative Tribunal constituted by the Administrative Tribunal Act 1980. It is further stated that the respondents issued the impugned circulars after following all legal formalities and in that view, the respondents did not commit any illegality. Accordingly, this rule is liable to be discharged.

7. The case of respondent No. 5 and that of respondent No. 2 is more or less same. Further case of respondent No. 5 is that the petitioners were appointed as Work Assistant, Estimator and Surveyor and then, through departmental examinations, they were promoted to the post of Sub-Assistant Engineer from 2003 and they have no diploma-in-engineering degree. The petitioners got promotion to the post of Sub-Assistant Engineer having known fully well about impugned circulars that they would not get equal pay scale and status at par with the Sub-Assistant Engineers having diploma-in-engineering degree and, as such, at this stage, the petitioners cannot claim that the impugned circulars are arbitrary and ultra vires the Constitution. The government, considering the constitutional as well as legal aspects of the matter, issued the impugned circulars because the educational qualification can be substantially reasonable ground for classification, and that the classification or alleged discrimination as has been occurred by the impugned notification is based on the doctrine of permissible criteria and intelligible differentia and thus intra vires the Constitution. Since the petitioners do not possess any diploma-in-engineering degree, they are not entitled to get same salary and status at par with Sub-Assistant Engineers who possess diploma-in-engineering degree.

8. Mr Sheikh Mohammad Zakir Hossain, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners. by drawing this Court's attention to the impugned Circular (Annexure-H to the application for issuance of supplementary rule), submitted that Annexure-H dated 19-11-1994 having been issued by the order of the Hon'ble President and duly notified in the official Gazette, have the force of law within the meaning of Article 152 of the Constitution and since the writ petitioners have challenged the vires of the Circular on the ground of its constitutionality, this writ petition is maintainable. In support of this contention, he referred to the case of Bangladesh vs Shaliuddin reported in 50 DLR (AD) 27, Bangladesh vs Md Shamsul Haq reported in 59 DLR (AD) 54 and Bangladesh vs Sontosh Kumar Saha reported in 21 BLC (AD) 94.

9. Learned Advocate further submitted that, though as per law the persons similarly situated should be treated equally and equal opportunity should be given to those who stand on the same footing, but the impugned Circulars though upgraded the status of Sub-Assistant Engineers having diploma-in-engineering degree to 2nd Class with higher pay scale, left other Sub-Assistant Engineers and equivalents like the petitioners having had no diploma-in-engineering degree. Such classification being discriminatory is hit by Articles 27 and 29 of the Constitution and ultra vires. Accordingly, the impugned Circulars along with other circulars, orders etc. issued pursuant thereto are liable to be struck down and necessary direction should be given upon the respondents to provide similar status and pay scale to the petitioners as has been given to Sub-Assistant Engineers possessing diploma-in-engineering degree. In this connection, learned Advocate referred to the decision of the case of Bangladesh Biman Corporation vs Rabiabashri Irene reported in 8 MLR (AD) 223 = 55 DLR (AD) 132, Carew and Company (BD) Limited vs Chairman, Labaur Court reported in 50 DLR 396 and Municipal Corporation of Delhi vs Gonesh Raj reported in 52 (1993) DIT 594.

10. As against the above submissions, Mr Rashed Zahangir, learned Deputy Attorney-General appearing for respondent No. 2, by drawing this Court's attention to Article 117 of the Constitution submitted that since the petitioners are government servants and the dispute relates to the terms and conditions of their service, the only forum available to them is before the Administrative Tribunal constituted under the provisions of Article 117 read with the provisions under Administrative Tribunal Act, 1980 and, as such, this writ petition is not maintainable. Learned Deputy Attorney-General, by referring to paragraph 29 of the case of Sheikh Abdus Sabur vs Returning Officer reported in 41 DLR (AD) 30, submits that 'equality before law' is not to be interpreted in its absolute sense to hold that all persons are equal in all respects disregarding different conditions and circumstances in which they are placed or special qualities and characteristics which some of them may process but which are lacking in others. A single law, therefore, cannot he applied uniformly to all persons disregarding their basic differences with others and if these differences are identified, then the persons or things may be classified into different categories according to those distinctions; this ,is what is called 'permissible criteria' or intelligible differentia" which have been done in the instant case. Learned Deputy Attorney-General further submits that, Sub-Assistant Engineers, who have diploma-in-engineering degree and Sub-Assistant Engineers who have no diploma-in-engineering degree cannot constitute one and single class and, as such, the classification made by the impugned circular is within the constitutional mandate and, as such, consistent with the provisions under the Constitution. Learned DAG further referred to the case of State of Mysore vs P. Narasingo Rao, AIR 1968 (SC) 349.

11. Mr Mintu Kumar Mondal, learned Advocate appearing for the respondent No.5, adopted the submissions of the learned Deputy Attorney-General. However, learned Advocate in addition, referred to a decision of the case of State of TN vs Mr Alagappan reported in (1997) 4 SCC 401.

12. The issue whether under Article 102(1) judicial review of a decision of authority relating to terms and conditions of service of a person serving in the Republic is maintainable is no longer a res integra. On several occasions, this issue went up to the Apex Court. Finally, in Bangladesh vs Sontosh Kumar Saha, 21 BLC (AD) 94, this issue has been settled in the following language:

"In this issue, this court clearly observed that except challenging the vires of law or violation of fundamental rights, judicial review of a decision of authority relating to the terms and conditions of service under article 102(1) is not permissible."

13. It appears that Appellate Division finally fixed two criteria to maintain a writ petition for invoking judicial review under Article 102(1) by a person relating to his terms and conditions of service serving in the Republic i.e the aggrieved party have to challenge the vires of law or he/she must satisfy that his/her fundamental rights have been infringed. Now we will consider whether the petitioners have been successful in fulfilling any of two criteria’s.

14. It appears that the petitioners have challenged the vires of two Circulars (Annexure H and H-1). The first one (Annexure-H) was published on 19-11-1994 upgrading the status of Sub-assistant Engineers having diploma-in-engineering degree to second class leaving other Sub-assistant Engineers and equivalents and Annexure-H(1) has been issued on 3-12-1994 pursuant to Annexure-H, upgrading their pay scale from Taka 1735-3725 to Taka 2300-4480 as per National Pay Scale 1991. Annexure-H is quoted below:

“সংস্থাপন মন্ত্রনালয়

বিধি-২ শাখা

প্রজ্ঞাপন

তারিখঃ (১৯ নভেম্বর ১৯৯৪ ইং)/(৫ অগ্রহায়ন ১৪০১ বাং)

নং সম (বিধি-২) পদোন্নতি-২৭/৯৪-১৬৪ সরকার এতদ্বারা উপ-সহকারী প্রকৌশলী ও সমমানের পদসমূহ কর্মরত ইঞ্জিনিয়ারিং এ ডিপ্লোমাধারী কর্মকর্তাদের ২য় শ্রেণীর পদ মর্যাদা প্রদানের সিদ্ধান্ত গ্রহণ করিলেন।

২। সকল মন্ত্রনালয়/বিভাগকে তাহাদের অধীনস্থ অফিস সমূহ উপ-সহকারী প্রকৌশলী ও সমমানের পদে কর্মরত ইঞ্জিনিয়ারিং এ ডিপ্লোমাধারী কর্মকর্তাদের ২য় শ্রেণীর পদ মর্যাদা উন্নীত করণের আদেশ জারী করিতে এবং সংশ্লিষ্ট নিয়োগ বিধিতে প্রয়োজনীয় সংশোধনী আনয়নের প্রক্রিয়া গ্রহণ করিতে অনুরোধ করা হইল।

রাষ্ট্রপতির আদেশক্রমে

কাজী আবুল কাশেম

উপ-সচিব (বিধি-১)।”

15. Now question arises as to whether the impugned Circular dated 19-11-1994 have the force of law. It appears that the Circular was issued by the order of the Hon'ble President and published in the official Gazette of Government. Law has been defined in Article 152 of the Constitution which provides that "law means any Act, ordinance, order, rule, regulation, bye-law, notification or other legal instrument, and any custom or usage, having the force of law in Bangladesh". Annexure-H having been issued by the order of the Hon'ble President and duly notified in the official Gazette have the force of law within the meaning of Article 152 of the Constitution. Since the petitioners have challenged the vires of the Circular, this writ petition is maintainable (ref: Govt. vs Md Shamsul Huq, 59 DLR (AD) 54).

16. A bare reading of Annexure-H and H-1 suggests that the first one has classified the post of Sub-assistant Engineer and equivalents into two groups: firstly, who have diploma-in-engineering degree and secondly, who have no diploma-in-engineering degree and after such classification the Government upgraded the 1st group to 2nd Class Officers and pursuant to Annexure H the later one (Annexure-H-1) was issued upgrading their pay scale leaving the other group like the petitioners from getting such status and benefit.

17. Now question arises whether the respondents by issuing such circulars disregarded the guarantee of the Constitution in Article 27 that "all citizens are equal before law and are entitled to equal protection of law" and the impugned circulars are hit by the provision of Article 27 and thus ultra vires to the Constitution.

18. In Bangladesh vs. Touhid Uddin reported in 16 BLC (AD) 116 it is held:

“সংবিধানের ২৯ অনুচ্ছেদ এবং উপরে আলোচিত নজিরগুলি হইতে নিম্নলিখিত মূলনীতি প্রতিফলিত হইতেছেঃ

ক) সরকারী চাকুরীতে নিয়োগ বা পদোন্নতির ক্ষেত্রে সকল নাগরিকের সুযোগের সমতা থাকিবে, কোনরুপ বৈষম্য সাধারণভাবে অবৈধ,

খ) এই সুযোগের সমতার অধিকার একই শ্রেণীভুক্ত ব্যক্তিবর্গের ক্ষেত্রে প্রযোজ্য,

গ) পূর্বে বিভিন্ন শ্রেণীভুক্ত থাকিলে পরবর্তীতে যদি একই শ্রেণীভুক্ত হয় তবে সেক্ষেত্রেও সংশ্লিষ্ট ব্যক্তিবর্গ অন্যান্য সকলের সহিত সুযোগের সমতার অধিকার ভোগ করিবে।”

19. In Sontosh Kumar case [21 BLC (AD) 94], our Appellate Division by analyzing a number of decisions of our jurisdiction and Indian jurisdiction explained equality before law and equal protection of law in respect of classification for the purpose of legislation and observed in paragraphs 162, 163 & 164 as follows:

"162. The expression equal protection of law or equality before law has to be interpreted in its absolute sense. All persons are equal in all respect disregarding different conditions and circumstances in which they are placed. Equal protection of law means all persons are equal in all cases. It means the persons similarly situated should be treated equally. The term equality is a dynamic concept with many aspect and diminution and it cannot be confined within traditional and doctrinaire limits. Indian Supreme Court taking into consideration Article 14 of the Constitution held that Article 14 does not forbid reasonable classification for the purposes of legislation. There can be permissible classification provided two conditions are satisfied namely; (a) the classification must be founded on an intelligible differentia which distinguishes persons or things that are grouped together for other left out of the group; (b) differentia must have a rational relation to the object sought to be achieved by the statute in question. The classification may be founded on different basis. There cannot be any question of decimation on the ground of some acts providing for different set up and is must be taken to be a class by itself. The legislature has right to make such provision for its Constitution as it things fit subject always to the provisions of the Constitution. References in this connection are EP Roy vs TN, AIR 1974 (SC) 555, Maleka Gandhi vs India, AIR 1970 (SC) 597, Romana Shetly vs International Airport Authority, AIR 1979 (SC) 1628, Ajay Hashia vs Khalid Mujud, AIR 1983 (SC) 130, AL Kalra vs P & N Corporation of India, AIR 1984 (SC) 1361, Sree Ram Kaishna Dal Mia vs Sree SR Tendulkar, AIR 1958 (SC) 538, S Azee: Basher vs Union of India, AIR 1968 (SC) 662, Jibendra Kishore Achary vs Province of East Pakistan, 9 DLR (SC) 21 and Kazi Mohammed Akhtaruzzaman vs Bangladesh, Writ Petition No.2252 of 2009 disposed of along with 3 (three) other writ petitions, Sheikh Abdus Sabur vs Returning Officer, 41 DLR (AD) 30 and Bangladesh vs Md Azizur Rahman, 46 DLR (AD) 19.

163. In Jibendra Kishore (supra), it has been observed, "It is not possible to formulate a comprehensive definition to the clause `equal protection of law'; nevertheless, some broad propositions as to its meaning have been enunciated. One of these propositions is that equal protection of the laws means that no person or class of persons shall be denied the same protection of the laws which is enjoyed by other persons or other classes, in like circumstances, in their lives, liberty and property and in pursuit of happiness. Another generalization more frequently stated is that the guarantee of equal protection of the laws requires that all personal shall he treated alike under like circumstances and conditions both in the privileges confirmed  And in the liabilities imposed. In the application of these principles, however, it has always been recognized that classification is not arbitrary or capricious, is natural and reasonable and bears a fair and substantial relation to the object of the legislation. It is not for the Courts, in such cases, it is said, to demand from the legislature a scientific accuracy in the classification adopted. If the classification is relevant to the object of the Act, it must be upheld unless the relevancy is too remote or fanciful. A classification that proceeds on irrelevant consideration, such as differences in race, colour or religion will certainly be rejected by the Courts. Applying these tests to the present case, it cannot but be held that if, in consequence of abolishing the system of private rent for agricultural land, it also became necessary to make some provision for the outgoing landlords, the classification of the landlords in the basis of their net incomes at the time of their expropriation was a necessary, and not an unreasonable classification.

164. In Sheikh Abdus Sabur (supra), this court held: "Equality before law" is not to be interpreted in its absolute sense to hold that all persons are equal in all respects disregarding different conditions and circumstances in which they are placed or special qualities and characteristics which some of them may possess but which are lacking in others. The term 'protection of equal law' is used to mean that all persons or things are not equal in all cases and that persons similarly situated should be treated alike. Equal protection is the guarantee that similar people will be dealt with in a similar way and that people of different circumstances will not be treated as if they were the same. A single law therefore cannot be applied uniformly to all persons disregarding their basic differences with others; and if these differences are identified, then the persons or things may be dissatisfied into different categories according to those distinctions; this is what is called' permissible criteria' or "intelligible differentia". The legislature while proceeding to make law with certain object in view, which is either to remove some evil or to confer some benefit, has power a make classification on reasonable basis. Classification of persons for the purpose of legislation is different from class legislation, which is forbidden. To stand the test of 'equality' a classification, besides being based on intelligent differentia, must have reasonable nexus with the object the legislature intends to achieve by making the classification. A classification is reasonable if it aims at giving special treatment to a backward section of the population; it is also permissible to deal out distributive justice by taxing the privileged class and subsidizing the poor section of the people. The above views have been approved in Azizur Rahman (supra)."

20. In Smt. Indira Gandhi vs Raj Narayan, AIR 1975, (SC) 2279 it was held that, "All who are equal are equal in the eye of law", meaning that it will not accord favoured treatment to persons within the same class."

21. The sum and substance of the observations made in aforesaid Sontosh Kumar, Jibendra Kishore, Shaikh Abdus Sabur and Smt. Indira Gandhi (supra) cases follows that there shall be no discrimination to persons within the same class and that persons similarly situated should be treated alike. Equal protection is the guarantee that similar people will be dealt with in a similar way and that people of different circumstances will not be treated as if they were the same. All who are equal are equal in the eye of law which means that it will not accord favoured treatment to persons within the same class. The concept of equality before law means that among equals the law should be equal and should be equally administered and that the likes should be treated alike.

22. But the question is what does this ambiguous and crucial phrase 'similarly situated' mean? Answer has been given in the case of Mohammad Shujat Ali vs Union of India, AIR 1974 SC 1631 saying that "Where are we to look for the test of similarity of situation which determines the reasonableness of a classification? The inescapable answer is that we must look beyond the classification to the purpose of the law. A reasonable classification is one which includes all persons or things similarly situated with respect to the purpose of the law. There should be no discrimination between one person or thing and another, if as regards the subject-matter of the legislation their position is substantially the same. This is sometimes epigrammatically described by saying that what the constitutional code of equality and equal opportunity requires is that among equals, the law should be equal and that like should be treated alike ----”

23. All employees standing on the same position (in this case Sub-Assistant Engineers and equivalents) make one class irrespective of their educational qualifications. According to the equality doctrine, no classification can be made among the employees holding same post for giving special status and benefits because of having special educational qualification or degree. In this case, as and when the petitioners were promoted to post of Sub-Assistant Engineer irrespective of their educational qualification, they grouped together with other Sub-Assistant Engineers having diploma-in-engineering degree and thus made one class. Sub-Assistant Engineers or equivalents cannot be classified into two groups namely Sub-Assistant Engineers having diploma-in-engineering degree in one group and Sub-Assistant Engineers and equivalents having no diploma-in-engineering degree in another group for the purpose of up-gradation of status and for giving special benefits or privileges to the 1st group and thereby depriving the other group of such status, benefits and privileges etc.

24. It appears that the Circular dated 19-11-1994 (Annexure-H to the application for supplementary rule) clearly made two classes of Sub-assistant Engineers and equivalents; first-Sub-assistant Engineer having diploma-in-engineering degree and second- Sub-assistant Engineer having no diploma-in-engineering degree by putting the words “ইঞ্জিনিয়ারিং-এ ডিপ্লোমাধারী” in the said circular and thereby upgraded the status of the 1st group as 2nd Class posts depriving the 2nd group of giving such status and benefit. This classification in the post of Sub-Assistant Engineer, on the face of it, is discriminatory and inconsistent with the previsions of Article 27 of the Constitution and thus ultra vires and void according to the provision under Article 26 (1) of the Constitution and, accordingly, the words “ইঞ্জিনিয়ারিং-এ ডিপ্লোমাধারী” employed in Annexure-H are liable to be struck down.

25. On the other hand, on perusal of Annexure-H-1 it appears that the same has been issued by the Ministry of Finance dated 3-12-1994 pursuant to Circular dated 19-11-1994 re-fixing the pay scale for Sub-Assistant Engineers having diploma-in-engineering degree from Taka 1725-3725 to Taka 2300-4480 as per National Pay Scale 1991 leaving other Sub-Assistant Engineers and equivalents from getting such benefit.

26. It is the case of the petitioners that, after their promotion in the post of Sub-assistant Engineer or equivalent posts, they stood on the same footing or at par with Sub-assistant Engineers having diploma-in-engineering degree, but the government by the impugned Circular upgraded the pay scale for them by depriving the petitioners and equivalents from getting such increased salary and other service benefits and thereby they have been discriminated and thus the action of the respondents has violated the principle of "Equal Pay for Equal Work."

27. It is true that the principle of "Equal pay for Equal work" is not expressly declared by our Constitution to be a fundamental right. Article 20(1) proclaims that everyone shall be paid for his work based on the principle 'from each according to his abilities, to each according to his work' as a directive principle of State Policy. But the principle "Equal pay for Equal Work" has assumed the status of fundamental right in service jurisprudence having regard to the constitutional mandate of equality in Articles 27 of the Constitution. References in this connection are Carew and Company Limited vs Chairman, Labor Court, 50 DLR 396, Bangladesh vs Shamsul Haq, 59 DLR (AD) 54 and Bangladesh Biman Corporation vs Rabia Bashri Irene 8 MLR (AD) 223 = 55 DLR (AD) 132.

28. In Carew and Company Limited (supra) it was held that "In such circumstances we fail to understand why the petitioner refused the similar benefits to the respondent Nos. 2 to 22 when they became illegible under the agreement being promoted to the post of office assistants or equivalents and thus became entitled to get the scale. Giving benefit to some and denying the same to others under the same agreement and service condition, is not only illegal but also offends fundamental rights of the respondents guaranteed under Articles 28 and 29 of the Constitution. We, therefore, hold that in the aforesaid facts and circumstances the agreement is also applicable to the respondents."

29. In Shamsul Haq (supra), our Apex Court held: "The respondent and Personal Officers of the Secretariat having been similarly situated have been discriminated and cannot be treated differently and is repugnant to the equality doctrine and, under like circumstances and conditions, should be treated alike both in their rights and privilege."

30. In Bangladesh Biman Corporation (supra) it was held: "Since one employees of the Corporation inter' se standing in the similar situation have not been treated in the similar manner or in other words have been treated differently from the others the contention of the writ-petitioners that they have been discriminated has rightly been found genuine by the High Court Division."

<u>31. Employees are entitled to receive equal pay who are discharging the same duties as their counterparts (Ref. Municipal Corporation of Delhi vs Ganesh Razak, 52 (1993) DLT 594). The principle of equal pay for equal work must prevail and inequality in wages cannot be allowed to stand (UP Rajya Sahakari Bhoomi Vikas Bank Ltd vs Its Workmen, AIR 1990 SC 495).</u>

32. It appears that, by order dated 3-12-1994 (AnnexureH-1), the Government amended “চাকুরী (বেতন ও ভাতাদি) ১৯৯৭ re-fixing the pay scale of Taka 2300-4480 for the Sub-Assistant Engineer who possesses diploma-in-engineering degree leaving other Sub-Assistant Engineers and equivalents. This memo was issued pursuant to Annexure-H dated 19-11-1994 to giving financial benefit to the Sub-Assistant Engineers of the same class though as per constitutional mandate all service holders standing on the same class are entitled to same service benefit and status. Accordingly, we are of the view that, the Administrative order dated 3-12-1994 upgrading the pay scale of Sub-Assistant Engineers having diploma-in-engineering degree leaving other sub-assistant engineers and equivalents based on extraneous or irrelevant consideration, discriminatory, actuated by mala fides, perverse and manifestly wrong and also liable to be struck down.

33. Now, question arises from which date the petitioners and left out sub-assistant engineers and equivalents would get the benefit of this judgment.

<u>34. Since the impugned Circulars (Annexures-H and H-1) have come into force long back in 1994 but the petitioners have challenged those in a belated stage and since the implementation of our decision retrospectively may incur huge monetary involvement of the government exchequer, we are of the view that, this verdict would operate prospectively from the date of this judgment in respect of giving financial benefit to the left out sub-assistant engineers and equivalents of the Government functionary including the petitioners.</u>

35. In view of the discussions made above, we find merit in this rule.

36. Accordingly, the rule is made absolute however, without any order as to costs.

37. Thus, the impugned Circulars dated 19-11-1994 (Annexure-H) and 3-12-1994 (Anne-xure-H-1), so far insertion of words “ইঞ্জিনিয়ারিং-এ ডিপ্লোমাধারী” therein, are declared ultra vires the Constitution, void and those words are struck-down from those Circulars prospectively with effect from today.

38. The respondents are directed to provide equal pay scale, status and other service benefits to the petitioners as have been provided by the impugned Circulars to the Sub-Assistant Engineers having diploma-in-engineering degree with effect from the date of pronouncement of this judgment within 60 (sixty) days from the date of receipt of the copy of this judgment in accordance with law.

39. It is also declared that, this judgment would operate as a judgment in-rem in respect of all Sub-Assistant Engineers and equivalents serving under the Government functionaries.

Communicate a copy of this judgment at once.

End.
