full_judgment:
This revisional application under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure is directed against the judgment and order dated 22-3-1995 passed by the District Judge, Mymensingh in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 14 of 1995 allowing the prayer of the plaintiff opposite party Nos. 1-2 for temporary injunction restraining the petitioners and opposite party No. 3 (the Additional Secretary General, Bangladesh Sarak Paribahan Samity) from disturbing the management of the affairs of the Executive Committee of Mymensingh Dhaka Coach Owners Association till disposal of the suit and further allowing the prayer for temporary mandatory injunction of the plaintiff-opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 directing to restore to their status quo ante till 15-2-1995 and 19-2-1995 in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 14 of 1995 (along with Miscellaneous Appeal No. 12 of 1995) and setting aside the order dated 9-2-95 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Mymensingh directing the parties to maintain status quo in OC Suit No. 19 of 1995.

2. It has been stated in the revisional application that the plaintiff opposite parties were members of the Executive Committee of the Mymensingh Dhaka Coach Owners Association and the said Executive Committee has remained virtually unaltered for the last 14 years with papers transaction showing Annual Elections. The last date of 'Elections' was on 6-8-1992 for a period of 2 years expiring on 5-8-1994.

3. It has been stated by the defendant petitioners that due to continual irregularities in the absence of proper elections and democratic norms, the defendant petitioners applied to the Bangladesh Sarak Paribahan Samity, a body corporate and parent organisation of all the road transport service in Bangladesh, to look into their situation and provide remedies there for.

4. It has been further stated in the revisional application that on 12-1-95 the Additional Secretary of Bangladesh Sarak Paribahan Samity in the absence of the Secretary General, addressed a letter to the President/General Secretary of the Mymensingh Dhaka Coach Malik Samity informing them that their committee stands dissolved for the several reasons cited therein and by the same communication appointed ad-hoc committee for holding elections within 3 months from that date.

5. It has been further contended by the defendant petitioners that by virtue of this letter the defendant petitioners decided to take charge of the functions of the said Malik Samity.

6. It has been further contended that on 15-1-95 the Secretary General of the Bangladesh Sarak Paribahan Samity issued a letter to the Additional Secretary General requesting him to withdraw his letter on 12-1-95.

7. It has been further stated in the revisional application that in view of an emergency situation having arisen the Bangladesh Sarak Paribahan Samity called all emergency meeting on 19-1-95 to discuss the situation in details and at the end of this thorough discussion the said Central Samity passed a number of resolutions, chief among them being (a) the approval of the ad-hoc committee contained in the communication of the Additional Secretary General on 12-1-1995 (b) fixing the date for bi-annual elections on 6-4-1995 and (c) denying all knowledge of letters and correspondence which are not brought to the samity's notice. It has been stated in the petition that the last named resolution is a direct denial of the alleged communication of the Secretary General dated 15-1-1995.

8. It has been further stated in the revisional application that with reference to this resolution, the convener of the newly formed ad-hoc committee, the defendant No.2, wrote to the former Chairman of the Mymensingh Dhaka Coach Malik Samity requesting them to hand over the organisational duties and function to the ad-hoc committee at 10-30 AM on 21-1-95.

9. It has been further stated in the revisional application that instead of handing over the duties and functions to the ad-hoc committee, the plaintiff respondent on 21-1-95 filed a declaratory suit before the Senior-Assistant Judge, Mymensingh being TS 19 of 1995 praying for the following relief

(a) a declaration that dissolution of Executive Committee of Mymensigh Dhaka Coach Malik Samity, and the appointment of an ad-hoc committee comprising defendant petitioners 2-10 by letter of defendant No. 1 dated 12-1-1995 is illegal and liable to be cancelled, and that plaintiffs are not bound by the same

(b) to restra tin the defendants 1 and 2 from interfering in the functions of committee by an order of permanent injunction. Along with this the plaintiff filed an application for temporary injunction.

10. The learned Sr. Assistant Judge having heard the plaintiffs was pleased to pass an order on 22-1-95 serving notice upon defendant-opposite parties asking them to show cause within 7 days as to why the order prayed for should not be granted, and in the meanwhile passed an order of ad interim injunction restraining the defendants from interfering with the working of the Executive Committee.

11. It has been further stated in the revisional application that before the order of the Senior Assistant Judge could be communicated the Assistant Commissioner and Magistrate acting under the orders of the Additional District Magistrate, Mymensingh and in apprehension of a breach of peace sealed the offices of the samity and left keys, with the report keeper of the settlement record room till disposal of the suit.

12.On 23-1-95 the defendant petitioners appeared and contested the matter by filing a written objection stating, inter alia, that plaintiffs have not made out an arguable prima facie case for injunction, that the balance of convenience is in favour of the defendants and against the plaintiffs inasmuch as the Executive Committee of the Mymensingh Dhaka Coach Malik Samity headed by the plaintiffs had been dissolved at the instance of the defendant No.1 due to malpractice, mismanagement and high-handedness of the plaintiffs in running the affairs of the Association. The defendants further stated that the term of the Executive Committee had expired on 5-8-94 and no fresh elections had been called for or held even 6 months after the expiry of that period, and that the plaintiffs were ignoring the directives of the Bangladesh Sarak Paribahan Samity and further there was even no constitution for Mymensingh Dhaka Coach Owners Association and no constitution could be given by committee whose term had expired 6 months earlier, and therefore, no such illegal committee could extend its own life with retrospective effect from 2 years to 3 years. And those arbitrary and high handed and unlawful acts of the plaintiffs have caused colossal damage to the spirit and image of the Samity and created an undesirable situation in the transport sector. And that at this juncture the President of the Bangladesh Sarak Paribahan Samity (to which all other such transport samities are affiliated) along with others called an Emergency Meeting of the Central Committee on 19-1-1995 and after a thorough discussion upheld the spirit of the letter written by the defendant No.1, Additional Secretary General on 12-1-95 and resolved further that the ad-hoc committee had been legally constituted, that elections to the Executive Committee of the Samity will be held on 6-4-1995 under the supervision of the Central Committee under the circumstances the plaintiffs being no longer in the Executive Committee cannot seek equitable relief or obtain an injunction and hence the same should be dismissed.

13. On perusal of the relevant documents and after hearing the parties the Senior Assistant Judge passed an order of status quo till disposal of the suit by his order dated 9-2-1995.

14. Against the said order the defendant petitioners preferred an appeal before the learned District Judge, being Miscellaneous Appeal No. 12 of 1995 along with at application for stay of the order of the Senior Assistant Judge. The appeal was admitted but the prayer for stay was refused by order dated 12-2-1995.

15. The opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 also filed an appeal being Miscellaneous Appeal No. 14 of 1995 before the learned District Judge, Mymensingh along with an application for temporary injunction.

16. The learned District Judge admitted the appeal against the order of status quo but rejected the prayer of the plaintiffs for temporary injunction in the followings words:

"By a petition they (Plaintiff appellants) now pray for temporary injunction. The order of status quo is also a sort of injunction in favour of the plaintiffs-appellants. I find no ground to issue an order of temporary injunction on the face of an order of status quo."

In course of the hearing the plaintiff respondents on 23-2-1995 put in 2 applications

(a) for withdrawal of their petition for temporary injunction and

(b) prayer for an order of mandatory injunction under Order 39, rules 1 and 2 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

The prayer for withdrawal of the application for temporary injunction was allowed, and the prayer for mandatory injunction was fixed for hearing on 25-2-95.

17. The application for mandatory injunction was contested by the defendants by filing written objections categorically denying all the allegations in detail.

18. The learned District Judge heard both the appeals together and disposed of the same by one order dated 22-3-95, setting aside the order of status quo, allowing the prayer for temporary injunction restraining the defendants from disturbing the plaintiffs in the management of the affairs of the Mymensingh Dhaka Coach Malik Samity till disposal of the suit. The learned District Judge was further pleased to pass an order restoring the plaintiffs to their status quo ante till before 15-2-95 and 19-2-95 by an order of temporary mandatory injunction and ordered that the same order shall govern the fate of the Miscellaneous Appeal No. 12 of 1995.

19. Against the said order dated 22-3-95 passed by the learned District Judge in Miscellaneous Appeal Nos. 14 and 12 of 1995, the present defendant petitioners have preferred this revisional application.

20. Mr. Ziaur Rahman Khan appearing for the defendant-petitioners has submitted that the order of the learned District Judge is erroneous, bad in law and has occasioned a failure of justice and should be set aside.

21. Mr. Ziaur Rahman Khan has further submitted that the learned District Judge committed an error of law by allowing the prayer for temporary injunction even after the plaintiffs had withdrawn their application for temporary injunction on 23-2-95 and this has resulted in an error in the decision occasioning a failure of justice.

22. M. Ziaur Rahman Khan has further submitted that the learned District Judge by granting a mandatory injunction at an appellate stage acted with material irregularity and beyond jurisdiction and hence the order in the decision is occasioning a failure of justice.

23. Mr. Khan has further submitted that the Executive Committee of the plaintiffs had no locus standi and the ad-hoc committee admittedly duly appointed by the Bangladesh Sarak Paribahan Samity was the lawful committee.

24. Mr. Khan has further submitted that the plaintiffs extended their committees with retrospective effect from 2 to 3 years, and this action was arbitrary, irregular, illegal and inequitable and hence the plaintiffs have disentitled themselves to the equitable remedy of injunction.

25. It has been further submitted by Mr. Khan that in an appellate stage the Court has no jurisdiction to entertain the application of temporary injunction and granting the order of injunction as a remedy of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. Mr. Khan further submitted that the granting of injunction by the learned District Judge without fresh evidence has caused an error of law occasioning failure of justice. Mr. Khan has further submitted that when disputed question of fact has arisen, no injunction should be granted. Mr. Khan further submitted that by giving retrospective effect of his order the learned District Judge committed illegality.

26. It has been further submitted that the impugned order suffers from non-application of judicial mind. Mr. Khan has also submitted that the plaintiffs have not come with clean hands and, as such, they are not entitled to an equitable relief. Mr. Khan has submitted that the balance of convenience is in favour of the defendant-petitioners.

27. Mr. Khan in support of his contention has argued that only in rare case the mandatory injunction is granted and in support of his submission has referred to AIR 1956 (Cal) page 428.

28. Mr. Habibul Islam Bhuiyan, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2, by filing a counter affidavit has submitted that the Additional Secretary of the Bangladesh Sarak Paribahan Samity has no lawful authority to dissolve the executive committee of the Mymensingh Dhaka Coach Malik Samity and the plaintiff opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 are duly elected President and Secretary of the Mymensingh Dhaka Coach Malik Samity and the dissolution of the executive committee of the Mymensingh Dhaka Coach Malik Samity by the Additional Secretary of the Bangladesh Sarak Paribahan Samity is totally illegal and without any lawful authority and that being the position the courts below committed no illegality deciding the issue in favour of the plaintiff opposite party Nos. 1 and 2.

29. It has been further submitted by the learned Advocate for the opposite parties that the injunction order of the trial Court was shown to the Commissioner and the Magistrate even then they in collusion with the defendants sealed the office of the Malik Samity in defiance of Court's order.

30. Mr. Bhuiyan also submitted that the Courts below reaching upon correct finding that the plaintiffs have a prima facie arguable case and, as such, there was no scope of interference in this Court in exercising its jurisdiction under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Mr. Bhuiyan submitted that the learned Court below committed no error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in passing the impugned order.

<u>31. Mr. Bhuiyan has further submitted that the appellate Court has given reasons for passing an order of mandatory injunction. Mr. Bhuiyan has submitted that the plaintiffs are in management of the affairs of the committee. Mr. Bhuiyan lastly submitted that the Court has inherent power to pass an order of injunction. Mr. Bhuiyan in support of his contention has referred to 35 DLR (AD) 42 and has submitted that mandatory injunction on an inter-locutory application may be granted to restore the status quo and the Court has inherent jurisdiction to pass an order of mandatory injunction in a proper case.</u>

32. I have heard both the parties at length, perused the application of the defendant petitioners and the counter affidavit on behalf of the plaintiff opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 and the impugned judgments.

33. The plaintiff opposite parties filed a declaratory suit before the Senior Assistant Judge, Mymensingh being OC Suit No. 19 of 1995 (Title Suit No. 19 of 1995) for declaration that the dissolution of the executive committee of the Mymensingh Dhaka Coach Malik Samity and the appointment of an ad-hoc committee comprising the defendant petitioners Nos. 2-10 by letter of defendant No. 1 dated 12-1-95 is illegal and liable to be cancelled and the plaintiffs were not bound by the same and to restrain the defendant Nos. 1 to 10 from interfering in the functions of the committee by an order of permanent injunction. Along with this the plaintiffs filed an application for temporary injunction.

34. The learned Senior Assistant Judge passed an order of ad-interim injunction restraining the defendants from interfering with the working of the Executive Committee on 22-1-95.

35. After hearing both the parties, the Senior Assistant Judge on 9-2-1995 passed an order of status quo till disposal of the suit.

36. Being aggrieved the defendants petitioners have preferred an appeal before the learned District Judge being Miscellaneous Appeal No.12 of 1995 along with an application for stay of the order of the Senior Assistant Judge. The plaintiff opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 filed an appeal being Miscellaneous Appeal No.14 of 1995 before the learned District Judge, Mymensingh along with an application for temporary injunction.

37. It appears that in the course of hearing the plaintiff opposite parties filed two applications a) praying for withdrawal of their petition for temporary injunction, b) praying for an order of mandatory injunction under Order 39, rules 1 and 2 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The prayer for withdrawal of the application for temporary injunction was allowed and the prayer for mandatory injunction was fixed for on 25-2-95. The application for mandatory temporary injunction of the plaintiffs was contested by the defendants by filing written objection.

38. The learned District Judge heard both the appeals together and disposed of the same by a single judgment dated 22-3-95, setting aside the order of status quo, allowing the prayer for temporary mandatory injunction restraining the defendants from disturbing the plaintiffs in the management of the affairs of the Mymensingh Dhaka Coach Malik Samity till disposal of the suit. The learned District Judge was further pleased to pass an order restoring the plaintiffs to their status quo ante till before 15-2-95 and 19-2-95 by an order of temporary mandatory injunction. It is admitted that there was an executive committee of the Mymensingh Dhaka Coach Malik Samity and it was headed by the plaintiffs respectively as the President and Secretary.

39. It appears that on 12-1-95 the Additional Secretary of the Bangladesh Sarak Paribahan Samity in the absence of Secretary General, addressed a letter to the President/General Secretary of the Mymensingh Dhaka Coach Malik Samity informing them that their committee stands dissolved for the several reasons cited therein and by the same communication appointed an ad-hoc committee for holding elections within 3 months from that date. And the defendant-petitioners by virtue of this letter addressed by the Additional Secretary of the Bangladesh Sarak Paribahan Samity decided to take charge of the function of the said Malik Samity.

40. It is contended on behalf of the plaintiff opposite party Nos.1 and 2 that they are President and Secretary respectively of the Bangladesh Sarak Paribahan Samity and that the Additional Secretary of the Bangladesh Sarak Paribahan Samity has no lawful authority to dissolve the executive committee of Mymensingh Dhaka Coach Malik Samity and it is further contended that the dissolution of the executive committee of the Mymensingh Dhaka Coach Malik Samity by the Additional Secretary of the Bangladesh Sarak Paribahan Samity is totally illegal and it has been contended that the life of the plaintiffs executive has been duly extended by the General Body of the Samity. It appears that the fight between the two sides is over the organisational functions and duties of the Mymensingh Dhaka Coach Malik Samity, on the one side there is a committee of the plaintiffs opposite party Nos.1 and 2 and on the other side, the newly formed ad-hoc committee of which defendant No.2 is the convener. It appears from the revisional petition, para 8 that the convener of the newly formed ad-hoc committee (defendant No.2) wrote to the Chairman of the Mymensingh Dhaka Coach Malik Samity requesting them to hand over the organisational duties and functions to ad-hoc committee at 10-30 AM on 21-1-95. That on the same date that is, 21-1-95, the plaintiff opposite parties filed a declaratory suit (OC Suit No.19 of 1995) for declaration that the dissolution of the executive committee was illegal. It appears that the executive committee of the plaintiffs claim themselves as the lawful committee as duly elected committee and their claim is that their life (the life of the plaintiff executive committee) has been lawfully and duly extended by the General Body of the Samity wherein 107 members including defendants No.2-10 were also present.

41. On the other hand, the convener of the newly formed ad-hoc committee (of the defendant No.2) claims to have the organisational duties and functions. The case of the defendant petitioners is that the term of the executive committee was over and the executive committee should hand over the organisational duties and functions to the ad-hoc committee and the unlawful acts of the plaintiffs in not doing so have caused colossal damage to the spirit and image of the Samity and created an undesirable and unbearable situation in the transport sector, and while the situation was such, the President and Secretary of the Bangladesh Sarak Paribahan Samity along with others called an Emergency Meeting of the Central Committee on 19-1-95 and after a full ledged discussion upheld the spirit of the letter written by the defendant No.1 and the ad-hoc committee has been legally constituted.

42. The learned Assistant Judge upon consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case finds in his judgment a prima facie arguable case in favour of the plaintiffs. On appeal the learned District Judge also found that the plaintiffs made out an arguable and prima facie case. The appellate Court found "since the plaintiffs are found to have made out an arguable and prima facie case for temporary injunction followed by an order of status quo on 9-2-95 any disturbance of theirs status quo ante till before 15-2-95 and 19-2-95 is to be restored".

43. The learned District Judge observed that the letter dated 15-1-95 written by the Secretary General of Bangladesh Sarak Paribahan Samity, adequately demonstrates that objective of

বাংলাদেশ সড়ক পরিবহন সমিতির কেন্দ্রীয় কর্মকর্তা ও শাখা সমিতির মধ্যে সৌহার্দমূলক সম্পর্ক অতীতের ন্যায় অব্যাহত রাখিয়া সাধারণ মালিকদের কল্যাণের অবদান রাখাই আমাদের মূল উদ্দেশ্য-কোন শাখা/ইউনিট এর কার্যকরী পরিষদের বিলুপ্তি ঘটাইবার মত কোন ক্ষমতা বাংলাদেশ সড়ক পরিবহন সমিতির গঠনতন্ত্রে কাহাকেও দেওয়া হয় নাই”।

44. It appears that by the letter dated 12-1-95 of the defendant No.1 the Executive Committee of Mymensingh Dhaka Coach Malik Samity has been dissolved on one hand (by the Additional Secretary General of Bangladesh Sarak Paribahan Samity). While court of appeal below found from the letter dated 15-1-95 of the Secretary General of the Bangladesh Sarak Paribahan Samity as mentioned above.

45. In view of the above circumstances of the case a great situation might arise over the whole affairs of the executive committee on one side and the ad-hoc committee on the other side.

46. It has been contended on behalf of the plaintiffs that defendant No.1 had not given the present executive committee a chance of being heard before dissolving their committee and, as such, natural justice has been denied to the plaintiffs by the defendant No.1.

47. Keeping in view of the facts and circumstances of the case both the Courts below found an arguable case in favour of the plaintiffs.

48. In view of the concurrent findings of the Courts below that the plaintiffs have a prima facie arguable case and multiplicity of proceedings are likely to be cropped up, I find that the suit itself should be heard expeditiously to avoid deterioration of the law and order situation concerning the associations of the parties.

49. I find that the learned District Judge acted within his inherent power and has rightly allowed the plaintiffs' prayer for temporary injunction and restraining the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 from disturbing the plaintiffs in the management of Mymensingh Dhaka Coach Malik Samity till disposal of the suit by the learned Assistant Judge.

50. Whether the newly formed ad-hoc committee or the existing committee of Mymensingh Dhaka Coach Malik Samity Association executive Committee is the proper committee to work till the next election may be decided in the original suit itself after taking evidence and hearing both the sides and I think the suit be heard expeditiously within two months after arrival of this order.

51. In this view of the discussions made above, I find no illegality in the impugned judgment passed by the learned District Judge, Mymensingh.

In the result, the Rule is discharged without any order as to costs.

End.

lawyer:
AB Roy Chowdhury, Advocate -----For the Petitioner. 
AQ Rashid Ahmed, Assistant Attorney-General -----For the Opposite Parties.
parties:
Hindu Deity Lakshmi Gobinda Jeu ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Deputy Custodian, Enemy Property (now vested property), Government of Bangladesh and others ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
This Rule is directed against the judgment and decree dated 7-11-1980 passed by the 5th Court of Additional District Judge, Dhaka in Title Appeal No. 165 of 1977 affirming the judgment and decree dated 18-8-77 passed by the Second Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 34 of 1970 dismissing the suit.

2. The petitioner as plaintiff instituted a suit in the Second Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka being Title Suit No. 34 of 1970 for declaration of title in the suit property and for a further declaration that the suit property cannot be treated as Enemy property (Vested property). The case of the plaintiff, in short, is that, Deity Lakshmi Gobinda Jeu is the owner of the property and it has been rightly recorded as such in CS Khatian Nos. 68 and 142 of Mouza Kirtibashdi under police station Raipura in the District of Dhaka as a rent-free debutter property of Bigraha Narayan Jeu and the plaintiff Narayan Jeu has been owning and possessing' the same although without any interruption. It has also been alleged that during the SA operation the suit property was wrongly recorded in the name of one Suresh Chandra. Roy, who had no right, title interest and possession therein at any point of time and there is absolutely no basis for the fraudulent entry in the SA Khatian. It has also been alleged that recently defendants 1 and 2 made illegal exercises for treating the suit property as an enemy property, now vested property, taking advantage of the wrong SA Khatian and this necessitated the filing of the suit. It has also been alleged that it was on 12-5-69 the plaintiff for the first time learnt that the suit property has been enlisted by the defendants as a vested property.

3. Defendant No. 2, the Assistant Custodian of Enemy Property Dhaka filed written statement in the suit denying the material allegations of the plaint and contended, inter alia, that the suit property is not a debutter property. It was also alleged that the suit property was the secular property of one Suresh Chandra, Roy who subsequently settled in India, following which the suit property has become enemy property by operation of law. It was also alleged that the suit property was made by the Government as an abandoned property under section 92 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act after meeting all legal formalities and thereafter the suit property was leased out to defendant No. 4 and the lessee has been in possession thereof.

4. Defendant No.4 also contested the suit by filing a separate written statement denying the material allegations of the plaint and contended, inter alia, that the suit property was the secular property of Suresh Chandra Roy and he abandoned the case property without making any arrangement for payment of rent following which the Government took over possession of the suit property as an abandoned property under section 92 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and thereafter settled the same with him and his brother Shafiuddin and since then they have been owing and possessing the same in their own right. It was further contended that the suit property is not a debutter property and the plaintiff has no right, title, interest and possession therein

5. At the trial, the plaintiff examined five witnesses and the contesting defendants examined three witnesses and exhibited a series of documents in support of their respective cases.

6. The learned Subordinate Judge by his impugned judgment dated 18-8-77 dismissed the suit on contest. Being aggrieved, the plaintiff petitioner took an appeal before the District Judge, Dhaka being Title Appeal No.165 of 1977, and the learned Additional District Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka who heard the appeal, has been pleased by his impugned judgment dated 17-11-80 to dismiss the appeal and to affirm the judgment and decree passed by the learned trial Court. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid impugned judgment and decree, the petitioner moved this court and obtained the present Rule.

7. Mr. AB Roy Chowdhury, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, submits that the learned Courts below evidently erred in law in dismissing the suit without admitting and considering the evidence of any of the eight witnesses examined by the contending parties and on misconstruction of CS Khatian Ext. 1 and 1(a) and the same has resulted in error in the impugned decisions occasioning failure of justice. The learned Advocate further submits that in the face of the consistent and overwhelming evidence proving that the plaintiff Deity is the owner of the suit property and the suit property is a deb utter property and the deity has been in physical existence in the suit property all through, the learned Court of appeal below evidently erred in law, on misreading and non-reading on the materials evidence and on mere surmises, to hold that the Deity migrated to India following which the suit property has become an enemy property and subsequently vested property and the same has occasioned failure of justice. The learned Advocate further submits that in the face of the CS khatian Exts.1 and 1(a) clearly showing the suit property as a rent free debutter property of Deity Lakshmi Gobinda Jeu Bigraha and there being absolutely no evidence on record to prove as to how the suit property became the secular property of Suresh Chandra Roy, and the plaintiff being in continuous peaceful possession of the same all through, the learned Courts below erred in law in holding on mere surmises and conjectures that the suit property was the personal property of Suresh Chandra Roy and the same has resulted in error in the impugned decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned Advocate submits that in the face of the clear assertion in the plaint and in the face of clear evidence of PW 1 that for the first time on 12-5-1969 he learnt that the suit property was being treated as vested property by the defendants and that he never filed any objection in any abandoned property proceeding or vested property proceeding in connection with the suit property and there being even no suggestion by the contesting defendants to that effect, the learned Courts below were manifestly wrong in illegally finding that the plaintiff had earlier knowledge about treating the suit property as an abandoned property, as a result of which the suit is barred by limitation under section 92/(A) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and the same has occasioned failure of justice.

8. Mr. AQ Rashid Ahmed, the learned Assistant Attorney-General appearing for the Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, opposite Party No. 3, submits that the learned Courts below rightly dismissed the suit after recording necessary findings and, as such, the impugned judgments being concluded by concurrent findings of fact are immune from attack in revision. The learned Assistant Attorney-General further submits that although the learned Courts below did not elaborately discuss and consider the evidence of the witnesses examined by the contending parties, the learned Courts below duly considered all material aspects of the case and, as such, the impugned judgments are sustainable in law as the same have not occasioned failure of justice.

9. The learned Advocate for the petitioner has placed before me the impugned judgments. As the learned trial Court as well as the learned appellate Court did not discuss and consider the evidence of the seven witnesses examined by the contending parties, I allowed Mr. Chowdhury to place before me the evidence of the witnesses examined by the contending parties for better appreciation of the submissions made by the learned Advocates of the parties.

10. PW 1 Prafullah Chandra Bhattacharjee stated in his evidence that he is the Shebait of the plaintiff Deity Sree Gobinda Jeu Bigraha and the suit land belongs to the plaintiff Deity. He also stated that the usufructs of the suit properties are used for the daily seva puja of the plaintiff and for holding periodical parvans of the Deity. He also stated that the properties belong to the Deity since time immemorial as debutter property. He added that before him his father Debendra was the Shehait and before him Sharat Chandra Bhattacharjee was the Shebait of the plaintiff. He also stated that in the CS Khatian Exts.1 and 1(a) the suit land has been recorded in the name of the plaintiff a debutter property. He further stated that the original Bigraha was installed in a mud-walled temple but this temple subsequently became dilapidated following which the Deity was installed in a thatched hut and a pucca building of the deity is already under construction. He further stated besides the plaintiff Deity there are other Deities in the suit premises for a long time and the plaintiff and the other Deities were never removed to any other place at any point of time. He also stated that he sees the plaintiff in possession of the suit property from his childhood. He stated that the suit property was wrongly recorded in the SA Khatian in the name of Chandra Roy, although he had no title interest and possession therein. He stated that he cultivated a portion of the suit property himself and his bargadars cultivated the remaining portion. He clearly stated that no notice was served upon the plaintiff or upon him for treating the suit property as enemy property. He also stated that he never heard earlier that the suit property had been declared as abandoned property. He asserted that the plaintiff was never dispossessed from the suit property. He clearly stated in his evidence that he did not file any objection in the Enemy property office or Abandoned property office in connection with the suit property. He sated that Naib of Harirobi Tahsil office took his signatures on some papers on the plea that he would get the debutter property released from the list of the enemy property.

11. In cross-examination he admitted his signatures in Exts A and A(1), the two notices under section 92 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. He also proved the signature of Subimal Kanti Pal in one of such notices Ext. A(3). He stated that his father Debendra Chandra Bhattacharjee and others did not file Miscellaneous Appeal No.395 before the Commissioner of Dhaka Division.

12. PW 2 Jogesh Chandra Dey, aged about 70 years, stated in his evidence that Kirtibashid village in at a little distance from his house and he goes to the Akhra for offering pujas. He stated that he knows PW 1 as the Shebait of the Deity. He also stated that he has seen the plaintiff Deity and other Deities in the Akhra since his childhood and none of the Deities was shifted to any other place at any point of time. In fact, these were shifted to an adjacent hut. He also stated that PW 1 is the Shebait of the Deity and he manages the suit property, as such. He further stated that before PW 1, his father possessed the suit property as the Shebait. He also stated that PW 1 became the Shebait of the Deity when his father became invalid. He clearly stated that the suit land never belonged to Chandra Roy and he never possessed it.

13. In cross-examination he stated that Chandra did not take away with him the Deity when he left for India. He refuted the defence suggestion that defendant No. 4 was inducted into possession in the suit property by the Additional Deputy Commissioner.

14. PW 3 Md Ali, aged about 59 years, stated in his evidence that he is a member of Daulatpur Union Parishad and the Akhra stands in his Union and he sees Deities in the Akhra since his childhood. He stated that the plaintiff owns and possesses the suit property through his Shebait. He stated that before PW 1 Profulla, his father Debendra was the Shebait of the Akhra and before him one. Sarat was the Shebait thereof. He clearly stated that pujas and melas are held in the Akhra. He also stated that defendant No. 4 serves in Dhaka .and he never possessed the suit land.

15. In cross-examination he stated that he was defeated in the last election held in 1965 by one Yunnus and defendant No. 4 canvassed for him.

16. PW 4 Md Amjad Ali, aged about 70 years, stated in his evidence that he sees the Deity in the Akhra since his childhood. He also stated that he cultivated some land of the Akhra as bargadar under PW 1 as the Shebait of the deity. He also stated that pujas are held in the Akhra with the usufructs of the suit property. He clearly stated that none but the deity ever possessed the suit land. He also stated that before PW 1, his father Debendra was the Shebait and defendant No. 4 never possessed the suit land.

17. In cross-examination he stated that he cannot say the plot No. and the Khatian No. of the land he cultivated as the bargardar of the plaintiff.

18. PW 5 Alauddin, an Advocate, stated in his evidence that he was appointed commissioner by the Court for holding local inspection of the suit property. After holding the said inspection he submitted his inspection report marked Ext. 3. He prepared the sketch map Ext. 4.

19. In cross-examination he stated that before holding local inspection he duly served notice upon the learned Advocate for defendant No. 4 but at the time of the inspection none from defendants' side remained present.

20. DW 1 Abdul Aziz stated in his evidence that the suit land belonged to Suresh Chandra, who was the local Zamindar. He stated that Suresh Chandra Roy left for India in 1962-63 making no arrangement for payment of rent or for the cultivation of the suit land, following which the government took over the suit property as abandoned property after meeting legal formalities. He proved notices under section 92 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy, Act 1950, marked Exts. C to C(3) series, in which PW 1 Profullah Chandra Bhattacharjee signed. He stated that in due course of law, the Government settled the suit property with him and his brother Shafiuddin and he obtained possession of the suit land on 12-11-63 and since then they have been owning and possessing the same. He further stated that Debendra Chandra Bhattacharjee and others filed Miscellaneous Appeal No. 395 of 1967 before the Divisional Commissioner, Dhaka objecting against the treating of the suit property as abandoned property. The Divisional Commissioner sent back the case on remand to the ADC (Revenue) Dhaka whereupon the ADC found that the suit property should not be declared as enemy property but the said order was subsequently set aside on review and the order of the settlement was maintained. He stated that the plaintiff Deity never possessed the suit land and the suit property was never a debutter property.

21. In cross-examination he stated that he is an auditor serving at Dhaka since 1967 and he lives in Dhaka. He admitted that he has no other paper except the SA Khatian to show that the suit property actually belonged to Chandra Roy. He denied the suggestion put by the plaintiff that they created false papers for illegally grabbing the suit property in collusion with some officials of the Revenue Department. He stated that he cannot say if pujas are held in the tin shed constructed by PW 1.

22. PW 2 stated in his evidence that defendant No. 4 has been in possession of the suit land since 12-11-67 after he was put into possession by the ADC (Revenue) he stated that the plaintiff Deity never possessed the suit land.

23. In cross-examination he stated that he was serving in the Revenue Department in Dhaka since 1969: He also stated that he is a co-villager of DW 1. He admitted that recently a tin-shed has been constructed in the suit land. He also stated that he cannot say how many plots are there in the suit land.

24. DW 3 Ramijuddin Ahmed stated in his evidence that defendant No. 4 possessed the suit land.

25. From the scrutiny of the evidence discussed above it is clearly seen that it has been established by most convincing and overwhelming evidence that Deity Lakshmi Gobinda Jeu Bigraha has been in physical existence in the suit premises from time immemorial and it never migrated to India at any point of time. It has also been proved by most cogent and consistent evidence that PW 1 Prafullah Chandra Bhattacharjee has been the Shebait of the Deity since the death of his father Debendra Chandra Bhattacharjee and before him Suresh Chandra Chakrobarty was the Shebait of the Deity. CS khatians Exts. 1 to 1(a) clearly prove that one Suresh Chandra Roy was the Shebait of the Deity at the time of the preparation of the CS record and Deity Lakshmi Jeu Bigraha is the owner of the suit property as a rent free jote. It is thus evident that the learned Courts below on misreading and non- reading of the material evidence on record and on misconstruction of the CS Khatians Exts.1 and 1(a) found that it has not been proved that PW 1 Prafullah Chandra Bhattacharjee is the Shehait of the Deity. It has been proved by most consistent and overwhelming evidence that the plaintiff has been in actual physical possession of suit property all through and the usufructs of the suit property are used for the daily seba pujas of the Deity. The witnesses examined by the plaintiff are all independent, natural and probable witnesses and their evidence does not suffer from any legal infirmity.

26. On the other hand, the DWs are not only interested witnesses but also they do not appear even to know the suit property. In this case, no witness has been examined on behalf of the Government. DW 1 Aziz serves in the AC Office at Dhaka and he is the alleged lessee of, a portion of the suit property. He has practically no knowledge about the origin of the suit property. DW 2 Md Sirajuddin serves in the T&T Department at Dhaka and he is a co-villager of DW 1. He has practically no knowledge about the suit property. DW 3 Ramijuddin Ali serves in the T&T Department at Dhaka. He admitted in his evidence that he cannot say if there is any hut in the suit property. It is thus evident that the DWs have- no direct knowledge about the possession of the suit property. The contesting defendants miserably failed to prove by any reliable evidence that they actually obtained delivery of possession in the suit property on the basis of the alleged settlement from the Government. The defence has totally failed to prove by any evidence as to how the contesting defendants possess the suit land. In the facts and circumstances of the case, it must be held that the paper relied on by the contesting defendants in support of their claim are essentially paper transactions for creating a basis of claim in support of the defendants' case. In the face of the CS khatian which clearly show that the suit property is a rent-free debutter property belonging to Deity Lakshmi Gobinda Jeu Bigraha and Suresh Chandra Roy was simply the Shebait of the deity at the relevant time, it is manifestly evident that the suit property belongs to the plaintiff Deity as a debutter property and it never belonged to Suresh Chandra Roy as his personal property. The SA khatian prepared in the name of Suresh Chandra Roy in thus found to be without any basis at all and consequently, it is of no legal consequence. The learned Courts below on mis-construction of the CS khatians Exts 1 and 1(a) took the suit property as the personal property of the Shebait of the plaintiff and fell in error in finding that the suit property, in course of time, became the secular property of Suresh Chandra Roy, on mere surmises and conjectures. These findings by the learned courts below are vitiated by misreading and non-reading of the materials evidence and misconstruction of CS khatians Exts 1 and 1(ka) has resulted in error in the impugned decision occasioning failure of justice. There is absolutely nothing on record to find that the Deity migrated to India at any point of time or that it was taken to India by the Shebait and consequently the finding of the learned Court of appeal below on this point is evidently against the evidence on record, simply being the product of wild imagination, which cannot be allowed to stand. Since the plaintiff has successfully proved that the suit property belongs to Deity Lakshmi Narayan Jeu Bigraha and the plaintiff has been in physical possession thereof all through, the illegal exercises made by the defendants to treat the suit property sometimes as an abandoned property and sometimes as a vested property are found to be patently illegal and malafide moves, having no sanction of law.

<u>27. This case involves an element of public importance in that the same property is once treated as an abandoned property and subsequently as an enemy vested property. Once a property becomes an abandoned property, it vests in the Government and, as such, the action of the defendants in treating the suit property as an enemy property is evidently illegal and without jurisdiction in the face of their claim that it earlier had become an abandoned property under section 92( 4) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. In view of the plaintiffs clear case that the plaintiff for the first time on 12-5-69 learnt that the defendants were trying to treat the suit property as an enemy property and soon thereafter he filed the present suit praying for declaration of the plaintiffs title therein and for a further declaration that the defendants cannot treat the suit property as a vested property, there is no reason to hold that the suit is barred by limitation. This finding of the learned Courts below is evidently illegal and arbitrary and consequently, the same is not sustainable in law. PW Profullah Chandra Bhattacharjee in his evidence clearly stated that he never filed any objection in any abandoned property proceeding or vested property proceeding. It was never brought to his notice at the time of his cross-examination by the contesting defendants that he himself filed objection before the Revenue Authority praying for release of the suit property from the abandoned list. In the facts and circumstances of the case and the evidence on record, it must be held that the learned Courts below were manifestly wrong in holding that the suit is barred by limitation as no objection within 90 days of the notice treating it as an abandoned property under section 92(4) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 was taken by the plaintiff overlooking the vital fact that the whole exercise to treat the suit property as an abandoned property and subsequently enemy property and vested property is evidently an illegal and malafide move having no' touch with the reality and all these did not in any way affect the interest of the plaintiff. Moreover, from a close reading of the proceedings under section 92(4) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 it appears to me that the provision for institution of a suit in the civil Court within 90 days of the order of the Government treating a property as an abandoned property does not provide any penal consequence for the failure of the aggrieved party to institute the suit within 90 days and, as such, it cannot be said that the aggrieved party is debarred from challenging the order of the Government subsequently by instituting a suit. The provision of section 92(4) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act is thus found to be merely directory and not mandatory and it does not stand as a bar against the suit as held by the learned Courts below. In this view of the matter the learned Court of appeal below erred in law in holding that the suit is barred under section 92(4) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950.</u>

28. In the facts and circumstances of the case and the evidence on record, I am constrained to hold that the learned Courts below. seriously erred in law in dismissing the suit on non-reading and misreading of the material evidence on record and on misconstruction of the important documents in the CS Khatians Exts. 1 and 1(a) and the same has occasioned failure of justice. As the plaintiff has been able to prove its title in the suit land and continuous possession therein, I do not find any reason as to why the suit should not be decreed. In view of the fact that the suit property is a Debutter property of the Deity and there is absolutely no basis for its becoming the secular property of its former Shebait Suresh, the mere recording of the suit property in the name of Suresh in SA khatian is evidently wrong and without any foundation whatsoever and the same cannot affect the plaintiffs right, title and interest in the suit property and any way there is no dispute to the proposition that the CS khatians has a presumption of correctness undersection 103(b) of the Bengal Tenancy Act while the SA khatian has no such presumptive value. The learned Courts below thus evidently erred in law in placing too much reliance on the SA khatians completely ignoring the overwhelming evidence on record to prove that it had no legal foundation and factual basis. For the reasons stated above, I am constrained to hold that the learned Courts below were wrong in passing the impugned judgments on erroneous view of law and on illegal and irrelevant considerations and the same are liable to be set aside in the interest of justice.

<u>29. Mr. Chowdhury has placed before me the case of Sukumar Bose and others vs Abani Kumar Halder and others reported in 60 CWN 778 in which it has been held that a debutter property can never be turned into a secular property. In view of the proposition that once a property becomes a property of the Deity, which is immortal, it continues to be a property of the Deity for all times to come. The dedication of any property to an idol takes place at the time of installation of the idol or preceding it or it many take place after the, installation of the Deity and after the dedication, in all cases, it becomes the property of the idol and ceases to be the property of the donor. Even if a particular image may be destroyed, the Deity whose visible form the image is, continues for ever and its property as debutter property remains totally unaffected. In this connection, we are required to remember the Hindu belief that Deity represents the Eternal Being and is therefore immortal. The named idol in whose favour the property is once dedicated can never cease to exist. If the image is mutilated or defiled, destroyed or lost, due to any reason, a new image is installed and consecrated. It is enough if an image is established substantially representing the old one and is treated as such. In our case under review, there is absolutely no evidence on record to hold that the Deity was destroyed or it was removed to India. On the other hand, the overwhelming and convincing evidence is that the Deity has been in physical existence in the suit property all through, exercising actual acts of possession therein and, as such, there can be no occasion for the extinction of the plaintiffs title in the suit property.</u>

30. The learned Courts below placed too much emphasis on Ext. 3 series showing the defendants' purported exercise of power under section 92 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 in which the signature of PW 1 Profullah Chandra Bhattacharjee, all along with others, appears. It is clear from the explanation of PW 1 Profullah Chandra Bhattacharjee that the Tahshilder concerned took his signature in the notice on the plea of releasing the suit property from the enemy property list. This evidence of PW 1 remains totally unchallenged. Moreover, mere putting a signature on a notice by PW 1, along with others, by itself does not mean that PW 1 had complete knowledge about the contents of the notice. If any authority is needed to fortify my view, we may profitably refer to the case of Amanatullah vs Ali Mohammad Bhuiyan reported in 1997 BLD (AD) 199 = 2 BLC (AD) 134. PW 1 who is evidently a man of little learning and simple manner, cannot thus be saddled with the liability of knowing the full contents of the notice so as to make this binding upon him as the Shebait of the Deity, plaintiffs.

31. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to cost. The impugned judgment and decree dated 7-11-80 passed by the learned 5th Court of Additional District Judge Dhaka in Title Appeal No. 165 of 1977 on affirming the judgment and decree dated 18-8-77 passed by the learned Second Court dismissing the suit, are set aside and Title Suit No. 34 of 1970 of the Second Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka is hereby decreed and plaintiffs title in the suit property is declared. It is further decreed that the suit property cannot be treated as abandoned property or vested property (enemy property) by the defendants.

Send down the lower Court records at once.

End.

parties:
Khadiza Begum ------ Petitioner 
Vs.
Shahjalal Islami Bank Ltd., and another ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Mahmudul Hoque J: On an application under Article 102 of the Constitution of Bangladesh this Rule Nisi has been issued at the instance of the petitioner calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why Order No. 19 dated 20-9-2011 (Annexure-F) passed by the respondent No.2 in the Artha Rin Execution Case No . 114 of 2010 issuing certificate in favour of the respondent No.1 in respect of the property of the Petitioner should not be declared illegal, without jurisdiction and is of no legal effect and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. Facts relevant for disposal of this Rule Nisi, in brief, are that the land measuring 41 sataks covered by CS Khatian No. 485, SA Khatian No. 16, RS Khatian No. 155 and City Jorip Khatian No. 2431, CS Plot Nos. 701 and 702 and SA Plot Nos. 1270 and 1271 and City Jorip Plot No. 7801 originally belonged to one Moimunnessa, who by a registered Sale Deed No. 4521 dated 17-5-1969 transferred the same to one Mosharraf Hossain. The said Mosharraf Hossain while in possession and enjoyment of the property obtained loan from Agrani Bank, Amin Court Corporate Branch, Dhaka on 3-1-1985 by mortgaging the said property as security against the loan. After the death of said Mosharraf Hossain his heirs redeemed the mortgage by a Deed of Redemption dated 29-3-2010. After redemption by an amicable partition amongst the heirs of Mosharraf Hossain, Md Nazirul Islam got the property in his share. Said Md Nazirul Islam sold 2.65 Kathas or 397 Sataks land out of aforementioned plots to the present Petitioner Khadiza Begum by Deed No. 4845 dated 19-5-2010. The petitioner after purchase constructed a two storied building thereon and residing in the said house. On 17-6-2012 an Officer of the respondent Bank visited the property purchased by the Petitioner and disclosed that the Bank acquired title of the property through Court. On coming to know the said fact the Petitioner by making a search obtained information from the Court concerned and came to know that the respondent Bank obtained an ex-parte Decree by filing Artha Rin Suit No. 45 of 2010 and thereafter by filing Artha Rin Execution Case No. 114 of 2010 obtained a certificate of title under section 33(7) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003("Ain") vide Order No. 19 dated 20-9-2011 and also came to know that the property in question was mortgaged to the respondent No.1 Bank by the petitioner's Vendor vide Mortgage Deed No. 3562 dated 17-7-2003 as second mortgage. It further stated that the Petitioner is the legal owner of the property in question but the respondent No. 1 by practicing fraud obtained an ex-parte Decree and a certificate of title from the Court. The Petitioner is a bonafide purchaser for valuable consideration and she has right to protect her property as a bonafide purchaser without notice of second mortgage. By filing Supplementary Affidavit the petitioner also states that the property in question is situated at Dhaka District but the certificate issued by the Artha Rin Adalat, at Chittagong had no territorial jurisdiction which is in violation of the provisions contained in section 27( 1) of the Ain. At this juncture the petitioner by filing this application challenged the validity and legality of the impugned order and obtained the present Rule and Order of Stay.

3. The respondent No.1 Bank contested the Rule by filing an Affidavit-in-Opposition denying all the material allegations made in the writ petition contending, inter alia, that the owner of the property Md Nazirul Islam mortgaged the property to the Bank as security against loan granted to M/s Eastern Accessories Industries a proprietor- ship concern of one Fazlul Haque. The borrower having been failed to pay the loan to the respondent No. 1 Bank, the Bank filed Artha Rin Suit No. 45 of 2010 and obtained an ex-parte Decree against the borrower and the guarantor." Thereafter, the Bank as Decree Holder put the decree into execution by filing Artha Execution Case No. 114 of 2010. In the said Execution Case, the property in question was placed on auction twice under sections 33(4) and (2) of the Ain but no bidder participated in the auction. Finally, the Decree Holder Bank obtained a certificate of title under section 33(7) of the Ain from the Court. While the respondent No. 1 Bank initiated the process for taking over possession of the property, the present petitioner with a view to obstruct the said process filed the instant writ petition and obtained the present Rule and Order of Stay. It is also stated that the Petitioner claimed that she has purchased a portion of the mortgaged property from the mortgagor Md Nazirul Islam on 19-5- 2010 i.e. after creation of mortgage with the Bank and, as such, the transfer is hit by section 530 of the Transfer of Property Act. It is also stated that the Artha Rin Adalat committed no illegality in issuing a certificate vesting the title in the Decree Holder Bank under section 33(7) of the Ain and, as such, the petitioner has no locus standi to challenge the impugned order by invoking writ jurisdiction.

4. Mr Nurul Amin, the learned Advocate appearing for the Petitioner submits that the property in question was mortgaged to the Agrani Bank by Mosharraf Hossain who died leaving Md Nazirul Islam and others as heirs. Nazirul Islam redeemed the mortgage from Agrani Bank and after redemption he sold 397 sataks from the said property to the Petitioner on 19-5-2010 and thereafter the Petitioner constructed a two storied building thereon. Mr Amin further submits that the Petitioner being a bonafide purchaser for value is protected by the provision of section 53 of the Transfer of Property Act. It is also argued that the Artha Rin Adalat before issuance of certificate under section 33(7) of the Ain took steps for holding auction twice under section 33(1) and (4). But on both occasions the Adalat failed to company, with the provisions contained in section 33(1) and (4) in its entirety such as beating drum in the locality and affixing of the notice in the Notice Board of the concerned Court as provided in section 33( 1) of the Ain. He also argued that the property situated in Dhaka District but the certificate issued by the Artha Rin Adalat, at Chittagong is in violation of the provision of section 27 of the Ain. He further submits that the Decree Holder Bank cannot directly obtain a certificate under section 33(7) without taking recourse to section 33(5) of the Ain when they took step under section 33(4) and, as such, the impugned order passed by the Adalat issuing a certificate under section 33(7) of the Ain is palpably illegal and without jurisdiction.

5. Mr Mukunda Chandra Devonath with Mr Khan Mohammad Shameem Aziz, the learned Advocates appearing for the respondent No. 1 Bank submit that the Artha Rin Adalat committed no illegality in issuing the certificate under section 33(7) of the Ain in favour of the Decree Holder Bank as the mortgaged property could not be sold in auction for want of bidders. It is also argued that the petitioner is not a party to the proceedings and her claim is based on a sale deed executed and registered on 19-5-2010 i.e. after the creation of the mortgage in question with the Bank by the vendor of the Petitioner and, as such, the said transaction is hit by section 530 of the Transfer of Property Act. Since the transfer is a void transaction as per section 530 of the T.P. Act, the Petitioner has no right to challenge the impugned order by filing this application. He also submits that since the Petitioner acquired no title in the property by alleged purchase in the year 2010, issuance of certificate under section 33(7) of the Ain by the Artha Rin Adalat at Chittagong has not in any way prejudiced the Petitioner and, as such, the Rule is liable to be discharged. In support of his submissions he has referred to the case of Rashid Mahbub vs IFIC Bank Ltd reported in 13 BLC 78, Mir Motiur Rahman Zihadivs Artha Rin Adalat, Tangail reported in 15 BLT (AD) 267 and Dr Md Habibuzzaman Chowdhury vs Bangladesh reported in 64 DLR 281.

6. Heard the learned Advocates for the parties, perused the Application, Supplementary Affidavits, Affidavit-in-Opposition and the Annexures annexed thereto.

7. In the instant Rule the first question raised is whether the Artha Rin Adalat can issue a certificate on application filed by the Decree Holder under section 33(7) of the Ain when they took steps under section 33(4) of the Ain for holding further auction of the mortgaged property and thereby, obviating the necessity of following the provisions contained under sections 33(5) and (6) of the Ain. To meet the question, as raised in the instant case the provisions of sections 33(5) and (7) of the Ain may be looked into which run thus:-

৩৩। (৫) কোন সম্পত্তি [উপ-ধারা] (১),(২),(২ক),(২খ),(২গ),(৩) ও (৪) এর বিধান অনুসারে] বিক্রয় করা সম্ভব না হইলে, উক্ত সম্পত্তি, ডিক্রীকৃত দাবী পরিপূর্ণভাবে পরিশোধিত না হওয়া পর্যন্ত, দখল ও ভোগের অধিকারসহ ডিক্রিদারের অনুকূলে ন্যস্ত করা হইবে, এবং ডিক্রিদার [উপ-ধারা] (১),(২),(২ক),(২খ),(২গ),(৩) ও (৪) এর বিধান অনুসারে]

উক্ত সম্পত্তি বিক্রয় করিয়া অপরিশোধিত ডিক্রির দাবী আদায় করিতে পারিবে, এবং আদালত ঐ মর্মে একটি সার্টিফিকেট ইস্যু করিবে।

(৭) উপ-ধারা (৪) ও (৫) এর বিধান সত্ত্বেও, ডিক্রিদার উল্লেখিত সম্পত্তি মালিকানা সত্ত্বে পাইতে আগ্রহী মর্মে আদালতের নিকট লিখিতভাবে আবেদন করিলে, আদালত,উপ-ধারা  (১),(২),(২ক),(২খ),(২গ),(৩) ও (৪) এর বিধানাবলীর কোনরূপ হানি না ঘটাইয়া। উপ-ধারা (৪) ও (৫) এর কার্যক্রম অনুসরণ করা হইতে বিরত থাকিবে; এবং ডিক্রিদারের প্রার্থিমতে  উল্লেখিত সম্পত্তির স্বত্ব ডিক্রিদারের অনুকূলে ন্যস্ত হইয়াছে মর্মে ঘোষণা প্রদানপূর্বক তৎমর্মে একটি সনদপত্র জারী করিবে এবং জারীকৃত এইরুপ সনদপত্র স্বত্বের দলিল, হিসাব গণ্য হইবে; এবং আদালত উহার অনুলিপি সংশ্লিষ্ট  স্থানীয় সাব-রেজিস্ট্রারের অফিসে নিবন্ধনের জন্য প্রেরণ করিবে।

8. From a plain reading of the aforesaid provision of law it appears that in the event of having a certificate of title under section 33(7) of the Ain the Decree Holder Bank required to follow the provisions of section 33( 1) to (3) and shall refrain from taking any steps under sub-sections (4) and (5). But in the present case the Decree Holder took steps under section 33(4) for holding further auction of the mortgaged property. It is noted that for the purpose of getting a certificate of title under section 33(7) of the A in the law does not enjoin upon a Decree Holder Bank to take step under section 33(4) of the Ain. However, as in the present case when the Bank takes steps under section 33(4) there is no escape route to sidetrack or jump over the provisions of sections 33(5) and (6). The Decree Holder Bank in this situation ought to have invoked the process under section 33(5) of the Ain since the auction have failed and there- after to follow other provisions as contained in section 33(6) of the Ain. Evidently the Decree Holder Bank deviating from that sequential process instead of taking resort to the aforesaid provisions of law straightway applied under section 33(7) of the Ain praying for issuance of the certificate declaring title of the mortgaged property vested in the Bank. This Court finds such invocation of the law to be contrary to the provisions contained in section 33(7) of the Ain. As per provisions of law once the Decree Holder takes steps under section 33(4) for holding further auction there remains no option but to follow the said provision to its statutarioly intended and prescribed

conclusion and progressing in stages through the express provisions of sections 33(5), (6) and (7) of the Ain.

9. Since the Artha Rin Adalat issued a certificate directly under section 33(7) of the Ain without allowing prior necessary recourse to the provisions of sections 33(5) and (6) the impugned order passed by the court is found to be illegal.

10. Second question raised is whether the Artha Rin Adalat, Chittagong can issue a certificate declaring the title of the property vested in the Decree Holder under section 33(7) of the Ain where the property is situated outside the territorial jurisdiction of the said Court. To meet the question raised, section 27(1) of the Ain may be looked into which runs thus:-

২৭।(১) অর্থ ঋণ আদালত কর্তৃক প্রদত্ত কোন আদেশ বা ডিক্রি উক্ত আদালত কর্তৃক, অথবা উক্ত আদালত জারীর জন্য যে আদালতে প্রেরণ করে, সেই আদালত কর্তৃক জারি হইবে।

<u>11. It appears from the language as used in the above quoted section 27 (1) should the mortgaged property situated beyond the jurisdiction of the Executing Court, it is incumbent upon the Court to send the case to the Court having local jurisdiction for execution of the same. In the present case admittedly the property situated in Dhaka District but the Artha Rin Adalat at Chittagong initiated the process of auction and issued the certificate under section 33(7) of the Ain which is absolutely beyond its territorial jurisdiction as per provision contained in section 27(1).</u>

12. In the unreported case of S.Co. Cement Limited represented by its Managing Director vs Artha Rin Adalat No.4, Dhaka (Writ Petition No. 5360 of 2010) a Division Bench of this Court held that:

"The mortgaged property in relation to an auction sale situated in another District, the Artha Rin Adalat is under a legal obligation to send the execution case to the concerned Artha Rin Adalat of the other District where the property is situated. This is unavoidably necessary for proper execution and satisfaction of the decree" (Per Md Emdadul Huq J).

13. Therefore, the certificate issued by the Court indeed, had no jurisdiction and, as such, the issuance of certificate by the Artha Rin Adalat, Chittagong is illegal and without jurisdiction.

14. Thirdly, whether the Sale Deed No. 4845 dated 19-5-2010 by which the Petitioner claims title in the property is hit by section 53D of the Transfer of Property Act. To answer this question raised, provision of Section 53D may be looked into which runs thus:

"530. Immovable Property under mortgage not to be transferred- No immovable property under registered mortgage shall be remortgaged or sold without the written con- sent of the mortgagee and any re-mortgage or sale made otherwise shall be void."

15. Admittedly, the property in question was mortgaged to the Bank by Md Nazirul Islam on 17-7-2003. The petitioner purchased the property by a deed dated 19-5-2010 i.e. after mortgage of the property to the Bank. Section 53D of TP Act came into force on 1-7-2005. Therefore, since the purchase of the petitioner is subsequent to the mortgage deed the same is apparently attracted by the provisions of section 53D of the Transfer of Property Act.

16. Finally, question raised by the respondent, whether this Court in writ jurisdiction can decide a claim of the petitioner claimant without evidence and who is not a party to the proceedings.

17. Admittedly, the petitioner before this Court is not a party to the proceedings. Her case is that she has purchased a little portion of the property from the mortgagor Md Nazirul Islam and is a bonafide purchaser of the mortgaged property for value without notice.

<u>18. It is in this context, this Court finds that the Petitioner has remedy under the provisions of Artha Rin Adalat Ain 2003 and an avenue to ventilate her grievance under sections 32 and 33(7kha) and also under sections 38 and 45 of the Ain as the claim of title of the petitioner is not independent of the mortgagor. Moreover, the question of third party claim raised before us is a question off act and requires evidence and enquiry by the Court. In these circumstances this Court is of the view that the petitioner either can settle the dispute amicably out of Court under sections 38 and 45 of the Ain or can take recourse to the relevant provisions of law contained in the Ain by filing an appropriate application before the Artha Rin Adalat, if so advised.</u>

19. With the above observations this Court is inclined to dispose of this Rule

20. In the result, the Rule is disposed of however, without any order as to costs.

21. The impugned Order is hereby, declared illegal and set aside.

22. The Artha Rin Adalat directed to transfer the Artha Jari Case to the competent Court having territorial jurisdiction as per provisions of section 27(1) of the Ain. The respondent Bank shall be at liberty to proceed with the Execution Case before the transferee Court by taking steps under section 33(1) on wards. The transferee Court is also directed to dispose of the case within a shortest time possible after receipt of the case from the transferor Court.

23. The Order of Stay granted at the time of issuance of this Rule by this Court is, hereby, recalled and vacated.

Communicate a copy of the judgment to the Court concerned forthwith.

End.

full_judgment:
Badrul Haider Chowdhury, J:- These two appeals by special leave arise out of an order dated 15.8.88 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division at Dhaka in Writ Petition Nos. 1252and 1176 of 1988. 	

2. The gist of the controversy is that the Commissioner of Affidavit refused to allow the counter- affidavit to be affirmed by the appel1ant at Dhaka on the ground that the writ petition stood transferred to the permanent Bench at Sylhet pursuant to the provisions of Rule 6 of the Supreme Court (High Court Division) Establishment of the Permanent Benches Rules, 1988 framed under Article 100(6) as amended by the Constitution (Eighth Amendment) Act, 1988

3. In the other case the Registrar of the Supreme Court had taken steps for sending the record to Chittagong Bench and the appel1ant was denied to affirm affidavit and have the writ petition heard in the High Court Division at Dhaka. 

4. In these circumstances the appel1ants challenged the constitutionality of amended Article 100 of the Constitution as amended by the Eighth Amendment Constitutional Act The High Court Division dismissed the petitions summarily. 

5. Leave was granted to both the petitions being Civil Petition Nos. 207 and 208 of 1988. In the leave granting order it was mentioned: "Dr. Kamal Hossain, learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner (in Civil Petition No. 207 of 1988), addressed the Court on the effect of the Constitution (Eighth Amendment Act, 1988) which has substituted the original Article 100 by a new Article. The whole argument of Dr. Hossain is that the Constitution contemplates a superior Court, namely, Supreme Court of Bangladesh comprising the Appel1ate Division and the High Court Division vide Article 94. By amending Article 100 for the purpose of setting up permanent Benches the basic structure of the Constitution has been altered and it seeks to destroy the independence of judiciary and the character and rule of effectiveness of the High Court Division. It is submitted that Article 100 (5) purports to mean that the President has been empowered to re-determine by executive fiat the territorial jurisdiction of the Permanent Benches which in effect renders the Constitutional provision e.g. Articles 94, 95 (3), 101,102 nugatory and irreconcilable.

6. 45. It will be appropriate to consider the historical background and the genesis of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh.

Proclamation of Independence
The Proclamation of Independence dated 10th April, 1971 issued from Mujibnagar read: 

Whereas free elections were held in Bangladesh from 7th December, 1970 to 17th January, 1971 to elect representative for the purpose of framing a Constitution, 
And
Whereas General Yahya Khan summoned the elected representatives of the people to meet on 3rd Mareh, 1971 for the purpose of framing a Constitution, 
And
Whereas the Assembly so summoned was arbitrarily and illegally postponed for indefinite period, 
And
Whereas the Pakistan Government by levying an unjust war and committing genocide and by other repressive measures made it impossible for elected representatives of the people of Bangladesh to meet and frame a Constitution and give to themselves a Government, 
And
Whereas the people of Bangladesh by their heroism, bravery and revolutionary fervour have established effective control over the territories of Bangladesh,

We, the elected representatives of the people of Bangladesh, as honour bound by the mandate given to us by the people of Bangladesh whose will is supreme duly constituted ourselves into a constituent Assembly, and having held mutual consultations, and in order to ensure for the people of Bangladesh equality. human dignity and social justice;

declare and constitute Bangladesh to be sovereign People's Republic and thereby confirm the declaration of independence already made by Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, and

do hereby affirm and resolve till such time as a Constitution is framed, Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman shall be President of the Republic and Syed Nazrul Islam shall be the Vice-President of the Republic, and that the President shall be Supreme Commander of all the Armed Forces of the Republic,

shall exercise all the Executive and Legislative powers of the Republic including the power to grant pardon,

Shall have the power to appoint a Prime Minister and such other ministers as he considers necessary,

shall have the power to levy taxes and expend monies,

shall have the power to summon and adjourn the Constituent Assembly, and

do all other things that may be necessary to give to the people of Bangladesh an orderly and just government:

We the elected representatives of the people of Bangladesh do further resolve that in the event of there being no President or the President being unable to enter upon his office or being unable to exercise his powers due to any reason whatever the Vice- President shall have and exercise all the powers, duties and responsibilities herein conferred on the President.

We further resolve that this Proclamation of In- dependence shall be deemed to have come into effect from 26th day of Mareh, 1971.

We further resolve that in order to give effect to this instrument we appoint Prof. Yusuf Ali, our duly constituted Potentiary, to give to the President and Vice-President oaths of office. 

46. This declaration envisages the following:-
(a) Because of the unjust war and genocide of the Pakistani authorities it became "impossible for the elected representatives of the people of Bangladesh to meet and frame a Constitution" although General Yahya Khan summoned the elected representatives earlier" to meet on the 3rd Mareh, 1971 for the purpose of framing a Constitution";
(b) The elected representatives duly constitute itself into a constituent Assembly because of the "mandate given to us by the people of Bangladesh whose will is supreme"
(c) It declared Bangladesh to be sovereign People's Republic in order to ensure equality, human dignity and social justice;
(d) Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman was declared to be President and Syed Nazrul Islam Vice-President "till such time as a Constitution is framed";
(e) President or in his absence the Vice-President "shall have the power to appoint a Prime Minister and such other Minister as he considers necessary" It was the presidential system that was envisaged;
(f) President or in his absence the Vice-President "shall have the power to summon and adjourn the Constituent Assembly".

47.This Proclamation was followed by Laws Continuance Enforcement Order dated 10th April, 1971 and the Vice-President ordered "all laws that were in force in Bangladesh on 25th Mareh, 1971 shall subject to the Proclamation aforesaid continue to be so in force" but nothing was said" about the High Court because as it will been seen later by P.O.5 of 1972 (The High Court of Bangladesh Order 1972) "the High Court at Dhaka shall be deemed to have ceased to exist on the 26th day of Mareh, 1971."

Provisional Constitution of Bangladesh Order, 1972 was promulgated on 11th January, 1972 whereupon Justice Abu Syed Chowdhury became the President and Sheikh Mujibur Rahman assumed the office of the Prime Minister. It was clear that shift had been given to the future constitutional framework-from Presidential system to Parliamentary system.

Paragraph 7 staled: "The Assembly shall frame a Constitution for the Republic

Now, the Constitution was promulgated.

In the Preamble it is stated:
"In our Constituent Assembly, this eighteenth day of Kartic 1379 B.S. corresponding to the fourth day of November, 1972 A.D. do hereby adopt, enact and give to ourselves this Constitution".
And Article 153 stated that the Constitution "shall come into force on the sixteenth day of December, 1972."
This is the background of the Constitution of the 1 People’s Republic of Bangladesh.
