Bimsankar, Shiba Bigraha and another ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
This rule on an application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure at the instance of Ashrafunnessa and others arises from the order No. 10 dated 27-9-2000 passed by the learned District Judge, Dhaka in Transfer Miscellaneous case No. 42 of 2000, allowing the Miscellaneous case and transferring the SCC Suit No. 20 of 1998 of the Court of 6th Assistant Judge and Title Suit No. 145 of the Court of 3rd Additional Assistant Judge, Dhaka to the Court of 1st Subordinate Judge, Dhaka for simultaneous hearing with Title Suit No.  240 of 1997 pending in the Court of 1st Subordinate Judge, Dhaka.

2. The opposite party No. 1 filed a transfer Miscellaneous Case No. 42 of 2000 in the Court of District Judge, Dhaka against the petitioners and opposite party No. 2 for transferring SCC Suit No. 20 of 1998 of the Court of 6th Assistant Judge, Dhaka and Title Suit No. 145 of 1997 of the Court of 3rd Additional Assistant Judge, Dhaka to the Court of 1st Subordinate Judge, Dhaka for hearing along with Title Suit No. 240 of 1997 pending in the said Court.

3. The case of the opposite party is that the land comprises in Mouza Shahar Dhaka CS Khatian No. 3926, plot No. 150 area 0616 Ajutansha, originally belonged to Sree Mata Sarajani Daisha, who by registered deed No. 274 dated 11-1-1922 transferred the said land to Sreejukta Rudra Tridandi Tripur Linga Swami and thereafter Swamji transferred the same to plaintiff Bigraha by will and the executors filed a probate case in the Court of learned district Judge and got an order and was possessing the land through tenants and that the predecessor of petitioner and opposite party No. 2,was a ten-ant under them and to grab the said property he managed to get the SA record in his name in collusion with the employees of settlement office and the opposite party No. 1 on 31-12-1996 came to know that SA record of the suit land has been prepared in the name of predecessor of the petitioner and, as such, the opposite party No.  1 has filed Title Suit No. 240 of 1997 in the Court of the first Subordinate Judge, Dhaka for correction of record; that the predecessor of the petitioner is a defaulter in respect of payment of rent and, as such, the opposite party No. 1 has filed SCC Suit No. 20 of 1998 in the Court of the 6th Assistant Judge Dhaka for the eviction of the petitioners; that the petitioners were taking steps for construction of new building in the suit land after demolishing the old and dilapidated building and, as such, the opposite party No. 1 has filed Title Suit No. 37 of 1996 for permanent injunction and the said suit has been transferred to the Court 3rd Additional Assistant Judge, and has been renumbered as Title Suit No. 145 of 1997 and these 3 suits are pending 3 different Courts though the suit property and plaintiffs and defendants are same and, as such, all three suits should be heard by the learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Court Dhaka.

4. The petitioners contested the case by filing written objection denying the material allegations made in the case and their further case is that the nature of 3 suits are different and the parties of the suits are also different, that/Title Suit. No. 145 of 1997 (Title Suit No. 37 of 1996) is a suit for permanent injunction and defendant No. 4 Tofazzal Hossain, son of late Arab Ali, is not a party in Title Suit No. 240 of 1997 and in SCC Suit No. 20 of 1998 and there title Suit No. 145 of 1997 is fixed for hearing and in these suits, the opposite party No. 1 filed an application for temporary injunction which was rejected by the learned Assistant Judge and against that, the plaintiff opposite party No. 1 preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No. 303 of 1997 in the Court of learned District Judge Dhaka who after hearing dismissed the appeal; that Title Suit No. 140 of 1997 pending in, the Court of 1st Subordinate Judge, Dhaka is fixed for filling written statements and SCC suit No. 20 of 1998 is fixed for return of summons as because the summons of said suit has not yet been served upon the petitioners, that the nature of all 3 suits are not similar and there is no land-lord and tenancy relationship between the plaintiffs and defendants; that there is no con-tract and there is no rent receipts and these petitioners are not tenants under the plaintiff opposite party and, as such, since the parities not same and nature of the suits are different, there is no scope for hearing all the three suits by one Court.

5. Learned District Judge after hearing by his judgment and order dated 27-9-2000 allowed the Transfer Miscellaneous Case No. 42 of 2000.

6. Being aggrieved by an dissatisfied with the order dated 27-9-2000 passed by the learned District Judge, Dhaka, the petitioner moved this revisional application before this Court and obtained the present Rule.

7. Mr Swapan Kumar Mitra, the learned Advocate for the petitioners submits that Title Suit No. 145 of 1997 (TS No. 37 of 1996) is a suit for permanent injunction and the parties of the suit are different. Moreover their suits are fixed for hearing and, as such, the learned District Judge committed illegality in transferring the suit for simultaneous hearing along with other two suit while these two suits are fixed for service of notice and for filing for written statements. He further submits that Title Suit No. 240 of 1997 is a suit for declaration of title. Title suit No. 145 of 1997 is a suit for permanent injunction and SCC suit No. 20 of 1998 is a suit for eviction of tenants and thus the nature of all these three suits are not same. It is further submitted that the learned District judge committed illegality in directing to try these three suits simultaneously without taking into consideration that Title Suit No. 240 of 1997 and SCC Suit No. 20 of 1998 are at a preliminary stage and it would come long delay to reach at the hearing stage for disposal along with Title Suit No. 145 of 1997 and, as such, the impugned order is liable to be set aside.

8. Mr HN Nondy, the learned Advocate for the opposite party on the order hand submits that these three suits are pending in different Courts though the suit properties and the plaintiff and defendants are same as such all these three suits should be heard by the learned Subordinate Judge first Court and the impugned order passed by the learned District Judge is legal and he did not commit any illegality in passing the impugned order.

9. The point for determination is to whether the learned District Judge has committed any illegality in passing the impugned order No. 10 dated 27-9-2000 in transferring the Miscellaneous case No. 42 of 2000 and SCC suit No. 20 of 1998 with Title Suit No. 240 of 1997 pending in the Court of Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka whether the petitioner is entitled to get any relief in this rule as prayed for.

<u>10. In the light of the above facts and circumstances of the case, it appears that Title Suit No. 145 of 1997 is a suit permanent injunction and the parties of the suit are different and other two suits are not of the same stage. It further appears from the evidence on record that Title Suit No. 240 of 1997 is a suit for declaration of title and Title Suit No. 145 of 1997 is a suit for permanent injunction and SCC suit No. 20 of 1998 is a suit for eviction of tenants and thus the nature of all three suits are different. Thus from the facts and circumstances of the case, it appears that the learned District Judge committed wrong in directing to try these three suits simultaneously without taking into consideration that Title Suit No. 240 of 1997 and SCC Suit No. 20 of 1998 at preliminary stage and it will take long time to reach at the hearing stage for disposal along with Title Suit No. 145 of 1997 and, as such, the order No. 10 dated 27-9-2000 passed by the learned District Judge is not legal and thus he has committed an error of law in passing the impugned order.</u>

11. It appears that the suits are long, which should be dispose of expeditiously. So the concerned Judge of the Courts where in above mentioned suits are pending are directed to dispose of the above mentioned suits expeditiously preferably within 6 (six) months from the date of receipt of this order without allowing any adjournment to any parties.

In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to cost with a direction to dispose of the SCC Suit No. 20 of 1998. Title Suit No. 145 of 1997 and Title Suit No. 240 of 1997 preferably within 6(six) months from the date of receipt of this order. Let a copy of this order be sent to the concerned Courts for compliance.

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 429 of 2008.
lawyer:
Md Ibrahim Khalil, Advocate-on-Record-----For the Petitioner.
Not Represented-----For the Respondents.
parties:
Abdul Jabbar ----- Petitioner 
Vs.
Akter Hossain Bhuiyan and others ----- Respondents
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 3-1-2006 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 1480 of 1997).
full_judgment:
Shah Abu Nayeem Mominur Rahman J : This petition for leave to appeal is against the judgment and order dated 3-1-2006 passed in Civil Revision No 1480 of 1997 by the High Court Division discharging the Rule, which was issued against the judgment and decree passed in Title Appeal No. 107 of 1994 by the Court of Additional District Judge, Munshiganj, allowing the appeal setting-aside the judgment and decree dated 27-7-1994 passed in Title Suit No. 34 of 1989 by the 1st Court of Sub-ordinate Judge, Munshiganj, dismissing the suit filed for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession.

2. The plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 34 of 1989 in the Court of Sub-ordinate Judge, 1st Court, Munshiganj, for declaration of title and for khas possession. The plaintiff's case in short is that one Kademunnessa Khatun was the superior landlord of the suit land and Salim Khan, Alep Khan and Fazil Khan, sons of Baru Khan, were bargadars under the said landlord and the same has been correctly recorded in the CS Khatian. Afterwards, the said bargadars handed over the said lands to the Zamindar's Seresta. Abdur Razzak, the son of the said Kademunnessa sold out lands in the suit plot No. 42 to Shamsuddin Bhuiyan alias Raja Mia, father of the plaintiff appellants, by registered sale deed dated 19-12-1942 and delivered possession thereof and later Abdul Kashem Sona Mia and Golam Saber Shamsuddin Ahmed grandsons of Kademunnessa became owner-possessors of suit plot No. 41 on basis of a gift and while thus they were owning and possessing the same, they sold out the said land of Plot No. 41 to aforesaid Shamsuddin Bhuiyan and at the relevant time vendor Golam Saber Shamsuddin Ahmed being minor, the patta deed dated 1-7-1944 was executed and registered by his father, the natural guardian, and accordingly said Shamsuddin Bhuiyan has been possessing as owner of the suit plots and enjoying usufructs therefrom on payment of rates and taxes to the Sheresta of the Zaminder and, after withdrawal of the Zamindari System, said Shamsuddin Bhuiyan became a tenant directly under the government pursuant to the provisions of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and, as such, was owning and possessing the suit lands on payment of rates and taxes to the government and that in the SA Khatian, along with the name of Shamsuddin Bhuiyan wrongly the names of aforesaid Salim, Alep and Fazil Khan appeared, and that said Salim, Alep and Fazil Khan did never claimed ownership or possession on the suit plots and they did not pay any rents ever to the government in respect of the suit land. After the death of Shamsuddin Bhuiyan and his wife Rahima Begum, their three sons, the plaintiffs, and one daughter inherited the properties left, including the suit land and on amicable partition, amongst themselves, the plaintiffs got the suit land in their saham and thus became the exclusive owner-possessors of the suit land and were enjoying usufructs there from through Bargader, since they were in employment at different places, and that the plaintiff No. 1 on his retirement, is possessing the suit land and cultivating the same with his own men and that on 9-8-1987 the defendant No. 1, taking advantage of the wrong recording of the names of said Salim Khan and others in the SA Khatian along with real owner Shamsuddin Bhuiyan, claimed the suit land alleging inter alia that father of the defendant No. 1 Abdul Jabbar on 18-3-1984 purchased the suit land from the heirs the SA recorded tenants namely Salim Khan and his two brothers and threatened to dispossess the plaintiffs from the suit land and that faced with such situation the plaintiffs filed criminal case in the Court of Magistrate, who upon hearing dismissed the case holding the defendant to be in possession of the suit land and that the plaintiff also lost in the appeal filed against the order passed by the Magistrate, however as per observation made by the appellate Court, the plaintiffs filed the suit. The defendant contested the suit denying ownership and possession of the plaintiffs in the suit land relying on purchase made by his father. The plaintiffs adduced four (4) witnesses and produced documents marked Exhibits-1 to 4 series in support of their case and the defendant adduced five (5) witnesses and produced documents marked Ka to Gha series in support of his case Five (5) issues were framed and the suit was dismissed holding that the plaintiffs failed to prove their title and possession in the suit land as well as their story of dispossession from the suit land. Being aggrieved the plaintiffs preferred Title Appeal No. 107 of 1998 in the Court of District Judge, Munshiganj, which on transfer was heard and disposed of by the Additional District Judge allowing the appeal and setting-aside the decree passed by the trial Court and thereby decreed the suit vide judgment and decree dated 22-3-1997 declaring the right, title and interest of the plaintiffs in the suit land and ordered for recovery of khas possession and that the defendant-respondents being aggrieved moved the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 1480 of 1997 and Rule issued therein was heard and disposed of by the judgment and order discharging the Rule, which has been impugned in his leave petition.

<u>3. The High Court Division discharged the Rule on detailed discussion of the materials available in the records of the case and that it has been observed that :—</u>

<u>"Mr Md Shafiqul Islam Dhali the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite-party in reply submits that the learned Sub-ordinate Judge, firstly committed error of law in misreading the Exhibit 3, registered deed of sale dated 1-8-1989 executed by CS recorded Zamindar Akkas Uddin in favour of Hazetun Nessa transferring the rent receiving interest of the suit land along with other land, inasmuch as, the same being a registered deed of sale executed and registered about 90 years old and negative presumption of the same could only be formed through evidence keeping in view of the development and circumstances consequent to the execution and registration thereof till the present. Mr. Dhali next submits that the plaintiffs exhibited as many as 20 rent receipts out of them some were issued by Zaminder and 18 of them issued by the Government, being Exhibit 4 series proved the payment of rent in respect of the suit land till 1988 by the plaintiff and also proved the possession and enjoyment of the suit property by the plaintiffs and further standing of collateral evidence of title of the plaintiffs in support of his contention, but the learned Sub-ordinate Judge in his judgment mentioned that the plaintiffs exhibited only 2 rent receipt and thereby proceeded towards by the erroneous decision in support of his contention Mr Dhali relies on the decision of our. Appellate Division reported in 35 DLR (AD) 216 wherein it has been held that rent receipts through not documents of title, are not items of evidence of possession and may be used as collateral evidence of title since possession generally follows of title. Mr Dhali further submits that SA Khatian being Exhibits Kha(2) and Kha(3) and RS Khatian finally published being recorded in the name of the predecessors of the plaintiffs and in the name of the plaintiffs respectively although one of the two SA Khatian being Exhibit Kha(2) contained the name of the CS recorded tenants along with the name of the predecessors of the plaintiff. In this connection Mr Dhali submits that it is settled principle of law that the last record of right will prevail than the earlier record of right, in support of his contention he relies on the decision reported in 35 DLR 295 and 17 DLR 392 and 27 DLR 589 relying on the decision of a Division Bench of this Court reported in 42 DLR 434. Mr Dhali submits that RS Khatian prepared under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act has the presumption of correctness under section 144 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. Mr Dhali finally submits that although the judgment of the learned Additional District Judge is not lengthy but the learned Additional District Judge refers the Judgment of the learned Subordinate Judge adverting the material findings of the learned Sub-ordinate Judge and discussed the oral and documentary evidence in doing so and that there is no misreading of any evidence on record and neither there is any non-consideration of material evidence on record on the part of the learned Additional District Judge and that being so the Additional District Judge being appellate Court and thereby being the final Court of facts, its judgment is not liable to be interfered with."</u>

<u>And thus found that the trial Court arrived at its wrong decision because of non-consideration of the material evidences on record, namely the rent receipts granted by the government marked Exhibits-4 series and the deed dated 1-8-1899, a 90 years old registered deed as well as the SA Khatian and RS Khatian, standing in names of the predecessor-in-interest and in the name of the plaintiffs respectively, marked Exhibits-Kha(2) and Kha(3). We do not find any reason of differ with the same.</u>

4. In view of our discussion and observation made above, and having regard to the decision of the Appellate Division in the case of Erfan Ali vs Joynal Abedin Mia, reported in 35 DLR (AD) 216, we are of the opinion that the High Court Division has passed the impugned judgment and order in accordance with law on due consideration of the materials on record and hence no interference is called for.

Accordingly the application for leave to appeal is dismissed without costs.

End.

lawyer:
Azizur Rahman Chowdhury with Mohd Feroz and Md Abdul Mannan, Advocates — For the Appellant. 
Dewan AMS Zaman with Osman Gani, Advocates — For the Respondent.
parties:
Osmanullah being dead his legal heirs, Kasimullah & others ------ Plaintiff-Appellants
vs
Faizullah & others ------ Defendant-Respondent
full_judgment:
This Second Appeal at the instance of the plaintiff appellant is directed against the judgment and decree dated 30-4-1973 passed in Title Appeal No.122 of 1973 by Mr MA Wahab, Special Judge and ex-officio Additional District Judge, Sylhet reversing those dated 24-7-1972 passed in Title Suit No.166 of 1970 by he learned Munsif, 1st Court, Sylhet decreeing the suit on contest against defendant No.1 with cost and ex-parte against the rest without cost and declaring that the ex-parte order dated 14-11-1969 passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 491/ 1969 under section 143A East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act of the said Court for correction of the record of rights in respect of the suit-land is illegal, void., fraudulent and without jurisdiction.

2. The case of the plaintiff-appellant briefly was that the schedule-lands measuring 1.83 acre and some other lands originally belonged to one Basanta Kumar Bhattacharjee of village Mobarakpur, under Balaganj Police Station and that the said Basanta Kumar Bhattacharjee was an employee of Khajurichara Tea Estate who used to live there with his family and as such, he asked the plaintiff to manage the property. While the plaintiff was managing the said property as a manager or caretaker, it was declared as enemy property as its owner, the said Basanta Kumar Bhattacharjee left for India and was absent from Bangladesh.

3. The plaintiff later on by a petition got settlement of the suit-property up to 1376 BS from the Assistant Custodian of Enemy Property and his petition for renewal of the lease was under consideration; that one Ahsanullah in the meantime filed a Miscellaneous Case No.413 of 1968 under section 143 A of the East Bangal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and the plaintiff on his prayer was added as a party in the same under Order 1 rule 10 Code of Civil Procedure and then contested the Miscellaneous Case, but Ahsanullah later on withdrew the case and set up the principal defendant No.1 Faizullah to file another Miscellaneous Case No.419 of 1969 by fabricating some false documents and clandestinely secured an ex parte order on 14-11-69 for correction of the record of rights in his favour, though he has had no right title or possession in the said land; that no notice was served on the said Basanta Kumar Bhatta-charjee or his co-sharers. The plaintiff however came to know about the Miscellaneous Case No.491 of 1969 when defendant No.1 gave out in the locality towards the last part of March, 1970 that he had secured an order for correction of the record of rights in his favour in respect of the suit-land. Hence, the present suit against the defendant No. 1 and the Assistant Custodian of Enemy Property, Sylhet as pro-forma defendant No.2.

4. The defendant No.1 contested the suit by filing a written statement wherein he contended, inter alia, that the suit was not maintainable in its present form and it was barred by limitation. He, however denied the case of the plaintiff and stated that he took the jote settlement from Jogendra Kumar Bhattacharjee about 20 years back at a monthly rental of Rs 1.50 per Kedar and since then he had been possessing the suit-land and that during the last survey and settlement operation, the record of rights stood wrongly in the name of the aforesaid Ex-landlord. The defendant No.1 having failed to get the record of right correctly and amicably recorded in his name in the Khatian, filed the Miscellaneous Case No.491 of 1969 and got an ex parte order in his favour for correction of the record of rights and accordingly, the Khatian was modified;. that there was no suppression of notices as alleged in the aforesaid Miscellaneous Case; it was rather the plaintiff who in collusion with the lower rank staff of the Enemy Property Office, Sylhet filed this suit having no subsisting interest in the suit-land and as such, the suit was liable to be dismissed with cost.

5. The learned Munsif, now Assistant Judge framed the following issues for determination in the suit:

i. Is the suit maintainable in its present form?

ii. Is the suit barred by limitation?

iii. Is the plaintiff entitled to get a declaration as prayed for?

iv. To what relief, if any is the plaintiff entitled? Both the parties examined one witness from each side and produced some documents in support of their respective cases.

6. The learned Munsif answered issue Nos.1 and 2 in favour of the plaintiff with the observation that the said issues were not pressed at the time of trial and that the impugned order was passed on 14-11-69 and the plaintiff filed this suit within time on 1-5-1970 and that there was nothing to show against the maintainability of the suit. As to issue No.3, the learned Munsif held that the service of notice upon the plaintiff-opposite party in the Miscellaneous Case No.491 of 1969 was fraudulently suppressed and that defendant No.1 committed fraud in obtaining the ex parte order in that Miscellaneous Case by suppression of facts and also notice and as such, the plaintiff was entitled to get the relief sought for in the suit. With the above findings and observations, the learned Munsif however decreed the suit on contest against the defendant No.1 with cost and ex parte against the rest without costs and further declared that the ex parte order dated 14-11-69 passed in Miscellaneous Case. No.491 of 1969 for correction of the record of rights in respect of the suit-land in favour of the defendant No.1 is void, illegal and without jurisdiction vide his judgment and decree dated 24-07-1972.

7. As against the said judgment and decree, the contesting defendant No.1 Faizullah preferred an appeal before the learned Special Judge and ex-officio Additional District Judge, Sylhet, who after hearing both the sides and on consideration of the materials on record was pleased to allow the appeal on contest and set aside the impugned judgment and decree passed by the learned Munsif and consequently dismissed the suit on contest against defendant No.1 and ex parte against the rest by his judgment and decree dated 30-4-73.

8. Being aggrieved by the same, the plaintiff Usmanullah as appellant preferred the present Second Appeal in this Court.

9. Mr Azizur Rahman Chowdhury, with Md Feroz and Md Abdul Mannan, the learned Advocates, appeared for the appellants who have been substituted on the death of appellant Usmanullah and Mr Dewan AMS. Zaman, with Mr Osman Gani, the learned Advocates, appeared for the defendants respondents.

10. Mr Azizur Rahman Chowdhury, the learned Advocate for the plaintiff-appellant has firstly submitted that the impugned judgment of the Court of appeal below is not a proper judgment of reversal and as such the same should be set aside. To elaborate his argument, the learned Advocate has drawn my attention to the impugned judgment of the Court of appeal below as well as the judgment of the trial Court and then submitted that the trial Court as to the maintainability of the suit and bar of limitation held that the said issues were not pressed before him at the time of trial but still he came to a finding that by suppression of notices the impugned order in Miscellaneous Case No.491 of 1969 was passed on 14-11-69 and the instant suit was filed within time on 1-5-70. He also found that there was nothing to show against the maintainability of the suit; hence he answered the above two issues in favour of the plaintiff. But the lower Appellate Court heard the learned Advocate for the defendant-appellant on the point of maintainability of the suit and ultimately found that the plaintiff had no locus standi to institute the suit and the same was not also maintainable and hence allowed the appeal and set aside the impugned judgment and decree of the trial Court without making any finding as to the question of fraud as determined by the trial Court. It is further submitted by the learned Advocate for the appellant that the lower appellate Court did not at all reverse the findings of the trial Court on the question of fraud and also adverse possession, not to speak of adverting to the reasoning of the trial Court for coming to such findings. The learned Advocate for the appellant further submits that the plaintiff had subsisting interest and possession in the suit-land at the time of passing the order dated 14-11-1969 under section 143A East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act but he was not purposely made a party to the said proceeding. Of course, the original owner of the suit land Basanta Kumar Bhattacharjee and his co-sharer Ranadhir were made parties in that application for correction of the record of rights, but admittedly no notice was duly served upon them. The learned Advocate for the appellant therefore contends that the summons was suppressed by fraudulent means and the ex parte order was obtained surreptitiously. He however asserted that the plaintiff had locus-standi to file the present suit challenging the ex-parte order dated 14-11-1969 of the Miscellaneous Case, though he was not made a party in the same. He claimed his interest in the said property because of his caretaker ship of the interest of the said original owner Basanta Kumar Bhattacharjee, and further on his departure from this country to India, his property became enemy property and the plaintiff then took lease of the same from the Custodian of the Enemy Property by a regular document of lease dated 19-2-1970 and, as such, the plaintiff had every right to challenge the ex parte order passed in the Miscellaneous Case under section 143A of East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act by filing the present suit and the suit was therefore quite maintainable.

11. Mr Dewan AMS Zaman, the learned Advocate for the defendant-respondent, on the other hand, submits that the plaintiff had no locus-standi to institute the suit as he could not show his legal character under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act to be entitled to a declaration of his right, title and interest in the suit-land and a further declaration to the effect that the ex parte order dated 14-11-69 in Misc. Case under section 143A of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act was false, fraudulent and void ab-initio. The learned Advocate further argued that, it was of course the claim of the plaintiff that he was a lessee in the suit-land which was declared as Enemy Property and thus being a lessee in possession of the suit-land, he was competent to challenge the ex parte order of correction of the record of right in the suit-land by institution of the suit, but a lessee was not a necessary party in a suit like this wherein the lessor was already made a party. In support of his contention, the learned Advocate referred to a decision in the case of Saifuddin Ahmed vs Deputy Custodian, Enemy Property Management Board, reported in 31 DLR 107. He further contended that the suit could be maintainable, had there been a prayer for declaration of plaintiff''s right, title or interest in the suit land together with a prayer for consequential relief. It is further submitted that a suit for a mere declaration to the effect that the impugned ex parte order was false, fraudulent, void, ab-initio and not binding on the plaintiff was not maintainable. Hence that learned Special Judge and ex-officio District Judge rightly held that the plaintiff had no locus standi to institute the suit and the same was not maintainable.

12. The learned Advocate for the respondents, of course submitted that there was no finding by the lower appellate Court as to the question of alleged fraud committed in obtaining the ex parte order in the proceedings under section 143A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act as found by the trial Court, but his contention was that this would not affect the merit of the decision of the lower appellate Court allowing the appeal and dismissing the suit on the ground of maintainability. As to the contention of the learned Advocate for the appellant that the minimum requirements for passing the ex parte order dated 14-11-69 in the proceeding under section 143A of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act were not complied with, apart from the fraudulent suppression of the process or notice and non-compliance of the provisions of inquiry as required under sub-section (4) of section 143A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act by local Revenue Officer in respect of possession of the parties over the land in question before passing such order. It is not clear whether the inquiry as required under the law was properly held in this case. The original records of the Miscellaneous Case are not available before this Court to verify the above contention regarding service of notices and the compliance of the provision of sub-section 4 of section 143A of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act.

13. The learned Advocate for the appellant however already submitted that the ex-parte order dated 24-11-69 was not passed in accordance with law after fulfilling the minimum requirements of passing an ex-parte order or decree and, as such, the same was bad and illegal. In support of his contention, he has referred to a decision, in the case of Bangladesh vs Abdul Wadud reported in 25 DLR (SC) 90.

14. The learned Advocate for the appellant has however taken me through the entire provisions of section 143A of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and tried to show the procedure to be followed in the case of disposal of an application under section 143A of East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. The said section 143A of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act reads as follows:

143A. (1) Any person aggrieved by an entry or omission of entry in record-of-rights prepared or revised and finally published under Chapter IV may, notwithstanding anything contained elsewhere in this Act, file an application along with necessary requisites, for the purpose of correcting mistakes in such record-of-rights in the civil Court which would have jurisdiction to entertain a suit for possession of the land to which such entry relates or in respect of which such omission was made.

(2) An application filed under sub-section (1) shall be deemed to be a plaint and order passed thereon shall have the force of a decree under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

(3) An application filed under sub-section (1) shall contain full particulars of persons likely to be affected by an order on such application and shall also contain the full particulars of the holding to which the entry relates or in respect of which the omission complained of was made.

(4) The Court shall, for the purpose of disposal of application filed under sub-section (1), follow the following procedure, namely:

(a) the Court shall cause notice to be served on the persons named in the application in the manner as provided in the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908;

(b) the Court shall, within seven days of the filling of an application under sub-section (1), send a copy thereof, by registered post at the appellant''s cost, to the Revenue officer concerned for holding a local inquiry, in presence of the parties, concerned, on the subject-matter of the application and the Revenue Officer shall, within fifteen days of the receipt of the copy, hold inquiry and submit the report to the Court;

(c) the Court may allow such reasonable time as it may think fit to file objection to the inquiry report referred to in clause (b) and, if no appearance is made by the opposite party within the time mentioned in the notice, and, if no objection is filed to the inquiry report within the time so allowed, the Court may proceed ex parte with disposal of the application after taking into consideration the said report and other material evidence on record; and

(d) where the report referred to in clause (b) is not submitted or where objection referred to in clause (c) is filed, the Court shall fix a date for hearing and on that date, after hearing the parties and taking into consideration the report, if any, and other evidence which may be adduced by the parties in this behalf, shall pass such order as it may think just and proper.

(5) Any person whose interest has been affected by reason of any entry or omission in the record-of-rights, referred to in sub-section (1), may, within fourteen days of the filing of an application under sub-section (1), appear to be added as co-applicant.

(6) The revenue-officer shall, for the purpose of an inquiry under sub-section (4), have the same power as vested in a civil Court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, including the power of,

(a) enforcing attendance of any person, and examining him on oath; and

(b) compelling the production of any document.

(7) Within thirty days from the date of an order under sub-section (4), an appeal from that order shall lie to the District Judge who may, either himself hear the appeal or transfer it to any other Court subordinate to him but not below the rank of a Subordinate Judge for hearing.

(8) Decision under sub-section (4), if no appeal is preferred from it, or under sub-section (7), shall be final and conclusive.

(9) Where the Court passes an order under sub-section (4), or sub-section (7), revising the entries or rectifying the omission complained of under-section (1), it shall notify the same to the Collector and the Collector shall correct the record-of-rights accordingly.

(10) Any person interested may produce a certified copy of the orders referred to in sub-section (4) or sub-section (7) to the Revenue-Officer and the Revenue-Officer shall make such alterations in the record-of-rights as may be necessary to give effect to such orders.

(11) The record-of-rights corrected under sub-section (9) or sub-section (10), shall be deemed to have been prepared and finally published under Chapter IV of this Act.

(12) An application under sub-section (1) or memorandum of an appeal under sub-section (7) shall, notwithstanding anything contained in the Court-fees Act 1807, bear a fixed Court-fee of rupee one.

(13) For the purpose of an application, appeal, review, revision and consequence of non-appearance, relevant provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure 1908, shall mutatis mutandis apply"

Now, from the above, it appears that on receipt of the application, a notice has to be served upon each of the persons named in the application and then in view of sub-section 4(b) of section 143A an enquiry is to be held as specified therein. Sub-section 4(b) may however be quoted again which is as follows:

The Court shall, within seven days of filing of an application under sub-section (1), send a copy thereof by registered post at the applicant''s cost, to the Revenue-Officer concerned for holding a local inquiry, in presence of the parties, concerned on the subject matter of the application and the Revenue-Officer shall within fifteen days of the receipt of the copy, hold inquiry and submit the report to the Court;

15. Thereafter, the learned Court will give some reasonable time for objection as laid down in sub-section 4(c) which reads as follows:

"The Court may allow such reasonable time as it may think fit to file objection to the inquiry report referred to in clause (b) and, if there is no appearance made by the opposite party within the time mentioned in the notice, and if no objection is filed to the inquiry report within the time so allowed, the Court may proceed ex parte with disposal of the application after taking into consideration the said report and other materials on record; and then comes sub-section 4(d) which is as follows:

"Where the report referred to in clause (b) is not submitted, or where objection referred to in clause (c) is filed, the Court fix a date for hearing and on that date, after hearing the parties and taking into consideration, the report, if any, and other evidence which may be adduced by the parties in this behalf, shall pass such order as it may think just and proper.

16. It also appears in sub-section (5) of the said section that:

"Any person whose interest has been affected by reason of an entry or omission in the record-of-rights, referred to in sub-section (1), may within fourteen days of the filing of an application under sub-section (1), may appear to be added as co-applicant.

17. Thereafter sub-section (6) of the said section:

"The Revenue-Officer shall, for the purpose of an inquiry under sub-section (4), have the same power as vested in a civil Court under the Code of Civil Procedure 1908, including the power of:

(a) enforcing attendance of any person, and examining him on oath; and

(b) compelling the production of any document

and thereafter sub-section (7) of the said section which provides for appeal;

"Within thirty days from the date of an order under sub-section (4), an appeal from that order shall lie to the District Judge who may either, himself hear the appeal or transfer it to any other Court subordinate to him but not below the rank of a Subordinate Judge for hearing" Sub-section (8) provides that:

"Decision under sub-section (4), if no appeal is preferred from it, or under sub-section (7), shall be final and conclusive".

Sub-section (9) of the said section provides as:

"(a) Where the Court passes an order under sub-section (4) or sub-section (7), reversing the entries or rectifying the omission complained of under sub-section (1), it shall be notified to correct the record-of-rights accordingly".

Sub-section (10);

"Any person interested may produce a certified copy of the orders referred to in sub-section (4) or sub-section (7) to the Revenue-Officer and the Revenue-Officer shall make such alterations in the record-of-rights as may be necessary to give effect to such order"

Sub-section (11):

"The record-of-rights corrected under sub-section (9) of sub-section (10) shall be deemed to have been prepared and finally published under Chapter IV of this Act.

Sub-section (12);

"An application under sub-section (1) or memorandum of an appeal under sub-section (7) shall, notwithstanding anything contained in the Court-fees Act 1970 bear a fixed Court-fee of rupee one.

Sub-section (13) of the East Pakistan State Acquisition and Tenancy Act provides that:

"For the purpose of an application, appeal, review, revision and consequence of non-appearance, relevant provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure 1908 shall mutatis mutandis apply."

In the instant case, it is submitted by the learned Advocate for the appellants that the provisions of sub-section (4) of section 143A have not been complied with before passing the ex parte order.

18. Now, it may be pointed out that section 143A of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act is a special provision inserted in East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act in 1965, of course the same has been repealed by another Ordinance No. LXIV of 1975. Its purposes was for correcting mistake in the record of rights on the basis of possession of the parties in the case land. However, the scope of section 143A has been discussed in a decision in the case of Assistant Custodiaiv Enemy Property (L&B) Tangail vs Bholanath Guha and ors reported in 36 DLR (AD) 79 and their Lordships have observed in the following terms therein,

"An application under section 143A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act is not a suit for declaration of title but is a proceeding for rectification of mistakes in the record of right prepared on the basis of possession in the land in question. The scheme of the section shows the possession is the material question. This was a special provision and this section was inserted after section 143 by East Pakistan. Ordinance VIII of 1965. It was however omitted after a few years by Ordinance LXIV of 1975".

Similar view has been expressed in another decision of this Court in the case of Reazuddin & ors vs Jatindra Krishore and others reported in 37 DLR (AD) 202 wherein it has been observed as follows:

"It is well settled that material consideration in a case under section 143A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act is a question of possession. Whatever may be the defect in title, if it is found that the appellants have been possessing the case land when the record of right was prepared, they are entitled to have their names recorded."

From a reading of the above provisions of law and the decisions cited above it is clear that section 143A is meant for a limited purpose for correction of the record of right on the basis of possession of the parties in the case land. Now, the records of the Miscellaneous Case under section 143A are not before this Court. It was also not before the Courts below. Of course, the Courts below could very well call for the same to verify whether the main provisions of sub-section 4 of the said section 143A were complied with before passing the impugned order. The trial Court it appears decided the question wrongly against the contesting defendant mainly on a plea that was non-service of notice upon the opposite parties, i.e. Basanta Kumar and his co-sharer Ranadhir. It has been contended on behalf of the defendant-respondent that mere non-service of notice, cannot be termed as a practice of fraud and it has been further contended that in fact the notice was served upon the principal opposite party, that is the original owner the said Basanta Kumar Bhattacharjee, and in the evidence of both the parties, it has been stated that the suit-land solely belonged to said Basanta Kumar Bhattacharjee. Therefore the learned Advocate submits that there was no fraudulent suppression of notice upon the opposite party No. 1 Basanta Kumar Bhattacharjee as alleged in the Miscellaneous Case. The learned Advocate for the appellant, of course has submitted that it is in the evidence led by defendant No. 1 of the suit that a different address of the said Basanta Kumar Bhattacharjee was given in the application under section 143A from that where he was actually residing and admittedly no notice was served upon the other opposite party namely, Ranadhir. Therefore according to the learned Advocate for the appellant, this kind of non-service of notice constituted fraud and hence the impugned order passed in the miscellaneous case was a nullity in the eye of law. He has relied on a decision in the case of Abul Khair Mia vs Abdul Latif Sarder reported in 32 DLR (AD)167. Now, this question of fraud appears to have been decided by the trial Court in favour of the plaintiff and against the defendant, but the same has been left undiscussed and undecided by the Court of appeal below. The only questions which have been decided by the lower appellate Court are the questions of locus-standi of the plaintiff to institute the suit and its maintainability and those have been decided against the plaintiff-respondent and in favour of the contesting defendant-appellant in TA No. 122 of 1973 and accordingly the trial Court''s decision was found illegal and the same was set aside. Now, question has been raised by the learned Advocate for the appellant that the lower appellate Court erred in law in deciding the question of locus-standi of the plaintiff and maintainability of the suit, particularly when the question of possession of the parties in the suit land was not properly and conclusively decided by a clear finding by both the Court''s below. It is of course the case of the plaintiff-appellant that he had locus-standi to institute the suit as he had subsisting interest and possession in the suit-land on the basis of his alleged caretaker ship of the property and also the alleged lease taken from the Enemy Property Authority. The learned Advocate for the plaintiff-appellant contends that the plaintiff was a caretaker, since before the property was declared as enemy-property on the basis of some letters allegedly written to him by the said Basanta Kumar while serving in the Tea Estate in Sylhet in the years 1961-62 and 65 which were marked as Exts. 9 series. But when he left for India leaving his service, his property was declared as enemy property and the plaintiff took yearly lease of the same from the Enemy Property authority by executing a lease deed in the year 1970. He accordingly paid the salamis and got receipts thereof and thereafter he filed an application for renewal of the said lease and therefore: he claims to have locus-standi to institute the suit.

<u>19. The learned Advocate for the defendant-respondent, on the other hand, submits that the alleged lease was given in the year 1970 according to the showing of the plaintiff and it is the contention on behalf of the defendant that the property was not declared Enemy Property and there was no valid lease granted in favour of the plaintiff. At this stage it may be noticed that the ex parte order which is under challenge in the suit was passed on 14-11-1969 by the learned Munsif in consideration of an application under section 143A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and granting of the alleged lease to the plaintiff by the enemy authority is subsequent to the passing of the said order. Hence, in my view subsequent lease is not material for consideration of the question as to whether the plaintiff had subsisting interest and possession in the land in question at the time of passing the ex parte order in the Miscellaneous Case under section 143A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. Therefore, in my view, both the Courts unnecessarily went into the discussion as to the alleged granting of lease of the property as enemy property to the plaintiff while determining the question of locus-standi of the plaintiff to challenge the order dated 14-11-69 passed in the Miscellaneous Case. Admittedly the plaintiff was not made a party in the Miscellaneous Case under section 143A of East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. Now the question is whether he can challenge the ex parte order passed in the above proceeding under section 143A East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act by institution of this present suit. It is contended by the learned Advocate for the appellant that the plaintiff was in possession of the suit-land at the relevant time as a caretaker of the said Basanta Kumar Bhattacharjee and, as such, he ought to have been made a party in the said proceedings along with said Basanta Kumar and that having not been done, he was seriously prejudiced, particularly when there was suppression of process upon the said Basanta Kumar and another. Hence, in view of the above submissions on the scope of section 143A, the question of possession was very material in determining the locus-standi of the plaintiff for institution of the suit, but unfortunately, both the Courts below over-looked this aspect of the matter and failed to come to any specific finding as to the possession of the parties over the suit-land at the relevant time. It further appears from the impugned judgment of the lower appellate Court that he found the suit to be not maintainable mainly on the ground that the suit was not instituted for declaration of title and for any other consequential relief. It is true that, if the plaintiff wants to base his claim on the basis of his alleged lease from the Enemy Property authority which was admittedly a subsequent event, then possibly that would not help him.</u>

<u>20. However for maintainability of the suit as contended there ought to have been a prayer for declaration of right, title and other consequential relief and for that purpose, the plaintiff could be given an option by the lower appellate Court to amend the plaint and incorporate such prayer for the purpose of the maintainability of the suit. Now, in the instant case, it appears that the plaintiff has come with his claims of interest and possession in the suit land at the relevant time on the basis of his caretaker ship of the suit-land, on behalf of the actual owner of the said land i.e. Basanta Kumar Bhattacharjee and to maintain the suit on that basis as I have said earlier that the determination of the question of possession of the parties over the land at the relevant time was very much material but evidence on the question of possession from both the sides appears to be very meagre and insufficient and further the record of the suit does not show as to whether there was an inquiry by the local revenue officer under sub-section 4(b) of the section 143A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act with regard to the possession of the parties at the relevant time and that could be correctly ascertained only by calling for the records of the Miscellaneous case under section 143A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and in this respect both the Courts failed to apply their judicial mind and to determine the question of actual possession of the parties in the suit-land at the relevant time. The learned Advocate for the defendant-respondent however raised some question with regard to the lease deed Exhibit 1 which shows that it was granted for one year that is for 1373 BS. But the receipt shows the granting of lease for the period of 4 years at a time which is not permissible in law. Of course, it appears that after 1376, the plaintiff filed an application for renewal of the said lease but nothing available on the record whether such renewal was at all granted.</u>

<u>21. Mr Zaman, the learned Advocate for the respondent, has refereed to some provisions of Enemy Property Laws and submitted that lease cannot be granted for more than one year at a time under the Enemy Property Law but the alleged lease deed Exhibit 1 shows that plaintiffs'' alleged lease was granted for 4 years at a time and, thereafter he filed an application for renewal of the same. The learned Advocate for the respondent has referred to a decision in the case of Saifuddin Ahmed vs Deputy Custodian, Enemy Property Management Board, reported in 31 DLR 107 in support of his contention.</u>

<u>22. Mr Chowdhury, the learned Advocate for the appellant, however contends that the relevant laws show granting of lease for 1 year at a time, but, in fact, in the Sylhet region, lease could be granted for more than 1 year at a time. He therefore submits that only for the reason that realisation of salami was made for the lease for 4 years at a time by the enemy authority and a receipt thereof was granted, it cannot be conclusively said that the lease was unlawful or bad. His further contention is that on the basis of the said lease, the plaintiff was in possession of the suit-land and has been still in possession of the same. In any view of the matter when I have observed that in the instant suit, that determination of possession of the parties in the suit land at the relevant time is very much material and the determination of the question as to whether lease as claimed by the plaintiff was valid or not was not so much relevant, for the purpose of deciding the question of locus-standi and the maintainability of the suit, the Court may not give so much weight to the question of the validity or invalidity of the alleged lease.</u>

<u>23. I also do not like to make any observation as to the merit of the submission of the learned Advocate for the appellant on this point of validity of the lease as Enemy Property. The main questions are whether the plaintiff had locus-standi to institute the suit and whether the suit was maintainable or not.</u>

<u>24. Mr Zaman, the learned Advocate for the respondent also argued that as against the order passed in the Miscellaneous case under section 143A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, there is provision for appeal before the learned District judge, the plaintiff could have sought relief to that very Court after passing of the ex parte order, if the relief was not otherwise barred by any other provisions of law, but the same having not been done the plaintiff wrongly instituted the suit for setting aside the impugned ex parte order passed by the learned Munsif. I do not find any substance in this contention of the learned Advocate, as the plaintiff was not made a party in the proceeding under section 143A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and secondly, fraud has been alleged in the plaint against the contesting defendant in obtaining the said ex parte order. It is well settled that an ex parte order under the general law can be set aside by taking resort to the provision of Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure also by review or by way of instituting a suit on the ground of fraud.</u>

<u>25. Therefore, in this respect, I think there is no bar in the institution of the suit on the ground of fraud without availing of the provision for appeal under the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. The plaintiff is however required to establish his locus-standi and the maintainability of the suit. Having considered all aspects of the matter and the relevant provisions of law and the decisions cited above by the parties before me, I am of the view that the lower appellate Court committed gross illegality in determining the question of locus-standi of the plaintiff and maintainability of the suit without coming to a positive finding as to possession of the parties over the suit-land at the relevant time i.e. in 1969 when the application under section 143A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act was filed in the Court of the learned Munsif for correction of record-of-rights and thereafter when the suit was instituted. At the same time, it is not at all proper for the lower appellate Court to avoid coming to a finding as to the question of fraud on discussion of the materials on record although the trial Court came to such a finding in clear terms. Therefore, the judgment of the Court of appeal below is not at all a proper judgment of reversal and the same is liable to be set aside.</u>

In the result, this appeal is allowed and the impugned judgment and decree of the Court of appeal below are set aside and the appeal is sent back on remand to the Court of the learned Additional District Judge and Special Judge for re-hearing and determining the material points as have been pointed out, on the basis of the materials on record and, if necessary, to take further additional evidence from both the sides and particularly with regard to the inquiry report of the revenue officer, if any, of the local. Circle Office, Revenue, concerned and compliance of the provisions of sub-section 4 of section 143A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, and for that purpose, if necessary, the records of that Miscellaneous Case under section 143A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act may be called for and on consideration thereof to dispose of the appeal by a proper judgment in accordance with law in light of the observations made above. In the facts and circumstances of the case, there will be no order as to costs in this second appeal. The learned Advocate for the appellants is permitted to take back his application for additional grounds in view of the above decision.

End.

বিচারপতি জনাব মোঃ আশরাফুল কালামঃ- বিজ্ঞ অতিরিক্ত জেলা জজ, ২য় আদালত, নারায়নগঞ্জ কর্তৃক সিভিল রিভিশন মামলা নং-১৮/২০০৯ এ প্রদত্ত বিগত ইংরেজী ৪.১১.২০০৯ইং তারিখের রায় ও আদেশের আইনানুগ বৈধতা চ্যালেঞ্জ করে দেওয়ান কার্যবিধি ধারা ১১৫(৪) মতে নিলাম ডাককারী দরখাস্তকারী অত্র সিভিল রিভিশন মামলাটি আনায়ন করলে অত্র বিভাগে বিগত ইংরেজী ১৭.১১.২০০৯ তারিখে প্রতিপক্ষগণের উপর নিম্ন রুল জারী করেনঃ

"On an application field under Section 115(4) of the Code of Civil Procedure the auction purchaser petitioner challenged Order dated 04.11.2009 passed by the Additional District. Judge, 2" Court, Narayangonj in Civil Revision No.18 of 2009 allowing the same upon settling aside the judgment and order dated 20.04.2009 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat, Narayangonj in Execution Case No.161 of 2003 and thereby allowing the application under Order XXXIV Rule 5 of the Code filled by the judgment debtor and releasing the mortgaged property upon setting aside the auction sale with direction upon the decree holder bank to handover the original document and possession of the mortgaged property to the judgment debtor. 

Mr. Mrinal Kanti Biswas, the learned Advocate appearing before this Court on behalf of the petitioner submits firstly that the learned Additional District Judge committed error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in interfering with the interim order of the Artha Rin Adalat passed in an execution proceeding initialed under the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003, whereas Section 44 of the said Ain clearly prohibits disturbance of any interim order passed by the Artha Rin Adalat in appeal or revision. He submits that the rejection of the application under Order XXXIV Rule 5 of the Code by the Artha Rin Adalat is an interim order and disturbing the same in revision is as such barred under the aforesaid provision. The only provision being Section 41 of the Ain provides filing of appeal against any order or decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat under certain limitations but the said provision also does not allow an interim order to be challenged, secondly, he submits that the Additional District Judge being a Civil Court has interfered with the order of the Artha Rin Adalat in revision under Section 115(2) of the Code the petitioner has statutory right of challenging the said order in revision under Section 115(4) of the Code subject to granting leave. 

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and also considering the submission advanced as above it appears that the question raised are important questions of law which requires decision. As such leave is granted for revision of the impugned order dated 04.11.2009 passed in Civil Revision No.18 of 2009 by the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Narayengonj. 

Pending hearing of this revision, let the operation of the impugned order dated 04.11.2009 passed in Civil Revision No.18 of 2009 by the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd  Court, Narangonj be stayed for a period of 3 (three) months form date. 
2 (two) sets of requisites be put in within 20.12.2009 for service of notices of this revision upon the opposite parties both by registered post with A/D and by usual course to be returnable within 8(eight) weeks from date." 

2. অত্র রুলটি নিষ্পত্তির নিমিত্তে মামলার সংক্ষিপ্ত বর্ণনা এই যে, 

অত্র সিভিল রিভিশন মামলার ১নং প্রতিপক্ষ অগ্রণী ব্যাংক বাদী হয়ে অত্র সিভিল রিভিশন মামলার ২-৫ নং প্রতিপক্ষণেকে বিবাদী শ্রেণীভূক্ত করে বিবাদীগন যথাক্রমে ১। মেসার্স এম আর ট্রেডার্স, ২। মোঃ মোতালেব চৌধুরী (মালিক), ৩। মোঃ আনোয়ার হোসেন, ৪। তসলিমা আক্তার (বন্ধকদাতা) মোকদ্দমা তায়দাদ মূল্য মং- ১১,৬৭,০৬৪/- (এগার লক্ষ সাতষট্রী হাজার চৌষট্রি) টাকা নির্ধারণ করে অর্থঋণ আদালত, নারায়নগঞ্জ-এ বন্ধকী মোকদ্দমা নং-১৫/২০০৩ দায়ের করে। বর্ণিত বন্ধকী মোকদ্দমা বাদী অগ্রণী ব্যাংক এর অনুকূলে বিগত ইংরেজি ২২.০৭.২০০৩ ইং তারিখে একতরফা সূত্রে প্রাথমিক ডিক্রী হয়। পরবর্তীতে বিগত ২২.১০.২০০৩ইং তারিথে চূড়ান্ত ডিক্রি drawn up হয়। অতঃপর বিগত ইংরেজি ২১.১০.২০০৩ তারিখে অত্র সিভিল রিভিশন মামলার ১নং প্রতিপক্ষ ডিক্রিদার-বাদী হিসাবে অর্থঋণ আদালত, নারায়নগঞ্জ এ সাকুল্য১৩,০৪,৯৮৪/- টাকা আদায়ের নিমিত্তে ডিক্রিজারী মামলা নং-১৬১/২০০৩ দায়ের করে। 

পরবর্তীতে বিগত ইংরেজি ০৮.০৩.২০০৫ ইং তারিখের ব্যাংকের দরখাস্তের প্রেক্ষিতে বন্ধকী সম্পত্তির বাজার দর ২০,০০,০০০/- টাকা র্নিধারিত হয়। পরবর্তীতে বিগত ইংরেজি ২৩.০৪.২০০৬ তারিখে নিলাম বিজ্ঞপ্তি প্রকাশের আদেশ হয়। পরবর্তীতে বিগত ই্ংরেজী ২৬.০৬.২০০৬ তারিখে সিভিল রিভিশন নং-৫৯/২০০৬ এর সিভিল রিভিশন মামলা নং-৫৯/২০০৬ বিগত ইংরেজী ০২.০৮.২০০৬ তারিখে নামঞ্জুর হয়। 

অতঃপর অর্থঋণ আদালত, নারায়নগঞ্জ বিগত ইংরেজী ০৩.০৮.২০০৬ ইং তারিখে নিলাম ক��র্যক্রমের সবোর্চ্চ দরদাতা হিসাবে অত্র সিভিল রিভিশন মামলার দরখাস্তকারী ডাঃ হাবিবুর রহমান (১০,০৪,০০০/-টাকার দরপত্র) এর দরপত্র গ্রহণ করার আদেশ প্রদান করেন এবং ইংরেজী ১৩.০৮.২০০৬ তারিখের মধ্যে অবশিষ্ট টাকা প্রদান করার জন্য দরখাস্তকারীকে নির্দেশ প্রদান করেন। বর্ণিত আদেশ অনুসারে দরখাস্তকারী নিলাম খরিদ্দার ডাঃ হাবিবুর রহমান অবশিষ্ট ৭,৫৩,০০০/- টাকা বিগত ইংরেজী ১০.০৮.২০০৬ইং তারিখে অগ্রণী ব্যাংক, মীরজুমলা রোড শাখায়, নারায়নগঞ্জ এর ০৯.০৮.২০০৬ ইং তারিখে ০৪-২৪২১৬৭১ নং পে-অর্ডার মূলে দাখিল করেন। 

পরবর্তীতে বিগত ইংরেজী ২১.০৮.২০০৬ তারিখে তসলিমা আক্তার দেওয়ানী কাযভিধির ২১ আদেশের ৯০ বিধি অনুযায়ী মিস কেইস নং-২৭/২০০৬ দায়ের করলে তা বিগত ই্ংরেজী ০৩.০৯.২০০৬ তারিখে খারিজ হয়। পরবর্তীতে বিগত ই্ংরেজি ০৪.০৯.২০০৬ তারিখে আদেশ নং ৩৬ মূলে বিগত ই্ংরেজী ০৩.০৮.২০০৬ তারিখের নিলাম বহাল করা হয়। 

অপরদিকে ৪নং প্রতিপক্ষ আনোয়ার হোসেন অর্থজারী মোকদ্দমা নং-১৬১/২০০৩ এর কার্যক্রম চ্যালেঞ্জ করে রীট পিটিশন নং-৮৪১৫/২০০৬ দায়ের করে, যা পরবর্তীতে বিগত ইংরেজী ০৭.০৪.২০০৯ তারিখে আনোয়ার হোসেন আর চালাবেনা মর্মে আদালতকে জ্ঞাত করলে অত্র বিভাগ উক্ত রীট পিটিশন নং-৮৪৫১/২০০৬ খারিজ করেন। 
পরবর্তীতে বিগত ই্ংরেজী ০৯.০৪.২০০৯তারিখে তসলিমা আক্তার দেওয়ানী র্কাবিধির ২১ আদেশে২র ৮৯ বিধি অনুযায়ী অর্ধঋণ আদালত, নারায়নগঞ্জ এ নিলাম রদের আবেদন করেন, যা বিগত ইংরেজী ১৬.০৪.২০০৯ইং তারিখে তামাদি হেতু আদালত খারিজ করেন। পরবর্তীতে বিগত ইংরেজী ১৯.০৪.২০০৯ইং তারিখে উক্ত তসলিমা আক্তার দেওয়ান কার্যবিধি ৩৪ আদেশের ৫ বিধি অনুযায়ী অর্থঋণ আদালত, নারায়নগঞ্জ-এ দরখাস্ত আনয়ন করেন যা বিগত ইংরেজী ২০.০৪.২০০৯ইং তারিখে আদালত নামঞ্জুর করে। 

অত্র সিভিল রিভিশন মামলার ৫নং প্রতিপক্ষ-দায়িক (অর্থজারী মামলার ৪নং দায়িক) তাসলিমা আক্তার অর্থঋণ আদালত নারায়নগঞ্জ এর জারী মামলা নং-১৬১/২০০৩ তে বিগত ই্ংরেজী ২০.০৪.২০০৯ তারিখে প্রদত্ত আদেশ দ্বারা সংক্ষব্ধ হয়ে জেলা জজ আতদালত, নারায়নগঞ্জ-এ দেওয়ানী কার্যবিধির ১১৫(২) ধারা মোতাবেক সিভিল রিভিশন নং-১৮/২০০৯ দায়ের করে। পরবর্তীতে বিগত ইংরেজী ০৪.১১.২০০৯ তারিখে অতিরিক্ত জেলা জজ, ১ম আদালত, নারায়নগঞ্জ সিভিল রিভিশন মামলাটি শুনানী অন্তে মঞ্জুর করেন। 

বিজ্ঞ অতিরিক্ত জেলা জজ, ২য় আদালত, নারায়নগঞ্জ কর্তৃক সিভিল রিভিশন মামলা নং-১৮/২০০৯ এ প্রদত্ত বিগত ইংরেজী ০৪.১১.২০০৯ তারিখে রায় ও আদেশ দ্বারা সংক্ষুব্ধ হয়ে নিলাম ডাককারী ডাঃ হাবিবুর রহমান দরখাস্ত কারী হয়ে দেওয়ানী কার্যবিধির ১১৫(৪) ধারা মোতাবেক সিভিল রিভিশন দায়ের করে অত্র রুলটি প্রাপ্ত হয়। 

3. দরখাস্তকারী পক্ষে জনাব এস,এন, গোস্বামী, এ্যাডভোকেট সংগে আফসানা বেগম ও লিল রানী সাহা এ্যাডভোকেটগণ যুক্তিতর্ক উপস্থাপন করে নিবেদন করেন যে, অর্থঋণ আদালত আইন হচ্ছে একটি বিশেষ (Special) আইন। এই আইনের বিধান মতে সকল আইনের উপর এই আইনটি প্রাধান্য থাকবে, অর্থাৎ যে বিষয়ে এই আইন বর্ণিত আচে সে বিষয়ে দেওয়ানী কার্যবিধির কোন বিধান প্রযোজ্য হবেনা। অর্থঋণ আইনের ধারা ৪৪(২) মোতাবেক অর্থঋণ আদালত কর্তৃক প্রদত্ত কোন অন্তবর্তীকালীন আদেশকে আপীল বা রিভিশন আকারে বিতর্কিত করা যাবেনা। সেমতে ৫নং প্রতিপক্ষ কর্তৃক অর্থঋণ আদালত, নারায়নগঞ্জ কর্তৃক জারী মোকদ্দমা নং-১৬১/২০০৬ এ প্রদত্ত বিগত ইংরেজী ২০.০৪.২০০৯ তারিখের রায় ও আদেশের বিরুদ্ধে জেলা জজ নারায়নগঞ্জ এ সিভিল রিভিশন দায়ের অর্থঋণ আইনের ধারা ৪৪(২) এর পরিপন্থী। 

4. মিঃ গোস্বামী আরও নিবেদন করেন যে, অর্থঋণ আদালত আইন, ২০০৩ এর ধারা ১২(৮) মোতাবেক ক্রেতার রায়কে কোন ভাবে তর্কিত করা যাবে না। তিনি তার বক্তব্যের সমর্থনে বানেসা বিবি বনাম সিনিয়র ভাইস প্রেসিডেন্ট এবং অন্যান্য (৬৩ ডিএলআর (এডি),১৬০) মামলার সিদ্ধান্তটি অত্র আদালতের নজরে আনেন। উক্ত মামলায় আপীল বিভাগ এই মর্মে সিদ্ধান্ত প্রদান করেন; 

In case of an auction sale held illegally or with irregularity the same cannot he challenged. However, owner may use the bank concern for any loss, if suffered because of such illegal or irregular auction sale."
 
5. পরিশেষ মিঃ গোস্বামী নিবেদন করেন যে, অর্থঋণ আদালত কর্তৃক ই্ংরেজী ২০.০৪.২০০৯ তারিখে প্রদত্ত অন্তর্বর্তীকালীন আদেশটি বিজ্ঞ অতিরিক্ত জেলা জজ, ২য় আদালত, নারায়নগঞ্জ কর্তৃক শুনানীর জন্য গ্রহণ অবৈধ এবং এখতিয়ার বহির্ভূত। ফলশ্রুতিতে তার কর্তৃক প্রদত্ত সিভিল রিভিশন মামলা নং-১৮/২০০৯-এ প্রদত্ত বিগত ইংরেজি ০৪.১১.২০০৯ তারিখে রায় ও আদেশও অবৈধ এবং এখতিয়ার বহির্ভূত। 

6. জনাব হিরন্ময় হালদা সংগে জনাব মোঃ জিয়াউদ্দিন মিয়া ১নং প্রতিপক্ষের পক্ষে জবাব দাখিল করে এই মর্মে নিবেদন করেন যে, ন্যায় বিচারের স্বার্থে আদালত যেসব আদেশ নির্দেশ প্রদান করবেন তা অত্র প্রতিপক্ষ সর্বান্তকরণে পালন করবেন। 

7. জনাব খায়ের এজাজ মাসউদ, এ্যাডভোকেট সংগে জনাব শিকদার মাহমুদুর রাজি ও মোঃ রাকিব উদ্দিন ভূইয়া এ্যাডভোকেটগণের ৫নং প্রদিপক্ষ পক্ষে যুক্তি উপস্থাপন করে নিবেদন করেন যে, ডিক্রীজারী পর্যায়ে বন্ধকরদাতাকে তার বন্ধক অবমুক্তকরণের অধিকার দেওযানী কার্যবিধির ২১ আদেশের ৮৯ বিধি, দেওয়ানী কার্যবিধির ২১ আদেশের ৯০ বিধি এবং দেওয়ানী কার্যবিধির ৩৪ আদেশের ৫ বিধিতে দেওয়া আছে। দেওয়ানী কার্যবিধির ২১ আদেশের ৮৯ বিধি ও ২১ আদেশের ৯০ বিধিতে দরখাস্ত দাখিলের নিদিষ্ট সময়সীমা (যা ৩০ তিন) থাকলেও ৩৪ আদেশের ৫ বিধি অনুযায়ী রখাস্ত দাথিলের নিদিষ্ট সময়সীমা নেই। উক্ত ধারার দরখাস্ত দাখিলের ক্ষেত্রে শুধু দেথতে হবে যে নিলাম ২১ আদেশের ৯২ ধারা মতে বহাল হয়েছে কিনা। যদি নিলাম বহাল (Confirm) না হয়ে থাকে সেক্ষেত্রে বন্ধকদাতা ৩৪ আদেশের ৫ বিধির শর্র্তাবলী প্রতিপালন পূর্বক কার বন্ধক অবমুক্তকরনসহ দলিলাদি ফেরত ও দখল পুনরুদ্ধার করতে আেইনগতভাবে অধিকারী। 

8.  জনাব মাসউদ আরও নিবেদন করেন যে, যেক্ষেত্রে বন্ধকী সম্পত্তি বা তার অংশ দেওয়ানী কার্যবিধির ৩৪ আদেশের ৫ বিধির (৩) উপবিধির অধীনে প্রদত্ত ডিক্রী অনুসারে বিক্রয় হয়ে থাকে সেক্ষত্রে বিবাদী (১) উপ-বিধির উল্লিখিত টাকা অতিরিক্ত ক্রেতা কর্তৃক আদালতে জমাকৃত ক্রয় মূল্যের টাকার শতকরা পাঁচ টাকার সমান অংশ ক্রেতা বরাবরে পরিশোধ করার জন্য আদালতে জমা না দেওয়া পর্যন্ত আদালত এই বিধির (১)উপ-বিধির অধীনে আদেশ প্রদান করেন না। যেক্ষেত্রে অনুরুপ টাকা জমা দেওয়া হয়ে থাকে সেক্ষেত্রে আদালত প্রয়োজনীয় আদেশ প্রদান করেন। 

তিনি আরও উল্লেখ করেন যে, যদি কোন বন্ধকদাতা দেওয়ানী কার্যবিধির ২১ আদেশের ৮৯ ও ৯০ বিধি অনুযায়ী দরখাস্ত করে ব্যর্থ হয় তারপরও তিনি ৩৪ আদেশের ৫ বিধির সুবিধা নিতে পারবেন। এর সমর্থনে তিনি গৌর দান্দ মল্লিক  বনাম প্রাদ্যমনা মল্লিক (এআ্ইআর)(৩২) ১৯৪৫ (কলকাতা) পৃষ্ঠা ৬) এবং ১১ ডিএলআর (১৯৫৯) (হাইকোর্ট বিভাগ) পৃষ্ঠা-৮৮, মোকদ্দমাসমূহ রেফারেন্স হিসাবে উপস্থাপন করেন। জনাব মাসউদ আরও নিবেদন করেন যে, বর্তমান মোকদ্দমাতে এটি সুস্পষ্ট যে, বিগত ইংরেজী ০৪.০৯.২০০৬ তারিখে উহা রি-কল হয় এবং পরবর্তীতে উক্ত নিলাম বহাল করে আর কোন আদেশ হয় নাই। সেমতে ৫নং প্রতিপক্ষ তাসলিমা আক্তারের আনীত দেওয়ানী কার্যবিধির ৩২ আদেশের ৫ বিধির দরখাস্ত সম্পূর্ণরুপে আইনসঙ্গত এবং তিনি আইনহত প্রতিকার পেতে হকদার। 

9. এছাড়া জনাব মাসউদ আরও নিবেদন করেন যে, ৫নং প্রতিপক্ষ আপীল না করা সত্ত্বেও রিভিশন-এ তাহাকে ন্যায় বিচার হতে বঞ্চিত করার কোন সুযোগ নাই। ৬৪ ডিএলআর (হাইকোর্ট) (ব্যাংক অব স্মল ইন্ডাস্ট্রিজ এন্ড কমার্সিয়াল বাংলাদেশ বনাম সাহাবুদ্দিন আহমেদ) পৃষ্ঠা-২৪১ এর প্রকাশিত রায়ে মহামান্য হাইকোর্ট বিভাগের একটি দ্বৈত বেঞ্চ এ মর্মে সিদ্ধান্ত প্রদান করেছেন যে, যদি দেখা যায়, বিজ্ঞ নিম্ন আদালত আইনগত কোন ভ্রম করিয়াছেন সেক্ষেত্রে উক্ত ভ্রমাত্মক সিদ্ধান্ত আপীলযোগ্য হওয়ার পরও উহার বিরুদ্ধে আপীল না করিয়া রিভিশন করা হইয়াছে শুধু এই কারণে সংক্ষব্ধ ব্যক্তিকে ন্যায় বিচার হইতে বঞ্চিক করা যাবে না। উক্ত সিদ্ধান্তও অর্থঋণ আদালতের একটি আদেশ সংক্রান্তে ছিল। 
10. জনাব মাসউদ নিবেদন করেন, ৫নং প্রতিপক্ষ ডিক্রীকৃত সমুদয় টাকা বিজ্ঞ অর্থঋণ আদালতে জমা প্রদান করেছেন বিধায় অর্থঋণ আদালতের ৪১(২) ধারার বাধ্যবাধকতাও সম্পূর্ণরুপে পুরন হয়েছে। ফলশ্রুতিতে বিজ্ঞ অতিরিক্ত জেলা জজ আদালত কর্তৃক যে আদেশে প্রদান করা হয়েছে তা যথার্থই আইনসঙ্গত। 

11. পরিশেষে জনাব মাসউদ নিবেদন করেন যে, ৫নং প্রতিপক্ষ অর্থঋণ আদালত আইনের ১২(৮) ধারার কারণে ক্রেতার ক্রয়কে তর্কিত করতে পারে না এমন যুক্তি সঠিক ও আইনসঙ্গত নহে। কারণ ১২(৮) ধারায় বলা হয়েছে যে, Mortgage এর অধীন প্রাপ্ত ক্ষমতা বলে সম্পত্তি বিক্রয় হলে সেইক্ষেত্রে ক্রেতার ক্রয়কে তর্কিত করা যাবে না। এখানে বিশেষভাবে উল্লেখ্য যে ১২ ধারার বিক্রয় মোকদ্দমা পূর্বকর্তী ধাপ যেখানে বিক্রয় দলিল ব্যাংক কর্তৃক সম্পাদিত হয়। অন্যদিকে জারী মামলায় বিক্রয় মোকাদ্দমার ডিক্রী পরবর্তী ধাপ যেখানে আদালত কর্তৃক বয়নামা সম্পাদিত হয়। উপরোক্ত জারী পর্যায়ে বিক্রয়ের ক্ষেত্রে বন্ধকদাতাকে বন্ধক অবমুক্তকরণের অধিকার আইনে প্রদান করা হয়েছে। অধিকন্তু অত্র ক্ষেত্রে ৫নং প্রতিপক্ষ নিলাম বিক্রয়কে তর্কিত Challenge করতে না বরং বন্ধক অবমুক্তকরণে তার আইনহত অধিকার প্রয়োহ করতে সচেষ্ঠ রয়েছে মাত্র। সুতরাং ১২(৮)ধারা অত্র ক্ষেত্রে আদৌ প্রযোজ্য নয় মর্মে নিবেদন করে তিনি অত্র রিভিশন মোকাদ্দমাটি খারিজযোগ্য বলে মনে করেন। 

12. আমার রিভিশন দরখাস্তটি, এর সাথে সংযুক্ত সতল কাগজপত্রাদি এবং প্রদর্শনীসমূহ পুঙ্খানুপঙ্খভাবে পর্যালোচনা করলাম এবং দরখাস্তকারী, ১নং প্রতিপক্ষ এবং ৫নং প্রতিপক্ষের যুক্তিতর্ক শ্রবণ করলাম। 

13. বর্তমান মামলাটি নিষ্পত্তিতে প্রাসংগিত এবং গুরুত্বপূর্ণ বিধায় বিজ্ঞ যুগ্ন জেলা জজ, অর্থঋণ আদালত, নারায়নগঞ্জ এর কয়েকটি আদেশ নিম্নে অবিকল উদ্ধুত হয়। 

14. বিজ্ঞ যুগ্ন জেলা জজ, অর্থঋণ আদালত, নারায়নগঞ্জ কর্তৃক প্রদত্ত ইংরেজী ০৩.০৮.২০০৬ তারিখের ২৮নং আদেশটি নিম্নে উদ্ধৃত করা হলঃ 

“বিজ্ঞ অতিরিক্ত জেলা জজ, ২য় আদালত, নারায়নগঞ্জ এর সিভিল রিভিশন মোকাদ্দমা নং-৫৯/২০০৬ এর ০২.০৮.২০০৬ইং তারিখের আদেশের কপিসহ নখি অদ্য পাওয়া গেল। দেখিলাম। আদেশ দৃষ্টে প্রতিয়মান হয় সিভিল রিভিশন মোকাদ্দমাটি দোতরফা সূত্রে বিনা খরচে নামঞ্জুর হয়। আদেশের কপি রখিভূক্ত রাখা হউক। অত্র মোকাদ্দমা বিগত ২৮.০৬.২০০৬ ইং তারিখে নিলামের জন্য দিন ধার্য ছিল। ডিক্রীদারা পক্ষে ফিরিস্তি দ্বারা ০৫.০৬.২০০৬ইং তারিখের দৈনিক ইত্তেফাক এবং ৩১.০৫.২০০৬ ইং তারিখে দৈনিক সোজাসাপটা পত্রিকা দাখিল দিয়াছিল। ধার্য্য তারিখে তিন বিডার নিলাম ডাকে অংশ গ্রহণ করেন। নিলাম ডাকে বীড সীট অনুযায়ী ১নং ক্রমিকের হাবিবুর রহামন যাকেন ১০,০৪,০০০/- টাকা ২নং ক্রমিকের মোসেলউদ্দিন আহমেদ ডাকেন ৮,৫৫,১০০/- টাকা এবং ৩নং ক্রমিকের ফয়েজ উদ্দিন আহম্মেদ (লাবলু) ডাকেন ৭,৩১,৬০০/- টাকা। দেখিলাম। যেহেতু সংশ্লিষ্ট নথি মাননীয় জেলা জজ মহোদয় কর্তৃক তলব করা হইয়াছে রিভিশন মোকাদ্দমা নং-৫৯/২০০৬ মূলে সেই হেতু নথি আসা সাপেক্ষে উপস্থাপন করা হোক। (দেঃ কাঃ মতো)। 

অদ্য মোকাদ্দমার নথি আসায় উপস্থাপন কার হইল। 

অদ্য ব্যাংক ডিক্রীদারাপক্ষে ব্যাংকের প্রিন্সিপাল অফিসার ব্যবস্থাপক, অগ্রনী ব্যাংক, মীরজুমলা রোড শাখা কর্তৃক সত্যপাঠ সহ এক দরখাস্ত দ্বারা দরখাস্তের বর্ণিত করেন জানাইয়াছেন যেম নিলাম খরিদ্দারের সর্বোচ্চ নিলাম ডাকে সম্পত্তি বিক্রয় করিলে ব্যাংক ডিক্রীদার পক্ষের কোন আপত্তি নাই এবং সর্বোচ্চ নিলাম ডাক গ্রহণ করার আদেশ দানের প্রার্থনা করিয়াছেন। দেখিলাম। নথিপত্র ও দরখাস্ত ও নাজিরের রিপোর্ট পর্যালোচনা করা হইল। সবোর্চ্চ দরদাতা ১০,০৪,০০০/- (দশ লক্ষ চার হাজার) টাকার দরপত্র দাখিল করিয়াছেন এবং তহাতে ডিক্রীদার ব্যাংক প্রার্থনা গ্রহণ করার প্রার্থনা করিয়াছেন। এবং যেহেতু ডিক্রীদার ব্যাংক প্রার্থনা গ্রহণ করার প্রার্থনা করিয়াছেন। এবং যেহেতু ডিক্রীকৃত টাকার প্রায় কাছাকাছি বলিয়া প্রতিয়মান অতএব সর্বোচ্চ দরদাতার দরপত্র গৃহীত হইল। তৃতীয় দরদাতার ব্যাংক ড্রাফট ফেরত দেওয়া হোক। আগামী ১০.০৮.২০০৬ ইং তারিখের মধ্যে বাকী টাকা দাখিল করিবার জন্য সর্বোচ্চ দর দাতাকে নির্দেশ প্রদান করা হইল।

	“নিলাম খরিদ্দার পক্ষে ওকালতনামা দাখিল করেছে এবং নিলাম খরিদের বিক্রী ৭,৫৩,০০০/- টাকা অগ্রনী ব্যাংক মীরজুমলা রোড শাখা, নারায়নগঞ্জ এর ০৯.০৮.২০০৬ ইং তারিখের ০৮বি-২৪২১৬৭১ নং পে-অর্ডার মূলে দাখিল করেছে। নথিভূক্ত রাখা হউক। দায়িকপক্ষ নতুন ওকলতনামাসহ এক দরখাস্ত দ্বারা দরখাস্তে বর্ণিত কারণে অত্র মোকাদ্দমার পরবর্তী কার্যক্রম স্থহিত রাথার আদেশ দানের প্রার্থনা করিয়াছেন। শুনিলাম। দেখিলাম। পর্যালোচনা করা হইল। যেহেতু দরখাস্তকারী উচ্চ আদালত হইতে কোন স্থগিত আদেশ দাখিল করিতে পারেন নাই। তাই দরখাস্তটি নমঞ্জুর কার হইল।

	16. বিজ্ঞ যুগ্ন জেলা জজ, অর্থঋণ আদালত, নারয়নগঞ্জ কর্তৃক প্রদত্ত ইংরেজি ১৩.০৮.২০০৬ তারিখের ৩১নং আদেশটি নিম্নে উদ্ধৃত করা হল: 

	ডিক্রীদার পক্ষ হাজিরা দাখিল করেছে। অদ্য নিলাম খরিদ্দার পক্ষে বাকী টাকা জমা প্রদানের জন্য দিন ধার্য্য আছে। নিলাম খরিদ্দারপক্ষ বিগত ১০.০৮.২০০৬ইং তারিখে পে-অর্ডার এর মাধ্যমে বক্রী টাকা জমা প্রদান করিয়া পে-অর্ডার দাখিল করিয়াছে। দ্বিতীয় দরদাতা ব্যাংক ড্রাফট ফেরৎ দেওয়া হউক। আগামী ০৩.০৯.২০০৬ইং নিলাম বহাল করার জন্য দিন ধার্য্য রইল।

	দায়িকপক্ষ হলফনামাসহ এক দরখাস্ত দ্বারা দরখাস্ত বর্ণিত কারণে মহামান্য বাংলাদেশ সুপ্রীম কোর্ট, হাইকোর্ট বিভাগ, ঢাকা এর রীট পিটিশন নং-৭৮১8/২০০৬ নিস্পত্তি না হওয়া পর্যন্ত অত্র মোকদ্দমার কার্যক্রম স্থগিত রাখার আদেশ দানের প্রার্থনা করিয়াছে ৷ দায়িক পক্ষ ফিরিস্তি দ্বারা বিজ্ঞ কৌসুলীর সার্টিফিকেট দাখিল করেছে ৷ শুনিলাম ৷ দেখিলাম ৷ ধার্য্য তারিখে উচ্চ আদালতের আদেশ দাখিলসহ দরথাস্ত শুনানী।

অদ্য নিলাম বহল আদেশ ও দায়িকপক্ষ কর্তৃক বিগত ১৩.০৮.২০০৬ইং তারিখের দৱখাস্ত শুনানীর জন্য দিন ধার্য্য আছে। ডিক্রীদারপক্ষ এবং নিলাম খরিদ্দাৱ পক্ষ আলাদা ভাবে দুইটি হাজিরা দিয়াছে। দায়িকপক্ষে নতুন ওকালতনামাসহ হলফনামা দ্বারা এক দরখাস্ত দ্বারা দরখাস্ত বর্নিত কারণে অত্র আদেশ দানের প্রার্থনা করিয়াছেন ৷ নিলাম খরিদ্দার পক্ষে নিলাম ডাকের ৩% অগ্রিম আয়কর বাবদ ৩০,১২০/- টাকা কোড নং ১-১১৪১-০০০০-০১১১৮৩ সোনালী ব্যাত্ক, নারায়নগঞ্জ কর্পোঃ শাখায় জমা প্রদান করিয়া চালান দাখিল করেছে এবং নিলম খরিদ্দার পক্ষ দলিলের ষ্ট্যম্পে বাবদ 8৯,০০০/-টাকার পে-অডরি ও ১২০০/- টাকা ট্যাম্প দাখিল করেছে ৷ নথিভুক্ত রাখা হোক ৷ আগামী ০8.০৯.২০০৬ইং আদেশ।

অদ্য দাইকপক্ষের বিগত ০৯.০৪.০৯ ইং তারিখের দাখিলী দরখান্ত শূনানীর জন্য দিন ধাঁয্য আছে। দাইকপক্ষ ও ভিক্রিদারপক্ষ হাজিরা দিয়াছে। নিলাম খরিদ্দারপক্ষ ওকালত নামাসহ এক দরখাস্ত দাখিল করিয়া দরখাস্ত বর্ণিত কারণে নিলাম খরিদ্দার দরখাস্ত কারীর অনুকুলে আদালত কর্তৃক নিলাম থরিদকৃত সম্পত্তির দখল প্রদানের আদেশ প্রার্থনা করিয়াছেন। 

উভয়পক্ষের বিজ্ঞ আইনজীৰির বক্তব্য শ্রবন করলাম। দরখাস্ত ও নথি পর্যালোচনা করলাম ৷ নথি দৃষ্টে দেখা যায় বিগত ২০.০৬.২০০৬ ইং তারিখের ২৬নং আদেশ পর্যালোচনার দেখা যায় উক্ত তারিখে অত্র মামলার নালিশা ভূমি ২৮.০৬.২০০৬ ইং নিলামের দিন ধার্য হয়। কিন্ত ২৬.০৬. ২০০৬ইং তারিখের অত্র মামলার নথি সিভিল রিভিশন মামলার প্রেক্ষিতে অত্র মামলার নখি সংশ্লিষ্ট আদালতে চলে যায় ৷ বিগত ০৩.০৮.০৬ ইং তারিখের ২৮নং আদেশ পর্যালোচনার দেখা যায় উক্ত তারিখে তর্কিত নিলামের সর্বোচ্চ দরপত্রটি গৃহিত হয় বিগত ০৪.০৯.০৬ ইং তারিখের ৩৬নং আদেশ পর্যালোচনার দেখা যায় উক্ত তারিখে তর্কিত নিলামটি বহাল হয়। নথিতে সামিল রীট পিটিশন মামলা নং-৮৪৫১/০৬ এর বিভিন্ন আদেশ পর্যালচনায় দেখা যায় অত্র জারী মামলার অন্যতম দাইক মোঃ আনোয়ার হোসেন উক্ত রীট পিটিশন মামলাঢি দায়ের করেছিলেন ৷ অত্র জারী মামলার বিগত ১ ৭.০৯. ০৬ ইং তারিখে 8০নং আদেশ দৃষ্টে দেখা যায় কোর্টের আদেশ মোতাবেক ২৮.০৮.০৬ ইং তারিখ হইতে পরবর্তী আদেশ সমূহের কার্যক্রম Re-call করা হয় ৷ নথিতে সামিল রীট পিটিশন নং-৮8৫১/০৬ মামলার ০৭.০৪.০৯ ইং তারিখের আদেশ দৃষ্টে দেখা যায় উক্ত রীট পিটিশন মামলাটি না চালানো হেতুতে খারিজ হয় এবং মহামান্য হাইকোর্টের ইতিপুঁবে প্রচারিত স্থগিতাদেশ সমূহ বাতিল করা হয়৷ উক্ত রীট পিঢিশন মামলাটি আবেদনকারী কর্তৃক প্রত্যাহার করার এবং উক্ত মামলার অন্তর্বর্তীকালীন আদেশ সমূহের কার্যকারিতা সক্তত্তে কারণেই থাকার কথা নয় ৷ মহামান্য হাইকোর্র্ট এ তাহার ০৭.০৪.২০০৯ ইং তারিখে আদেশে উক্ত আদালত কর্তৃক ইতিপূর্বু প্রচারিত স্থপিতড়াদেশ সমূহ বাতিল করা
হইয়াছে মর্মে আদেশে উল্লেখ করেছেন।তদুপরি নিষ্পত্তির জন্য নেওয়া দেঃ কাঃ বিঃ ২১ আদেশের ৮৯ বিধি মোতাবেক আনিত দরখান্তথানা দৃষ্টে দেখা যায় উক্ত দৱখাস্তটি দায়ের করেছেন 8নং দাইক তাসলিমা আক্তার যিনি ইতিপুঁবে উল্লেখিত রীট পিটিশন মামলার আবেদনকারী নহেন ৷ অর্থাৎ অত্র দরখাস্তকারী দেঃ কাঃ রিঃ ২১ আদেশের ৮৯ বিধি মোতাবেক ইতিপূর্বে আবেদন করার ক্ষেত্রে কোন আইনগত বাধা নাই ৷ ১৬৬ অনুচ্ছেদ পর্যালোচনার দেখা যায় ডিক্রী জারীতে বিষয় রদ করিবার জন্য দেঃকাঃবিঃ অনুসারে দরখাস্ত দাখিল করিলে উহা নিলাম বিক্রয় তারিখ হইতে ৩০ দিনের মধ্যে দাখিল করিতে হইবে ৷ অত্র মামলার নালিশী ভূমি নিলাম হয় ২৮.০৬.০৬ইং তারিখে যাহা গৃহীত হয় ০৩.০৮.০৬ইং তারিখে বহাল হয় ০৪.০৯.০৬ইং তারিখে প্ৰকারন্তা ৪নং দাইক দে: কা: বি: ২১ আদেশের ৮৯ বিধি মতে দরখাস্ত দায়ের করেন ০৯.০8.০৯ ইং তারিখে মধ্যে ৷ নিলাম বিক্রয় তারিখ হইতে ৩০ দিনের মধ্যে ঊত্ত দরখাস্তটি দায়ের না করার ঊহা তামাদিতে বারিত ফলে ৪নং দাইকের ২১ আদেশের ৮৯ বিধি মতে আনিত দরখাস্ত থানা নামঞ্জুৱ করা হইল।

নিলাম খরিদ্দার পক্ষের দরখাম্ভ ও নথি পর্যালোচনা করলাম। নিলাম খরিদ্দারের দরখান্তখানা সার্বিক বিবেচনায় মঞ্জুর করা হইল ৷ নিলাম খরিদ্দারকে বয়নামার মূল কপি ফেরত প্রদান হউক ৷ দখলী পর ওয়ানার দাখিল সাপেক্ষে পরবর্তী আদেশ।

এখন সময় ৪:২৫ মিনিট ৷ দাইকপক্ষ দূইখানা দরখাস্ত দাখিল করিয়াছেন। একটি দরখাস্ত যোগে দাইকপক্ষ অর্থঋণ আদালত আইনের ২০০৩ এর ৫ ৭ ধারা ও দে:১৫১ ধারামতে অত্র মামলার পরবর্তী কার্যক্রম স্থগিত রাখার আবেদন করেন। অপর দরখাস্ত যোগে বায়নানামা ও  দখল প্রার্থীত সংক্রান্তে নিলাম খরিদ্দারের ১৬.০৪.২০০৯ ইং তারিখের লিখিত দাখিলের জন্য সময়ের আবেদন করেন দাইক পক্ষের বিজ্ঞ আইরজীবি কোন দরখাস্তই শুননী করেন নাই এবং অপর 'পক্ষকে কপি প্রদান করেন নাই। দরখাস্তদ্বয় পর্যালোচনা করলাম ৷ অর্থঋনঃ আদালত আইনু ২০০৩ এর ৩১ ধারার বিধান মোতাবেক উচ্চতর আদালতে সুস্পষ্ট স্থপিতাদেশ ব্যাতিত জারী মামলার কাযাক্রমে স্বয়ংক্রিয় ভাবে অত্র আদালত স্থগিত
করিবেন না ৷ ফলে 8নং দাইকের অত্র মামলার কার্যক্রম স্থগিত করার দরখাস্ত থানা সরাসরি না মঞ্জুর করা হইল ৷ নিলাম খরিদ্দার পক্ষ অদ্য এজলাস চলাকালীন সময়ে বায়নমা ও দখল প্রাপ্তি সংক্রাম্ভে একখানা দরখাস্ত দেন ও দরখাস্ত শুনার্নী করেন। উক্ত দরখাস্তের কপি ডিক্রীদার
বিনা আপত্তিতে গ্রহণ করিয়াছেন ৷ ঊক্ত এ মামলা চলাকালীন সময়ে দাইক পক্ষের বিজ্ঞ আইনজীবী নিলাম খরিদ্দারের দরখাস্তের বিরুদ্ধে লিখিত আপত্তি দাখিলের জন্য সময়ের আবেদন করতে পারতেন কিংবা মৌখিকভাবে ইহা নিবেদন করতে পারতেন ৷ কিন্তু দাইকপক্ষ তদ্রুপ কোন পদক্ষেপ গ্রহন করেন নাই। দাইক পক্ষের দরখাস্তখানা মঞ্জুর ক্রমে আদেশ প্রচারিত হইয়াছ���৷ এমতবস্থায় বিকাল 8:২৫ মিনিটে 8নং দাইকের আপত্তি দাখিলের দরখাস্তখানা বিবেচনা করার কোন সুযোগ নাই। কেননা দাইকপক্ষ 'শুনানীকালে এরূপ আপত্তি দিতে চেয়েছেন সে বিষয়টি ইতিমধ্যে নিষ্পত্তি
হইয়া গিয়াছে৷ উপরোক্ত আংলাচনার আলোকে দাইক পক্ষের আপত্তি দাখিলের গাংনািয় আনিত সময়ের প্রার্থানা না মঞ্জুর করা গেল।
