23. We have heard the learned advocates for both the sides and perused the writ petition, affidavits-in-opposition with annexures thereto and the relevant laws and decisions placed before us, which have been carefully considered by this Court.

24. The moot question in this writ petition is whether the respondents are empowered to correct the Gazette Notification dated 4-3-1965, which was published in connection with acquisition of a quantum of land of 5.59 acres of plots No. 33, 40, 41, 42 and portion of plots No. 43 and 44 vide LA Case No. 77 of 1963-64. In other words, we are to adjudicate upon the issue as to whether the insertion of plot No. 41 in the Gazette Notification dated 4-3-1965, which was published in connection with the concluded LA Case No 77 of 1963-64, by the impugned amendment circular dated 7-10-2010 is lawful. However, some intricate questions of law, such as application of doctrine of res-judicata, Estoppel, petitioner's protection under section 41 of the Transfer of Property Act and section 27(b) of the Specific Relief Act, are also involved in the adjudication of the present case, which would be dealt with at an appropriate part of this judgment.

25. It is an admitted position that the Gazette Notification dated 4-3-1965 mentions plot Nos. 33, 40, 42 and parts of the plot Nos. 43 and 44 but misses plot No. 41. It is also admitted that the total quantum of acquired land is 5.59 acres. Now, by the impugned amendment circular, the said plot No. 41 has been shown as an acquired plot under LA Case No. 77 of 1963-64, Gazette of which was published on 4-3-1965 though it has finally been adjudicated upon by the competent Courts that plot No. 41 has never been acquired. Thus, the present writ petition involves a two-fold Situation.

26. Scenario No. 1 in the instant writ petition is that in LA Case No. 77 of 1963-64, plot No. 41 was acquired but the same was inadvertently not published in the Gazette Notification dated 4-3-1965. In order to adjudicate upon the above scenario, this Court's task will be only to examine and asses the legality or validity of the publication of the impugned amendment circular dated 7-10-2010 (Annexure-E) and, in that evident, this Court is required to see whether plot No. 41 was at all acquired by LA Case No. 77 of 1963-64.

27. Scenario No. 2 in the instant case is that non-mentioning of plot No. 41 in the Gazette Notification dated 4-3-1965 was not a mere typing mistake, rather, they said plot was never acquired vide LA Case No. 77 of 1963-64 as has been adjudicated upon by a competent Court of law in the Title Suit No. 20 of 1991, which has been upheld up to the Appellate Division. In that event, the task of this Court will be to examine as to whether the said judgment and decree dated 18-11-1991 is erroneous or not and, from our examination, if it reveals that the said judgment and decree was erroneous, then the further task of this Court will be to examine as to whether the power of this Court is unfettered or limited in questioning the decisions arrived at by the trial Court in Title Suit No. 20 of 1991 upon digging out the correctness of the findings of the said decree and judgment.

28. Let us first deal with the aforesaid "Scenario No. 1". It appears from the notice under section 5(7) (annexure-1 series to the affidavit-in-opposition by respondent No. 4) of the (Emergency) Requisition of the Property Act, 1948 that plot No. 41 is included in the schedule of the said notice. It further appears from the certificate of possession of the acquired land of 5.59 acres that on 28-5-1964 (Annexure 1 to affidavit-in-opposition of Respondent No. 3) the acquisition officer has handed over 5.59 acres of land of plot Nos. 33, 40, 41, 42 and parts of the plot Nos. 43 and 44 to the District fishery office Sylhet, which includes the case land, i.e., plot No. 41. It further appears from the map of the lands to be acquired under LA Case No. 77 of 1963-64 (annexure-1 series to the affidavit-in-opposition filed by respondent No. 4) that plot No. 41 is included in the said acquisition proceeding. Thus, there are abundant documents to substantiate that plot No. 41 has been acquired under LA Case No. 77 of 1963-64. Also, from the calculation of the quantum of the land of plots Nos. 33, 40, 41, 42 and parts of the plot Nos. 43 and 44, it transpires that without inclusion of 1.10 acres of land of plot No. 41, the total quantum of land does not come to 5.59 acres of land. But due to printing error, plot No. 41 is missing in the Gazette Notification dated 4-3-1965.

29. Now, the question is whether a typing mistake can be corrected by publishing another Gazette Notification. In other words, whether inclusion of plot No. 41 in the Gazette Notification dated 4-3-1965 as an acquired land can be done without starting a fresh acquisition case for the said plot No. 41. We have already found hereinbefore that in order to acquire plot No, 41 together with plot Nos. 33, 40, 42 and parts of the plot Nos. 43 and 44, the entire process has been completed long ago (in the year 1964) under the relevant laws but a typing mistake was committed in publishing the Gazette Notification on 4-3-1965 causing exclusion of the said plot No. 41. Section 21 of the General Clauses Act, 1897 provides that an authority which can pass order, it can vary, amend, alter or rescind that order. From the aforesaid provisions of law, it appears that mere typing mistake in any Gazette Notification can be corrected at any point in time by publication of another Gazette Notification and, thus, the authority in publishing the impugned amendment circular dated 28-8-2010 has resorted to section 21 and, with its aid, the said authority has given the shape of original position of the Gazette Notification dated 4-3-1965, and it does not appear to us that the impugned Gazette Notification, in fact, has altered the original position of the said Gazette Notification dated 4-3-1965. The case of the Government of Bangladesh vs Nurjahan Begum 59 DLR (AD) 80, as referred to by the learned advocate for the petitioner has no manner of application in the instant case given that the fact of the said referred case is quite different from the fact of the case in hand. In the cited case, no material document as to acquisition of the property was placed before the High Court Division to enable the Court to draw an inference to the effect that notices under section 3 and section 5(7), possession certificate and other dealings or communications were made in respect of a particular quantum of land and only at the time of publication of the final Gazette Notification a printing error occurred but in the present case, from the annexures to the affidavits-in-opposition, it clearly transpires that all the work and trans-actions were done with the aim to acquire 5.59 acres of land but in the final publication of Gazette Notification one plot, out of six plots, was not mentioned therein. Thus, subject to our findings and decision on the "Scenario No. 2", for now, we hold that there is no necessity to start a fresh acquisition processes and no illegality has been committed in publishing the impugned amendment circular.

30. To attach the instant writ petition with the "Scenario No. 2", the competency of this Court in making any findings on the issue of acquisition of plot No. 41, which has been finally adjudicated upon by the competent Courts, becomes pertinent. As it is a settled principle of the law that writ Court is not an appellate Court and, thus, it cannot get engaged in appreciation of the evidences and examine the correctness of the finding arrived at by the trial Court, we, notwithstanding the aforesaid position of the law, would undertake the task of going through the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court in Title Suit No. 20 of 1991 for the reasons to be stated at the last part of this judgment.

31. It appears that the suit was for permanent injunction, which was filed in the early part of the year 1991 and decreed on 18-11-91. It further appears that the father of Rajani Ranjan Gupta was the original owner of the suit land and it was the case of the plaintiffs of the aforesaid suit that Rajani Ranjan Gupta entered into an agreement in the middle of the year of 1982 to sell the suit land and, accordingly, the said Rajani Ranjan Gupta, upon taking the earnest money from the plaintiffs and receiving required income tax certificate, gave delivery of possession of the suit land to the plaintiffs and the registration of the suit land was agreed to be executed after receiving the remaining amount which he could not do due to his death. Then, the sole son of Rajani Ranjan Gupta, Rakkhani Ranjan Gupta executed the said registration of the suit land in favour of the plaintiffs, who, upon mutating their respective names therein, became the owners and possessors of the suit land. The cause of action of the said suit arose when the plaintiffs cultivation of the land in question was halted by the District Fishery Office in the month of Agrahayan of 1397 BS, as appears from the judgment and decree dated 18-11-1991 passed in Title Suit No. 20 of 1991, though from the averments of the instant writ petition it transpires that the suit was instituted when the said office mutated its name behind the back of the plaintiffs upon opening Khatian No. 7640.

32. It was the case of defendant No. 1 that the Government acquired 5.59 acres of land vide LA Case No. 77 of 1963-64, which includes the suit land of plot No. 41 consisting of 1.10 acres, and the concerned Acquiring Officer handed over possession of the entire 5.59 acres of land to the requiring body, District Fishery Officer, Sylhet and since then the said department has been possessing the said entire 5.59 acres of land without any hindrance from any quarter. The office of the Fishery Department, graveyard for the officers and employees of the said office and a number of ponds and paddy fields are situated on the said acquired 5.59 acres of land. The paddy fields lands are being possessed through Mr Abdur Noor, son of Hasan Ali of Village-Kumargaon, who vide an agreement with the office of the Fishery Department is cultivating the said land. The records relating to LA Case No. 77 of 1963-64 have been preserved in the office of the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet. Rajani Ranjan Gupta or Rakkhi Ranjan Gupta has never possessed the suit land and no agreement was made between Rajani Ranjan Gupta and the plaintiffs and, as such, no question arises as to the execution of any registered deed to sell the suit property by Rajani Ranjan Gupta to the plaintiffs and the claimed registered deeds of 5-11-90 and 641-90 are forged, false and non-effective, which do not confer title upon the plaintiffs. The defendants have possessed the suit land since 28-5-64 and the story of creating disturbance to the plaintiffs by the defendants in cutting the paddy from the suit land in the month of Agrahayan of 1391 BS is concocted.

33. The case of defendant No. 2 (Government of Bangladesh) was that the Government acquired 5.59 acres of land, consisting of Plots Nos. 33, 41, 42 and the parts of the plot Nos. 43 and 44 under the Mouza of No. 1 Municipality appertaining to Khatian No. 9687 for setting up the "Whole Sale Fish Market at Sylhet" vide LA Case No. 77 of 1963-64 and the said lands were handed over to District Fishery Officer on 18-5-64.

34. Now, let us see the performance of the DWs at the trial of the said suit. It was stated in their written statement that 5.59 acres of land was acquisitioned vide LA Case No, 77 of 1963-64, which is consisted of Plot Nos. 33, 40, 41, 42 and the parts of the Plot Nos. 43 and 44 and the entire acquired 5.59 acres of land is a compact block which is fenced with wires and was handed over by the acquisition officer to the District Fishery Officer on 28-5-64 and in support of the case of the defendants a photocopy of the Gazette Notification of the said LA Case No. 77 of 1963-64 dated 4-3-65 was produced before the trial Court, which was marked as exhibit-Ka, and the certified photocopy of the 'Certificate of Possession' dated 28-5-64 was produced before the trial Court, which was marked as exhibit-Kha.

35. Let us look at the performances of the learned trial Court. It appears that there is no corroborative evidence regarding the claim of entering into an agreement by Mr Rajani Ranjan Gupta with the plaintiffs as no copy of the said agreement was produced before the trial Court. In the plaint, no date of entering into an agreement or the amount of money paid by the plaintiffs to the said Rajani Ranjan Gupta was mentioned. As to the non-production of the said deed of the agreement, PW 1, who is stated to be the sole son of Rajani Ranjan Gupta, makes the following deposition “ বাদীর পক্ষের ১নং সাক্ষী ১নং বাদী নিজে জবান বন্দীতে বলেন উক্ত চুক্তি পত্র তাহার নিকট ছিল, কিন্তু তিনি তাহা খুঁজিয়া পান নাই। Thus, it appears that the very basis of the claims by the plaintiffs over the suit land is based on an agreement (which is undated and does not state the amount of earnest money), which the plaintiffs could not execute due to the alleged death of Rajani Ranjan Gupta, has not been established by any oral or documentary evidence and, therefore, the statements pleaded in the Title Suit no. 20 of 91, that following his death his claimed son Rakkhi Ranjan Gupta came forward to execute the registered deed on behalf of his late father remains questionable. More importantly, there is no evidence, oral or documentary, regarding the identity of Rakkhani Ranjan Gupta by producing any birth certificate or school certificate or his father Rajani Ranjan Gupta's death certificate or any other documentary evidence to ascertain the fact as to whether he is a genuine son of Ranjani Ranjan Gupta.

36. In the absence of any oral or documentary evidence as to the identity of Rakkhani Ranjan Gupta as the legal heir of Rajani Ranjan Gupta, the statements made by the respondents in the instant writ petition, being not controverted by the writ petitioner, appears to be true that Rajani Ranjan Gupta left this country during Hindu-Muslim riot and, as such, a fake person with the name of Rakkhani Ranjan Gupta as the son of Rajani Ranjan Gupta was in personated to grab the suit land. In view of the failure of the plaintiff to establish the title of Rakkhani Ranjan Gupta, the trial Court ought to have drawn an inference under section 114(g) of the Evidence Act that he does not have any title to the suit land and, accordingly, it was destined to have been held by the trial Court that the sale agreement by him with the plaintiffs is void ab initio. Also, the Courts below as well as the High Court ought to have examined the law point as to whether is there any bar to file the said Title Suit No. 20 of 91 in an acquired property as laid down in sections 10 &12 of the Government lands and Buildings (Recovery of Possession) Act, 1952 and in section 14A of the (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act, 1948 as well as in section 44 of the Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Ordinance, 1982.

37. It is the findings of the trial Court that Plot No. 41 is not in the said Gazette Notification dated 4-3-65, the said findings of the trial Court may be quoted:—

“ বিবাদীপক্ষের দাখিলী গেজেটের ফটোকপি পর্যালোচনা দেখা যায়, উহাতে নালিশী ৪১নং দাগের ভূমি হুকুম দখল করা হইয়াছে, তৎমর্মে কোন লিখা নাই। উহাতে ৩৩/৪০/৪২ নং দাগের সাকুল্য ভূমি এবং ৪৩/৪৪ নং দাগের আংশিক ভূমি সহ একুনে ৫.৫৯ একর(কম বেশী) হুকুম দখল করার কথা উল্লেখ আছে।

বিবাদীগনের জবাবের বর্ণিত মতে হুকুম দখল সংক্রান্ত অন্যান্য তথ্যাদি সম্পর্কিত কাগজাদি জেলা প্রশাসক, সিলেট কার্যালয়ে রহিয়াছে। বিবাদিপক্ষের ১নং সাক্ষী জেরার জবাবে বলেন যে, LA case Record 77 of 1963-64 তিনি সর্বপ্রথম ১৯৮২ইং সনে দেখিয়াছেন এবং তাহা অদ্য তারিখেও দেখিয়াছেন এবং LA case রেকর্ড বিবাদিপক্ষ আদালতে দাখিল করেন নাই এবং উক্ত রেকর্ড ডি,সি সাহেবের অফিসে আছে এবং উক্ত রেকর্ড আনার প্রয়োজনীয়তা হয় বা সমীচীন মনে করেন নাই।

বিবাদীপক্ষের জবাবে এমন কোন কথা নাই যে, উপরোক্ত গেজেটে নালিশা দাগের ভূমি ভূলে বা অন্য কোন কারণে উঠে নাই।

LA case Record 77 of 1963-64 এর মূল রেকর্ড যদি জেলা প্রশাসক সিলেট কার্যালয়ে থাকে এবং তাহা দাখিল না করার কোন যুক্তিসঙ্গত কারন দেখি না।

এমতাবস্থায় সাক্ষ্য আইনের ১১৪ নং ধারার বিধান মতে আদালত ইহা অবশ্যই ধরিয়া নিবেন যে নালিশা দাগের ভূমি রজনী রনজন গুপ্ত হইতে হুকুম দখল করা হয় নাই বা LA case Record 77 of 1963-64 নং হইতে উক্ত দাগের ভূমি হুকুম দখল করার কথা লিখা নাই।

১নং বিবাদী জেরার জবাবে আরো বলেন যে, দলিল মূলে হুকুম দখলকৃত ভূমি মৎস্য বিভাগের নিকট হস্তান্তর করিয়া ছিলেন। তিনি বলেন যে, সেই দলিল দাখিল করা হয় নাই।

38. From the aforesaid findings it transpires that Plot No. 41 is missing in the Gazette Notification dated 4-3-1965 but no endeavour was made by the defendants to justify the factor of non-mentioning/non-printing of Plot No. 41 in the said Gazette Notification. If the fact is that the said Plot No. 41 was not printed mistakenly in the said Gazette Notification dated 4-3-1965 of LA Case No. 77 of 1963-64, it could have been justified by producing the relevant papers of the LA Case No. 77 of 1963-64, such as Notice under section 5(7) (which contains the schedule of acquired land), payment of awards to the awardees (where the quantum of land is mentioned), the possession certificate and the other communications between the acquiring body and the requiring body.

39. The more important and easier steps would have been for the defendants to measure the quantum of land of each plot inasmuch as the aggregate of Plot Nos. 33, 40, 41, 42 plus the portion of Plot Nos. 43 and 44 must have to be 5.59 acres of land and, by such calculation, if it is found that without including 1.10 acres of land of Plot No. 41, total land does not become 5.59 acres of land, then the trial Court might not have avoided or ignored the argument that there was a printing error in the Gazette Notification dated 4-3-1965 given the fact that there is no dispute as to the quantum of total acquired land, which is 5.59 acres. Shockingly, the Court failed to take into consideration that it is well empowered to count the quantity of the land of each plot namely Plot Nos. 33, 40, 41, 42 and parts of the Plot Nos. 34 and 44 and upon counting the quantum of the land if the total aggregate arrives/becomes 5.59 acres, then confusion as to non-printing of Plot No. 41 in the Gazette Notification would have been removed. Furthermore, the fact of non-consideration of possession certificate produced by the defendants is seriously dubious, as evident from the following findings “ বিবাদীপক্ষের দখলদেহী সার্টিফিকেটদ্বয় আপত্তি সহকারে প্রদঃ চিহ্তি করা হয়। বাদীপক্ষ বলেন যে, উক্ত দখলদেহী সার্টিফিকেট যোগসাজসীতে সৃজন করা হইয়াছে। উহা পর্যালোচনায় দেখা যায় অন্যান্য দাগসহ নালিশী ৪১নং দাগের ভূমির দখল অর্পন করা হইয়াছে বলিয়া উল্লেখ আছে।Thus, non-consideration of the aforesaid certificates as to the delivery of possession of Plot No. 41 as an acquired land by the Acquisition Officer to the requiring body is palpably a perverse finding of fact, in particular, when the trial Court appears to be comfortable to take into consideration a photocopy of the news report by the following words “বাদীপক্ষ এই মর্মে একটি সংবাদের ফটোকপি দাখিল করেন। নালিশী দাগের ভূমি La case Record 77 of 1963-64 এর মূলে হুকুম দখল করা হয় নাই এবং জেলা প্রশাসক সিলিট কার্যালয় হইতে ৮-২-১৯৯১ ইং তারিখে উহা প্রদান করা হয় নাই।” The facts and background of the case of the People’s Republic of Bangladesh vs Most Sharifian Bibi 43 DLR (AD) 112 are almost similar to the present case. In the said case the suit was decreed for want of production of the case record of the concerned LA case and, conversely, production of notice under section 4 and certificate of possession before the trial Court was underscored and the said findings and decisions were maintained up to the High Court Division but the Appellate Division held that the said two documents were sufficient to hold that the suit land was acquired. In view of the fact that the documents of the LA Case No. 77 of 1963-64 have been produced before this Court, it is to be held that the same were available for production before the trial Court but the concerned officers and employees of the office of the Deputy. Commissioner as well as the District Fishery Office deliberately refrained from producing the record of LA Case No.77 of 1963-64 to establish the factum of acquisition of Plot Nos. 33, 40, 41, 42 and parts of the Plot Nos. 43 and 44. It further appears that the defendants also did not produce the most crucial witness Mr. Abdur Noor son of Hasan Ali of Village-Kumargaon, who has been cultivating the said land by taking Borga from the Fishery Department, to corroborate their claim of possession of the suit land. The findings of the trial Court as to the non-production of the said witness Abdur Noor goes as follows

“ বিবাদীপক্ষ যে বর্গাদার আব্দুর নুর মারফৎ নালিশী জমিতে বর্গাচাষ করান তাহা প্রমান করিবার জন্য আব্দুল নুরকে সাক্ষী হিসাবে আদালতে উপস্থিত করান নাই।"

40. We consider it pertinent to observe here that, in an adversarial system of judiciary, such as ours, the trial Court cannot escape its responsibilities of taking necessary steps by applying its ordinary prudence in addition to the application of section 165 of the Evidence Act and provisions of the different procedural laws including sections 30, 31 and 32 and Order 19, Rule 1 and 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure in order to ensure a fair trial inasmuch as avoiding the said duty by the trial Court may convey a negative message to the readers of the judgment on top of questioning about the standard and quality of the performance of the judiciary as a whole. For ease of discussion, let the above provisions of law be reproduced: section 165 of the Evidence Act:

"Judge's powers to put questions or order production: The Judge may, in order to discover or to obtain proper proof of relevant facts, ask any question he pleases, in any form, at any time, of any witness, or of the parties about any fact relevant or irrelevant; and may order the production of any document or thing: and neither the parties nor their agents shall be entitled to make any objection to any such question or order, nor, without the leave of the Court, to cross-examine any witness upon any answer given in reply to any such question:

Provided that the judgment must be based upon facts declared by this Act to be relevant, and duly proved: Provided also that this section shall not authorize any Judge to compel any witness to answer any question or to produce any document which such witness would be entitled to refuse to answer or produce under sections 121 to 131, both inclusive, if the question were asked or the document were called for by the adverse party; nor shall the Judge ask any question which it would be improper for any other person to ask under section 148 or 149; nor shall he dispense with primary evidence of any document, except in the cases hereinbefore excepted".

Section 30 "Power to order discovery and the like: Subject to such conditions and limitations as may be prescribed, the Court may, at any time, either of its own motion or on the application of any party,—

(a) make such orders as may be necessary or reasonable in all matters relating to the delivery and answering of interrogatories, the admission of documents and facts, and the discovery, inspection, production, impounding and return of documents or other material objects producible as evidence;

(b) issue summonses to persons whose attendance is required either to give evidence or to produce documents or such other objects as aforesaid;

(c) order any fact to be proved by affidavit.

Section 31. "Summons to witness: The provisions in sections 27, 28 and 29 shall apply to summonses to give evidence or to produce documents or other material objects".

Section 32: Penalty for default: the Court may compel the attendance of any person to whom a summons has been issued under section 30 and for that purpose may—

(a) issue a warrant for his arrest;

(b) attach and sell his property

(c) impose a fine upon him not exceeding five hundred [Taka]

(d) order him to furnish security for his appearance and in default commit him to the civil prison.

Order 19, Rule 1: Power to order any point to be proved by affidavit: Any Court may at any time for sufficient reason order that any particular fact or facts may be proved by affidavit, or that the conditions as the Court thinks reasonable:

Provided that where it appears to the Court that either party bona fide desires the production of a witness for cross-examination, and that such witness can be produced, an order shall not be made authorizing the evidence of such witness to be given by affidavit.

Order XIX, rule 2: Power to order attendance of deponent for cross-examination: (1) Upon any application evidence may be given by affidavit, but the Court may, at the instance of either party, order the attendance for cross-examination of the deponent.

(2) Such attendance shall be in Court, unless the deponent is exempted from personal appearance in Court, or the Court otherwise directs.

41. Upon reading through the aforesaid provisions of law any one will be of the view that the aforesaid provisions of law give the Court unlimited powers to arrive at the truth. If the intention of the law is that the person who has to give a decision is to sit entirely unconcerned during the proceedings like an unthinking statue, in our opinion, it will be a serious misconstruction or gross ignorance of the aforesaid provisions of law. To us, the position of a person who presides over a civil trial as a Judge is just as important as of any of the parties and, in certain respects, his responsibilities are much greater than that of the legal practitioners who represent one party or the other. One has to be a party or the counsel of a party to be of the view that the interests of justice can be served only if he succeeds, but that should not be the view of the Judge who has to do justice not to one party alone but between the parties in the proceedings before him. Persons who have been entrusted with the duty of doing justice have to do things which cannot meet with the approval of all the parties because if one party considers an action of the presiding officer to be just, the opposite party will describe it as unjust.

42. The Legislature which enacted section 165 of the Evidence Act and aforesaid provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure could not have been unaware of the fact that unlimited powers to produce any documents before the Courts or to ask questions were being conferred on the Courts and if the source of the authority of the Courts of law to decide disputes between parties before them chose to confer powers which appear unlimited it is, in our opinion, not open to anyone to urge that a particular piece of document should not have been directed for production or a certain question should not have been asked by the Court. Those, therefore, who think that they can curtail the power of a Court regarding production of document or asking Court questions, think on wrong lines. The position in law is that the aforesaid provisions of law not only authorizes a Court but made it a bounden duty of the Court to ensure production of a document or to call as witnesses persons whose evidence appears to the Court essential to the just decision of the case. Judicial officers holding trials should not be dummies or act merely like referees in boxing bouts leaving it to the contestants to do what they like and should not interfere unless they violate the rules of the game. To us, the action of judicial officers with regard to a trial should be actuated by no other motive but a desire to do justice between the parties. The invocation of the oft-invoked maxim to the effect be done would not be apt in a case where the Court has followed the law because in a Court of law justice means neither more nor less than the administration of the law of the land.

43. We find that when defendant No. 1 said in his cross-examination "LA Case No. 77 of 1963-64 LA Case Record 77 of 1963-64  তিনি সর্বপ্রথম ১৯৮২ ইং সনে দেখিয়াছেন এবং তাহা অদ্য তারিখেও দেখিয়াছেন এবং LA Case রেকর্ড বিবাদীপক্ষ আদালতে দাখিল করেন নাই এবং উক্ত রেকর্ড ডি,সি সাহেবের অফিসে আছে এবং উক্ত রেকর্ড আমার প্রয়োজনীয়তা হয় বা সমচীন মনে কনে নাই।” it was the duty of the learned trial Court to pass necessary orders to ensure that the case record of LA Case No. 77 of 1963-64 is produced before it without fail by directing the Government Pleader to produce the same and if the concerned Government pleader comes out with an excuse as to non-cooperation by any government functionary for production of the said case record, in that event, the Government Pleader has to produce the written refusal by the concerned authorities and, thereafter, by summoning the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet seeking his explanation as to non-production of the same. Also, it is our considered view that the trial Court on its own motion could have taken the burden of calculation of the quantum of land situated in each of the plots mentioned in the Gazette Notification dated 4-3-1965 of LA Case No. 77 of 1963-64 and thereby could have aggregated the said quantum to find out as to whether the total quantum of land of the plots mentioned in the said Gazette Notification becomes 5.59 acres of land. Further, we do not find any cogent reason for not taking the "certificate of possession" into consideration, which was produced before the trial Court by the defendants to corroborate the factum of handing over the possession of the suit land by the acquisition officer to the District Fishery Office and, further, we find ourselves at a loss when we noticed that no reasons have been recorded for non-consideration of the said document. On the other hand, the learned Court appears to be happy to accept a photocopied news cutting as a piece of evidence to corroborate the factum of non-acquisition of Plot No. 41 in LA Case No. 77 of 1963-64.

44. The crucial role was supposed to play by the concerned government functionaries, whose imperative duty was to produce case record of LA Case No. 77 of 1963-64 as well as to produce the relevant witnesses before the trial Court. Their deliberate failure manifest the fact that Title Suit No. 20 of 1991 was instituted and concluded in collusion with the concerned government employees of the District Fishery Office, Sylhet and office of the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet. Also, the Government Pleader, who was engaged in conducting the said suit on behalf of the government, was also involved in conniving with the parties of the suit inasmuch as the factum of acquisition of total 5.59 acres of land could have been established simply by aggregating the land appertaining to each plots namely, Plot Nos. 33, 40, 41, 42 and parts of Plot Nos. 43 and 44 even if it is conceded that he was really not provided with the case record of LA Case No. 77 of 1963-64 or the relevant witnesses were not presented to him by the concerned government officers and employees of the Deputy Commissioner's Office.

45. From the above discussions on the "Scenario No. 2" of this case, any one with ordinary prudence shall have no option but to arrive at a conclusion that fraud has been practiced upon the trial Court and lower appellate Court by the parties of the Title Suit No. 20 of 91 in connivance with the officers, employees of the office of the Deputy Commissioner, Office of the District Fishery Office and Government Pleaders (GP) and, thereafter, the same kind of performance was demonstrated by the law officers of the Attorney-General's Office in dealing with the Civil Revision in the High Court Division and in preferring Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal in the Appellate Division. Accordingly, we hold that fraud has been practiced in obtaining the judgment and decree in TS No. 20 of 91.

46. However, it should be noted down here that for the instant writ petition the learned Deputy Attorney-General and Assistant Attorney-General tried their best to assist this Court, as this Court noticed that they devoted themselves to unearth the fact of connivance of the aforesaid people, who were responsible and connected in dealing with the Title Suit No. 20 of 91. Further, their bonaflde is evident from the statements made in their affidavits-in-opposition to the instant proceedings as to taking preparation to file a Revision Petition against the judgment passed by the Appellate Division in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 2041 of 2008 on 14-5-2009.

47. Now, let us deal with the other submissions, advanced by the learned advocate for the petitioner on the point of res-judicata, estoppel, petitioner's protection and safeguard under section 41 of the Transfer of Property Act and under section 27 (b) of the Specific Relief Act, succinctly. Let us look at the relevant provisions of law thereto. Section 44 of the Evidence Act provides that:

"Fraud or Collusion in obtaining judgment, or incompetency of Court, may be proved: Any party to a suit or other proceeding may show that any judgment, order or decree which is relevant under sections 40, 41 or 42, and which has been proved by the adverse party, was delivered by a Court not competent to deliver it, or was obtained by fraud or collusion",

Section 40: "Previous judgments relevant to bar a second suit or trial: The existence of any judgment, order or decree which by law prevents any court from taking cognizance of a suit or holding a trial, is a relevant fact when the question is whether such Court ought to take cognizance of such suit or to hold such trial".

Section 43: "Judgments, etc. other than those mentioned in sections 40 to 42 when relevant: Judgments, orders or decrees, Other than those mentioned in sections 40, 41 and 42, are irrelevant. Unless the existence of such judgment, order or decree is a fact in issue, or is relevant under some other provision of this Act".

<u>48. In the light of the provisions of law as provided in section 44 of the Evidence Act as well as the settled principle laid down by our Apex Court in a number of cases that fraud vitiates every right, be that a legal or vested right, our view, in line with the aforesaid provisions of law and principle, is that whatever the right may have accrued by the petitioner, if the government can prove through a competent Court that fraud has been practiced upon the trial Court in obtaining the judgment and decree of the TS No. 20 of 91, the procedural law like res-judicata or shield like estoppel are hardly able to defend the petitioner inasmuch the said doctrine or principles are not capable to stand in the way of granting justice by a competent Court when the fact of practicing fraud upon the Courts will be proved and established before the said competent Court. In the case of Begum Khaleda Zia vs Government of Bangladesh 63 DLR 385, the plea of estoppel, waiver and acquisance could not stand in the way though the petitioner, upon mutating her name, was owning and possessing the land for 28 years without facing any hindrance from any corner. Therefore, the performance demonstrated by a group of unscrupulous government officers or employees cannot be said to be the true "representative" (wording from section 115 of the Evidence Act ushering the concept of Estoppel) in a litigation where public property and interest is involved and, as such, the subsequent bonafide step (declaration, act or omission) by another group of government officials with patriotic zeal should be taken into consideration. In the case of People's Republic of Bangladesh vs Most Sharifian Bibi 43 DLR (AD) 112, the RS Khatian was prepared in the name of the plaintiffs predecessor who paid rent to the government and the plaintiff subsequently, upon mutating its name, also paid rent to the government, nonetheless, the Appellate Division discarded the application of doctrine of Estoppel.</u>

49. In order to deal with the submission on section 41 of the Transfer of Property Act, let the said section be reproduced herein below:

Section 41: Transfer by ostensible owner—Where, with the consent, express or implied, of the persons interested in immovable property, a person is the ostensible owner of such property and transfers the same for consideration, the transfer shall not be voidable on the ground that the transferor was not authorized to make it: provided that the transferee, after taking reasonable care to ascertain that the transferor had power to make the transfer, has acted in good faith.

<u>50. From a bare reading, we do not find any scope of its application in a property owned by the government inasmuch as no one can be allowed to pretend to be the owner of a government owned property and, as such, the concept of the "ostensible owner" is not applicable where the dispute is with regard to "Khas land" and "acquired land". Further, the word "person" used therein does not denote the government inasmuch as from the definition clauses of the General Clauses Act, it does not appear that government is meant to be a "person".</u>

51. For dealing with the submissions advanced by the learned advocate for the petitioner as to being endowed with the protection under section 27(b) of the Specific Relief Act, let the said section be reproduced herein below:

27(b) Relief against parties and persons claiming under them by subsequent title: any other person claiming under him by a title arising subsequently to the contract, except a transferee for value who has paid his money in good faith and without notice of the original contract;

52. From the reading of the above provisions of law, we find it difficult to understand that how the provisions of the said section can be of any assistance for the petitioner as apparently the said provisions deals with the case related to specific performance of contract.

53. With regard to the submissions as to the application of section 114(g) of the Evidence Act, we find that since the plaintiff of the Title Suit No. 20 of 91 did not make any application to the trial Court for production of the case record of LA Case No. 77 of 1963-64, drawing an adverse inference against the defendants of the said suit was improper.

54. Regarding the submissions on "Explanation IV" to the section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure, our view is that in a case where government is a party to a suit or other proceeding, though law places the government on a similar position to an individual party and does not grant any special privilege, nonetheless, the said provisions should be cautiously applied, particularly where conduct of the government employees/officers becomes question-able due to non-rendering their diligent assistance in dealing with government property, in view of the prevailing tendency among the said category of people as to the treatment of the government property differently from their own property and, thereby, differentiate their obligation in performing their duties in protecting the national interest with that of their own. It is not out of place to mention here that every law is created by the state to the advantage and for the benefit of the state as well as of its citizens and both the groups, that is state functionaries and citizens are expected and, thus, presumed to act innocently and bonafide. Enactment of any law is never aimed at bestowing unfair advantage to unscrupulous citizens or state functionaries.

55. The above painstaking exercises on the "Scenario No. 2" of this writ petition take us to deal with the competency of this Court as to whether the findings of facts of practicing fraud upon the Courts in Title Suit No. 20 of 91, which derived from the threadbare discussion on the judgment and decree of the learned trial Court and appellate Court, examination of the cases of the plaintiffs and defendants, appreciation of the evidences of both the parties, observations on the performances of the learned Judges at the trial and appeal Courts as well as of the Government Pleaders, is capable of vitiating the operation of the judgment and decree passed in the said suit.

56. Its unanimous and obvious answer is that this Court is not competent to set-aside the findings as well as decrees and judgments of the said suit while exercising its power and jurisdiction of certiorari. Thus, unless and until the said judgment and decree is set-aside, which might still be possible by filing a Review Petition before the Appellate Division, the aforesaid painstaking exercise in unearthing the fact of practicing fraud upon Courts shall remain useless inasmuch as by virtue of the operation of the said judgment and decree, the predecessors of the petitioner successfully established themselves as the owners in possession of the case land in spite of the fact that the said suit was for permanent injunction, not for declaration of title. Consequently, as long as the said judgment and decree remains in operation, the findings in the said suit, that plot No. 41 was never acquired in LA case no, 77 of 1963-64, remains alive. It follows that Without setting-aside the said judgment and decree in Title Suit No. 20 of 91, plot No. 41 cannot be included in the LA Case No. 77 of 1963-64 by a mere amendment circular albeit we have held that the judgment and decree in TS No. 20 of 91 has been obtained by practicing fraud upon the trial Court but without any consequence to the present writ petition.

57. Thus, though in dealing with the "Scenario No. 1" of the instant writ petition, it was apparent that mere printing mistake was occurred in publication of the Gazette Notification dated 4-3-1965, however, in the light of the findings of this Court on the "Scenario No. 2" of the instant writ petition that the existence of the judgment and decree of Title Suit No. 20 of 91 debars the government from including plot No. 41 in the LA Case No. 77 of 1963-64, we are constrained to hold that the publication of the impugned amendment circular was illegal and without lawful authority while the operation of the said judgment and decree remains effective.

58. From the above discussions and observations, this Court is led to hold that in spite of detecting the fact of practicing fraud upon the Courts in obtaining the judgment and decree in Title Suit No. 20 of 91, the same being not set-aside by a competent Court and, thus, being in operation as of now, the hands of this Court are tight and not well equipped to discharge the instant Rule. Consequently, the impugned "Amendment Circular" being নং জে প্র সি/এল, এ/ ৪৪৭(৩)dated 28-8-2010 published in the Bangladesh Gazette dated 7-10-2010 (Annexure-E) appears to be without any arms to protect it for now and, accordingly, the same is declared to have been published without lawful authority and is of no legal effect.

59. Accordingly, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs.

60. Before parting with the judgment, we consider it appropriate to pass some directions in the following manner, otherwise, the whole exercise, as to examining the poor performances of the trail Court as well as appellate Court, unearthing the motivated conducts of the government employees and officers and detecting the poor role of the Government Pleaders in TS No. 20 of 1991 will remain as a futile exercise by this Court. It is not out of place to mention here that this Constitutional Court, on its own motion, is well empowered to pass appropriate direction to any state functionary, such as the Office of the Attorney-General, when this Court takes judicial notice of any action, omission, failure or occurrence by the said state functionaries. In this connection we can profitably refer to the Case of Siddiqur Rahman vs State, (popularly known as amendment Case) 65 DLR (AD) 1, wherein it was observed that the Supreme Court cannot keep its eyes shut when a Constitutional violation or illegality is surfaced as the judges of this Court are oath bound to safeguard and protect the Constitution and other laws of the land, in other words, play pivotal role in establishing the rule of law in the land.

61. Accordingly, the Anti-Corruption Commission is directed to investigate in to the matter as to why the concerned officers/ employees employed at the relevant point in time with the office of the Deputy Commissioner and office of the District Fishery did not produce the file of LA case No. 77 of 1963-64 before the trial Court or appellate Court.

62. The Office is directed to send a copy of this judgment to the Chairman, Anti-Corruption Commission, 1, Segunbagicha, Dhaka to enable him to comply with the aforesaid direction of this Court.

63. The Registrar of this Court is directed to send a copy of this judgment to Mr Shaha-e-Alam Chowdhury, who was serving as a Senior Assistant Judge in the District of Sylhet and conducted the trial of the Title Suit No. 20 of 1991 and delivered its judgment and decree on 18-11-1991 and also to Mr Manjur Qader, who was serving as an Additional District Judge of the District Sylhet and delivered the judgment and decree on 17-2-2004 in the Title Appeal No. 06 of 1992 having affirmed the judgment and decree of the trial Court, upon tracing their present respective job stations, in order to enable them to be appraised of the questions raised in this judgment as to their performance. The Registrar is further directed to convey the concerns expressed by this Court in the instant judgment about the standard of performance demonstrated by the said two judicial officers to the General Administrative (GA) Committee for its record.

64. However, we do not fancy to pass any order of direction to the Office of the learned Attorney-General asking it to take the necessary steps in the CPLA No. 2041 of 2008. We leave it upon the good conscience of the said office to consider as to whether it should immediately take necessary steps in line with its own statement made in its affidavit in opposition in view of our finding as to the involvement of corruption by the Government Headers in con-ducting both the trial and appeal in Title Suit No. 20 of 1991 and Title Appeal No. 06 of 1992 respectively.

Mirza Hussain Haider J: Having gone through the judgment delivered by my brother I agree with the decision of making the Rule absolute only. But I have my own reasoning’s to arrive at such decision. Facts and submissions being thoroughly discussed by my brother in his judgment, I do not need to elaborately discuss the same except which are necessary along with some of the submissions of the learned Assistant Attorney-General which are not fully contemplated in the affidavit in opposition and relying upon which, my brother has taken much pain in coming to a conclusion that fraud has been practiced upon the Court in obtaining the Judgment and decree in Title Suit No. 20 of 1991 and accordingly directed the Anti-Corruption Commission to investigate the matter and also directed the Registrar, Supreme Court, to take the matter to the notice of the General Administration (GA) Committee of the Supreme Court, upon holding that the said judgment and decree "being not set-aside by a competent court and thus being in operation as of now the hand of the Court are tight and not well equipped to discharge the instant Rule", I, with much anxiety cannot humbly agree with these parts of judgment.

66. So far my reasoning’s are concerned, my looking at the matter is from the angle that the Rule in this writ petition has been issued upon the respondents "to show cause as to why the amendment circular being JaPro C/LA/ 447(3) 'dated 7-10-2010 (Annexure-E) issued under the signature of Respondent No. 7, Land Acquisition Officer, Syhlet by inclusion of the petitioner's land as described in the schedule to the writ petition as Acquisitioned land of LA Case No. 77 of 1963-64 shall not be declared to have been published without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect, "From the aforesaid terms of the Rule it appears that the whole question encircles as to whether the publication of the impugned amendment circular (Annexure-E) was in accordance with law. To answer the query and to come to a conclusion of this point in issue we need to see firstly; as to who issued the impugned amendment circular, Annexure E and whether he had/has the authority to issue such circular under section 5(7) of the (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act, 1948; and secondly: if the same is for the purpose of amending/correcting the original circular dated 4-3-1965 then whether the same has been issued or published by the appropriate authority and whether the same can be done after 45 years of final publication of the same in the Gazette under section 5(7) of the said Act 1948, when the said law has been repealed by section 1(3) and (4) read with sections 16 and 17 of the said Act itself.

67. The background of the case is, admittedly, Rajani Ranjan Gupta was the CS recorded tenant of CS Plot No. 41 covering an area of 1.10 acres of land whose name was rightly recorded and published in SA Khatian No. 1687 in 1962; after his death his son Rakkhini Ranjan Gupta became the owner of the said property. On the other hand, it is alleged by the respondents that in LA Case No. 77 of 1963-64, the entire 1.10 acres of land in Plot No. 41, along with the entire land of CS Plots Nos. 33, 40 and 42 and parts of Plots Nos. 43 and 44 total 5.59 acres of land were acquired by the authority which was published finally in the Dhaka Gazette on 4-3-1965. It is also admitted that Abdus Sahid and others claimed to be the owners of the entire 1.10 acres of land in Plot No. 41 by purchase from Rakkhani Ranjan Gupta, son of Rajani Ranjan Gupta by five deeds of sale all in 1990 whereupon, they got their names mutated in place of Rajani Ranjan Gupta and enjoying the same by paying rents to the government in their respective names. In 1991 when the District fishery officer, Sylhet, threatened them to dispossess from the said land on the plea that the property is an acquired property, they filed Title Suit No. 20 of 1991, for permanent injunction, against the District Fisheries Officer, Subid Bazar, Syhlet and Bangladesh represented by the Deputy Commissioner Sylhet. It is also admitted that the said two defendants contested the suit by filing written statement contending intralia that entire 1.10 acres of land of Plot No. 41 along with full Plots Nos. 33, 40 and 42 and parts of Plots No. 43 and 44, total 5.59 acres of land, are acquired property and the District Fisheries Office is in possession of the same by way of possession handing over certificate dated 28-5-1964, Ext 'Ka' (Annexure A-I to the affidavit in opposition filed by Respondent No. 3). It is further admitted that the said suit was finally decreed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Sylhet, by his judgment and decree dated 28-11-1991 holding that on the face of nonproduction of the records of LA case No. 77 of 1963-64; and on the face of plaintiffs' registered title documents, Mutation Khatian and the proof of possession through payment of land revenue taxes to the government by rent receipts; and on the face of all the evidences, both oral and documentary, of the plaintiffs proving their possession; and on the face of Abdun Noor, the alleged bargadar of the District Fisheries Office, being not produced and examined to prove possession of District Fisheries Office; and in the absence of any pleading as to non-mentioning Plot No. 41 in the finally published gazette dated 4-3-1965 was erroneous or due to mistake the said Plot No. 41 was not mentioned in the said gazettee dated 4-3-1965 as to final acquisition; and also on the face of advocate commissioner's report which concurrently proved plaintiffs' possession in the said Plot No. 41, even after being cross examined by the defendants, the learned Assistant Judge held that 'the plaintiffs have been able to prove their prima facie title in the 1.10 acres of land of Plot No. 41 and also having successfully proved their exclusive possession in the suit land both by oral and documentary evidences and also through the Advocate Commissioners' report and accordingly decreed the suit and the defendants were permanently restrained by an order of injunction from dispossessing the plaintiffs from the said land in Plot No. 41. It is also admitted that the said decree was affirmed in Title Appeal No. 6 of 1992, preferred by the aforesaid two defendants who then unsuccessfully moved the High Court Division and also the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court in Civil Revision No. 4627 of 2004 and CPLA No. 2041 of 2008 respectively. Thus the findings and decision of the learned Assistant Judge in Title Suit No. 20 of 1991 is a valid judgment which is still in operation. After the appeal in the Appellate Division was dismissed on 4-5-2009 the present respondents published the impugned amendment circular on 7-10-2010. Hence this Rule.

68. With this backdrop this writ petition has been taken up for hearing and my brother in his judgment made the Rule absolute with observations and directions as mentioned earlier. My anxiety is when the law provides that with the final publication in the Gazette Notification the entire acquisition process ends and when the gazette notification was published in 1965 without incorporating Plot No. 41 and when the law, under which the acquisition was made, has been repealed, whether the said gazette of 1965 can be rectified by the impugned amendment circular dated 7-10-2010 after unsuccessful exercise up to the Appellate Division and after the law being repealed , on the plea of mistake and of course behind the back of the plaintiffs or the writ petitioner, the subsequent transferees. If we, at all, take it as a mistake then question arises whether the said mistake can be rectified after final publication in the gazette in 1965 and whether the land acquisition officer, Sylhet, has any authority to publish the said impugned amendment circular, whereby he tried to include Plot No. 41 in the Gazette Notification of 1965. In this respect we need to see section 5 of the Act of 1948 which deals with final publication. The same reads is as follows:

"5. Acquisition of Property—(1) The Government may, if it thinks fit, acquire any requisitioned property on the proposal of the Deputy Commissioner in the manner hereafter provided in this section.

(1a)The Deputy Commissioner shall, if he considers that the acquisition of any requisitioned property is expedient for a public purpose or in public interest, cause a public a notice to be given at convenient places on or near the requisitioned property stating that the property is proposed to be acquired.

(2) Such notice shall state particulars of the property to be acquired, and shall require all persons interested in the property to appear personally or by agent before the Deputy Commissioner at a time and place therein mentioned (such time not being earlier than fifteen days after the date of publication of the notice) and to state the nature of their respective interests in the property, their objections (if any) to the acquisition of the property and particulars of their claims to compensation for their respective interests.

(3) Notice shall also be served to the above effect on the owner of such property and on all such persons known or believed to be interested therein or to be entitled to act for persons so interested as reside or have agents authorized to receive service on their behalf within the revenue district in which the property is situated.

(4) In case any person so interested resides elsewhere and has no such agent, the notice shall be sent to him by registered post in a letter addressed to him at his last known residence, address or place of business.

(4a)Every person required to make or deliver a statement under sub-sections (2) (3) and (4) shall be deemed to be legally bound to do so within the meaning of sections 175 and 176 of the Penal Code (XLV of 1860).

(5) The Deputy Commissioner shall after hearing all objections and after making such further enquiry, if any, as he thinks necessary submit the case for the decision of the Government together with the record of the proceedings held by him and a report containing his recommendations on the objections.

(6) The Government, after considering the record made under sub-section (5), shall make a decision about the acquisition of the requisitioned property and such decision of the Government shall be final.

(7) The Government shall then publish in the Official Gazette a notice to the effect that the Government has decided to acquire the requisitioned property. On and from the beginning of the day on which the notice is so published the requisitioned property vest absolutely in the Government free from all encumbrances and the period of such requisition of such property shall end."

69. Having gone through the aforesaid provision of law it appears that it is the "government" who, as it thinks fit, may acquire any requisitioned property, on the proposal of the Deputy Commissioner in the manner as provided thereafter. Interestingly, sub section (la) to subsection (5) of section 5 of the Act of 1948 deals with the power of the Deputy Commissioner to deal with the matters relating up to proposal for and report regarding acquisition. Whereas sub section (6) and (7) thereof, empowers the "government" only to finalize the acquisition upon considering the report of the Deputy Commissioner and thereby finally publish the same in the Gazette which accordingly brings the entire proceedings of requisition and acquisition to an end upon absolute vesting of the said property in the government free from all encumbrances on and from the date of publication of the gazette notification. One thing is required to be bear in mind that after the gazette notification the requisition or acquisition of the property comes to an end which means it becomes a 4 past and closed transaction, empowering no-one to make any amendment or correction of the same. If, for argument sake, it is taken that non-inclusion of any plot/property in the finally published gazette notification was a mistake, which is of course not the case of the respondents in the civil suit, even then the correction, if any, is to be made or allowed under the law, by the government not by the Land Acquisition Officer, who being a subordinate officer to the Deputy Commissioner, under no circumstances can be treated as the "government". Although Act of 1948 did not define the word 'government' but reading section-2 of the said Act, as a whole it appears that the government is someone else other than the Deputy Commissioner or Additional Deputy Commissioner, Joint Deputy Commissioner and Assistant Commissioner or [Deputy Magistrate and Deputy Collector] authorized by the Deputy Commissioner to exercise any power conferred, or perform any duty imposed, on the Deputy Commissioner by or under the said Act. The Land Acquisition Officer being subordinate to the Deputy Com-missioner, does not have any authority to correct the gazette notification published by the government in 1965. In this respect we can also take the assistance of the (Emergency) Requisition of Property Rules, 1948 wherein, though government has not been defined like the Act, but the forms printed for the purpose of issuance of notice under section 3, namely, requisition or under section 5 (1) and 5 (3) namely, intention of the government to acquire a property or filing of objection, if any, to requisition of a property, or claim for compensation; and also if we see Form D which is for the purpose of issuing notice under section 5(7) for final acquisition of a property, we find that form A to C are used for notices to be issued under section 3, 5(1) and 5(3), respectively, which shows that those are to be issued/published under the signature of the "Deputy Commissioner" or "Additional Deputy Commissioner." Interestingly, the notice under form D, which is for the purpose of final acquisition of a property to be issued under section 5(7) is required to be published under the signature of the "Secretary/ Deputy Secretary" "by Order of the President". So, if we take into consideration the provision of section 21 of the General Clauses Act then we find that the authority which can pass order it can vary, after, amend or rescind that order. In the present case when the final notice was published by the "Government" under section 5(7) of the Act of 1948 meaning "by order of the President" under the signature of Secretary or Deputy Secretary it is only the Government not the Land Acquision officer who has the authority to amend or correct the said gazette notification not the "Land Acquisition Officer" as has been done in the present case as appears from the impugned Annexure-E to the writ petition.

70. On the other hand when the Act of 1948 was given a longevity up to 34 (thirty four) years from the date of its effect i.e. from 16-8-1948 (under section 1(3) and 1(4) of the said Act) meaning the longevity of the said law was till 15-8-1982. With the end of 15-8-1982 the said (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act, 1948 had its natural death and under section 16 of the said Act it has been provided that 'on the expiry of this Act, the provisions of section 8 of the General Clauses Act, 1897 shall apply, as if this Act has been repealed by an Act of the Legislature'. So the law which had its natural death, pursuant to section 1(3) and 1(4) read with section 16 of the Act of 1948 and thereafter when the new law namely the "Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Ordinance 1982" came into operation and there being no saving clause provided for in either of the two laws to protect the acts and deeds or anything made under Act of 1948, the authority, not to speak of the Land Acquisition Officer, under no circumstances had any power to amend or correct the finally published Gazette Notification of 1965 by the impugned amendment circular, Annexure E.

71. On the other hand, when the District Fisheries Office or the Deputy Commissioner, Syhlet, did not produce anything to prove that the property was requisitioned property and subsequently was acquired, by producing any piece of paper nor admitted in the suit that mistakenly the same was not published in the gazette of 1965 and accordingly having lost in all the courts up to the Appellate Division, the respondents, under no circumstances, now can issue such impugned amendment circular on the plea that mistakenly the said plot was not incorporated in the gazette of 1965. This is nothing but sheer Latches on the part of the Respondents and, as such, they cannot take advantage of their own laches. Thus publication of the impugned amendment circular after 45 years from the final publication of Gazette Notification or 20 years from the institution of the suit under no circumstances can be termed as a bonafide action on the part of the respondents. Moreover, when by virtue of decree dated 28-11-1991 the plaintiffs' possession have been affirmed and subsequently the writ petitioner having purchased the same from the plaintiffs after the dismissal of the CPLA by the Appellate Division the writ petition is a bonafide purchaser with value and notice of the contested decree as well as the government records and having mutated its name with the government offices and is paying land development taxes to the government the publication of the impugned amendment circular in the gazette (Annexure E), without serving any notice upon the petitioner or its predecessors, is nothing but an arbitrary action of the respondents which proves their high handedness whereby the judgment and decree affirmed up to the Appellate Division has tried to be made frustrated. Such arbitrary action of the respondents has also violated the principle of natural justice of being heard.

72. Thus the respondents having failed to prove the acquisition of the disputed land in the finally published Gazette Notification of 1965 up to the Appellate Division on contest and the predecessors in interest of the petitioner having got their names mutated and recorded in the government record as evident from Annexure A and A (1) series, and the petitioner having got its name also mutated vide Mutation case No. 4214/10-11 after the purchase as evident from Annexures C-3 , the petitioner is a bonafide purchaser with notice on payment of adequate value, as such the respondents, under no circumstances have any authority to issue the impugned amendment circular (Annexure-E) without notifying the petitioner.

<u>73. Since the subject matter of the Rule is 'whether the impugned amendment circular inserting Plot No. 41 in the Gazette Notification of 1965 in connection with LA Case No. 77 of 1963-64 is proper and since I have come to a conclusion that the said publication of Gazette Notification of 1965 was the finality of the requisition/acquisition proceeding, the correction of the said gazette of 1965 by the impugned amendment circular (Annexure E) published by the land Acquisition Officer, Sylhet after more than 45 years without having any authority of such publication, the impugned circular (Annexure E) thus is without lawful authority as stated hereinabove and since the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No. 20 of 1991 is not the subject matter of this Rule rather the same has been produced as an Annexure to prove that how the respondents miserably failed to prove any title and possession on the said piece of land, I have got no other option but to constrain myself to remain within the discussion as to the legality of the publication of the impugned Gazette Notification not anything beyond that. Under the present context we cannot extend ourselves to scan the judgment passed in Title Suit No. 20 of 1991 or in the appeal/revision arose out of the same. Moreover, till the said decree is in force and not set-aside by a competent court, the impugned amendment circular, published after leasing the case up to the Appellate Division, shall have no bearing other than Creating chaos and confusion in the mind of the Public. Our jurisdiction being limited within Article 102 of the Constitution we are not empowered to sit as an appellate court to see the validity of the said judgment and the same being not the subject matter of this Rule any observation/finding on the same is nothing but at best be an academic discussion which the Appellate Division directed all to refrain from as has been held in the case of Abdul Mannan Khan vs Bangladesh reported in 64 DLR (AD) 169 that 'while deciding a case, a Court shall not embark upon unnecessary academic discussions and shall confine itself within the issues, which will crop up from the pleadings of the respective parties.' Here in the present case decree of Title Suit No. 20 of 1991 being not the subject matter in issue we are not empowered to see the validity of the same not we can make any observation as to genuinenity of the same and accordingly direct anybody to investigate into the matter.</u>

74. Accordingly, I am of the view that the publication of the impugned amendment circular, Annexure E, is fully without lawful authority, as the publication of the same by the Land Acquisition officer Sylhet is beyond his jurisdiction and the present respondents cannot take any advantage of the same as the same has no legal effect.

75. Hence, the Rule is made absolute and, the impugned amendment Circular being No. JaPro C/LA/447(3) dated 7-10-2010 (Annexure-E) issued under the signature of Respondent No. 7, Land Acquisition Officer, Sylhet whereby the petitioner's 1.10 acres of land in CS Plot No. 41, fully described in the schedule to the writ petition, as acquisitioned land of LA Case No. 77/63-64 is hereby declared to have been published illegally, without lawful authority and of no legal effect.

76. With these findings and reasoning’s, as stated hereinabove, I agree with the decision as to making the Rule absolute only but I thus cannot agree with other directions of my brother.

There will be no order as to cost.

End.
