parties:
Government of Bangladesh, represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Education and others ----- Petitioners
VS
Md Abul Kalam Azad and others  ----- Respondents
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 27-1-2011 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 4008 of 2010).
full_judgment:
SK Sinha J: This petition at the instance of the writ respondents is against a judgment of the High Court Division in Writ Petition No.4088 of 2010 directing the petitioners to transfer the service of the writ petitioners against the vacant posts under the revenue set up.

2. Facts relevant for the disposal of this petition are thus; the writ petitioners along with others were appointed as sweepers under 53 Thana Education Project Officers. Initially the project was valid till December 1999 but it was subsequently extended under different names and continued until the year 2007. Since 2007, they have been working without any salary. The Ministry of Education has recommended for absorbing the writ petitioners posts in the revenue budget. From the same project 256 post holders were absorbed in the revenue budget. Ultimately by the impugned memo dated 17th March 2009 the Ministry of Establishment declined to transfer the writ petitioners to the revenue budget. Inspite of that the Ministry of Education requested that the sweepers should be transferred to the revenue budget and by its memo dated 9th September, 2009 the intimated the writ petitioners that in view of the memo of the Ministry of Establishment dated 17th March, 2009 transfer of their posts to the revenue, budget would not be considered. It was contended that in project profile, there was provision for transferring the writ petitioners to the revenue set up after conclusion of the project and that since there were 130 vacant posts of sweepers there was no reason for the petitioners not to absorb them in those vacant posts.

3. It was argued on behalf of the petitioners that though the post of 7 sweepers appeared to have been approved by the Ministry of Education, there was no evidence that they had actually been absorbed in those posts; that the appointment letters of the writ petitioners clearly stated the conditions of service to the effect that they were temporarily appointed against a project and that as such, they could claim to be absorbed as of right in the revenue set up.

<u>4. The High Court Division upon hearing the parties observed that though there is no direction that the persons appointed under the project would be absorbed in the revenue set up after completion of the project, there is indication from annexure-D that they would be absorbed that in the absence of project profile it is not possible for ascertaining the terms upon which the project document refers to the aspect to the revenue set up; that the Ministry of Education has decided to absorb 7 out of 63 persons appointed as sweepers in the same project and thus the writ petitioners could expect that they would be treated in the same way subject to the availability of the posts. The High Court Division then considered an unreported judgment dated 22nd April, 2010 of the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 849 of 2009, in which, another Division Bench directed to absorb 20 sweepers out of 63 who were appointed at the same time and observed that the Government should not discriminate the writ petitioners in considering their case of transferring their service to the revenue set up.</u>

5. The learned Deputy Attorney-General has taken us to the writ petition, the annexures, the previous judgment of this Division on the same subject matter and submits that since this Division has settled the point on the question of absorption in the revenue budget, who had been appointed in various development projects after reviewing all previous judgments, the judgment of the High Court Division is apparently inconsistent with the views taken by this Division.

<u>6. Admittedly the writ petitioners were appointed on a development project on temporary basis. They claimed their absorption in the revenue set up on the ground that some other sweepers who stand on the same footing have been absorbed in the revenue set up and that here is also recommendation for their absorption in the revenue set up. This Division after reviewing all previous judgments on the question of absorption has given guide lines for absorption in the revenue set up in Civil Petition No. 1781 of 2011 disposed of with 8 other petitions in which cases, the writ petitioners were also appointed in development projects. We cannot take any contrary view in the absence of cogent ground for taking exception from the said views. In view of the above, the judgment of the High Court Division is modified and the writ petitioner's claim for absorption in the revenue set up will be considered by the petitioners in the light of the guidelines given by this Division in the above judgment which are as under:</u>

<u>(i) Whenever any vacancy in LGED is created in the revenue set up it shall consider for absorption of employees or officers of the development projects within the meaning of section 2(ga) of the Rules, 2005, if the project in which s/he is working is completed subject to the condition that such employee or officer has requisite qualifications for the said post.</u>

<u>(ii) Whenever a vacant post is created in the revenue budget, the LGED shall absorb/ transfer an employee or officer from the development project mentioned in clause (1) to fill up that post in accordance with Rules of 1985 and the ECNEC's decision dated 10th January, 2008.</u>

<u>(iii) An officer or employee shall be absorbed if s/he was appointed in the development project within the meaning of rule 2(ka) of Rules, 2005 in accordance with the procedures prescribed for appointment in public employment.</u>

<u>(iv)An officer or employee must have requisite qualifications for the post in which he is seeking absorption.</u>

<u>(v) An officer or employee must have continuity in service in the project in which he is working.</u>

<u>(vi)An officer or employee must have satisfactory service record before his case is considered for regularization in the revenue budget.</u>

<u>(vii) If an officer and employee whose rank and status does not relate to the posts advertised by the impugned notifications on the day of its publications, such officer or employee would not be eligible for consideration for absorption.</u>

<u>(viii) The employees and officers who have been working in the development projects mentioned in clause (1) on monthly pay basis would only be eligible for consideration for absorption in the revenue budget.</u>

<u>(ix) Unless, and until vacancies in revenue budget in the LGED are created, the employees and officers of the development projects mentioned in clause (1) cannot claim as of right to be absorbed in the revenue budget.</u>

<u>(x) while considering and selecting an employee or officer of the development project for absorption on the revenue budget, the appointing authority shall maintain strictly the prevailing quota system for employment in the public employment being followed by the Government.</u>

<u>(xi) The LGED shall consider the cases of those working on master roll basis for absorption in the revenue budget by phases if they have requisite qualifications subject to availability of vacancies according to their seniority.</u>

<u>This petition is disposed of with the above observations.</u>

End.

lawyer:
Mr. Abdul Quaiyum, with Mr. Selim Reza Chowdhury, Advocates ------ For the Petitioners 
Mr. Md. Mainul Islam, Advocate ------ For Opposite Party Nos.1-7, 12, 14, 16-19, 23-24 
Mr. A. K. M. Rezaul Karim, Advocate ------ For Opposite Party no.22
parties:
Most. Mariam Begum and others ------ Petitioners
Versus
Nuijahan Begum and others ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
Mr. Borhanuddin, J :- This Rule was obtained by the plaintiffs upon making a revisional application under Section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure against judgment and decree dated 08.05.2008 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 8th Court, Dhaka, in Title Appeal No. 405 of 2006 affirming those of dated 10.07.2006 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Court, Dhaka, in Title Suit No.451 of 2005 decreeing the suit. 

2. Facts relevant for disposal of the rule are that plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No.79 of 1990, renumbered as Title Suit No.451 of 2005, in the Court of learned Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka, for setting aside preliminary decree dated 05.06.1979 passed in Title Suit No.118 of 1963, renumbered as Title Suit no.20 of 1967, and final decree dated 08.12.1988 signed on 26.01.1989 pursuant to preliminary decree and also for declaration that those are not operative against and binding upon the plaintiffs contending inter alia that plaintiff no.1 Kalu Khan is a non Bengali Bangladeshi who cannot sign his name in Bengali; Said Kalu Khan purchased 5(five) kathas of land from C.S. Plot No.137 under C.S. Khatian no.167 vide registered kabala dated 05.12.1956 and has been residing therein by erecting houses; Plaintiff nos. 2 and 3 purchased 10 decimals of land from Abu Sayed Farajee and Nilufar Begum on 25.02.1971 and residing therein by erecting houses; said Abu Sayed and Nilufar Begum purchased the land on 05.11.1964 from Badrunnessa Chowdhury who purchased the same vide registered kabala dated 20.12.1961 from Anwaruddin Ahmed and Khandker Kamrul Huda; Father of plaintiffs no.4 and 5 Hafez Sarkar purchased 2 gondas of land from C.S. plot no.125 under C.S. Khatian No.167 vide registered kabala dated 19.04.1961 and residing therein by erecting houses; After his expiry, his share devolved upon his wife, three sons and four daughters; Plaintiff no.6 Abdus Sobhan purchased 2 gondas of land from Md. Abdul Hafiz vide registered kabala dated 09.03.1965 from C. S. Plot No.139 and possessing the same through tenants; Abdul Hafiz purchased 5 gondas of land from C. S. Plot No.139 vide registered kabala dated 25.01.1962; on 28.03.1990 defendant no.3 informed plaintiff no. 5 that they obtained decree relating to the lands of plaintiffs; On query through their advocate plaintiffs for the first time came to know about the judgment and decree under challenge and after procuring certified copy of the same filed the suit. 

3. Defendant Nos. l, 3-7, 21 and 22 contested the suit by filing written statement denying material allegations made in the plaint and contending inter alia that the suit is not maintainable and bad for defect of parties. Further contending that summons of Title Suit no.118 of 1963 were duly served upon all the defendants, some of them contested the suit by filing written statement and some others prayed saham; On the expiry of defendant no. 93 Fazlur Rahman, suit was abated but abatement order was cancelled in Miscellaneous Case No.10 of 1974; Summons of said miscellaneous case also served upon all the opposite parties; Predecessor of defendant nos.16-21 along with five other defendants filed Title Suit No.16 of 1978 against exparte decree; Father of plaintiff nos.4 and 5 i.e Abdul Hafiz, who was impleaded as defendant no.54 in the Title Suit, along with other two filed Miscellaneous Case No.11 of 1978 which was allowed and the exparte decree was set aside; Thereafter, preliminary decree passed on 05.06.1979 in presence of contesting defendants and subsequently final decree drawn up in accordance with law; Plaintiffs of the present suit and their predecessors has/had prior knowledge about preliminary decree and final decree passed in the Title Suit; Present suit filed only to harass the defendants; Suit is liable to be dismissed. 

4. Defendant Nos.16-21 contested the suit by filing written statement supporting case of the plaintiffs. 

5. After hearing the parties and assessing evidence on record learned Joint District Judge, Court, Dhaka, decreed the suit. 

6. Being aggrieved, defendants as appellants filed Title Appeal No.451 of 2006 in the Court of learned District Judge, Dhaka. On transfer, said appeal was heard and disposed of by the learned Additional District Judge, 8th Court, Dhaka, who after hearing the parties and reassessing evidence on record disallowed the appeal and thus affirmed findings of the trial court. 

7. Having aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree, defendant nos.1, 3-7-appellants as petitioners preferred this revisional application under Section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the present rule with an order of status-quo. 

8. Mr. Abdul Quiyum, learned advocate for the petitioners submits that admittedly plaintiff of original suit no.118 of 1963 Adam Ali was owner of 1/3rd share of the suit land by inheritance and the suit was decreed allowing saham to the plaintiff accordingly as such, appellate court below committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in not holding that plaintiffs are not aggrieved by the impugned judgment and decree. He also submits that appellate court below committed an illegality in not holding that if the summons were not served upon some of the defendants that was mere irregularity which cannot be ground for setting aside a decree under Section 99 of the Code of Civil Procedure. He next submits that the court below committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in not considering that original suit was filed in the year 1963 before promulgation of S. A. and R. S. record as such, mentioning number of unborn S. A. and R. S. khatian relating to suit plots were not possible. He also submits that plaintiff nos. 2, 3, 7-18 are not parties in the original suit and as such allegation of non-service of summons against them is not tenable in the eye of law. He submits that plaintiff nos.1, 4-6 were impleaded as defendants in the original suit as such, burden of proof lies upon them to prove that summons were not served. He lastly submits that appellate court below committed an illegality in not holding that the suit is barred by limitation inasmuch as final decree was drawn up on 28.04.1980 and the present suit filed long after 10 years on 08.04.1990 which is barred under Article 91 and 120 of the Limitation Act as such, impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set aside. In support of his submissions, learned advocate referred to the case of Ratan Chandra Dey and others-Vs- Jinnator Nahar and others, reported in 13 MLR (AD)168, the case of Bhashani Mondal being dead his heirs; Nanda Rani Mondal and another-Vs- Md. Abdus Stikur and others, reported in 18 BLT(AD)497, the case of Girish Chandra Jana-Vs- Kala Chand Maity, reported in AIR 1957 (Calcatta) 242 and the case of Government of Bangladesh, represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Forest, Secretariat Building, Dhaka and others-Vs-Md. Osimuddin, reported in 11 MLR (AD)132.

9. On the other hand Mr. Md. Mainul Islam, learned advocate for the opposite parties submits that it is evident from record of the Title Suit that when preliminary decree was passed then the suit was not ready for hearing inasmuch as court below fixed 16.06.1979 for submitting written statement but PW.1 Md. Habibullah examined on 01.06.1979 and preliminary decree passed on 05.06.1979 as such, there is nothing to interfere with the impugned judgment and decree. He also submits that record of the Title Suit shows that PW.1 Md. Habib Ullah did not file any document in support of his deposition. He again submits that both the courts below upon assessing and reassessing evidence on record arrived at a concurrent finding that summon of the original suit was not served upon plaintiff no.1 of the present suit Kalu Khan who was impleaded as defendant no.14 in the original suit inasmuch as Mujibul Huq who allegedly received summon on behalf of Kalu Khan had no manner of relation with said Kalu Khan and defendants of the present suit failed to prove that Mujibul Huq was an agent of Kalu Khan. He next submits that plaintiffs having impeached the decree passed in earlier suit on ground of collusion and fraud on the assertion that they are owners in possession of the suit land, they are not required to seek any further relief to their main relief of declaration. He submits that once an amendment is allowed, said amendment relates back to the date of institution of the suit. He lastly submits that there is no question of limitation when it is proved that summons were fraudulently suppressed and limitation will run from the date when the fraud was detected. In support of his contention, learned advocate referred to the case of Abdus Sukur (Md) and others-Vs- Bhasani Mandal' and another, reported in 53 DLR 452, the case of Doon Valley Rice Limited-Vs-MV Yue Yang and others, reported in 48 DLR 531 and the case of Abul Khair Mia-Vs- Abdul Latif Sarder, reported in 32 DLR (AD) 167. 

10. Mr. A. K. M. Rezaul Karim, learned advocate for the opposite party No.22 by adopting submissions of Mr. Md. Mainul Islam add that plaintiffs of Title Suit no.118 of 1963 obtained the decree by suppressing summons and this finding of fact has been arrived at both by the trial court and appellate court below which is not revisable in this jurisdiction. He again submits that the finding of fact arrived at by the appellate court below which is the last court of fact that summons were fraudulently suppressed. He also relied upon the case reported in 32 DLR (AD) 167. 

11. Heard the learned advocates Perused revisional application, judgment of the courts below along with lower courts record of the present suit and Title Suit No.118 of 1963 and decisions cited by the learned Advocates. 

12. Main contention of the plaintiffs in the present suit are that preliminary decree and final decree obtained in Title Suit No.118 of 1963 by suppressing summons fraudulently and also that at the time of passing preliminary decree, original suit was not ready for hearing. Relevant orders from order sheet of Title Suit no.118 of 1963 are reproduced below: "Order no.289 dated 31.5.79: Pltff. and the defdt. nos. 89, 91, 24, 101, 104 and some added defdts. file hajiras. One Gaznafar Ali Chowdhury and two others and one Manjur Murshed Waliur Rahman and two others (all are minors) file two petitioners under order I rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure with a prayer to add them as defendants in this suit on the ground stated in the petition. Copy served upon the pltff. Put up tomorrow for orders. 

Order no.290 dated 1.6.79: Pltff. and the defendant No.89 file hajiras. Petitions dated 31.05.1979 filed by one Goznafar Ali Chowdhury and two others and one Manjur Murshed Waliur Rahman and two others are put up for hearing and order. Today defdt. no. 46 also file a petition with court fees of taka 20/- and prays for separate saham. It appears from the certified copy of the kabalas that the petitioners purchased a portion of Dag no.151. So, prayer is allowed. Amend the plaint and register accordingly. To 16.06.1979 for w/s. Keep it with file. Order no.291 dated 1.6.79: Added defendants Manjur Murshed Waliur Rahman and two others defdt. no. 104- 106 file a joint petition with court fees of taka 20/- and prays for compact saham for their share. Keep it with file. 

Order no.292 dated 1.6.79: Plaintiffs and the defdt. no. 46 and 111-113 file hajiras and ready. The suit is taken up for hearing. PW. 1 Md. Habubullah is examined. Put up on 5.6.79 for order. 

Order no.293 dated 2.6.79: Defendant nos.97 and 98-100 file two petitions with court fees of taka 20/- in each petition and prays for separate saham for their shares. Let the petitions be kept with the record. Order no.294 dated 4.6.79: Defdt. no. 105 files a petition with court fees of taka 20/- and prays for separate saham. Let this petition be kept with the record. 

Order no.295 dated 5.6.79: Case is proved. C. F. paid is correct. Hence, Ordered that the suit be decreed in preliminary form on admission with cost against defdt. nos.7, 16(Ka) 16(gha), 18, 26, 46, 95-96, 97, 98-100, 101, 104, 105, 111- 113, who do get their saham as prayed for and exparte against the rest with cost. Plaintiffs do get a saham of 1/3rd share in "C" schedule land. Parties may effect partition amicably within 60 days from today, failing which plaintiffs are entitled to get their saham separated by metes and bounds through court, by appointment of commissioner, who, if appointed and commissioned, is to respect possession and convenience and transfers of by respective parties so far as practicable." From the above orders, it appears that vide order no.290 dated 01.06.1979 though trial court fixed 16.06.1979 for written statement but on the same date i.e. 01.06.79 examined PW.1 Habibullah vide order no. 294. More interesting is that suit decreed on 05.06.1979 though 16.06.79 fixed for written statement. From the above quoted orders it is evident that when preliminary decree passed, suit was not ready for hearing. So, I cannot disagree with finding of the appellate court below that decree was not passed in accordance with law. On perusal of the order sheet, I find that some of the orders i.e. from order no. 247-253 are missing from the record. 

13. On perusal of the record, it appears both the courts below arrived at a concurrent finding that summon was not served upon plaintiff no.1 Kalu Khan inasmuch as Mujibul Huq who allegedly received summon on behalf of Kalu Khan was not his agent and defendants failed to prove that he had any manner of relationship with Kalu Khan. From the plaint of present suit it also appears that owners of lands namely Anwaruddin Ahmed and Khandker Kamrul Huda who purchased the land on 18.03.1953 and sold the same to Badrunnessa Chowdhury vide kabala dated 20.12.1961 who on her turn sold the land to vendor of plaintiffs no. 2 and 3 were not made party in the original suit. It is also stated in the plaint that predecessor of plaintiff nos. 4 and 5 Abdul Hafiz Sarker purchased the land on 19.04.1961 but he was not made party in the original suit though one Howfader Abdul Hafez Sarker without mentioning father's name impleaded in the original suit as defendant no. 54. Order V of the Code of Civil Procedure deals with the issue and service of summons.

14. Finding of facts arrived at by the appellate court below as the last court of fact that summons were suppressed and decree obtained in the original suit fraudulently and collusively are not perverse and based on evidence on record. It is settled that once fraud is established, limitation will run from the date when it was detected. 

15. It is not clear from the order sheet of Title Suit no.118 of 1963 whether Md. Habibullah who deposed as PW. 1 submitted documents in support of his testimony. Learned Advocate for the petitioners submitted that the plaintiffs of the present suit are not aggrieved by the judgment and decree of the previous suit inasmuch as plaintiff of the original suit allowed saham in respect of 1/31.4 share as claimed by him as C.S. recorded tenant but on perusal of the plaint of Title Suit it appears that contentions of the plaintiff in the suit could be reverted by the defendants by filing written statement and adducing evidence if summons were duly served upon them as such, submission of the learned advocate does not hold water in the present context. 

16. Under the facts and circumstances of the case and for the reasons stated above, I am of the view that preliminary decree passed in the Title suit when suit was not ready for hearing as such, preliminary decree and subsequent final decree were not passed in accordance with law and summons of the Title Suit no.118 of 1963 were fraudulently suppressed as such, question of limitation does not arise. Furthermore, plaintiff of the Title suit obtained preliminary and final decree without impleading the persons who owned and possessed suit land before institution of Title suit. 

17. In the present suit, plaintiffs impeached preliminary decree and final decree passed in Title Suit no.118 of 1963 on ground of collusion and fraud on the assertion that they are owners in possession of their portion in the suit land before institution of the Title Suit in the year 1963. 18. Both the courts below found that the plaintiffs are in possession in their portion of the suit land and the predecessor of the defendants obtained the decree collusively and fraudulently. In such view of the matter, plaintiffs are not required to seek any other relief as 'further relief' to their main relief of declaration. 

19. Facts and circumstances of the cases cited by the learned Advocate for the petitioners are quite distinguishable from the facts and circumstances of the case in hand. 

20. Accordingly, the rule is discharged without any order as to cost. 

21. Impugned judgment and decree dated 08.05.2008 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 8th Court, Dhaka, in Title Appeal No.406 of 2006 is maintained. 

22. Order of status-quo granted at the time of issuance of the rule is hereby vacated. 

23. Accordingly, Title Suit No.118 of 1963, renumbered as Title Suit No.69 of 1986, is restored. Court concern is directed to dispose of the suit as soon as possible preferably within 1(one) year from the date of receipt of this judgment. 

24. It is pertinent to mention here that disposal of the Title Suit should be confined within the present parties without allowing any further application for addition of party, otherwise it will be an unending process. 

25. Send down lower courts record along with a copy of this judgment to the court concern at once. 

End.

lawyer:
Anwarul Azim Khair, Advocate-For Petitioners. 
Rafiqul Islam, Sr. Advocate—For the Respondent No. 6.
parties:
Khorshid Nayeem and others ----- Petitioners
Vs
Land Appeal Board and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
AKM Abdul Hakim J: On an application under Article 102 of the Constitution, this Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the order dated 9-12-2003 passed by the Full board in case No. 3 -108 of 1995 (Review) Dhaka (Annexure D), order dated 29-8-1995 passed by the Chairman, Land Appeal Board in case No. 3-85 of 1984 (Appeal) -Dhaka (Annexure-C) and the order dated 8-10-1989 passed by the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Tejgaon Circle, Dhaka in Miscellaneous Case No9. 19 of 1987 (Annexure-A (1) should not be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and of no legal effect and why the respondent Nos. 3-5 should not be directed to mutate the names in Miscellaneous Case No. 19 of 1987 as per decree passed-in Title Suit No. 280 of 1970 in respect of the 7 (Seven) SA Plots measuring 5-17 acres and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this court may seem fit and proper.

2. Facts leading to the institution of the writ petition are as follows:—

That the land of Mouza- Tejkunipara under Police Station Tejgaon, previously Keranigonj, District Dhaka measuring a total area of 37.66 acres of land appertaining to CS Khatian No. 211, CS Plot No. 560/669 originally belonged to Satinath Bandapaddhaya alias Sagar Babu. The said land was put to auction sale for arrears of rents and one Promode Bala Devi auction purchased the same. While in possession, she sold away demarcated block of land measuring 5.88 acres to Jinnatun Nessa Bibi and Kashem Ali by registered Sale Deed dated 16-5-1941 and delivered possession to them. Thereafter Jinnatun Nessa Bibi died leaving behind only son Kashem Ali and one daughter Joynab Bibi and they transferred their share of 5.88 acres to Syed Ahmed, Moqbul Ahmed and Khurshid Jahan Akhter, (predecessor of the petitioners) by two registered Kabalas dated 25-7-1958 and 7-8-1958. But by mistake, the relevant SA Khatian in respect of said land along with other land was wrongly recorded in the name of Satinath Bandapaddhaya. The predecessor of the petitioners filed Miscellaneous Case No. 110 of 1969 for correction of SA Record. Abdus Sattar Chowdhury-Respondent No. 6 claiming himself to be owner of 8.70 acres of land of aforesaid CS Plot No. 560/669 on the basis of Amal-nama dated 18th Srabon, 1350 BS on receipt of Salami and on Payment of Rs 10 as annual rent alleged to have been executed by Satinath Bandapaddhaya. Respondent No. 6 filed Miscellaneous Case No. 355 of 1968 in the First Court of Munsif, Dhaka on 16-12-1968 for correction of SA record under section 143A of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act against Pirjada Abul Kashem and Md Hasnain Siddiqui as the same was wrongly recorded in their names.

3. The predecessor of the writ petitioners having come to know about the said Miscellaneous Case filed an application on 2-8-1969 for addition of party which was kept with the record. Subsequently upon an application for amendment, Satinath BandaPaddhaya was added as Opposite Party Nos. 3 in the said Miscellaneous Case No. 355 of 1968 by order dated 16-8-1969. Meanwhile Circle Officer (Revenue), Tejgaon, Dhaka after holding local enquiry submitted a report on 7-7-1969. The Miscellaneous Case was taken up for ex-parte hearing and petitioner-Abdus Sattar Chowdhury was examined and on the basis of the enquiry report, the learned Munsif held that the Miscellaneous Case is not maintainable and accordingly dismissed the Miscellaneous Case by Order No. XXVI dated 1-8-1970.

4. It may be mentioned that the predecessor of the petitioners did not proceed with the Miscellaneous Case No. 110 of 1969 on the expectation that the khatian would be corrected by the authority in view of the report of the Circle Officer (Revenue) Tejgaon; Dhaka dated 7-7-1969. Subsequently in the said Miscellaneous Case Abdus Sattar Chowdhury-Respondent No. 6 filed an application under Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for vacating the dismissal order dated 1-8-1970, but the same was rejected as not maintainable by Order No. XXVIII dated 27-8-1970. Then the respondent No. 6 filed an application under Order XLVII Rule 1 read with section 114 of the Code of Civil Procedure for review of the order dated 1-8-1970 and the same was allowed by vacating the order of dismissal dated 1-8-1970 and Miscellaneous Case No. 355 of 1968 was restored to its file and number by Order No. XXIX dated 29-8-1970. Subsequently the Miscellaneous Case No. 355 of 1968 was allowed ex-parte by order dated 2-9-1970 and the names of the Opposite-Parties were deleted and the Tahshilder was directed to insert the names of the petitioners in the SA Khatian in place of SA record owner Satinath Bandapaddhaya.

5. That the predecessors of the petitioners having come to know about the order dated 2-9-1970 passed in the Miscellaneous Case No. 355 of 1968 instituted Title Suit No. 280 of 1970 in the First Court of Sub-Ordinate-Judge, Dhaka on 29-12-1970 impleading the respondent No. 6 as defendant No. 1 and others as defendants for declaration of right and title in the suit CS Khatian No. 211 CS Plot No. 564/669, of Mouza No. 278 Tejkunipara under Police Station Tejgaon, previously Keranigonj, Dhaka corresponding to RS Khatian No. 605, RS Plot Nos. 1353/1354/1355/1356/1357/1358 and 1365 for an area 5.17 acres out of 5.58 acres being demarcated. Since incorrect entries and non entry of the names of the plaintiffs in the said RS khatian and malafide claim of interest in the suit land by the principle defendants, a cloud was created over the right, title and interest of the plaintiffs in the suit land. The Title Suit No. 280 of 1970 was decreed ex-parte against the defendant No. 1 by the judgment and decree dated 26-8-1972, declaring right, title and interest of the predecessors of the petitioners in respect of 5.17acres of land in suit CS Plot 560/669. It may be noted that the Circle Officer (Revenue) Tejgaon, Dhaka in his report dated-74969-filed in Miscellaneous Case No. 355 of 1968 clearly mentioned that in the copy of Record of Right (RoR) the suit plots were recorded in RoR Khatian No. 605, and RoR Plot Numbers have been recorded in the name of Satinath l3andapaddhaya, son of Jadunath Bandapaddhaya. 32. Let us first consider the relevant provision of Section 143A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy act 1950 under which the respondent No. 6 filed the Miscellaneous Case No. 355 of 1968 for correction of SA record. Section 143A was inserted after Section 143 by East Pakistan Ordinance No. VIII of 1967. It was however, omitted after few years by ordinance No. LXIV of 1975. So Section 143A provides for an alternative right to right to file a case before the Civil Court for correction of bona fide mistakes of the record of rights.

33. The omitted Section 143A runs as follows:

"Special provisions for correcting mistakes in the record of rights:—

(1) Any person aggrieved by an entry or omission of entry in the record-of-rights prepared or revised and finally published under Chapter IV may, not withstanding anything contained elsewhere in this Act, file an application along with necessary requisites, for the purpose of correction of mistakes in such record of rights in the civil court which would have jurisdiction to entertain a suit for possession of the land to which such entry relates or in respect of which such omission was made.

(2) An application filed under sub-section (1) shall be deemed to be a plaint and order passed thereon shall have the force of a decree under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (Act V of 1908).

(3) An application filed under sub-section (1) shall contain full particulars of persons likely to be affected by an order on such application and shall also contain the full particulars of the holding to which the entry relates or in respect of which the omission complained of was made.

(4) The court shall, for the purpose of disposal of application filed under sub-section (1), follow the following procedure, namely:

(a) The court shall cause notice to be observed on the persons named in the application in the manner as provided in the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (Act V of 1908).

(b) The court shall, within seven days of the filing of an application under sub-section (1), send a copy thereof, by registered post at the cost of applicants to the Revenue-Officer concerned for holding a local inquiry, in presence of the parties concerned, on the subject matter of the application and the Revenue-Officer shall, within fifteen days of the receipt of the copy, hold inquiry and submit the report to the court.

(c) The court may allow such reasonable time as it may think fit to file objection to the inquiry report referred to in clause (b) and, (3)of no appearance is made by the opposite party within the time mentioned in the notice, and if no objection is filed to the inquiry report within the time so allowed, the court may proceed ex-parte with disposal of the application after taking into consideration the said report and other material evidence on record; and (d) where the report referred to in clause (b) is not submitted, or where objection referred to in clause (c) is filed, the court shall fix a date for hearing and on that date, after hearing the parties and taking into consideration the report, if any, and other evidence which may be adduced by the parties in this behalf, shall pass such order as it may think just and proper.

(5) Any person, whose interest has been affected by reason of any entry or omission in the record of rights, referred to in sub-section (1), may, within fourteen days of the filing of an application under sub-section (1), appear to be added as co-application.

(6) The Revenue-Officer shall, for the purpose of an inquiry under sub-section (4), have the same power as vested in a civil Court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (Act V of 1908), including the power of:

(a) Enforcing attendance of any person, and examining him on oath; and

(b) Compelling the production of any document.

(7) Within thirty days from the date of an order under sub-section (4), an application from that order shall lie to the district Judge who may, either himself hear the appeal or transfer it to any other court subordinate to him but not below the rank of Subordinate Judge for hearing.

(8) Decision under sub-section (4) if no appeal is preferred from it, or under sub-section (7), shall be final and conclusive.

(9) Where the court passes an order sub-section (4), or sub-section (7), revising the entries or rectifying the omission complained of under sub-section (1), it shall notify the same to the Collector and the collector shall correct the record-or-rights accordingly.

(10) Any person interested may produce a certified copy of the orders referred to in sub-section (4) or sub-section (7) to the Revenue-Officer and the Revenue-Officer shall make such alterations in the record-of-rights as may be necessary to give effect to such orders.

(11) The record-of-rights corrected under sub-section (9) or sub-section (10) shall be deemed to have been prepared and finally published under Chapter IV of this Act.

(12) An application under sub-section (1) or memorandum of an appeal under sub-section (7) shall, not withstanding anything contained in the Court-Fees Act, 1870, (Act VII of 1870), bear a fixed court fee of rupee one.

(13) For the purpose of an application, appeal, review, revision and consequence of non-appearance, relevant provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (Act V of 1908), shall mutatis mutandis apply."

34. Now let us see whether the order passed in the Miscellaneous Case No. 355 of 1968 passed by the learned Munsif, First Court Dhaka was in accordance with relevant provision of section 143A the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950.

35. We have already seen from the order sheet of the Miscellaneous Case No. 355 of 1968 (Annexure-F (1) to the Affidavit-in-Reply) that the Miscellaneous Case was filed by the respondent No. 6 for correction of the SA record. It appears from the said Annexure that initially Miscellaneous Case was dismissed ex-parte by order dated 1-8-1970 and thereafter the petitioner filed an application under section 151 for rejecting the order passed on 1-8-1970 and the learned Munsif by order dated 27-8-1970 rejected the application under section 151. Against the order of ex-parte dismissal dated 1-8-1970 passed in the Miscellaneous Case No. 355 of 1968, the petitioner filed an application under Section 114 read with Order XLVII Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure on 27-8-1970 for review of the order. It transpires that without issuing any notice to the opposite parties just after two days, which is on 29-8-1970 the learned Munsif allowed the said review application. Thereafter the said Miscellaneous Case was taken up for ex-parte hearing on 2-9-1970 just after 3 days and PW1 Abdus Sattar Chowdhury was examined and the learned Munsif again allowed the Miscellaneous Case ex-parte and passed order to delete the names of the opposite parties from the case SA khatian and insert the name of the respondent No. 6 therein.

36. Thus it is evident that the ex-parte order passed in Miscellaneous Case for deleting names of opposite-parties and recording the respondent No. 6's name in the case SA Khatian without serving any notice upon the opposite parties as per law and without impleading the heirs of the predecessors of the petitioners, Moqbul Ahmed and others cannot be binding upon them and the said order is of no avail to the respondent No. 6. Moreover, Sub-section 13 of section 143A of the State acquisition and Tenancy Act clearly provides that the relevant provision of the Civil Procedure Code, that is, order XLVII shall be applicable for the purpose of filing an application for review. Sub rule 4(2) of order XLVII provides that the no application for review shall be granted unless notice of the application has been served upon the Opposite-Party and discovery of new and important matter or evidence which, after the exercise of due diligence, was not within his knowledge or could not be adduced by him when the order was passed, without strict proof of such allegations. In the present case Miscellaneous Case was allowed ex-parte by the learned Munsif without complying with the mandatory provision of Sub-Section 13 of Section 143A.

37. Mutation proceedings are done under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act (SAT Act) and the Rules framed there under. Section 143 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act provides, inter alia, that the record of rights prepared or revised shall be maintained upto-date in the prescribed manner under part IV, or under Chapter XVII by correcting clerical mistakes and, by incorporating the changes of account of (a) the mutation of names as a result of transfer or inheritance, Chapter VI of the Tenancy Rules, 1995 consists of rules 22-25 of which rules 22-24 relate to mutation proceedings.

38. Section 143A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act is attracted only when a person aggrieved by wrong entry in the record of rights finally published and for correcting mistakes in the record of rights on the basis of the possession of the parties in the case land in the Civil Court. This section is not attracted when the record of right is to be corrected after a finding to be given as to the title of the holders or challengers. An application under section 143A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act is not a suit for declaration of title but is a proceeding for rectification of mistakes in the record of right prepared on the basis of the possession of the parties in the land in question. This section is only concerned with the question of possession of the land and question of title to the land is beyond the scope of this section.

39. In this connection, reliance may be placed on the cases of Assistant Custodian Enemy Property (Land Appeal Board) Tanga vs Bholanath Guha reported in 36 DLR (AD) 79 Reazuddin vs Jatindra Kishore reported in 37 DLR (AD) 202.

40. From a plain reading of the above provision of law and the decisions cited above, it is clear that section 143A is meant for a limited purpose for correction of the record of rights of the basis of possession of the parties in the case land. The respondent No. 6 filed the Miscellaneous Case No. 355 of 1968 not only for correction of mistakes in the SA Khatian but for some other reasons.

41. In the unreported decision of the Appellate Division is the case of Bangladesh and others vs Mariam Khatun and others (Civil Appeal No. 8 of 1972), the fact are that the respondent who, along with others took settlement of land from Zamindars and were in possession thereof, challenged the order of the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Faridpur cancelling the names of the respondent and his co-sharers from the record of rights which were recorded in the name of the then Province of East Pakistan. By four different orders from 1960 to 1963 the Revenue Settlement Officer corrected the record of rights and inserted the names of the respondent and his co-sharers in the disputed Khatian. The Deputy Commissioner of Faridpur purchased some of the land in dispute from the respondent in 1964, but on 17-10-1966 the respondent and his co sharers were served with notice to show cause why the record of rights shall not be changed in favour of the Province of East Pakistan. The respondent showed cause but the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Faridpur cancelled the names of the respondent and his co-sharers by order dated 13-7-1967 and inserted the name of the Province of East Pakistan in respect of the disputed khatian. The case of the Province of East Pakistan was that the names of the respondent and his co-sharers were recorded as a result of fraudulent transaction between the respondent and his co-sharers on the one hand and some of the revenue authorities on the other hand.

42. The Appellate Division quoted with approval the judgment of the then Dhaka High Court in Writ Petition No. 386 of 1967 arising out of the above proceeding as follows :—

"The scope of section 143 of the Act is, is our opinion, of a very limited nature. It authorizes the Collector to maintain up to date record of rights and to make such correction as occurred as a result of bona fide mistake committed in preparing the record of rights. It does not, in our opinion, authorize Collector to correct the record-of-rights which affects the question of title or possession relating to disputed question of fact. Bona fide mistake, as contemplated under section 143 of the Act, in our opinion, relates to the mistake of the nature where a mistake has crept in which is not supported by the records or where there has been a mistake in recording quantum of the land which again is no supported by facts but where name of a person stands recorded and another person challenges that such entry cannot be said to have been made as a result of bona fide mistake, and that cannot be corrected by the Collector under section 143 of the Act."

43. The Appellate Division was unable to find fault with or take exception to the views so expressed. The Appellate Division held that the facts which were required to be determined prior to correcting the record-of-rights by a proceeding under section 143 of the Act involved the examination of documents of title relating to the lands in dispute, commission of fraud, if any, and the interpretation of various sections of the Act. The summary method under section 143 cannot be strained to consider question relating of such facts.

44. In the present case also the questions, for example, whether Syed Ahmed, Moqbul Ahmed and Khurshid Jaban Akhter, predecessors of the petitioners by two registered kabalas dated 25-3-1958 and 7-8-1958 purchased 5.58 acres. Whether the respondent No. 6 was possessing the remaining 8.70 through unregistered Amalnama and if so under what title, whether the unregistered Amalnama date 18th Sraban, 1350 BS created any title in favour of the respondent No. 6 and other questions can be determined only after examining witnesses and documents in a full-scale title suit. None of these things can conveniently or even suitable by done by the Collector under the terms and provisions of aforesaid section 143, as it now stands. If "bona fide mistake" was not covered by the facts disclosed in the aforesaid civil Appeal No. 8 of 1972, we fail to see how "clerical mistake" can be found in the present case.

45. We have already seen that the predecessors of the petitioners acquired title in the case property on the basis of the decree dated 29-12-1970 passed in Title Suit No. 240 of 1970 against the respondent No. 6 and others.

46. We have also seen that on the basis of an ex-parte order passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 355 of 1968 the respondent No. 6 filed the Miscellaneous Case No. 19 of 1987 before the Circle Officer (Revenue) Tejgaon, Dhaka (Annexure-H to the Affidavit-in-Reply) for mutation and correction of the SA record long after 17 years without impleading Moqbul Ahmed and others, predecessor of the writ petitioner and when the name of Satinath was recorded in the finally published SA Khatian No. 605. It appears that long before filing of the said Miscellaneous Case No. 19 of 1987 the Circle Officer (Revenue) Tejgaon opened mutated SA Khatian No. 605/1 of Mouza Tejkunipara in the name of Syed Ahmed, Moqbul Ahmed and Mrs Khurshid Jahan Akhter in Miscellaneous Case No. 9 of 1977-78 and they have been possessing the same by paying rents to the Government regularly. But the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Tejgaon Circle Dhaka by order dated 9-1-1988 Passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 19 of 1987 erroneously cancelled several Mutation cases including the Mutation Case No. 9 of 1977 filed by the petitioners predecessors, Moqbul Ahmed and others. Thus the order of the Assistant Commissioner (Land) dated 9-1-1988 is not operative against the predecessors of the petitioners who were admittedly not parties to the Mutation proceedings (Miscellaneous Case No. 19 of 1987).

47. That subsequent to the decision passed by the Full Board in Case No.3-108 of 1995 (Review) on 9-12-2003 the respondent No. 6 as petitioner again filed an application before the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Tejgaon Circle, Dhaka for mutation of his name and same was registered as Miscellaneous Case No. 42 of 2006. The Assistant Commissioner (Land) after considering all aspects of the case and report of the Kanungo held that since the Rule and stay order passed by the Hon'ble High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 3229 of 2004 is still in force, there is no scope to consider the prayer of the petitioner and accordingly he rejected the Miscellaneous Case filed by the respondent No.6 on 19-10-2006.

48. It appears that undisputedly the case land of Mouza-Tejkunipara, Police Station Tejgaon, previously Keranigonj appertaining to CS Khatian No. 211, CS Plot No. 560/669 (Annexure-E) and Satinath Bandapaddhaya alias Sagar Babu was the CS recorded owner. Subsequently, the lands in CS Plot No. 560/669 was finally recorded as SA Khatian No. 605, Plot Nos. 1355/1354/1355/1356/1357/1358/ 1365/1370/1377/1383/1384 and 1385 .(Annexure-E(1) in the names of Satinath Bandapaddhaya.

49. It will be further evident from the Certified Copy of the CS Khatian (Annexure-E), SA record of rights being SA Khatian No. 605(Annexure-E(1) in the name of Satinath Bandapaddhaya, (Mutated) SA Khatian No. 605/1 (Annexure-G) wherein out of 12 SA Plots 7 SA Plots being SA Plot Nos. 1353/1354/1355 /1356/1357/1358/ and 1365 of SA Khatian No. 605/1 total area of 5 17 have been recorded in the names of Syed Ahmed, Moqbul Ahmed and Khurshid Jahan Akhter by Miscellaneous Case No. 9 of 1977-78.

50. Annexure G(1) is the certified copy of the Finally Published RS Khatian No. 76, RS Plot Nos. 1617/1618/1619/1620/1621/1670/ 1671 of Mouza-Tejgaon Shilpa Elaka which was recorded in the name of aforesaid 3 persons in respect of the case property. The aforesaid facts have been clearly admitted by the respondent No. 6 and it will be further proved from (Annexure-H) Certified Copy of application (Miscellaneous Case No. 19 of 1987) filed by the respondent No.6 through his constituted Attorney, Md Azharul Islam for Mutation and correction of record under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act impleading Pirjada Abul Kashem, Md Hasnain Siddiqui as Opposite-Parties, wherein it is stated that case property is of Mouza-Tejkunipara, at present Tejgaon Shilpa Elaka.

51. It further evident that in the said Miscellaneous Case No. 19 of 1987, the predecessors of the petitioners, Moqbul Ahmed, Syed Ahmed and Khurshid Jahan Akhter and original SA recorded owner, Satinath Banda-paddhaya were not made parties. Therefore, the order passed in the said Miscellaneous Case on 9-1-1988 by the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Tejgaon (Annexure-H(1) cancelling several Mutation cases including Miscellaneous Case No. 9 of 1977-78 and passed order for correcting SA record of right in the name of respondent No. 6-Abdus Sattar Chowdhury in place of SA recorded owner, Satinath Bandapaddhaya without impleading the names of the Satinath and predecessors of the petitioner cannot be binding upon them and the said order is of no avail to the respondent No. 6.

52. Therefore, it is apparent from the record that the petitioner's predecessors got the title of the suit property on the basis of the decree passed in Title Suit No. 280 of 1970 on 29-12-1970 against the respondent No.6 and mutated their names in the record of rights by filing Miscellaneous Case No. 9 of 1977-78 and paying rents to the Government.

53. Moreover, during pendency of the Review application before the Land Appeal Board, respondent No. 6-Abdus Sattar Chowdhury made an oral gift to his son Mintu Chowdhury, added respondent No. 6 on 14-3-2002 and in recognition of said oral gift swore an Affidavit on 21-3-2002, and became absolute owner in possession on the basis of the said oral gift. Though added respondent No. 6 became owner of the case land on 14-3-2002 but curiously enough his father, Abdus Satter Chowdhury filed the Miscellaneous Case No. 42 of 2006 for cancellation of the earlier Mutation cases in respect of 12 SA Plot Nos. 1353 /1354/1355/1356/1357/1358/1365/1370/ 1377/1383/1384 of SA Khatian No. 605 and 1385 for an area of 8.70 acres to correct his name in the said SA Khatian No. 605 of Mouza Tejkunipara, at presents Tejgaon Shilpa Elaka.

54. It is pertinent to note that once Revision of Record of Rights was finally published under section 144(7) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act (SAT Act) and the publication shall be conclusive evidence that the record has been duly prepared or revised under this section. Section 144A lays down that a finally published record of rights prepared or revised under section 144 of the state Acquisition and Tenancy Act has a presumption of correctness and that presumption continues till it is otherwise rebutted by reliable evidence. In the present case it is evident from Annexure-G (1) to the Affidavit-in-Reply that the names of the petitioner's predecessors were finally published in the RS Khatian No. 76, Plot NICS. 1617/1618/1619/ 1620/1621/1670/ 1671 of Mouza-Tejgaon Shilpa Elaka. In such view of the matter, continuation of Miscellaneous Case No. 19 of 1987 and decisions passed by the Revenue Officers and the Land Appeal Board become inoperative since RS Khatian No. 76 has finally been published in respect of the case property in the name of the predecessors of the petitioners during continuation of Miscellaneous Case No. 19 of 1987.

55. Regard being had to the facts and circumstances of the present case and the above legal position, we do not find any merit in the submission of Md Rafiqul Islam that 7 RS Plot Nos. 1353/1354/1355/1356/1347/1358 and 1365 of RS Khatian No. 605 of Mouza Tejkunipara are not related to same SA Khatian and plots as claimed by the writ petitioners. Actually .those RS 7 plot are SA plots but due to oversight of the learned Advocate for the pre-decessors of the petitioners, those are inadvertently stated as RS Khatian and RS plots is the schedule of the plaint of Title Suit No. 280 of 1870 but those RS plots correspond to CS Khatian No. 211, CS Plot Nos. 560/669 This fact of mistake will be abundantly proved from the Certified Copy of SA Khatian No. 605 and Mutated SA,. Khatian No. 605/1 (Annexure-E and E (1) to the Affidavit-in-Reply) that those 7 Plots are SA Plots Nos. 1353/1354/1355/1356/ 1347/1358/ and 1365 of SA Khatian No. 605 and not RS khatian and RS Plots. Given this scenario, it cannot be said by any stretch of imagination that there was existence of any RS Khatian and RS Plots in the year 1970. In fact RS record of rights was prepared and finally published long after 1970 and during 1975-1990.

56. Further more, the learned Advocate for the petitioner, Mr Anwarul Azim Khair has especially drawn our attention to paragraph No. 4 of the Supplementary-Affidavit-in-Opposition dated 11-11-2009 wherein it has been stated that by Annexure-1, the writ petitioners want to introduce new facts but in the Supplementary-Affidavit-in-Opposition dated 18-5-2010 in paragraph 2 (i) it is stated that Miscellaneous Case No. 42 of 2006 (Annexure-1) was not filed by the Abdus Satter Chowdhury which was a collusive one. In such situation, we have no option but to hold that those statements made in Paragraph Nos. 4 and 2(i) of the Supplementary-Affidavit-in-Opposition are deemed to have been admitted by the added respondent No. 6. Having regard to the statements, made in aforementioned paragraphs of the Supplementary-Affidavit-in-Opposition dated 11-11-2009 and 18-5-2010 and in consideration of (Annexure-1) dated 19-10-2006, we are led to hold that the instant writ petition is quite competent. So the submissions of Mr Rafiqul Islam on those aspects of the matter stand negative.

<u>57. In the present case, it is an admitted fact that the names of the predecessors of the petitioners have already been recorded in the finally published RS Khatian No. 67(Annexure-G(1) to the Affidavit-in-Reply). In such circumstances, the High Court Division by exercising the power of judicial review under article 102 (2) (a) (ii) of the constitution was competent to inquire into the correctness of the decision if it finds that all the circumstances needed for passing the order were not forthcoming, it will declare the order to be void. In this context, Mr Anwarul Azim Khair has drawn our attention to a decision in a case of Munipal Council, Sujanpur vs Surinder Kumar reported in (2006) 5 SCC 173 wherein it has been stated in paragraph 11:—</u>

<u>"11. The High Court's Jurisdiction to issue a writ of certiorari is limited, a writ of certiorari can be issued if there is an error of law apparent on the face of record. What would constitute an error of law is well known. In judicial Review of Administrative Action. IV the Edition page 136-37, SA desmith has summed up the position:</u>

<u>"(5) The concept of error of law includes the giving of reasons that are bad in law or (if there is a duty to give reasons) inconsistent, unintelligible or, it would seem, substantially inadequate, It includes also the application of a wrong legal test to the facts found, taking irrelevant considerations into account and failing to take relevant considerations into account, exercising a discretion on the basis of any other incorrect legal principles, misdirection as to the burden of proof, and wrongful admission or exclusion of evidence, as well as arriving at a conclusion without any supporting evidence."</u>

<u>(See also SN Chandrashekar vs State of Karnataka, (2006) 3 SCC 208 and Bombay Dyeing and Mfg. Co. Ltd, vs Bombay Environmental Action Group (2006) 3 SCC 434.)</u>

58. Thus, we find that Full Board has misdirected itself as to the question of law involved in the case and reviewed the matter which are not within its jurisdiction as provided under Rule 3(3) of the Land Appeal Board Rules, 1990. We are of the opinion that under circumstances the decision passed in the review of the Full Board of the Land Appeal Board is liable to be interfered by this court as the Full Board travelled beyond its jurisdiction in deciding matters not within its jurisdiction contemplated under the Land Appeal Board Rules, 1990.

59. With reference to the decisions of 8 MLR (AD) 149, 10 MLR (AD) 2005, 47 DLR (AD) 9 and 50 DLR (AD) 213 made by the learned Senior Advocate for the respondent No. 6, we opine that the said decisions, in the facts and circumstances of the present case, have no manner of application. So the reference to the above decisions by Mr Rafiqul Islam does not help him in any way.

60. The impugned order dated 9-12-2003 (Annexure-D to the writ petition) indicate that Full Board without discovery of new and important matter or evidence or any mistake or error on the face of the record or showing any sufficient ground granted review in setting aside the order passed by the Board. In such view of the matter, we find that the Full Board exceeded its jurisdiction under the statute in setting aside the order passed by the Board dated 29-4-1995 in Case No. 3-85 of 1984 (Appeal)-Dhaka (Annexure-C to the writ petition).

61. From the foregoing discussions and having regard to the factual circumstances of the case, we are of the opinion that the order dated 9-12-2003 passed by the Full Board of the Land Appeal Board in Case No. 3-108 of 1995 (Review) Dhaka allowing the review and revising the decision passed by the Chairman, Land Appeal Board dated 29-8-1995 in Case No. 3-85 of 1994 (Appeal) Dhaka (Annexure-C) and allowing the Miscellaneous Case No. 19 of 1987 are without lawful authority and of no legal effect. The Rule therefore, succeeds.

62. We, therefore, make the rule absolute without any order as to cost. It is declared that impugned order dated 9-12-2003 (Annexure-D) has been passed without any lawful authority and of no legal effect and the respondent No. 1 is directed to cancel the same and the respondent No. 5 is directed to restore the SA records in the names of the petitioners to the extent of 5.17 acres as it originally stood.

Communicate this Judgment to the Land Appeal Board (respondent No. 1) at once.

End.

full_judgment:
ABM Khairul Haque J: BCS Recruitment Rules; 1981, সংশোধন করতঃ ১০-১১-২০০৬ ইং তারিখে প্রকাশিত প্ৰজ্ঞাপনটির বৈধতা Challenge করিয়া অত্র রীট মোকাদ্দমাটি দায়ের করা হইয়াছে৷

২৷ দরখাস্তকারীগণ সকলে নিজ নিজ বিষয়ে স্নাতকোত্তর শিক্ষাগত যোগ্যতা অর্জন করতঃ যথানিয়মে বিভিন্ন কলেজে প্রভাষক হিসেবে নিয়োগপ্রাপ্ত হন ৷ তৎপর তাহারা বিভিন্ন সময়ে তাহাদের নিজ নিজ পদে সফলতার সহিত বুনিয়াদি প্রশিক্ষণ ও বিভাগীয় পরীক্ষা র্সমূহে কৃতকার্য হইবার পর যথানিয়মে ও যথাসময়ে চাকুরীতে স্থায়ী হন।

৩৷তাহারা যখন বিভিন্ন কলেজে শিক্ষকতা পেশায় নিয়েজিত রহিয়াহেন সেই সময় বাংলাদেশ সরকার ১১-১০-২০০৬ ইং তারিখে BCS Recruitment Rules, 1981. (সংক্ষেপে 'বিধিমালা ১৯৮১'), সংশোধন বরেতঃ বিসিএস (সাধারণ শিক্ষা) ক্যাডারে যাহারা ১২-১-১৯৯২ ইং তারিখের পূর্বে নিয়োগপ্রাপ্ত হইয়াছিলেন তাহাদের চাকুরীতে স্থায়ী করণের জন্য বিধি অনুসারে প্ৰয়েজেনীয় বুনিয়াদি প্রশিক্ষণ ও বিভাগীয় পরীক্ষা হইতে অব্যাহতি প্রদান করতঃ ১১-১০-২০০৬ইং তারিখে একটি প্রজ্ঞাপন জারী করেন (এ্যানেকচার-সি)। ১-৫ নং দব্রখাস্তকারীগণ সকলেই ১৯৯২ ইং সনের পরবর্তী বিসিএস (সাধারণ শিক্ষা) ক্যাডার যোগদান করিলেও তাহারা সকলেই বুনিয়াদি প্রশিক্ষণ ও বিভাগীয় পরীক্ষায় উত্তীর্ণ হইয়া তাহাদের নিজ নিজ চাকুরীতে স্থায়ী হন। তাহারা যথানিয়মে ও চাকুরী বিধি অনুযায়ী যাহারা চাকুরীতে স্থায়ী হইয়াছিলেন তাহাদের মধ্য হইতে জ্যেষ্ঠতা অনুসারে চাকুরীতে পদোন্নতি প্রাপ্ত হইবার জন্য অপেক্ষমান থাকাকালীন সময়ে অকষ্মাৎ তর্কিত প্ৰজ্ঞাপন মারফ্ত বিধি সংশোধন করিয়া মূল বিধি অনুসারে বৃনিয়াদি প্রশিক্ষণ ব্যতিল্পেকে ও বিভাগীয় পরীক্ষায় অনুত্তীর্ণ শিক্ষকদের অস্বাভাবিকভাবে স্থায়ী করতঃ দরখাস্তকারীগণ ও তাহাদের সম পর্ষায়ভুক্ত বিধি অনুসারে স্থায়ী শিক্ষকগণের পদোন্নতি প্রাপ্ত হ্ইবার ক্ষেত্রে তাহাদের জ্যেষ্ঠতা লঙ্ঘন করতঃ প্রদত্ত অব্যাহতির ক্ষুব্ধ হইয়া অত্র রীট্ মোকাদ্দমাটি দায়ের করিলে অত্র আদালত বাংলাদেশ সংবিধানের ১০২ অনুচ্ছেদ অনুসারে ১৯-১০-২০০৬ ইং তারিখে প্ৰতিবাদীগণের বরাবরে নিম্নলিখিত রুলটি জারী করেনঃ

Let a Rule Nisi be issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the impugned Circular issued by the respondent No. 2 vide এস আর ও নং ২৫০ আই/২০০৬ সম (বিধি-৫)-১৫/২০০২ dated 11-10-2006 (as of Annexure-C) amending the Bangladesh Civil Service (Recruitment) Rules, ।98। (as of Annexure-A) with effect that a member of the BCS (General Education) appointed on or before the 12th January, 1992 will be exempted from the requirements of foundation training, Departmental Examination for performance and promotion in service, in a mechanical manner without any application of mind nor considering the adverse impact upon the quality of the Teaching Cadre in general education, and particularly those who are already in service having successfully passed examinations and having completed the training becoming junior to those who are otherwise not qualified, causing serious inequality being violative of Articles 27 and 29 of the Constitution and is of no legal effect and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

Pending hearing of the Rule, let the process of promotion in pursuance to the impugned Circular (as of Annexure-C) issued by respondent No. 2 vide এস আর ও নং ২৫০ আই/২০০৬ সম (বিধি-৫)-১৫/২০০২ dated 11-10-2006 be stayed for a period of 3 (three) months from date.

The Rule is made returnable within 3(three) weeks from date."

৪ ৷ ১নং প্রতিবাদী ২৬-৭-২০০৭ ইং তারিখে হলফকৃত এফিডেভিট ইন্ অপজিশান্ দাখিল করতঃ রীট্ মোকাদ্দমাটিতে প্ৰতিদ্বন্দ্বিতা করেন ৷ ইতিমধ্যে ৫-১১-২০০৬, ২৬-১১-২০০৬ ও ১৩-৫-২০০৭ ইং তারিখে পৃথক পৃথক আবেদনগুলির মাধ্যমে ৪-১৭ প্রতিবাদীগণ অত্র রীট্ মোকাদ্দমায় প্রতিবাদী হিসেবে নিজে দিগকে পক্ষভূক্ত করেন ৷ তাহাদের এফিডেভিট্ ইন্ অপজিশান গুলিতে মোটামুটি বর্ণনা এই যে, ১৯৯২ইং সনের বিসিএ্যাস (সাধারণ শিক্ষা) শিক্ষানবীশ বিধিমালা, ১৯৯২, প্রকাশিত হইবার পূর্বে বিসিএস ক্যাডারে যোগদানকৃত শিহ্মকগণের চাকুরী স্থায়ীকরণের জন্য ১৯৮১ইং সনের বিসিএস নিয়োগ বিধিমালার শর্ত অনুসারে বুনিয়াদি প্রশিক্ষণ এবং বিভাগীয় পরীক্ষায় উত্তীর্ণ হইবার বিধান থাকিলেও যথাযথ কর্তৃপক্ষ কর্তৃক এ সম্পর্কে কোন পদক্ষেপ গ্রহণে ব্যর্থতার কারণে ১৯৯২ইং সনের পূর্বে নিয়োগ প্রাপ্ত শিক্ষকগণ ঊক্তরূপ পরীক্ষা সমূহে অবতীর্ণ হইতে পারেন নাই এবং সেহেতু তড়াহাদের চাকুরী স্থায়ীকরণ করা হয় নাই ৷ ফলশ্রুতিতে চাকুরীতে তাহাদের জ্যেষ্ঠতা ক্ষুন্ন হইবে ও ভবিষ্যৎ তাহারা পদোম্নতির যোগ্যতা হারাইবেন বিধায় অত্র প্ৰজ্ঞাপন মারফত ১২-১-১৯৯২ইং তারিখের পূর্বে নিয়োগপ্রাপ্ত শিক্ষকপণকে ন্থায়ীকরণের জন্য বুনিয়াদি প্রশিক্ষণ ও বিভাগীয় পরীক্ষা হইতে অব্যাহতি প্রদান করা হয় ।

৫ ৷ দরখাস্তকারীগণপক্ষে বেগম তানিয়া আমীর ও তৎসঙ্গে জনাব মোঃ মনিরুজ্জামান আসাদ, এ্যাডভোকটবৃন্দ বক্তব্য উপস্থাপন করেন ৷

৬ ৷ বেগম নাঈমা হায়দার, ডেপুটি এটর্নী জেনারেল ও তৎসঙ্গে জনাব মোঃ জাফর ইমাম, সহকারী এ্যাটর্নী জেনারেল, ১-৩ নং প্রতিৰাদী পক্ষে, বক্তব্য উপস্থাপন করেন ৷

৭ ৷ অপরদিকে ৪ ও ৫ নং প্রতিবাদীপক্ষে জনাব এ,এফ, হাসান আরিফ ও জনাব রাজিক-আল-জলিল, এ্যাডভোকেটবৃন্দ, বক্তব্য উপস্থাপন করেন ৷

৮ ৷ ৬-১৭ নং প্রতিবাদীপক্ষে জনাব আব্দুর রব্ চৌধুরী ও তৎসঙ্গে জনাব সালাহ উদ্দিন, এ্যাডভোকেটবৃন্দ বক্তব্য উপস্থাপন করেন ।

৯ ৷ দরখাস্তকারীপক্ষে বেগম তানিয়া আমির তাহার দরখাস্তের সহিত সংযুক্ত ১১-১০-২০০৬ ইং তারিখের প্ৰজ্ঞাপনটি (এ্যানেকচার-সি) অবৈধ ও অকার্যকর নিবেদন পূর্বক বলেন যে, বাংলাদেশ সরকারের বিভিন্ন বিভাগে একটি মাত্র চাকুরী বিধি মারফত সমন্বয় করিবার স্বার্থে ১-১-১৯৮১ ইং তারিখে বাংলাদেশ সিভিল সার্ভিস নিয়োগ বিধিমালা, ১৯৮১, জারী করা হয়। বাংলাদেশ সরকারের ৩০টি ক্যাডারের জন্য উক্ত বিধিমালা একিভুত ও স্বয়ং সম্পূর্ণভাবে প্রণিত৷ চাকুরীতে স্থায়ীকরণের বিধিণ্বিধানঃ ৭নং বিধিতে প্রণয়ন করা হইয়াছে ৷ তিনি জোরালোভাবে উক্ত বিধির ২ উপবিধির প্রতি দৃষ্টি আকর্ষণ পূর্বক নিবেদন করেন যে বুনিয়াদি প্রশিক্ষণ ও বিভাগীয় পরীক্ষায় উত্তীর্ণ হওয়া চাকুরীতে স্থায়ী হইবার পূর্ব শর্ত ৷ এই শর্ত সকল ক্যাডার এর প্রার্থীগণের জন্য প্রযোজ্য৷ ৬নং বিধি অনুসারে সাফল্যজনকভাবে শিক্ষানবিশ কাল সমাপ্ত এবং ৭ বিধি অনুসারে বুনিয়াদি প্রশিক্ষণ ও বিভাগীয় পরীক্ষায় উত্তীর্ণ না হইলে কোন প্রার্থীকে চাকুরীতে স্থায়ীকরণ করা যায় না৷ তিনি এই পর্যায়ে ১১-১০-২০০৬ ইং তারিখের প্রজ্ঞাপনটির (এ্যানেকচার-সি) প্রতি আমাদের দৃষ্টি আকর্ষণ পূর্বক নিবেদন করেন যে, যেহেতু ১৯৮১ ইং সনের বিধিমালায় বিভাগীয় পরীক্ষা ও বুনিয়াদি প্রশিক্ষণ স্থায়ীকরণের পূর্বশর্ত এবং উক্ত পূর্ব শর্ত গ্রহণ করিয়াই শিক্ষা ক্যাডারসহ সকল ক্যাডারের প্রার্থীগণ স্ব স্ব চাকুরীতে যোগদান করিয়াছিলেন সেহেতু তর্কিত প্ৰজ্ঞাপন মারফত কতক সংখ্যক প্রার্থীকে বুনিয়াদি প্রশিক্ষণ ও বিভাগীয় পরীক্ষায় অংশগ্রহণ হইতে অব্যাহতি প্রদান করতঃ তর্কিত প্রজ্ঞাপন মারফত বিধিমালা ১৯৮১ তে যে সংশোধনটি আনায়ন করা হইয়াছে তাহা সরকারের ৩০টি ক্যাডারের সকল প্রার্থীদের প্ৰতি, যাহারা ৭ বিধির শর্ত পূরণ করিয়াছেন, তাহাদের প্ৰতি বৈষম্যমূলক এবং সেই কারণে ইহা আইনের চোখে অবৈধ ও বে-আইনী ৷

১০ ৷ অপরপক্ষে জনাব আব্দুর রব চৌধুরী ও জনাব এ,এফ, হাসান আরিফ ব��জ্ঞ এ্যাডাভোকেট মহোদয়গণ তাহাদের এফিডেভিট-ইন-অপজিশান ণ্ডলির প্রতি দৃষ্টি আকর্ষণ পূর্বক নিবেদন করেন যে, ৪-১৭ নং প্ৰতিবাদীগণ এবং তাহাদের ন্যায় আরও বহু সংখ্যক প্রভাষক বিধিমালা ১৯৮১ এর আওতায় সংশ্লিষ্ট পরীক্ষায় সাফলজেনকভাবে উত্তীর্ণ হইয়া বিসিএস (সাধারণ শিক্ষা) ক্যাডারে যোগদান করেন৷ কিন্তু ঐ সময়ে বিধিমালা ১৯৮১, এর ৬ এবং ৭ বিধিতে বর্ণিত শর্তাবলী অনুসারে তখন বুনিয়াদি প্রশিক্ষণ ও বিভাগীয় পরীক্ষা গ্রহণ না করার ৪-১৭ নং প্রতিবাদী এবং তাহার মত আরও ১২০০ এরও অধিক প্রভাষকগণ যথাসময়ে উক্ত বুনিয়াদি প্রশিক্ষণ ও বিভাগীয় পরীক্ষায় অংশ্ গ্রহণের কোন সুযোগ গ্রহণ করিতে পারেন নাই ৷ তাহারা বলেন যে, প্রকৃতপক্ষে ইহা তাহাদের নিজেদের ব্যর্থতা ছিল না কারণ চাকুরীর শর্তানুসারে তাহাদের সংশ্লিষ্ট প্রশিক্ষণ ও বিভাগীয় পরীক্ষায় অংশগ্রহণ করিবার জন্য তাহারা প্রস্তুত ছিলেন কিন্তু সংশ্লিষ্ট কর্তৃপক্ষের অবহেলার কারণে তাহারা বূনিয়াদি প্রশিক্ষণ গ্রহণ করিতে পারেন নাই এবং বিভাগীয় পরীক্ষা অনুষ্ঠিত হয় নাই ৷ কাজেই উক্তরুপ ব্যর্থতার দায়ভার বা দায়িত্ব তাহাদের উপর বর্তাইতে পারে না, বরঞ্চ ইহার জন্য সংশ্লিষ্ট কর্তৃপক্ষই দায়ী ৷ ইহার পর তাহারা বাংলাদেশ সিভিল সার্ভিস (সাধারণ শিক্ষা) শিক্ষানবীশগণের প্রশিক্ষণ ও বিভাগীয় পরীক্ষা বিধিমালা, ১৯৯২ (সংক্ষেপে ‘বিধিমালা ১৯৯২') এর বিধানাবলীর প্রতি দৃষ্টি আকর্ষণ পূর্বক নিবেদন করেন যে, উক্ত বিধিমালা ১২-১-১৯৯২ ইং তারিখে প্রণিত এবং ১৮-২-১৯৯২ ইং তারিখে বাংলাদেশ গেজেট প্ৰজ্ঞাপন আকারে প্রকাশিত হইয়াছে৷ উক্ত বিধিমালার ৩ ও ৪ নং বিধিতে সাফল্যজনকভাবে বুনিয়াদি প্রশিক্ষণ ও বিভাগীয় পরীক্ষা সমাপন সাপেক্ষে চাকুরীতে স্থায়ীকরণের জন্য সুনির্দিষ্ট শর্ত আরোপ করা হইয়াছে ৷ উক্ত বিধিমালার প্রতি আমাদের দৃষ্টি আকর্ষণ পূর্বক বিজ্ঞ এ্যাডভোকেট মহোদয়গণ নিবেদন করেন যে, যদিও ১৯৯২ ইং সনের বিধিমালায় প্রশিক্ষণ ও বিভাগীয় পরীক্ষা চাকুরীতে স্থায়ী করণের জন্য পূর্বশর্ত হিসেবে সুস্পষ্টভাবে সুনির্দিষ্ট করা হয় কিন্তু ৪-১৭ নং প্রতিবাদীগণ ও তাহাদের মত বহু শতাধিক প্রভাষক যেহেতু ১৯৯২ নং সনের পূর্বেই নিয়োগ প্রাপ্ত হইয়াছিলেন সেহেতু ১৯৯২ ইং সনের উক্ত বিধিমালা তাহাদের জন্য প্রযোজ্য হইতে পারে না, কারণ তাহা ছাড়া নিয়োগ ২৯৯২ ইং সনের পূর্বে৷ তাহারা আরও বলেন যে, উক্ত বিধিমালার মাধ্যমে আরোপিত নূতন শর্তাদি ১২-১-১৯৯২ ইং তারিখের পূর্বে নিয়োগ প্রাপ্ত প্রভাষকগণের জন্য অসুবিধাজনকও বটে, এতদবিধ কারণে ২০০৬ইং সনের প্রজ্ঞাপনটি জারীপূর্বক সরকার ১২-১-১৯৯২ ইং তারিখের পূর্বে নিয়োগ প্রাপ্ত প্রভাষকগণকে বুনিয়াদি প্রশিক্ষণ ও বিভাগীয় পরীক্ষায় অংশগ্রহণ হইতে অব্যাহতি প্রদান করিয়া বরঞ্চ ন্যায় বিচারই করিয়াছেন ৷ তাহারা দরখাস্তের প্রতি আমাদের দৃষ্টি আকর্ষণ পূর্বক নিবেদন করেন যে, দরখাস্তকারীগণ সকলেই ১৯৯৬ ও তৎপরবর্তীকালে বিভিন্ন সময়ে নিয়োগ প্রাপ্ত বিধায় স্বীকৃত মতেই তাহা ছাড়া নিয়োগ প্রাপ্তির তারিখ অনুসারে ৪-১৭ নং প্রতিবাদীগণ দরখাস্তকারীগণ হইতে চাকুরীতে জ্যেষ্ঠতা পাইবার যোগ্য বটে ৷ কিন্ত ১৯৯২ ইং সনের বিধিতে আরোপিত নূতন শর্তাদির কারণে যেহেতু তাহারা শিক্ষানবীশকালের মধ্যে তাহাদের বুনিয়াদি প্রশিক্ষণ ও বিভাগীয় পরীক্ষায় অংশগ্রহণ সংশ্লিষ্ট কর্তৃপক্ষের কর্তব্যে শিথিলতার কারণে সম্ভব হয় নাই সেহেতু তাহারা একটি বঞ্চনার স্বীকার হইয়াছেন যাহা সরকার অনুধাবন করতঃ ২০০৬ ইং সনের তর্কিত প্রজ্ঞাপনটি মারফত আইনানুসারে প্রতিকার করিয়াছেন বিধায় অত্র রীট মোকাদ্দমাটির আইনগত কোন সারবত্তাই নাই এবং খারিজ যোগ্য।

১১ ৷ দরখাস্তকারিনীগণ পক্ষে বেগম তানিয়া আমীর বিজ্ঞ এ্যাডভোকেট মহোদয় তাহার জবাবে অত্যন্ত জোরালো ভাষায় নিবেদন করেন যে, দরখাস্তকারীগণ প্রতিবাদীগণের ন্যায় সকলেই বিভিন্ন কলেজে শিক্ষক হিসেবে কর্মরত রহিয়াছেন ৷ তাহাদের মত আরও অনেকে বুনিয়াদি প্রশিক্ষণ ও বিভাগীয় পরীক্ষায় অংশ্যাহণ করিয়া চাকুরীতে স্থায়ী হইয়াছেন । তিনি ৪-১৭ প্রতিবাদীগণের যুক্তি খণ্ডন পূর্বক নিবেদন করেন যে, এই বুনিয়াদি প্রশিক্ষণ ১৯৯২ ইং সনের বিধিমালার মাধ্যমে আনয়ন করা হয় নাই বরঞ্চ বিসিএস নিয়োগ বিধিমালা ১৯৮১ এর বিধান অনুসারে ১৯৮১ ইং সন হইতেই উক্তরূপ ৰুনিয়াদি প্রশিক্ষণ ও বিভাগীয় পরীক্ষায় সাফল্য মণ্ডিত হইয়াছে সাপেক্ষে চাকুরীতে স্থায়ী হইবার বিধান রহিয়াছে । বিধিমালা ১৯৮১ এর ৬ ও ৭ বিধির প্ৰতি আমাদের দৃষ্টি আকর্ষণ পূর্বক তিনি নিবেদন করেন যে, যেহেতু এর ৪-১৭ নং প্ৰতিবাদীগনের নিয়োগ প্রাপ্তির পূর্বহইতেই মূল ১৯৮১ বিধি অনুসারে চাকুরীর শিক্ষানবীশ এবং চাকুরীতে স্থায়ীকরণ সম্পর্কিত শর্তাবলী যথা বূনিয়াদি প্রশিক্ষণ এবং বিভাগীয় পরীক্ষায়" অংশ্যাহণের শর্ত সুনিল্টিভাবে নির্ধারিত রহিয়াছে সেই কারণেই ১৯৯২ ইং সনের বিধিমালার অযুহাতে তর্কিত প্রজ্ঞাপনটির মাধ্যমে তাহা অব্যাহতি পাইতে পারেন না। তিনি আরও বলেন যে ৭(২) বিধিতে পরিষ্কারভাবে বর্ণনা করা হইঁয়াছে যে কোন কারণে নিয়োগপ্রাপ্ত কোন প্রার্থী যদি সাফল্যজনকভড়াবে বুনিয়াদি প্রশিক্ষণ সমাপ্ত ও বিভাগীয় পরীক্ষায় উত্তীর্ণ না হইতে পারিলে তাহাকে চাকুরীতে স্থায়ী করা যাইবে না ৷ তিনি ২ নং উপবিধি হইতে আরও নিবেদন করেন যে, যেহেতু ১৯৮১ বিধিতে বুনিয়াদি প্রশিক্ষণ ও বিভাগীয় পরীক্ষায় অংশ্যাহণ এবং উত্তীর্ণ হওয়া চাকুরীতে স্থায়ী হইবার পূর্ব শর্ত হিসেবে সুস্পষ্ট ও সুনির্দিষ্টভাবে উল্লেখ করা হইয়াছে সেহেতু উক্ত বাধ্যবাধকতা (mandatory requirement) হইতে অব্যাহতি প্রদান করিবার কারণেই সুযোগ নাই । এই প্রসঙ্গে তিনি প্রতিবাদী পক্ষে এ্যাডভোকেট মহোদয়গণের যুক্তি খণ্ডন পূর্বক নিবেদন করেন যে, ১৯৯২ ইং সনের পূর্বে কোন প্রভাষক পরীক্ষায় অবতীর্ণ হইতে পারেন নইি এই যুক্তি সঠিক নহে। তিনি এ্যানেকচার-এস এর প্রতি দৃষ্টি আকর্ষণ পূর্বক নিবেদন করেন যে, ১৩ জন শিক্ষক ১৯৯০ ইং সনে সাফল্যজনকভাবে উত্তীর্ণ হইয়াছিলেন যাহা হইতে প্রতীয়মান হয় যে ১৯৯২ইং সনের বিধিমালা কার্যকর হইবার পূর্বেও বিভাগীয় পরীক্ষা গ্রহণ করা হইত এবং মূল ১৯৮১ বিধিমালার আওতায় অনুষ্ঠিত বিসিএস ক্যাডার এর অন্তর্ভুক্ত সকল প্রার্থী নিয়মিত বিভাগীয় পরীক্ষায় অংশ্যাহণ করিতে তাহার সুনির্দিষ্ট সক্ষো এ্যানেকচার বহন করে ৷ এমতাবস্থায় প্রতিবাদীগণের বিজ্ঞ এ্যাডভোকেট মহোদয়ের বক্তব্য যে ১৯৯২ ইং সনের পূর্বে বুনিয়াদি প্রশিক্ষণ ও বিভাগীয় পরীক্ষা গ্রহণ করা হয় নাই এইরূপ যুক্তি গ্রহণঘেগ্যে নয় বলিয়া তিনি নিবেদন করেন । তিনি আরও বলেন যে, মূল বিসিএস নিয়োগ বিধিমালা ১৯৮১, মারফত বিসিএস শিক্ষা ক্যাডারসহ সকল ক্যাডারের নিয়োগ, শিক্ষানবিশ ও বিভাগীয় পরীক্ষার কার্যক্রম পরিচালিত হইয়া আসিতেছিল কিন্তু ১৯৯২ইং সনের বিধির অযুহাতে বৃনিয়াদি প্রশিক্ষণ ও বিভাগীয় পরীক্ষায় অংশগ্রহণ সম্পর্কিত ১৯৮১ ইং সনের স্বয়ং সম্পূর্ণ মূল বিধিমালা তর্কিত প্ৰজ্ঞাপনেরমারফত অকার্যকর করা অবৈধ ও বে-আইনী। এই প্রসঙ্গে তিনি তাহার ১-১০-২০০ ইং তারিখে হলফকৃত সম্পূরক এফিডেভিট-ইন অপজিশন এর সহিত সংযুক্ত সংস্থাপন মন্ত্রণালয়ের ৩১-১২-১৯৮৭ইং তারিখের প্রজ্ঞাপনের (এ্যানেকচার-ডি) প্ৰতি "দৃষ্টি আকর্ষণ পূর্বক নিবেদন করেন যে, যেহেতু বাংলাদেশ সিভিল সার্ভিস (সাধারণ শিক্ষা) ক্যডারের প্রভাষক পদে নিয়োগকালে আরোপিত ক, খ, গ ও-ঘ শর্তাবলী ১৯৮১ ইং সনের ৭ বিধিতে প্রদত্ত শর্তাবলী নিয়োগ প্রজ্ঞাপনের মধেইি বর্ণিত রহিয়াছে সেহেতু বিসিএস সাধারণ শিক্ষা ক্যাডার এর সকলের প্রতি উপরোক্ত শর্তাবলী আরোপিত হইবে ।

১২ ৷ প্রতিবাদীপক্ষ জনাব এ, এফ, হাসান আরিফ, এ্যাডভোকেট এ্যানেকচার-এস ও ডব্লিউ-১ এ্যানেকচারে বর্ণিত ১৩ জন শিক্ষক সম্বন্ধে বলেন যে, তাহারা শিক্ষা অধিদপ্তরের কর্মকর্তা এবং প্রকৃতপক্ষে সংশ্লিষ্ট সময়ে তড়াহারা শিক্ষকতার সহিত জড়িত ছিলেন না, তাহারা অধিদপ্তরের কর্মকর্তা ছিলেন ৷ তাহা ছাড়া উক্ত প্রজ্ঞাপন অন্য শিক্ষকদের ক্ষেত্রে প্রযোজ্য ছিল না, কাজেই প্রাক ১৯৯২ ইং সনে আরোপিত শর্ত বর্হিভূতভাবে বুনিয়াদি প্রশিক্ষণ ও বিভাগীয় পরীক্ষায় অংশগ্রহণের সুযোগ ১৯৯২ ইং তারিখের পূর্বে কখনই ছিল না ৷

১৩। অদ্য রায় প্রদানের পূর্বে জনাব আব্দুর রব চৌধুরী, এ্যাডভোকেট ৬-১৭ নং প্ৰতিৰাদী পক্ষে ২-১০-২০০৭ ইং তারিখে হলফকৃত আর ও একটি এফিডেভিট দাখিল করিয়াছেন ৷ বিজ্ঞ এ্যাডভোকেট মহোদয় উক্ত এফিডেভিট এর প্ৰতি দৃষ্টি আর্কষণ পূর্বক দরখাস্তকান্নীগণ পক্ষে ১-১০-২০০৭ ইং তারিখে হলফকৃত এফিডেভিট প্রদত্ত বিভিন্ন বর্ণনাকে অস্বীকার করতঃ নিবেদন করেন যে সকল প্রতিবাদীর চাকুরীর বয়স ১৪ বৎসরের ঊর্ধ্বে বিধায় বাংলাদেশ সিভিল সার্ভিস (পদোন্নতির জন্য পরীক্ষা) বিধিমালা, ১৯৮৬ এর ৫(৩) বিধির কারণে তাহারা পদোন্নভির জন্য কোন পরীক্ষায় অংশ গ্রহণ করিতে পারিবেন না । তিনি আরও বলেন যে, ১৯৯২ ইং সনের বিধিতে শিক্ষানবিশকালের মধ্যে পরীক্ষায় অংশ গ্রহণের বিধান রাখার প্রতিবাদীগণের ন্যায় যাহারা বহুপূর্বে শিক্ষানকিণীকাল সম্পন্ন করিয়াছেন তাহারাও বিভাগীয় পরীক্ষায় আর অংশ গ্রহণ করিতে পারিবেন না বিধায় তর্কিত প্ৰজ্ঞাপন মারফত আইন সঙ্গতভাবেই সংশ্লিষ্ট প্রভাষকগণকে বুনিয়াদি প্রশিক্ষণ ও বিভাগীয় পরীক্ষা হইতে অব্যাহতি প্রদান সরকারের এখতিয়ারভূক্ত।

১8 ৷ উভয়পক্ষের বিজ্ঞ এ্যাডভোকেট মহোদয়গণের বক্তব্য শ্রবণ, দরখাস্ত, এফিডেভিট ইন অপজিশান ও সম্পূরক এফিডেভিট এবং তদসংযুক্ত কাগজাদি পরীক্ষা নিরীক্ষা করা হইল।

১৫ । ১৯৭৫ ইং সনে বাংলাদেশের সংবিধানের ১৩৬ অনুচ্ছেদে এবং ৪র্থ তফসিলের ১০ম দফায় বর্ণিত ক্ষমতা বলে The Service (Re-Organisation and Conditions) Act, 1975 (Act No. XXXII of 1975) প্রণীত হয়। উক্ত আইনের 8র্থ ধারায় বাংলাদেশ সরকারের বিভিন্ন সার্ভিস সমূহে সমতা আনয়ন করণের জন্য বিভিন্ন সার্ভিসকে reorganise করিবার লক্ষ্যে creation of new services অথবা amalgamation অথবা unification of existing service সম্বন্ধীয় বিষয়াদিতে সরকারকে ক্ষমতা প্রদান করা হয় ৷ উক্ত আইনের ৫ম ধারায় বিভিন্ন সার্ভিসের গ্রেড ও পে-স্কেল এবং চাকুরীর শর্তাবলী নির্ধারণ করিবার ক্ষমতা প্রদান করা হয় ৷ ৭ম ধারায় সরকারকে চাকুরীর যেকোন শর্ত পরিবর্তন পরিবর্ধন ও রহিত করণের ক্ষমতা প্রদান করা হয় । বিভিন্ন সার্ভিসের এইরূপ আইনগত অবস্থানকালে বাংলাদেশ সরকারের সংস্থাপন মন্ত্রণালয় কর্তৃক ইহার ১-৯-১৯৮০ ইং তারিখে প্রকাশিত Bangladesh Civil Service (Reorganization) Order, 1980, জারী করা হয়। উক্ত আদেশনামা উপরে বর্ণিত আইনের আওতায় ৪ ধারা অনুসারে জারী করা হয় ৷ উক্ত আদেশের বিধানানূসারে তদানীন্তন সময়ে বাংলাদেশ সিভিল সার্ভিস ১৪টি ক্যাডার সার্ভিসে বিভক্ত করতঃ পুনর্গঠন করা (Re-organisation) হয় । তৎপর বাৎলাদেশের রাষ্ট্রপতি সংবিধানের ১৩৩ অনুচ্ছেদে প্রদত্ত ক্ষমতাবলে ১-১-১৯৮১ ইং তারিখে BCS Recruitment Rules, 1981 প্রবর্তন করেন । উক্ত বিধিমালা বিসিএস (সাধারণ শিক্ষা) সহ বাংলাদেশে বিদ্যমান সকল সার্ভিস ক্যাডার জন্য প্রযোজ্য ছিল ৷ একই ধারাবাহিকতায় পরবর্তীতে ৩১-৮-১৯৮৬ ইং তারিখে উপরোক্ত আদেশটি সংশোধন করতঃ বাংলাদেশ সিভিল সার্ভিসগুলিকে ৩০টি ক্যাডারে পূনর্গঠন/পূনর্বিন্যাস করা হয়।

১৬ I BCS (General Education) কেও উক্ত মূল বিধিমালার আওতাভুক্ত করা হয়। এই মূল বিধিমালার ৩য় বিধিতে নিয়োগ পদ্ধতি, ৬ষ্ঠ বিধিতে শিক্ষানবীশকাল, ৭ম বিধিতে চাকুরী স্থায়ীকরণের বিধান বর্ণনা করা হইয়াছে ৷ ৮ম বিধিতে শর্তাবলী শিথিলকরণের ব্যবস্থাও রাখা হইয়াছে ৷ উক্ত বিধিমালায় শিক্ষানবীশ সম্বন্ধে ৬ বিধি নিম্নরূপঃ

6. Probation

Probation:--(I) A person initially appointed to a Service against a substantive vacancy shall remain on probation for-

(a) a period of two years if he is appointed by direct recruitment, and (b) a period of one year if he is appointed on promotion:

Provided that the period of probation may be extended by the Government for a further period not exceeding two years;

১৭ ৷ শিক্ষানিবিশকলে সমাপনান্তে চাকুরীতে স্থায়ীকরণ সম্বন্ধে ৭ বিধিতে বর্ণনা করা হইয়াছে ৷ ৭ বিধি নিম্নরূপঃ

7. Confirmation:

Confirmation-(1)-[A person] initially appointed to a Service shall be required to undergo-

(a) foundational training for a period not less than four months at the Public Administration Training Centre, or at any other institute and in such subjects or fields as may be determined, from time to time, by the Government:

Provided that the Government may, by order, increase or decrease the period of foundational training under special, circumstances:

Provided further that an officer who has attained the age of 45 years on or before 1-1-1988 shall not be required to undergo foundational training; and

(b) After the completion of, the aforesaid foundational training, such professional and Specialized training as may be determined by the Government, to be imparted by the respective Institution for a Service.

(2) No person shall be confirmed in the concerned Service unless he has successfully completed the training under Sub-rule (1), has passed such departmental examination as may be prescribed by order by the Government and has served the period of probation under rule 6 and unless his conduct and work have been found satisfactory.

(3) Omitted. 8

(4) A person shall be confirmed in the Service, after all the conditions have been fulfilled, from the date of his appointment in the Service.

১৮ । সরকারি চাকুরীর যে কোন ক্যাডারে প্রাথমিক নিয়োগ প্রাপ্ত ব্যক্তিকে চাকুরীতে স্থায়ী হইতে হইলে সাফল্যজনক ভাবে শিক্ষানবিশকাল সমাপ্ত করিতে হয় । উহা সরকারি চাকুরীর একটি সুনির্দিষ্ট শর্ত । তাহাছাড়া, প্রয়োজনীয় বূনিয়াদি প্রশিক্ষণ এবং পেশা ভিত্তিক ও বিশেষ প্রশিক্ষণে অংশ গ্রহণ করিতে হইবে। তাহাছাড়া, সরকার কর্তৃক নির্ধারিত বিভাগীয় পরীক্ষায় উত্তীর্ণ হইতে হইবে৷
