full_judgment:
Sharif Uddin Chaklader J: This appeal by the plaintiffs directed against judgment and decree dated 1-2-2012 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Gazipur dismissing Title Suit No. 23 of 2008.

2. Plaintiffs instituted the aforesaid suit praying amongst other for the following reliefs:—

“(ক) বাদীপক্ষগন নালিশী খ তফসিলের সম্পত্তি রায়তি স্বত্ত্ব এবং বিকল্প বিরুদ্ধ দখলমূল মালিক মর্ম বিবাদীগন বিরুদ্ধ ঘোষনামূলক ডিক্রী দিত।”

3. The case of plaintiffs is that, suit land originally belongs to Bhawal Raj. The suit land of schedule 'Ka' comprising of an area of 23.13 acres of land recorded in CS khatian No. 7 along with other lands in the name of Kumar Rabindra Narayan Chowdhury settled the suit land in raiyati right. On the death of Kumar Rabindra Narayan Roy Chowdhury, his heirs as of tenanted right was owner in possession of the entire land of Kumar Rabindra Narayan Roy Chowdhury. As per Court of Wards Act 1879, the management and administration of the property including "Ka" schedule land of CS khatian No.  7 was taken over by the Court of Wards. During the last CS record, it was recorded in the name of Court of Wards, for Kumar Rabindra Narayan Roy Chowdhury and others, which was subsequently named as Bhawal Raj Courts of Wards Estate or Bhawal Court of Wards Estate or Court of Wards Bhawal Raj Estate. Bhawal Court of Wards Estate as owner and possessor of `Ka' schedule land with other lands of CS khatian No.  7, settled 'Ka' schedule land with the father and husband of the plaintiff. Bashoruddin and co-sharer, Chand Mia through its own printed pattannama. Basiruddin and Chand Mia became owner and possessor in equal share. While Basiruddin and Chand Mia on the basis of pattannama and dakhila and by paying zamindari taxes to Bhawal Court of Wards Estate, the Government, then province of East Pakistan by giving effect of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act acquired the rent receiving interest of the Zaminder and on taking nominal taxes as land development tax, the tenants were classified as owner of their respective land as per sections 3 and 42 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. After acquisition of the rent receiving interest as aforesaid, Government published final gazette as per provision of section 3 of the aforesaid Act on 24-3-1952. After acquisition of the land as aforesaid, Compensation Assessment Roll were prepared and Zaminder as per the aforesaid compensation assessment roll received compensation and gazette was published on 29-5-1956 as per section 42 of the aforesaid Act by which the Zamindari of Kumar Rabindra Narayan Roy Chowdhury of `Ka' schedule land, was acquired and the status of tenant. Basiruddin and Chand Mia were changed and become owners. Accordingly SA khatian was finally published in their names. By opening jote in the revenue office and by paying nominal land development tax possessing the suit land SA khatian No.  63 was finally published in the name of Basiruddin and Chand Mia in equal 8 annas share. Basiruddin and Chand Mia upon an amicable settlement partitioned the kha schedule land by which 'Ka' schedule land fallen in the saham of Basiruddin. After acquisition of the land by the Government, 5.40 acres of land remain in the hand of Basiruddin alone which has been mentioned in 'Kha' schedule. Chand Mia got 'Ga' schedule land which comprising of 0.39 acres of land of dag No. 155/1061, 0.51 acres of land of dag No. 1059, 1.42 acres of land of dag No. 1063, 1.18 acres of land of dag No. 1058, 0.60 acres of land of dag No. 1060, in total, 4.10 acres of land and remaining land, in total 13.36 acres including 12.5 as mentioned in 'Gha' schedule was in ejmlali and co-sharers as owners owned and possessed by cultivation. While the aforesaid land was in possession of co-sharers, 1.48 acres of land was acquired by the Government out of 13.63 acres of land for road and remaining land i.e. 12.15 acres of land, "Gha' schedule, was in ejmali of the co-sharers. While co-sharers as aforesaid was in possession having title there to, Government acquired portion of land for defendant No. 16, the Ministry of Agriculture, defendant No. 17, Rice Research Institution from the land of Chand Mia to the very knowledge of defendant No.  1 and 14 in LA Case No.  100/65-66, recognizing Chand Mia as the owner of the aforesaid land. Compensation was received by Chand Mia while in possession, 12.15 acres of land described in schedule `Gha', constructed homestead, planted trees and cultivated agricultural lands in ejmali, died leaving, defendant No.  6 as heir who along with other co-sharers possessing the land in ejmali. While defendant No. 6, plaintiff and Chand Mia was in possession of the ejmali property of 'Gha' schedule comprising 12.15 acres, Government in LA case No.  5/85-86 acquired 10 acres of land for defendant No.  19, Gazipur District Police Line under defendant No.  18, Ministry of Home Affairs. In LA Case No.  3/2001-2002 Government acquired 0.33 acres of land for defendant No.  26, District Fisheries Officer under defendant No.  25, Ministry of Fisheries and Veterinaries under Government of Bangladesh, in LA Case No.  7/90-91 acquired 0.09 acres of land for defendant No. 20, District Jail, Gazipur under defendant No.  18, Ministry of Home Affairs, in LA Case No.  3/95-96 acquired 0.33 acres of land for Defendant No.  District primary Education office under defendant No. 21 Ministry of Education, Government of Bangladesh, in LA Case No.  5/90-91 acquired .50 acres of land for defendant No.  24, Public Health Engineering Department under defendant No.  23, Ministry of Health, Government of Bangladesh. Government disbursed compensation money part of the afore-said 5 LA cases to the plaintiffs and to the co-sharers having found they are legal title holder. Some greedy person of the locality created obstruction in getting compensation money and gave proposal to defendant No. 6, son of defendant No. 9 and brother of defendant Nos.  1 and 8, but recognized their title over 'Kha' schedule land when they would manage in getting the compensation money to the plaintiffs. Later on, Chand Mia died leaving defendant Nos.  2-5 as heirs. Plaintiffs, the heirs of Chand Mia, defendant Nos. 2-5 are waiting for getting compensation money. Suddenly, on 12-12-2007 the manager of defendant No. 14 and the officer of Bhawal Court of Wards came to 'Kha' schedule land whereupon plaintiff could know that defendant No. 1 of the instant suit along with defendant No. 1 of Title Suit No.  1219 of 1985 filed in the court of Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Gazipur against defendant Nos. 3-6, in total against 11 persons as defendants and they got decree. Defendant No. 1 of the instant suit got decree up to the Appellate Division of the Hon'ble Supreme Court. In RS record 18.70 acres of land of 'Kha' schedule recorded in the name of defendant No. 1 and they requested plaintiffs to give up possession of the suit land. Defendant No.  1 of the instant suit threatened plaintiff that if they did not give up possession to the defendant No.  14 amicably then they by force evicted the plaintiffs from the suit land. Plaintiffs went to defendant No.  14 to know about the decree, then, the manager of defendant No.  14, Abdur Rouf, gave a paper book to plaintiff No.  1 and requested plaintiff No.  1 to go through paper book to find out how the suit was decreed. Plaintiffs after getting paper book asked defendant Nos.  6 and 3 as to how they got decree in the suit to which they kept silence. Defendant No. 1 with connivance with defendant Nos.  6-13 got the decree surreptitiously.

4. It is further case of plaintiffs that defendant No. 1 was never owner and possessor of the suit land from defendant No.  14 in any manner either as tenant or as Raiyat. 29. It is the case of plaintiff that when the land recorded as projabili, Zaminders looses control over this land and tenant become land lord or owner of the land and is protected by law. This dispute as we see reflected in some of the decisions of India and also of our country. In the decision of Sushil Kumar vs. Rajendra Lal, reported in AIR 1954 Calcutta, 413, where it is held that:—

The only point which requires consideration in this appeal is whether the tenancy created in favour of the defendant by Jatindra Nath Bose in the year 1936 is a protected interest under section160(g), Bengal Tenancy Act. This section was enacted to protect a right created with the express permission in writing of the landlord at whose instance the tenure or holding was sold. In order that a lease granted by a defaulting tenant may be a protected interest under this clause, the power to grant it must have been given "expressly and in writing" by his lessor. We have accordingly to consider whether Jatindra Nath Bose was "expressly and in writing" given the power to grant the lease of the description which has been granted in favour of the defendant. The kabuliat executed by the predecessor of Jatindra Nath Bose is Exhibit "A". The relevant recital of this kabuliat is as follows:

"Jamite pushkaradi Khanan o imarat o bagbagicha or ghar chhappar tayyar o nijakarkite kumba projabili kariya pattai hakuke danbikrayadir sattadhikari hayiya putra poutradi warisan krame upasattadhi bhog tapab-shat karite thakibe."

30. It means that the leassee will be entitled to enjoy the usufruct of the land through his sons and grandsons and successors in interest by digging tanks, constructing buildings and raising structures and by exercising rights of gift, sale etc., and by cultivating the land in khas or by establishing tenants. We are informed that the expression "Nijakarkite" 1 which occurs in this kabuliat means khas cultivation, that is, cultivation, by one's own labour. The expression "Projabili" (establishing tenants) has been judicially interpreted by reference to section 160 (g) in some of the decisions of this Court. In the case of Akhil Chandra Mandal vs Ssurendra Nath Dutt, 11 Cal LI 87 (A), the head lease authorized the lessee to raise embankments, bridges, damkhals, cut jungles and "establish tenants according to your desire, construct houses .... And do other acts". Acting under this authority, the leassee created an 'istemrari maurasi mokarari makadami' tenure which is a kind of subordinate tenure and not a raiyati holding. Mr Justice Sarada Charan Mitra who was affirmed on Letters Patent Appeal held:

"The words 'established tenants' do not necessarily indicate that the lessor gave the lessee express authority to create tenancies of the kind set up by the plaintiffs in this case. They are words commonly used in leases to indicate that the tenure created entitled the tenure holder either to cultivate the land himself or cause cultivation by means of tenants."

31. It was accordingly held that the sub-lease was not a protected interest under section 160(g), Bengal Tenancy Act. In our opinion what was decided by Mitra, J in this case was that under the head lease right was conferred upon the lessee to bring in only the cultivating raiyats and as the lessee created a permanent tenure, his act was not an exercise of the power expressly and in writing given to him.

32. The expression "Projabili" as used in this kabuliat was held to include the grant of permanent tenure. With great respect to Mr justice Das, We must observe that he was not quite correct in distinguishing the case of Afazuddi (B) (39 Cal 138) on the ground that what was held to be a protected interest in that case was a non-occupancy right. The facts of that case will show that one Prasanna Kumar Mitra created a permanent tenure in favour of Bhojendra Kumar Sen who in his turn granted a permanent tenure in favour of Bahojendra Kumar Sen who in his turn granted a permanent lease to one Ganesh Chandra Chatterjee and Ganesh Chandra Chatterjee created a raiyati lease in favour of the plaintiff. The tenancy of Bhojendra was sold in execution of a decree for arrears of rent and the purchaser at the rent sale sought to annul the interest of Ganesh and also of the plaintiff. Jenkins CJ and D Chatterjee J held that the interest of Ganesh was protected and therefore the interest of the plaintiff could not be touched.

33. It was clearly held in this case that the permanent tenure in favour of Ganesh was included in the expression "Projabili" which occurred in the head lease and therefore the interest of Ganesh was protected under cl. (g) of section 160, Bengal Tenancy Act, Unfortunately the earlier decision in the case of - "11 Cal LJ 87 (A), was brought to the notice of the learned Judges in 'Afazuddi's case, (B)' with the result that the expression " Projabili" was held to include the creation of a tenure in the latter case, while the decision in the former case was to the contrary. In the case before us, however, the recital in the head lease (Exhibit A) is somewhat different from the recitals in the leases in the two cases discussed above. In this case the expression "projabili" is placed in juxtaposition to the word "Nijakarkite" (cultivation by the lessee himself) and is an alternative to khas cultivation. From these facts it is reasonable to conclude that the expression "Projabili" in Exhibit 'A' means settlement with cultivating raiyats only.

34. The expression "Projabili" as used in this pathname is held to include the grant of a permanent tenure.

35. Facts of this suit involve the implication of President order No.  90 of 1972. We quote here the relevant portion of President Order No.  90 of 1972 which runs as follows:—

"Prajabili is alternative to khas cultivation, means settlement with cultivating settlement with cultivating laws raiyats. Under the Revenue laws the person is given a right to hold land for agricultural purpose and cultivation by himself and by his heirs or by his servants. When in a case the expression 'prajabili' is placed in juxta-position of the word 'Nejakarkile' cultivation by the lessee himself and is an alternative to khas cultivation, it is reasonable to conclude that the expression 'prajabili' means settlement with cultivating raiyats only.

36. In the case of the expression "projabili" is placed in juxtaposition to the word "Nljakarkite" (cultivation by the lessee himself) and is an alternative to khas cultivation. From these facts it is reasonable to conclude that the expression 'Projabili" means settlement with cultivating raiyats only.

37. In the case of Promode Ranjan Saha vs Govt. of Bangladesh. 33 DLR (AD) 53 it is held:

"There can be no denying the fact that the plaintiffs sought to challenge the acquisition of their Hats and Bazars made under the general notification dated 2-4-56 issued under section 3(1) of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, and so it is directly hit by President's Order No.  90 of 1972, which gives a clear mandate of law that notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, on the commencement of this Order, all suits , appeals, applications and other legal proceedings pending or continuing or deemed to be pending or continuing in any Court against the Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh in which the legality of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (EB Act No.  XXVIII of 1951) of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy (Amendment) Ordinance 1956 (EB Ordinance No.  III of 1956) or of any other law making any amendment in the said Act or of the acquisition of any property made under any provision thereof is challenged or called in question shall abate, and all orders, including orders of injunction and other interlocutory orders passed in such suits, appeals, applications and other legal proceeding shall cease to have any effect: and no Court shall entertain and no person shall bring any fresh suit, appeal, application or other legal proceedings in which the legality or validity of any such law or acquisition is challenged or called in question.

38. We had occasion, in Civil Appeal No.  46 of 1979. People's Republic of Bangladesh vs Sri Sri Madan Gopal Jew Bigraha wherein the acquisition of debtors estate by general notification dated 2-4-56 under section 3(1) of East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act was challenged, to hold on a reference to President's Order No.  90 of 1972, that the directive in law is clear, that, on coming into operation of this Order, notwithstanding earlier view of the law on the subject, a pending proceeding seeking to challenge or call in question the acquisition of any property under any of the provisions of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act shall abate and no proceedings shall be in stated in any Court.

39. In the case of Bangladesh vs Chowdhury Tanvir Ahmed Siddiky 2 MLR (AD) 156 = 2 BLC (AD) 129 it is held "The moot question that aries therefore is whether the learned Judge of the High Court Division was justified in not affirming the order of abatement of the whole suit passed by the trial court under Article 4(2) of President's Order No.  69 of 1972 and Article 2 of President's Order No.  90 of 1972.

40. From a mere reading of the provisions of the two President's Orders quoted earlier it is clear that President's Order No.  69 of 1972 envisages abatement of all kinds of suits or other legal proceedings against the Government of Bangladesh whether or not related to acquisition under the Act when the Government opts not to be a party thereto, while President's Order No.  90 of 1972 seeks abatement only of suits and other legal proceedings in which the legality or validity of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (EB Act No.  XXVIII of 1951), or of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act (Amendment) Ordinance, 1956 (EB Ordinance No.  III of 1956), or of any other law making any amendment in the said Act, or of the acquisition of any property made under any provision thereof is challenged or called in question. President's Order No.  69 of 1972 covers a much bigger field than President's Order No.  90 of 1972. President's Order No.  69 of 1972 is so to say the genus of which President's Order No.  90 of 1972 is specie. Article 2 of President's Order No.  90 of 1972 begins with the phrase "notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force". Such a non-obstante clause, it is true, has the effect of abrogating the provisions of prior statute in the event of a conflict between the same and the new statute. But such a non-obstante clause cannot reasonably be read as overriding anything contained in any relevant existing law which is not inconsistent with the new statute. We are unable to see any inconsistency or mutual exclusiveness between the two President's Orders both of which aim at abatement of a suit. As logical sequel the provisions of President's Order No.  69 of 1972 cannot be said to have been abrogated because of the non-obstante clause added to President's Order No.  90 of 1972.

41. One might notice that, although redundant, the Government of Bangladesh made an application for abatement of the suit even under President's Order No.  90 of 1972. Therefore, we have to look into the facts disclosed in the plaint and the prayers made there in to see whether the plaint was hit by the President's Order No.  90 of 1972. The learned Judge of the High Court Division opined that paragraphs 14-16 of the plaint and prayer No.  (ii) thereof came within the mischief of President's Order No.  90 of 1972 and not the rest of the allegations and the prayer. We think that not only the allegations in paragraph 14-16 and prayer No. (ii) had abated but also the suit itself had abated as a whole, being hit by Article 2 of President's Order No.  90 of 1972. The averments in the plaint and the prayers made therein amount to a challenge of the acquisition of the wakf estates concerned, apart from a challenge of EB Ordinance No.  III of 1956 as noticed by the learned Judge of the High Court Division. In the People's Republic of Bangladesh vs Sri Sri Madan Gopal Jew Bigraho, 33 DLR (AD) 13 this Court had the occasion to consider the question of abatement of a suit under President's Order No.  90 of 1972 in a similar case. The prayers in the case were couched in more or less identical terms as in the present case. The plaint of that suit was found to have been hit by President's Order No.  90 of 1972."

ডি, ডব্লিউ-১, মোঃ ছাব্বিৱ হোসেন বর্ননা করেন যে, নালিশী সম্পত্তির এস,এস, রেকর্ড দাখিল করতে পারিনি ছেড়া থাকায় সেই মর্মে প্রতিবেদন মুল কপি দাখিল আছে যা প্রদঃ-খ চিহ্নিত হল ৷ এস,এ ও আর, এস, খতিয়ানের সার্টিফইিড কপি প্রদঃ-ক (সিরিজ) হোল নালিশী সম্পত্তির মূল মালিক কুমার রবীন্দ্র নারায়ন রায় চৌধুরী গং পক্ষে কোর্ট অব ওয়ার্ডস ভাওয়াল কোর্ট অব ওয়ার্ডস এর কার্যক্রম শুরু হয় ১৯১১ সালে নালিশী সম্পত্তি দেবাত্তর সম্পত্তি যা মানিক্য মাধবের শ্রী শ্রী এর জন্য উৎসর্গকৃত ইহা ম্যানেজার ৰর্গা দেন । আর, এস, ৩০৬ নং খতিয়ান শ্রী শ্রী মানিক্য মাধবের নাম রেকর্ড হয় ৷

আমরা বর্গা দেই চান মিয়া গংকে তারা বর্গা ফসল না দেওয়ার আমরা ১৯৮/৭১ নং মোকদ্দমা ও ২২৬/৭১ নং মোকদ্দমা করা হয় I যা ভাওয়াল কোর্ট অব ষ্টেট পক্ষ রায় ও ডিক্রী হয় I ঐ মামলা অনুযায়ী দখলে যাই । পরে চান মিয়া পং ৩/৭৩ নং বন্টন ও স্বত্ব ঘোষনা মামলা করলে খারিজ হয় ৷

৩-৩-০৮ ইং এ তারিখ আমরা অবৈধ দখলদারদের উচ্ছেদে নির্বাহী ম্যাজ্যিষ্ট্রট প্রথম শ্রেণী অংশ গ্রহন করে । উচ্ছেদ মোকদ্দমা নং ৩/০৬ যা জেলা প্রশাশক গাজীপুর, আমাদের দরখাস্তের প্রেক্ষিতে রুজু কর ৷ ১১.৪৫ মিনিট ৩-৩-০৮ ইং তারিখ আমাকে বুঝিয়ে দেন ম্যাজিষ্টেট মল্লিকা খাতুন দখল নামায স্বাক্ষী আছে। পুলিশ সহ অনেক ৷ ১৩ কোটি টাকার সম্পত্তি উদ্ধার হয় ৷

পুলিশ, মৎস্য কৃষি, জেলা থানা পশু সম্পদ ও স্থানীয় সরকারের বরাবর হুকুম দখলের টাকা ভাওয়াল স্টেট ভুলে নেয় ৷ টাকা তুলে নেওয়ার এল, এ, কেসের এওয়ার্ডর ফটোকপি দাখিল করিয়া গ সিরিজের অন্তর্ভুক্ত হলো ।

দেঃ ১২১৯/৮৫ নং মোকদ্দমা ভাওয়াল কোট অব ওয়ার্ডস বাদী হইয়া মামলা করে আমি জানি। সেই মামলায় আমি সরকারকে পক্ষ করিনি । কারন সরকারকে পক্ষ করার দরকার নই ৷ আমি যে সংস্থা গুলির নাম বলি আমার জবান বন্দিতে সেগুলির কথা উক্ত মামলায় বলি কিনা আমার জানা নই ৷ নালিশী সম্পত্তি থেকে বিভিন্ন দাগের জমি সরকার বিভিন্ন সংস্থার নাম অধিগ্নহন করে এবং বিল গ্রহন করি আমরা ৷ কতটা বিল পাই কোন সংস্থা হতে তা খেয়াল নই এবং এই সংস্থাগুলি বিদ্যমান আছে এগুলির উপর আমাদের কোন দাবী নেই ৷ ৬টি সংস্থা আছে ৷ আমরা ডিক্রী নিয়েছি তার জন্য ডিক্রীজারী মামলা করব না ৷

আমি ১নং বিবাদী শ্রী শ্রী মাধব বিগ্রহের কেউ নই ৷ আমি ভাওয়াল রাজ স্টেটের ম্যানেজার ৷ নালিশী সম্পত্তির প্রকৃত মালিক কুমার রবীন্দ্র নারায়ান রায় চৌধুরীর পদ ভাওয়াল কোর্ট অব ওয়ার্ডস ৷ শ্রী শ্রী মাধব বিগ্রহ মালিক নন নালিশী সম্পত্তির ৷ এই বিগ্রহের বাস্তব অস্তিত্ব আছে ৷ উহা কের্টি অব ওয়ার্ডস কর্তৃক পরিচালিত হয় ৷ বিগ্রহ মাধব বাড়ীতে আছে ৷ বিগ্রহ একটা মন্দির আছে । মাধব বাড়ীর হোল্ডিং নং- মনে নেই ৷ বিগ্রহের সেবাইত ম্যানেজারই ৷ চীপ ম্যানেজার এর পূর্বে সেবইিত ছিল ১৯৭২ এর শেষ আর, এস, রেকর্ড প্রকাশ হয়। আর, এস, ব্লেকর্ডে কোর্ট অব ওয়ার্ডস ভাওয়াল নাম হয়।  আর, এস, রেকর্ড মন্দিরের নাম রেকর্ড আছে ৷ মন্দিরের সবাইতের নাম রেকর্ড হয়নি ৷ কুমার রবীন্দ্রর কোন পুত্র সন্তান ছিল না । কন্যা সন্তানের নাম মনে নই ৷ কন্যা সন্তান বা তাদের ওয়ারিশরা কবে মারা যায় জানি না । আর, এস, রেকর্ডের পূর্বেই ভারত গিয়ে মারা যায় কিনা জানি না ৷ মন্দিরের সেৰাইত Court of Wards Act অনুযায়ী নিযুক্তহয়েছে ৷দেঃ ১২১৯/৮৫ নং মামলা ভাওয়াল রাজ ষ্টেটের ম্যানেজার দায়ের করেন ৷ ঐ মোকদ্দমা দায়েরের সময় কোন সেবাইত ছিল কিনা জানি না ৷ ভাওয়াল কোর্ট অব ওয়ার্ডস এর ম্যানেজার কোন হস্তান্তর দলিলে মুল নালিশী জমির মালিক নন ৷ বিগ্রহ বন্দাবস্ত নেয়নি Court of Wards থক ৷ এস, এ, রেকর্ড ছাড়া তাই সেই মর্মে প্রতিবেদন দাখিল করি ৷ এস, এ, রেকর্ডের ভলিউম AC Land অফিস থাকে কিনা জানি না, এস, এ, রেকর্ড আর, এস, রেকর্ড থাকে ৷ A/C Land অফিসে। বিগ্রহ Court of Wards এর অধিন প্ৰজা ছিল না ৷ সত্য নয় এজন্য এস.এস রেকর্ডের ভলিওম দাখিল করিনি একারন ৷ প্ৰজা সত্ব নালিশী সম্পত্তির মালিক বছির উদ্দিন এবং চান মিয়া ছিল তা সত্য নয়।এস, এ , রেকর্ড তাদের নাম আট আনা আট আনা অংশ সত্য নয় ৷

A/C Land এর অফিসে যদি থেকে থাকে তাহলে তঞ্চকতা পূর্ন ভাবে আছে ৷

নালিশী সম্পত্তি সরকার নিয়ন্ত্রন করে কোর্ট অব ওয়ার্ডের মাধ্যম ৷ RS রেকর্ড কোর্ট অব ওয়ার্ডের এর উল্লেখ নেই তা সত্য ৷ উহা কের্টি অব ওয়ার্ডস এর সম্পত্তি বিগ্রহের সম্পত্তি নয় ৷ আগর মামলাঢি কোর্ট অব ওয়ার্ডস করেছিল ৷ আগর ১২১৯/৮৫ নং মোকদ্দমা করছে কিনা আমার স্বরন নেই ৷ RS রেকর্ড বেগ্রহর নাম হওয়ার ভিত্তি আছে কিনা আমার জানা নেই।বর্তমান মোকদ্দমা চালূ থাকাকালীন বাদীপক্ষ নালিশী সম্পত্তি হতে উচ্ছেদ হয় ৷ বাদী একটি নিষেধাজ্ঞা দরখাস্ত দায়ের করেছেন ৷ যা এই আদালতে নিষেধাজ্ঞা না হলেও বাদীপন হাইকের্টি থেকে নিষেধাজ্ঞা পান তা সত্য ৷ আমরা তখন জারী মোকদ্দমা না করে ডিসি এর মাধ্যমে দখলে নেই ৷ সত্য নয় যে জারী মোকদ্দমা না করে ডিসি এবং এস, পি, এর সাহায্য নিয়ে উচ্ছেদ করা বেঅইিনী হয়েছে ৷

এই সম্পত্তি মালিক নন কোর্ট অব ওয়ার্ডস তা সত্য। ওয়ার্ভসরা সাধারন ব্যক্তি নন ৷ পরে বলে ওয়ার্ডসরা সাধারন ব্যক্তি ৷ সাধারন ব্যক্তি এবং ওয়ার্ডসদের সম্পত্তিতে কোন পার্থক্য নেই তা সত্য নয় ৷ উচ্ছদ যেখান বল্মছি সেখান ঘর বাড়ী ছিল ৷ খ(২) আরজির তফসিল বর্নিত সম্পত্তি হইত উচ্ছেদ করি।

নাঃ সম্পত্তি পৌরসভার মধ্যে পৌর হোল্ডিং ২২০ স্থির কিনা জানি না ৷ নাঃ সষ্পত্তিতে যে যে বাদীদেৱ ঘর বাড়ী সরিয়ে নিতে বলা হয় ৷ নালিশী সম্পত্তিতে এখনো দুইটি ঘর আছে ৷ ৩-৩-০৮ তাং উচ্ছেদ হয় ৷ আনসার নিয়োগ হয় কতদিন পর জানি না ৷ আনসার নালিশী সম্পত্তির ঘবেই উঠে এবং সে খানেই অবস্থান করে ৷

খ(২) তফসিল বর্নিত সম্পত্তি ছাড়া অন্যান্য সম্পত্তি ফাকা সম্পত্তি যাতে ধান, চাষ করতে দেখছেন তা সঠিক নয় ৷ ঐ প্রতিবেদন এর বিরুদ্ধে কোন লিখিত আপত্তি দেই নি ৷

আমাদের ঊছেদের মোকদ্দমার পূর্বে হইতেই তারা এখানে দখলে ছিল ৷ বাদীদের পক্ষ করিনি উছেদের মামলায় তা সত্য ৷ আমাদের ঊচ্ছেদের মোকদ্দমায় ২নং বিবাদীর নাম আশরাফ আলী পিতা বাহাউদ্দিন তা সত্য ৷ ঠিকানায় পৌর হোন্ডিং নেই ৷ এই মামলায় বিবাদীর পিতার নাম মৃত বছর উদ্দিন তা সত্য ৷ মোকদ্দমায় ২ নং বিবাদী বাদীদের ভাই তা মিথ্যা বলি তা সঠিক।

দেবত্তর সম্পত্তি কে পরিচালনা করে তদসম্পর্কে আমার ধারনা আছে ৷ দেবাত্তর সম্পত্তির দেখাশুনা করেন সেবইিত তা সত্য a RS রেকর্ড সঠিক প্রদঃ ‘ক’ হয় উহা শ্রী মাধব বিগ্রহ পারিবারিক বিগ্রহ ছিল ৷ কুমার রবীন্দ্র নারায়ন চৌধুরী নিজ সেবাইত ছিলেন । RS রেকর্ড ৮৭ ইং সন শেষ হয় ৷ RS রেকর্ড উল্লেখিত সরাজবালা দেবী ও বিভাবডী দেবী তাদের আত্মীয় হয় কুমার রবীন্দ্র নারায়নর । তারা কেউই জীবিত ছিল না এবং তারা ভারত পাকিস্তান ভাগ হওয়ার পূর্বেই তারা ভারত চলে যান ৷ RS রেকর্ড সঠিক ৷ রেকর্ডের সময় Court of Wards মালিক ছিলেন । সত্য নয় যে State Acquisition TenancyAct এর হওয়ার পর Court of Wards এর কোন স্বত্ব ছিল না নালিশী সম্পত্তির উপর ।

49. Since Gazette has been published as projabili and thereafter, State Acquisition and Tenancy Act washed away Zamindari system, plaintiff became owner of their respective land as it is asserted by provision of law.

50. From Dhaka gazette, published on Monday, March, 1954, it appears that Zaminderi system has been abolished and it was taken over by the Government giving status of tenant of land as 'Malik'. Let us quote from the gazette itself:- which runs as:—

"No.  2773 LR -26th February 1952. In exercise of the power by sub-section (f) of section 3 of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (East Bengal Act No.  XXVIII of 1951), it is hereby notified, for the information of all concerned, that the 'Governor is pleased to acquire, with effect from the 14th April, all interests of the rent-receivers named in column 1 of the schedule below in the estates and taluks and tenures, the particulars whereof are given in column 2 of the schedule against their names including all their interests in all such-soil and rights to minerals in such estates and taluks and tenures."

51. So, after promulgation of the gazette in 1952, March, 24, Zamindari system having been abolished the plaintiffs predecessor became land owner. Section 3 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act speaks that rents receiving interest has been devolved upon the Government not upon the Zaminder. Exhibit-7, a copy of Dhaka gazette wherein the suit land has been included. Exhibit-8, compensation assessment roll shows that some lands were acquired by the Government from the predecessor of the plaintiffs taking them as 'Malik' of the suit land as projabili. Exhibit-9 also a copy of Dhaka Gazette, the last gazette published under State Acquisition and Tenancy Act includes the suit land as:—

"Under the provision of sub-section (2) of section 43 of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (East Bengal Act No.  XXVIII of 1951), read with section 46 C of the said Act, the Governor is pleased to declare that Compensation Assessment-rolls in respect of such properties of the rent-receivers mentioned in the Schedule below as have been acquire under section 3 or will be deemed to be acquired under clause (3) of section 46 E of that Act, have been finally published under section 42 of the said Act on the date shown against each."

52. Exhibit-11 official document, a notice, issued as per section 3 for acquiring the land by the Additional land Acquisition Officer, Gazipur to Chand Mia and also to the predecessor of the plaintiffs. This document goes to show continued possession of the plaintiffs in respect of the suit land. In front of all these government documents RS khatian was published in the name of defendant No. 1 showing Surjabala Debi and Bibhabatibala Debi, wife of Kumar Rabindra Narayan Roy Chowdhury as possessor in 8 annas share each is totally baseless. It is admitted position that RS khatian was prepared in between 1969-1985.

53. Here we may also lay our hand to history.

54. Bhawal Raj is known to all of Bangladesh for many reasons including the famous case of Mejo Kumar and Bhibaboti Debi. For this reason family of Bhwal Raj is well known to all of us. It is also known that Bhibaboti Bala Debi as well Surjabala Debi left this country (East Bengal) just after pronouncement of judgment in 1919, as such, in 1985 their names cannot appear as possessors in the RS khatian, as such, it can be definitely said that RS khatian has been prepared illegally without any basis.

55. There is another factum.

56. After promulgation of Bangladesh Laws (Amendment) Ordinance, 1976 (Ordinance No.  IX of 1976), new law under section 2(A) inserted i.e. the power of the Court of Wards vested in the Divisional Commissioner of respective areas. By the Bangladesh law, Board of Land Administration of the Government took place in place of Court of Wards, after acquisition of rent receiving interest of the concerned estate the tenants of the Bhawal Raj Estate were no more tenants under them and became "Malik" directly under the Government. Management of the properties of disqualified owners by the Court of Wards is a matter of long past. Either they have overcome their disqualification in the meantime or have died leaving heirs to inherit the estates. Alter publication of general notification No.  2773 dated 26-2-52, exhibit-7, under section 3 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and the notification No.  3126 dated 27-2-56, exhibit-11, declaring the Compensation Assessment-rolls under section 43(2) read with section 46 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, all rent receiving interest stood acquired and the tenants of any such rent receivers became "Malik" directly under the Government and all non-retainable khas land vested in the Government.

57. In the case of Bangladesh vs Sree Sree Madan Gopal Jew, (1981) 33 DLR (AD) 13, the Appellate Division set at rest all controversy regarding impact of such wholesale acquisition as under:—

"It is to be further observed that it is now well settled on the authority of Jalil Ahmed vs the Province of East Pakistan: (1967) 19 DLR 106 decided by a Special Bench and affirmed by the Supreme Court of Pakistan in Tanvir Ahmed Siddiki vs the Province of East Pakistan (1968) 20 DLR (SC) 144 PLD 1968 SC 185 that on the publication of the notification under section 3 of the Act, all rent receiving interests including that of Debuttor and Waqf estate stood acquired and all non-retainable khas land also stood vested in the Government." In paragraph 4 of the judgment, it is held: "There is another fact which needs to be noted that in the year 1963 notifications under section 43 of East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act have been published acquiring of all interests other than already acquired under section 3 of the Act completing all acquisition proceedings under the Act. All the notifications have been published in the Official Gazette covering all districts of Bangladesh. Another fact that requires to be noted is that President's Order No. 90 of 1972, the Bangladesh (Legal Proceedings) (Third) Order 1972, was promulgated on 3rd August, 1972 long after the observation made in some of the decisions of the High Court, Dacca on the retention by the Mutwalli or Shebait of an estate on account of non-preparation of the compensation assessment roll. This enactment has been promulgated long after all the acquisition proceedings were completed and long after the observations of the High Court made regarding the non-preparation of the compensation assessment roll. This enactment made in President' Order No.  90 of 1972 clearly states that notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, appeals, applications and other legal proceedings pending or continuing or deemed to be pending or continuing in any court against the Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh in which the legality or validity of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (EB Act No.  XXVIII of 1951), or of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy (Amendment) Ordinance 1956 (EB Ordinance No III of 1956) or of any other law making any amendment in the said Act or of the acquisition of any property made under any provision thereof is challenged or called in question shall abate, and all order, including orders of injunction and other interlocutory orders passed in such suit, appeals applications and other legal Proceeding shall cease to have any effect; and no court shall entertain and no person shall bring fresh suit, appeal, application or other legal proceedings in which the legality or validity of any such law or acquisition is challenged or called in question."

92. From the aforesaid facts, evidences both oral and documentary and also law involved in the case we conclude that the entire 23.13 acre `Ka' schedule property was a probability property before SAT Act. 1950. So, the said 23.13 acre 'Ka' schedule property was duly recorded in the names of the then projas namely Chan Mian and Basaruddin in SA Khatian No.  63 (Exhibit-1) by operation of section 3 of the SAT Act, through publishing probability property Gazette (Exhibit-7) and also by PO 90 of 1972 the RS Khatian No.  506(Exhibit-12) recorded in the name of  শ্রী মাধব বিগ্রহ সেবাইত দং সুরুজ বালা দেবী। বিভাবতি দেবী। জং কুমার রবিন্দ্র নারায়ন রায় চৌধুরী সাং নিজ।” is baseless and without foundation, as such, the same is not binding upon the plaintiffs. The defendant No.  14, Court of Wards, Bhowal Raj Estate claiming as shebaiyet of defendant No.  1 and the defendant No.  15, Land Reform board had illegally evicted the plaintiffs appellants on 3-3-2008 and 5-3-2008 from the `Kha' schedule property violating the order of injunction passed by the High Court Division on 3-3-2008 in Civil Rule No.  132(FM) of 2008 and also during the pendency of Title Suit No.  23 of 2008 of the joint District Judge, 1st Court, Gazipur and as such, the plaintiffs are entitled to recover the said dispossessed 'Kha(2)' schedule property as prayed for in their petition dated 10-7-2008. The plaintiffs appellants having proved their right, title and possession in the rest of the 'Kha' schedule property i.e, `Kha(1); 'Kha(3); 'Kha(4); 'Kha(5)' and Kha 6 schedule property are entitled to protect their said property by the decree of confirmation of possession and permanent injunction.

93. The possession of the plaintiffs appellants in the rest of the 'kha' schedule properties, i.e. 'Kha (1); 'Kha (3)'; 'Kha (4),"Kha (5)' Kha 6 schedule properties hereby confirmed against the defendants respondents Nos.  1, 14 and 15 the defendants-respondents Nos.  1,14 and 15 are also restrained by a decree of permanent injunction from disturbing the possession of the plaintiffs and evicting the plaintiffs-appellants from the 'Kha (1)'; `Kha (3)'; 'Kha (4),' 'Kha (5)' and Kha 6 schedule properties. Defendant's witnesses stated that the aforesaid eviction was not done by executing decree of court but by force through the said combined force which according to us illegal. If the dis-possession took place by executing the decree on the event of success by the plaintiff in the appeal, plaintiff could take shelter as per provision of section 144 of the Code of Civil Procedure but it is admitted position that plaintiff was dispossessed by force as such the possession of the plaintiff requires to be restored with immediate effect. On this point let us lay our hand to certain decisions by force as such the possession of the plaintiff requires to be restored with immediate effect. On this point let us lay our hand to certain decisions.

94. In the case reported in 15 MLR (AD) 89 where it is held that "The state of things existed just at the date of institution of the filed suit to prevent defendant doing an act-Defendant to defeat the very purpose for which the suit has been instituted does an act before the interlocutory order reaches him Court in such case may issue an order in mandatory form to demolish the thing done by defendant.

<u>95. If a party to a suit does an act to bring about a change in the state of things existing at the date of the suit or just prior to that date, in order to forestall a possible order of the court, the Court may, in an appropriate case, in exercise of its inherent power, require the offending party, by issuing a temporary injunction in mandatory form to restore the status-quo ant. This principle is in consonance with fair administration of justice and this power of making an order of mandatory injunction on an interlocutory may be exercised, irrespective of the merits of the main case as it is one of the main concerns of a Court of law to see that no one dares to interfere with the course of justice by presenting the court with a fait accompli"</u>

96. In the case reported in 35 DLR (AD) 42 it is held that "The Court, in an appropriate case, exercise of its inherent power, require the offending party, by issuing a temporary injunction in mandatory from, to restore the status-quo ante.

97. It does not appear from the facts and circumstances of the case that the matter is purely a concern between the private rights of two parties. The matter assumed a new character and it turned into a matter concerning public policy relating to administration of justice. The present case falls squarely within the perimeter of the case reported in 35 DLR (AD) 42 and we find that the trial court acted judicially in passing the temporary and mandatory injunctions and 47 DLR will consider this decision when we complete our judgment."

98. So, the First Appeal No.  128 of 2012 is hereby allowed with contest against defendant respondents Nos.  1, 14 and 16-32 without cost. The judgment and decree binding upon plaintiffs. The decree passed in Title Suit No.  1219 of 1985 of the Court of 1st Joint District Judge, Gazipur which affirmed by the High Court Division in FA No.  104 of 1997 and by the Appellate Division in CPLA No.  94 of 2006 is hereby declared collusive and illegal and not binding upon the plaintiffs-appellants. The defendant Nos.  1, 14 and 15 are directed to hand over possession of the 'Kha(2)' schedule dispossessed property within 60 days from today to the plaintiffs-appellants, failing which they will get compensation @ Taka 1,00,000 per day till the plaintiffs get possession thereof through the process of the Court. The possession of the plaintiffs-appellants in the rest of the 'Kha' schedule properties, i.e. 'Kha(l)', 'Kha(3)', 'Kha(4),"Kha(5)' and Kha (6) schedule proper-ties hereby confirmed against the defendants respondents Nos.  1, 14 and 15. The defendants-respondents Nos.  1, 14 and 15 are also restrained by a decree of permanent injunction from disturbing the possession of the plaintiffs in and evicting the plaintiffs-appellants from the `Kha (1)', 'Kha (3)', 'Kha (4); 'Kha (5)' and Kha (6) schedule properties.

99. As such, we are directing defendant to restore possession of the plaintiffs on the suit land within 60(sixty) days from the date of receiver of this judgment by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Gazipur. If defendants failed to restore possession of the plaintiffs on the suit land as per direction, then defendant shall pay Taka 1,00,000 per day as compensatory cost from the date of dispossession till restoring possession of the plaintiff. 100.

100. Send down the lower court records.

Communicate this judgment at once.

End.
