full_judgment:
Mirza Hussain Haider J: These two Rules Nisi, obtained by two different parties, involves similar facts and concerning common question of law, as such both are taken up together for hearing and accordingly disposed of by this single judgment.

2. In Writ Petition No.17056 of 2012, Rule Nisi has been issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the impugned Memos, bearing No. BR Dhaka No. 98/98/792 dated 1-10-2012 and No. BR Dhaka 98/98/799 dated 2-10-2012, Annexures-1 and 1(1) respectively, both issued under the signature of Respondent No. 4 requesting Respondents No. 5 to 7 not to register any type of transfer/sale deed covering the properties in CS Plot No. 2497 and 2582 of CS Khatian No. 118 Mouza Baunia, JL No. 211 as found at page 510 of the "projabily property" Gazette (Annexure-C) which corresponds to SA Khatian Nos. 118/41, 118/76, 183, 184, 188, 198, 212, 220, 174, 179, 118/2 and 234 and also corresponds to RS Plot Nos. 6108, 6109, 6110, 6112 and 6116 of RS Khatian Nos. 63, 116, 117, 181, 240, 811, 818, 819, 862, 1083, 1371, 1490 and 1589, should not be declared to have been issued without lawful authority and of no legal effect, and/or pass such other or further order or, orders to this Court may seem fit and proper.

3. Similarly, in Writ Petition No.17216 of 2012, Rule Nisi has been issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the impugned Memos, bearing No. BR Dhaka No. 98/98/792 dated 1-10-2012 and No. BR-Dhaka/98/98 / 799 dated 2-10-2012, Annexures J and J(1) respectively, both issued under the signature of Respondent No. 4 requesting Respondent Nos. 5 to 7 not to register any type of transfer/sale-deed covering the properties in CS Plot Nos. 2035, 2106, 2137, 2142, 2151, 2176, 2972, 2976, 2977, 2987, 3280, 3290 and 2977/3459 recorded in Khatian No, 556, along with Plots of two other CS Khatians being CS Khatian Nos. 554 and 555 belonging to other private persons' "projabily property" and CS Plots No. 2748 and 2970 of CS Khatian No. 118 CS Plot No. 3280/3438 of CS Khatian No, 646 and CS Plot No. 3279 of CS Khatian No. 12 of Mouza Baunia of JL No. 211 corresponding to RS Plot Nos. 9175, 9176, 9177, 6928, 7113, 6881, 6862, 6911, 6609, 6743, 6735, 6735/6993, 6735/6994, 6868, 6868/6995, 6868/6996, 6709, 6711, 6853, 6841, 10054, 10055, 6869, 6996, 6911, 10056, 11400, 10050, 10057, 10058, 10066, 10059, 10060, 10064, 10063, 10061, 10062, 10040, 10043, 10045, 10046, 10044, 10047, 10048, 10084, 10081, 10082, 10083, 10017, 10018, 10116, 11387, 10113, 10112, 11386, 10111, 10108, 10110, 10109, 10115, 10114, 10121, 10122, 10120, 3857 and 10135, of RS Khatian Nos. 139, 1194, 695, 1447, 1644, 855, 515, 1447, 264, 515, 743, 265, 1050, 1051, 1464, 210,910, 1538,1490, 706, 707, 1087, 1327, 694, 968, 94, 648, 720, 1539, 661, 68, 1326, 216, 126, 1051, 379, 384, 968, 1577, 699, 714, 148, 216, 571, 1538, 1650, 631, 714, 1577, 741,700, 1390, 1243. 281, 366, 1601, 430, 998, 632, 769, 743, 1568, 626, 276, 382, 876, 486, 678, 1190,106, 301, 456, 924, 1197, 129, 687, 694, 1645, 877, 1082, 367, 978, 632, 628, 337, 726, 278, 303, 382, 209, 1406, 89 and 208, should not be declared to have been issued without lawful authority and of no legal effect, and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

4. Facts necessary for the disposal of Rule in Writ Petition No. 17056 of 2012, in short, are that the writ petitioners being involved in purchase and selling lands upon developing the same, intended to purchase 5.16 acre land of CS plot No. 2497 and 9.72 acre land of CS plot No. 2582, both of CS khatian No.118 of Mouza Baunia, under Police Station Pallabi, District-Dhaka, and accordingly contacted Md Ahsanullah and others, the SA, RS and Dhaka City Survey recorded owners, who are owning and possessing the same upon paying the land Development Taxes, in their names, to the government regularly. The said Writ petitioners, after being satisfied with the right, title and possession of the said owners in the aforesaid government records, took 9 registered powers of Attorney in their favour from the aforesaid owners in possession. But when the writ petitioners went to the respondent No. 6, the concerned sub-Registrar of Mirpur, for execution and registration of the deeds of sale by using those powers the said respondent refused to register the same on the plea that by the aforesaid two impugned Memoranda, being No. BR Dhaka-98/98/792, dated 1-10-212 and BR Dhaka-98/98/799 dated 2-10-2012 issued under the signature of respondent No.4, the present Manager, Court of Wards, Bhawal Raj Estate, under the management of the land Reform Board (Respondent No.3), he has been directed not to register any deed of transfer in respect of the said plots mentioned in the said two impugned memoranda.

5. On the other hand, the facts of the writ petition No. 17216 of 2012, in short, are that the writ petitioners, being a developer Company and its Managing Director, respectively, earlier purchased the properties contained in 17 CS Plots of Baunia Mouza, under Police Station Pallabi, from its lawful owners in possession, whose names have been duly successively recorded in the SA, RS and Dhaka City Survey khatians. Out of the aforesaid 17 CS plot 12 CS(plots being No. 2035, 2106, 2137, 2142, 2151, 2176, 2972, 2976, 2977, 2987, 3280, 3290 and 2977/3459, were commonly recorded under three CS Khatians being No. 554, 555 and 556 amongst which, two CS khatians, namely, 554 and 555 comprising of plot numbers 13, 285, 212, 3280, 2035, 2106, 3290, 2116, 3295, 2137, 2142, 2150, 2151, 2176, 2972, 2976, 2977, 2987, 3001, 3030, and 2977/3457 are recorded in the name of two private persons in the cadastral survey (CS) Khatian, who have had no connection, whatsoever, with the Court of Wards, Annexures B and B(1), respectively. The other CS khatian, being No. 556, was recorded in the name of the original owner, the then Zamindar, represented by the Court of Wards(Annexure-B-2). The remaining four CS plots, being No. 2748 and 2970 under CS khatian No. 118 and CS plot No. 3279 and No. 3280/3438 under CS khatian No. 12 and 646 respectively, were also recorded in the name of the original owner, the then Zamindar, represented by the Court of Wards in the CS record Annexure-C, C(1) and C(2) respectively, which were settled with the "projas" and, as such the said lands covering the aforesaid four khatians being "Projabily properties" the rent receiving interests thereof were acquired by the then government under the then government under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, by way of publishing "projabily property" gazette (Annexure-D) for which the rent received i.e. the Zamindar received compensations, as evident from Annexure-D(1). Pursuant to Annexure D and D (1) the Zamindars, as well as the Court of Wards, lost all right, title, interest and possession in those properties/plots by operation of section 3 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. Consequently, all the subsequent record of rights, namely, the SA, RS and Dhaka City Survey. were duly prepared and finally published in the names of the previous projas upgrading them as owners and their subsequent successors and transferees as "owners' in possession whose title and possession are protected against all, under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 as well as by the subsequent enactment of President's Order (PO) 90 of 1972. Under such circumstances, the writ petitioners, having purchased the said properties from the SA, RS and Dhaka City Survey recorded owners, went to respondent No. 6 for registration of the deeds of transfer of their purchased properties from those khatians to the subsequent transferees as well as also for registration of the deeds of purchase of other properties from the said plots but the said respondent, pursuant to the aforesaid two impugned Memoranda No. BR Dhaka-98/98/ 792, dated 1-10-2012 and BR Dhaka-98/98/799 dated 2-10-2012, Annexure-J and J(1), respectively, declined to register any transfer deed on the plea that respondent No. 4, Manager, Court of Wards, prohibited him from registering any deed connecting the aforesaid CS plots.

6. Further case of the writ petitioners of both the writ petitions are that the aforesaid two impugned memos are illegal and are of no legal effect as Respondent No. 3, the Manager Court of Wards, has no right, title, possession or authority to issue such, impugned Memos after publication of the "projabily property" Gazette (Annexure-C and D in the aforesaid two writ petitions respectively) after the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 came into operation and also that the Respondent No. 3 and 4 are neither the controlling authority of the respondent Nos. 5 to 7 nor those-respondents are answerable to respondent Nos.3 and 4. Moreover, President's Order No. 90 of 1972 has imposed a complete bar in claiming ownership over the "projabily properties" by the previous Zamindars or any one claiming through the said Zamindars. Hence these two Rules.

7. The Respondents Nos. 3 and 4 namely, the Land Reforms Board and the Court of Wards, entered appearance in both the Rules and filed affidavits in opposition contending inter alia that on the basis of recent decision and the directive of the Ministry of Land and also the Parliamentary Standing Committee for Ministry of Land, registration of any deed of transfer of any property belonging to the then Bhawal Raj Estate which are managed by the Court of Wards, has been stopped for the purpose of preserving the historic and heritage properties of the Bhawal Raj as such the said respondents have issued the impugned memos being duty bound to protect the interest of the Bhawal Raj. The said respondents in their affidavits did not deny the facts of acquisition of the rent receiving interest by the government. Rather in para 3 they also admitted the facts stated in the writ petitions stating to be matters of record. However, in para 10 they stated that the last record of right i.e. ''Dhaka City Survey;" was erroneously prepared and published in the name of illegal occupiers, which they did not establish by any paper. Having gone through the said affidavit-in-opposition, we could not understand the head and tail of the same. The affidavits in opposition filed in Writ Petition No.17056 of 2012 is not only chaotic but also Confusing. The respondents did not state as to how the property belongs to the court of wards or how the same are not "Projabily Properties" or how Annexure C and D to the aforesaid two writ petitions respectively, do not focus on the correct picture nor they could show that the court of wards took appropriate steps in last 60 years to protect the properties of the Bhawal Raj. Similar is the position in respect of the affidavit-in-opposition filed in Writ Petition No. 17216 of 2012.

8. Mr M Khalilur Rahman, the learned advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners in both the Rules, submits that when by operation of law the rent receiving interests of all the properties possessed by "projas", of all the seminaries vested with the government pursuant to sections 3 of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and thereby raising the status of "projas" to those of "owners" of such lands and also declaring them to be the owners of the said land which they were settled with by the then Zamindars and accordingly, gazette notifications. (Annexure C in Writ Petition. No. 17056 of 2012 and Annexure D in Writ-petition No. 17216 of 2012) have been published incorporating the CS khatian numbers with mouzas, JL Numbers, thanas and, districts throughout the then East Pakistan, which were thereafter, by operation of law recorded in the names of the said "projas" transformed as "owners", the predecessors in interest of the petitioners, in the subsequent SA and RS records, giving them the title and accordingly, in the last Dhaka City Survey, the successors of such owners' name being recorded, the respondents have no right under any law to direct the registering authority not to register any document and as such, the embargo, as imposed by the impugned memos are not only illegal but also examples of high handedness.

9. He next submits that as it is known to everybody that in one khatian there may be several plot numbers and similar plot numbers may be available in different khatians citing ratio of shares of the owners, and in the impugned two memoranda no khatian number having been mentioned, the same are vague, indefinite and rather incomplete which cannot be applied on any land. In the absence of stating any khatian number in the impugned orders, rather simply upon incorporating only the CS plot numbers no specific right over any property can be construed, rather than to create confusion in the mind of the respondents No. 5 to 7, i.e. the registering authority as such the impugned orders are not sustainable under any law as the same are vague and indefinite.

10. He further submits that section 53A of the Registration Act gives the authority to the Registrar to register any deed of transfer, instrument, subject to compliance of some conditions as required under the said law. As such the Registrar, under any circumstances, cannot be bound by any other authority or by directives to do or not to do anything relating to registration of any deed. Referring to section 43 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 he, lastly, submits that the property intended to be transferred or purchased by the petitioners with notice that the same are owned and possessed by the appropriate person, upon examining the records of the government imposition of embargo on the registering authority not to register any Document in respect of the said property is not sustainable in law. Hence the Rules should be made absolute.

11. On the other hand, Mr Faizul Kabir, along with Ms. Aysha Flora, the learned advocates appearing on behalf of Respondents No. 3 and 4, on the face of the submissions made by the learned advocates for the petitioners, in both the writ petitions, as to acquisition of the rent receiving interests of the Zamindars under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, could not make out any case in favour of the respondents. Mr Kabir did not put forward any argument on the publication of the "projabily property" gazette notification (Annexure-C in Writ Petition No. 17056 of 2012 and Annexure-D in Writ Petition No. 17216 of 2012) and also on finally published Dhaka City Survey in the names of the predecessor in interest of the petitioners. The learned advocate did not make any statement or submission on the presumptive value of the latest survey i.e. Dhaka City survey nor as to why no step has been taken for correcting the Dhaka City Survey, if any. Rather he simply confined himself within the submission that the property being historic and heritage property of Bhawal Raj, the respondents have taken appropriate steps to stop transferring such properties by the present petitioners, who are, according to him, mere "illegal occupants" and, as such, the impugned memos have been properly issued. Thus the writ petitions are not maintainable and both the Rules are liable to be discharged.

12. Heard the learned Advocates of both the parties, perused the two writ petitions, the affidavits in opposition and the Annexures appended to the two writ petitions. It appears that the properties of writ petition No. 17056 of 2012 bearing CS plot No. 2497 and 2582 have been recorded in CS Khatian No. 118 along with other CS plots. The said CS khatian No.118 appears at page 510 of the "projabily property" Gazette dated 24-3-1952 (Annexure-C) by which the rent receiving interest of the then Zamindars have been acquired by the government under section 3 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. It also appears that the previous Zamindar Kumar Rabindra Narayan Roy Chowdhury has been paid up compensation for that purpose, as evident from compensation payment Gazette Notification No. 3126 dated 27-2-1956 published on 29-2-1956 in the then Dhaka Gazette, Annexure-C(1), by the then Government. Similarly, the properties of the writ petition No. 17216 of 2012, as it appears from Annexure B, B(1), B(2) and Annexures C, C (1) and C(2), that 43 CS plots in 6 Khatians out of which plots No. 2035, 2106, 2137, 2142, 2977, 2151, 2176, 2972, 2976, 2977, 2987, 3280, 3290 and 2977/3459 of CS Khatian 554 as well as those total khatian No. 555, total 26 plots, have been recorded in the names of private individuals, not the Zamindar or the court of wards. As such the court of wards has no connection, whatsoever, with the same. On the other hand 13 plots bearing same numbers namely, 2035, 2106, 2137, 2142, 2151, 2176, 2972, 2976, 2977, 2987, 3280, 3290 and 2977/3459 of CS Khatian No. 556 along with CS plots No.2748 and 2970 of CS khatian No.118 CS plot No.3280/3438 of CS Khatian No. 646 and CS plot No. 3279 of CS khatian No. 12 (total 17 plots) all were originally recorded in the name of the then Zamindar, Kumar Rabindra Narayan Ray Chowdhury, represented by the Court of Wards, the respondent No. 4, in the CS Survey, as appears from Annexure B, B(1), B(2), C,C(1) and C(2) respectively, which were settled with the. "projas" as underraiyts. Thereafter, with the enactment of the Statement Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 the rent receiving interest the raiyots i.e. the then Zamindars vested with the government and the "projas" were upgraded and recognized by the government as owners of their settled land they had been possessing under the Zamindar. Under such circumstances in all subsequent surveys the previous "projas" and their successors names have been recorded as owners, duly recognized by the government. But it reveals that all the plots mentioned above in six khatians which have been recorded in the names of the then projas or their successors have been claimed as the properties of the Court of Wards without providing any khatian number by the impugned memos. On Examination of the "projabily property" Gazette it appears that the plots of CS khatian No. 556, 118, 646 and khatian No. 12 have been duly recorded as "projabily properties" whose "rent receiving" interests of the then Zamindars have been acquired by the government under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act 1950. As such whatever rights, title and interest, the Court of Wards, if any, had, in all these plots, have been ceased by the Government. In Annexure C to writ petition No. 17056 of 2012, the "Projabily Property" Gazette, at page 510 plots of CS khatian No. 118 have been enlisted as projabili properties. Similarly in Annexure-D to the writ petition No. 17216 of 2012 all the plots of CS khatians No.12, 118, 556 and 646 have been shown at pages 503, 510 and at page 516 respectively in the "projabily property" Gazette.

13. It further appears that following the "projabily property" Gazette the SA khatianswere published recording the names of the then "projas" upon upgrading their status as the "owners" in different SA khatians by the Survey and Settlement Department of the Government. Similarly, the next RS khatians were also prepared and published recording the names of the said "projas"/"owners" and their subsequent legal heirs and assignees as "owners". The Land Reform Board and the Court of wards as respondent No. 3 and 4, in both the writ petitions, respectively, did not deny the statements in respect of publishing the "projabily property" Gazette and the compensation payment Gazette and preparation and final publication of the SA and RS record of rights in the names of the previous "projas" and their successors in interests as "owners". Even in respect of preparation and publication of the recent Dhaka City Survey record the respondents frankly admitted, in paragraph-10 of their affidavit that those were recorded in the name of the previous "projas" as "owners" but claimed that those recordings as wrong although no step has yet been taken by the respondents to correct the said final recording, of course time allowed for correction of such wrong recording, as alleged, has expired long before. The learned Advocate for the petitioners referring to the "projabily property" Gazette (Annexure-C and D in the aforesaid two writ petitions, respectively) and also to the PO 90 of 1972 (Annexure-D and E in the aforesaid two writ petitions, respectively) and also to the decision of the Appellate Division in the case reported in 33 DLR (AD) /3 and 53, 27 DLR (SC) 109, and14 MLR (AD) 401 submitted that the Appellate Division in those cases has, already settled that the property mentioned in the "projabily property" Gazette are the properties of the projas and their successors in interests, as the rent receiving interest, therein, of the previous Zamindars have been acquired by the Government. As such when the petitioners went for registering the transfer deeds of the land purchased from the successor in interest of the then "projas", whose names 'have been correctly recorded and finally published in the aforesaid Khatians, the respondents No. 5 to 7' have no authority to refuse registration on the direction of respondents No. 3 and 4. Thus haying not done what they are suppose to do under the law they have committed illegality in not registering the deeds.

14. Under such circumstances, when the said plots are published, in the gazette notification as "Projabily Properties" and the rent receiving interests of the then Zamindars are acquired under section 3 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act 1950 (hereafter referred to as the SAT Act) the same no longer belongs to the then Zamindars or the Court of Wards rather to the "projas" as per SAT Act 1950 who have been upgraded and declared to be the "owners", the respondents have no authority to issue the impugned notices. Moreover when no khatian number has been mentioned, in the impugned memos simply mentioning the CS plot, numbers does not specify the land as such, the impugned notices are vague and indefinite by which no legal force can be ascertained. Section 3 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, reads as follows:

"3. Acquisition of the interest of certain rent-receivers and consequences thereof—(1) At any time after the Commencement of this Act, it shall be lawful for the (Government) to acquire by notification in the official Gazette, with effect from such date as may be specified in the Notification( hereinafter referred to as the notified date),—

(i) all interests of such of the rent-receivers as may be specified in the notification, in their respective estates (taluks, tenures, holdings or tenancies), as the case may be, in any district', part of a district or local area, and

(ii) All interests of all rent-receivers whose properties are, the court of Wards Act, 1879, in their respective estates, (taluks, tenures, holdings ortenancies), as the case may be including all their interests in all sub-soil and rights to minerals in such estates, (taluks, tenures, holdings or tenancies)

(2) Subject to the provisions of sub-sections [(4), (5) and (6)] of section 20, the Government may also, simultaneously with or at any time after the publication of a notification under sub-section (1) in respect of the interests of any rent -receiver in any estate (taluks, tenure, holding or tenancy) acquire, by notification in the official Gazette, with effect from such date as may be specified in the notification (hereinafter referred to as the notified date), [all or any of the lands in his khas possession of which he shall not be entitled to retain possession under the said section and so much of the lands in his khas possession as has been acquired under this sub- section and has not vested in the [Government ] under clause (a) of sub-section (4), shall vest absolutely in the [Government] free from all encumbrances.

[(2a) In a notification issued under this section, rent-receivers may be specified or described by name, or by reference to are as wherein they have interests or in such other manner as the [Government] may determine].

(3) The notification referred to in sub-section (1) or sub-section (2) shall be in such form and shall contain such particulars as may be prescribed.

(4) On and from the date specified in a notification under sub-section (1)—

(a) all interests of the rent receivers in the estates, [taluks, tenures, holding, or tenancies] specified in the notification, including their interests in all lands in their khas possession, and interests in all subsoil and rights to minerals, in such estates, [taluks, tenures, (holding or tenancies] and also including the interests of any such rent-receiver in any building or part of a building standing on any such land and used primarily as office or kutchery for the collection) of rent of any estate [taluk, tenure, holding or tenancy] shall vest absolutely in the [Government] free from all encumbrances; 4

Provided that nothing in this clause shall apply to any building within the home-stead of the rent-receiver concerned ;

(b) all arrears of revenue or rent and all cesses, together with interest, if any, payable thereon, remaining lawfully due to the Collector on the notified date in respect of any. "interest acquired under sub-section (I) shall after the said date; continue to be recoverable from the person by whom they were payable and shall, without prejudice to any other mode of recovery, be recoverable by the deduction of the amount of such arrears, cesses and interest from the compensation money payable to such person under this section 58, when so ordered by the collector, (c)...............

(d).........................

(dd).....................

(e).......................

(f)......................

(g)......................

(h)......................

(5) The outgoing rent-receivers, whose interests have been acquired under this section, shall be entitled to compensation as provided in this Act."

15. On the other hand, Presidents order (PO) 90 of 1972 has given the protection to such projas. Article 2 of PO 90 reads as follows:

"2. Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, on the commencement of this order, all suits, appeals, application and other legal proceedings pending or, continuing or deemed to be pending or continuing in any court against the Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh in which the legality or validity of the State and Tenancy Act, 1950 (EB Act No. XXVIII of 1950), or of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy (Amendment) Ordinance, 1956 (EB Ordinance No III of 1956), or of any other law making any amendment in the said Act, or of the acquisition of any property made under any provision thereof is challenged or called in question shall abate, and all orders, including orders of injunction and other interlocutory orders, passed in such suits, appeals, applications and other legal proceedings shall cease to have any effect; and no court shall entertain, and no person shall bring, any fresh suit, appeal, application or other legal proceedings in which the legality or validity of any such law or acquisition is challenged or called in question ."

16. The Appellate Division in the case of People's Republic of Bangladesh vs Sri Sri Madan Gopal Jew Bigraha , reported in 33 DLR (AD) 13 after considering and discussing the legal effect of the aforesaid laws, held that 'with the publication of notifications under section 3 all rent-receiving interests including wakf and debuttor property stood acquired by and vested in the Government'. Again in the ease of Promode Ranjan Saha and others vs Government of Bangladesh and another, reported in 33 DLR (AD) 53 it has been observed that 'after the promulgation of PO 90 of 72 all orders including orders of injunction, etc. passed in appeals, application, etc. shall cease to have any effect and no court shall entertain any fresh suit, appeal, application, etc. in which the legality of any such law of acquisition is challenged or called in question'. In the case of Anwara Begum Chowdhurani vs Nur Jahan Begum reported in 27 DLR (AD) 109 it has been held that 'after the notification issued under section 3 of the Act the status of the under-raiyat became upgraded to that of raiyat. The rent receiving interests can be acquired even before the preparation of record of rights and publication of compensation assessment rolls'. It has further been held therein that 'with the acquisition of the rent-receiving interests by the government all intermediary interests disappeared and a person holding the land under the government becomes a "tenant", becomes a "raiyat" or a "Malik" of the land recognized by the government. Consequently, the under-raiyat who actually holds the land becomes a tenant under the government. Superior land lord (i.e. the raiyat) of an under-raiyat by virtue of elimination of his rent-receiving interests disappears and the under-raiyat is upgraded to the status of a "raiyat". Lastly, in the case of Bhawal Raj Court of Wards Estate vs Rasheda Begum and others reported in 14 MLR (AD) 401 the Appellate Division has held " record of rights prepared and finally published under section 144 cannot be varied by any authority and remedy of wrong entry if any lies with the appropriate court'. It has further been held in that judgment by the Appellate Division that "Manager, Bhawal Raj estate, Court of Wards can manage only the retainable land." The Appellate Division in the aforesaid cases has already settled that the property enlisted/ shown in the "projabily property" Gazette are the properties of "projas" who have been accepted as "owners" and the "rent receiving" interest whatsoever it had therein, of the Zamindars all vested to the Government by operation of SAT Act, 1950. The relevant portion of the finding of the Appellate Division in the case reported in 14 MLR (AD) 401 are as follows:

"The learned advocate appearing for the leave petitioner, when confronted with the aforesaid gazette notifications dated 24-3-1952 and 29-2-956, as to acquisition of rent receiving interest and the vesting of lands of the leave petitioners, including the case lands, found it difficult to substantiate the locus-standi of the leave petitioner in challenging the draft records of right prepared in the names of the respective writ petitioners in respect of their respective case lands prepared during the Mohanagar Survey. Further with the publication of the gazette notifications dated 24-3-1952 and 29-2-1956 the leave petitioner ceased to have any right, title and interest and possession in the case lands, because of acquisition, and vesting of said lands in the Government. "Thereafter, the full bench of the Hon'ble Appellate Division, on an application corrected the said judgment stating that the rent receiving interest of Projabily Property had vested to the Government and land has been vested to the projas as owners. In that case the Court of Wards, Bhawal Raj Estate and the Land Reform Board the present contesting respondents were parties and had challenged the Dhaka City Survey khatian prepared and published in the names of the successors in interests of the projas". The Apex Court in that case further held:

"Thus we are of the view that the leave petitioner had no locus-standi to challenge the draft Mohanagar Survey khatian as prepared in the names of the respective writ petitioners, at-least after publication of the gazette notifications dated 24-3-1952 and 29-2-1956."

17. In the aforesaid judgment the Appellate Division lastly held that the Court of Wards can only keep in his custody, the retainable khas land of the previous Zamindars (which was 375 bighas at the time of SAT Act, 1950) and not the "projabily property". It may be mentioned, in this connection, that the land holding limitation (hereafter has been reduced to 100 bighas and lastly to 60 bighas). On the face of the aforesaid decision of the Appellate Division the Court of Wards and Land Reform Board, cannot, under any circumstances, claim ownership over the Projabily Property of the previous Zamindar, Kumar Rabindra Narayan Ray Chowdhury and, as such, cannot issue the impugned two Memoranda, specifically when they were parties in the aforesaid case before the Appellate Division. Such interference by the respondents are nothing but harassment to the previous "projas" who has become owners of their respective properties by operation of law.

18. On the other hand, section 144A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 provides "Every entry in the record of rights prepared or revised under section 144 shall be evidence of the matter referred to in such entry, and shall he presumed to be correct until it is proved by evidence to be incorrect". Thus after final publication of the records under the Revisional survey and the Dhaka City Survey in the names of the predecessors in interest of the petitioners and the respondents having not taken any step against the same till date by producing any evidence to prove that the entries in those records are incorrect, the law clearly provides that the names of the predecessors in interests of the petitioners recorded in those surveys are presumed to be correct. On this score also the respondents case are not sustainable in law.

19. Considering the provisions of law mentioned above and the findings of the Appellate Division in the aforesaid cited cases we are of the view that the property in question in both the Rules being "Projabily properties", as evident from Annexures C and D to Writ Petition No. 17056 of 2012 and Writ Petition No. 17216 of 2012, respectively, and the same being finally published in SA, RS and Dhaka Mohanagar City Survey khatians in the name of the predecessors in interest of the petitioners and the then Zamindars having not taken any step in respect of wrong entry, as claimed by the respondents, the court of wards, the said respondents cannot, under any circumstance, claim that the property belongs to the court of wards. As such when the property does not belong to the court of wards the court of wards has no legal authority to direct the registering authority not to register any deed of transfer in respect of the said properties.

<u>20. The right to transfer the property being a part of enjoyment of property, is a fundamental right of the citizen under article 42 of the constitution, it cannot be curtailed by issuing Memoranda by the third party who does not have any right, title, interest or possession in the property. Moreover, section-10 of the Transfer of Property Act provides that even the owner of the property cannot impose any condition upon the transferee, in his transfer deed prohibiting its transfer and enjoyment by the transferee, as it violates the principle of 'rule against perpetuity'. So, on that score also the impugned orders, prohibiting the transfer of other persons' property is illegal and of no legal effect.</u>

<u>21. Moreover, under the Registration Act and the Registration Manual the Registrar derives its powers and authorities of registering any deed as well as the same is under the control of the Ministry of Law. Whereas, the Court of Wards being under the control of the Land Reform Board is not a superior authority of the Registrars and Sub-Registrars to impose any prohibitory order in respect of registering any deed. According to section 53(A) of the Registration Act, the concerned Registrar/Sub-Registrar has been given a guideline as to which property can be registered and which property cannot be registered. So, if the Registrar/Sub-Registrars are restrained by the two impugned Memos at the instance of the Manager, Court of Wards, even if the criteria of section 53A is fulfilled, it would be an unwarranted interference by an unauthorized person in the lawful function of the registrar/sub-Registrar which is not permitted under the law. Nor the respondents have any right to issue such direction upon respondents No. 5 to 7 and the Registrar, under the law, is not obligated to abide by such illegal directions issued by unauthorized persons like respondents No. 3 and 4.</u>

22. Apart from the above, we want to focus about the role of the learned advocate for the respondents as well as the respondents No. 3 and 4. We find it very difficult to understand from the affidavit-in-opposition filed by the Respondents No. 3 and 4 that what is the gist of the case of the respondents and the respondents without stating the fact that the respondents are the owners of the land and, as such, have issued such directions upon the registering authority rather stated that the impugned memos have been issued for protecting the historic and heritage properties of Bhawal Raj. Nor the respondents could show that the registering authority has responsibility to abide by such directions and thereby refusal to registration has been done in accordance with law. On the other hand, respondents No. 3 and 4 could not come forward with any piece of document to show that they have right, title or possession in the land in question, specifically, when the property has been published in the gazette notification under section 3 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and the said publication being finalized and protected by PO 90 of 1972, the respondents No. 3 and 4 did not come for-ward to assist the court by showing a piece of paper for the said plots, which have already been recorded in the name of the projas fall within the "retainable khas land" of the Zamindars being up to 375 bighas with the commencement of the SAT Act, 1950 which has subsequently been reduced to 100 Bigas and lastly to 60 bighas. The respondents No. 3 and 4 did not even come forward with any piece of paper to show that the limit of retainable khas land has been raised to more than 60 bighas for which the court of wards can act as the custodian.

23. For the reasons and discussions made hereinabove we find merit in both the Rules.

Accordingly both the Rules in Writ Petitions No. 17056 of 2012 and 17216 of 2012 are made absolute.

24. The two impugned Memos bearing No. BR-Dhaka No. 98/98/792 dated 1-10-2012 and No. BR- Dhaka 98/98/799 dated 2-10-2012 Annexures-1 and 1(1) in Writ Petition No. 17056 2012 and Annexure J and J-(1) in Writ Petition No. 17216 of 2012 are declared to have been issued without lawful authority and of no legal effect.

25. Before withdrawing our pen, we would like to note that, now a days time and again we are confronted with unnecessary and uncalled for litigations like the present one in spite of settling the selfsame issue connecting with "projabily property" by the Apex court in its different decisions reported in, 33 DLR (AD) 13 and 53, 27 DLR (SC) 109 and lastly in the case reported in 14 MLR (AD) 401. In these two writ petitions the question over the title of "projabily property" of the previous Zamindar, Kumar Rabindra Narayan Roy Chowdhury, represented by the Court of Wards, Bhawal Raj Estate, again came up for our consideration as the court of Wards claimed the "projabily property" as its own property and accordingly issued the two "impugned Memoranda, though it has already been settled earlier in the aforesaid cases holding that the "projabily properly" can never be claimed by the previous Zamindars represented by the court of Wards. The Court of Wards though legally bound to follow the said decision according to Article 112 of the constitution but time and again they are harassing the people claiming title over the "projabily property", either by issuing Memorandum or by other ways and means and thereby also wasting the courts valuable time. So it is high time to caution the Court of Wards, Bhawal Raj Estate and also the Land Reform Board to abstain from creating such situation on frivolous issues and thereby pushing the public to the Court. Thus they are cautioned not to harass anybody specifically the previous "projas" or their successors-in-interests any more, claiming title over the "projabily property" as cited in the "projabily property" gazette published on 24-3-1952. If in future, any such illegal and uncalled for claim is sought for by the court of wards or if any litigation is continuing or started afresh because of court of wards action by claiming title over the said "projabily property" by the Court of Wards and the Land Reform Board, then they would be liable to be dealt with for contempt of Court, apart from such litigations been abated under PO 90 of 1972.

26. Under such circumstances we think it would be proper to call the manager, court of wards and the Land Administrator to explain their position in this respect because the government officials under no circumstances can play with the property of the general people. This court thus thought that exercising the power conferred under the law we should call the said officials to explain their conduct as to these two cases in particular. But considering that it will be nothing but a futile exercise of this Court on the matter, because when the respondents could not come forward with a proper affidavit giving proper explanations supported by the papers, we simply can express our anxiety and great concern that the government officials are doing this only to harass the general people of the country and thereby they are trying to have some personal gain over it As such the respondents No. 3 and 4 are cautioned not to deal with such property of the general people in such manner which can be subject matter of harassment of the general people.

27. Let a copy of the judgment and order be communicated to the Hon'ble Minister, Ministry of Land, Hon'ble Minister, Ministry of Law for issuing guidelines to the concerned officers for the purpose of dealing with such property of the public in accordance with law so that the government officials do not create any impediment in general peoples' enjoyment of property right freely or harass the people upon taking undue advantage of being a government official.

However, there will be no order as to cost.

End.

full_judgment:
Mr. Borhanuddin, J:- This rule has been issued calling upon the opposite party nos.1 and 2 to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 10.05.2000 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Magura, in Title Appeal No. 91 of 1999 reversing those of dated 29.06.1999 passed by the learned Additional Assistant Judge, Magura, in Title Suit No.41 of 1999 should not be set aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this court may seem fit and proper.

2. Facts relevant for disposal of the rule are that the petitioner herein as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No.65 of 1994 in the Court of learned Assistant Judge, Mohammadpur, Magura, with the following prayers:

“ক) আরজি বর্ণিত মতে ও কারণে আরজীর তপশীল বর্ণিত নালিশী দাগের জমি সংশ্রবে শ্রী শ্যামা প্রসাদ বট্রাচার্য এর পিতা-সৌরিন্দ্র মোহন ভট্রাচার্য ও ১নং বিবাদী গ্রহীতা বরাবরীয় মহম্মদপুর সাব-রেজিষি্ট অফিসের তথাকথিত ১২/০৩/৬৯ তারিখের রেঃ কৃত খোষ কবলা দলিল জাল স্বত্ব সৃজনের অনুপযু্ক্ত দলিল ঘোষনার ডিক্রি দিতে।

খ) যাবতীয় আদালত ব্যয়ের ডিক্রি দিতে।

গ) আইন ইকুইটি মতে বাদী বিবাদগন বিরুদ্দে আর আর যে সকল বিহিত প্রতিকার পাইতে পারে তাহারও ডিক্রি দিতে মর্জি হয়।

Schedule of the suit as described in the plaint is quoted herein under:

“তপশীল সম্পত্তি

জেলা-মাগুরা থানা মহম্মদপুর ১১নং নাগড়া মৌজার জমি খতিয়ান নং ৪৩৪ দাগ নং ২৫০ জমির পরিমান .৮০ শতক এর মধ্যে .৫৪ শতক জমি বিরোধীয়।”

3. On transfer in the court of learned Additional Assistant Judge, Magura, the suit was renumbered as Title Suit No.41 of 1999.

4. Facts relevant for disposal of the rule are that suit schedule land originally belonged to Sourendra Mohon Bhattacharji who orally gifted .20 acres of land to the plaintiff school on 15.03.1968 and delivered possession but could not register the land in favour of the school during his life time; Said Sourendra Mohon Bhattacharji had 3 sons namely, Nandadulal, Debprashad and hyamaprashad; Amongst the sons, Nandadulal and Debprashad left this country for India during life time of their father; Shaymaprashad had been living with his father; Sourendra Mohon Bhattacharji gifted all his moveable and immoveable property in the name of Shaymaprashad by executing a will on 2nd Baishak, 1379 B. S.; Sourendra Mohan Bhattacharji died on 11.04.1973; Shaymaprashad Bhattacharji filed Case No.209 of 1978 for probate of the Will impleading Peoples' Republic of Bangladesh, represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Jessore, as defendant; Said case was allowed ex-parte; Shaymaprashad Bhattacharji sold .27 acres of land to Kamala Khatun, wife of Md. Moenuddin Mollah vide registered kabala no.1305 dated 13.02.1975; Kamrul Hassan son of defendant no.3 as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No.54 of 1993 in the Court of learned Assistant Judge, Mohammadpur, impleading Shaymaprashad Bhattacharji as defendant; In the said suit, copy of the registered kabala no.1228 dated 12.03.1969 was submitted by the plaintiff as evidence; During proceeding of the suit, defendant no.3 of the present suit Moenuddin, father of the plaintiff of that suit, submitted an application for withdrawal of the suit and take back the documents filed by the plaintiff; Learned Assistant Judge allowed the application and permitted to take back the documents vide order no.4 dated 23.06.1993; Shaymaprashad Bhattacharji executed registered deed of gift in favour of the school for the land orally gifted by his father Sourendra Mohon Bhattachargi; After registration, Secretary and Head Master of the school filed an application to the Revenue officer for mutation of the land; At that time defendant nos. 2 and 3 also filed application for mutation of .54 acres of the suit land claiming title by dint of kabala no.1228 dated 12.03.1969 allegedly executed by Sourendra Mohon Bhattacharji in favour of father of the defendant no.1 late Abdul Gani Molla; Said deed is a forged one, created by the defendant no.3 in connivance with defendant no.1 with a motive to grab the land and on the basis of said kabala created another registered deed being no. 3674 dated 15.02.1992; Plaintiff for the 1st time came to know about the forged kabala on 14.06.1993 while he went to the Office of Revenue Officer for mutation of .20 acres of land gifted by Sourendra Mohon and subsequently registered by his son Shaymaprashad and thus constrained to file present suit.

5. Defendant No.3 contested the suit by filing written statement contending interalia that the suit is barred by limitation, there is no cause of action and the suit is not maintainable under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. Further contending that .80 acres of land of Nagra Mouza no.250 belonged to Sourendra Mohon Bhattacharji and settlement khatian recorded in his name; During possession, Sourendra Mohon Bhattacharji sold .54 acres of land vide registered kabala no.1228 dated 12.03.1969 to the defendant no.1; Subsequently, defendant no.3 purchased the land on behalf of his minor son defendant no.2 vide registered kabala dated 15.12.1992; Shaymaprashad Bhattacharji son of Sourendra Mohon Bhattacharji sold .27 acres of land to Kamala Khatun wife of defendant no.3 vide registered kabala dated 13.02.1975; Defendant no.2 and his mother are bonafide purchasers; Kamala Khatun is a necessary party of the suit; Present plaintiff earlier filed Title Suit No.73 of 1993 in the Court of learned Assistant Judge, Mohammadpur, for .04 acres of land under suit plot no.250 and prayed for injunction but his prayer for injunction was rejected by the Court below; Against the order of rejection, plaintiff as appellant preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No.35 of 1993 which is still pending; Present suit is only to harass the defendants; Suit is liable to be dismissed.

6. After hearing the parties and assessing evidence on record, leaned Assistant Judge, Magura, decreed the suit vide judgment and decree dated 29.06.1999.

7. Being aggrieved, defendant opposite party nos. 1 and 2 herein as appellants filed Title Appeal No.91 of 1999 in the Court of learned District Judge, Magura, which was ultimately heard and disposed of by the learned Additional District Judge, Magura, who after hearing the parties and reassessing evidence on record allowed the appeal vide judgment and decree dated 10.05.2000.

8. Having aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree, plaintiff-respondent as petitioner preferred instant civil revision by filing an application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained present rule along with an order of stay.

9. This matter is sent by the Hon'ble Chief Justice to this Bench for hearing and disposal vide order dated 11.08.2016. This matter has been appearing in the cause list since 16.10.2017 with name of the learned advocates for the parties. On 17.10.2017, one of the learned advocate on behalf of the petitioner prays for adjournment for one day. Accordingly, adjournment was allowed. Today court peon again informed learned advocate for the parties but no one appears to press or oppose the rule. Since this matter is of the year 2000, I do not find any reason to sit over the matter without disposing the same.

10. 1 have gone through the revisional application, judgment and decree passed by the courts below along with lower courts record.

11. On perusal of the judgment and decree passed by the trial court, it appears that learned Assistant Judge framed following issues for adjudicating the case:

১) মোকদ্দমাটি বর্তমান আকারে রক্ষনীয় কিনা?

২) মোকদ্দমাটি তামাদি বাধিত কিনা?

৩) মোকদ্দমাটি পক্ষ দোষে দুষ্ট কিনা?

৪) বর্ণিত ইং ১২/০৩/১৯৬৯ সালে রেজিষ্ট্রিকৃত ১২২৮নং দলিলটি বাতিল যোগ্য কিংবা জাল জালিয়াতি কিনা?

৫) বাদী তাহার প্রার্থীত প্রতিকার  পাইতে পারেন কিনা?

৬) মোকদ্দমাটি দেওয়ানী কার্যাবিধি আইনের ১১ ধারা মতে (res judicata) দোষে অচল কিনা?

৭) বাদী আর কিকি প্রতিকার পাইতে পারে?

12. In deciding issue no. 6, learned Assistant Judge discussed about the earlier suit no.73 of 1993 filed by the plaintiff. Relevant portion of the judgment is quoted herein below:

“নথি দৃষ্টে দেখা যায় পূর্বে এই নালিশী জমি সংশ্রবে ৭৩/৯৩নং দেওয়ানী মােকদ্দমাটি একই পক্ষদ্বয়ের মধ্যে হইয়াছিল, উক্ত ৭৩/৯৩নং দেওয়ানী মাকদ্দমা ছিল “ক” তপশীল বর্ণিত জমিতে স্বত্ত্ব স্বাবস্থ, দখল কায়েম এবং “খ” তপশীল বর্ণিত হইতে ঘর সিকস্থি পূর্বক খাস দখলের প্রার্থনায় আনীত দেওয়ানী মোকদ্দমা এবং বর্তমানের মাকদ্দমাটি হইলা ১নং বিবাদী গ্রহীতা, দত্তা সৌরিন্দ্র মোহন ভট্টাচার্য বরাবরীয় নালিশী দাগের সংশ্রবীয় গত ইংরেজী ১২-৩-৬৯ তারিখের রেজিস্লিকৃত থাকে কবলা দলিল নং ১২২৮ জাল, জ্যলিয়ার্তী, ভূয়া, ভয়েড, তঞ্চকী, আদান-প্রদান বিহীন স্বতু সৃজনের অনুপযুক্ত এবং উক্ত তারিখের রেজিষ্ট্রকৃত ১২২৮ নং দলিল বাদী পক্ষের উপর বাধ্যকর নহে মর্মে ঘোষনামূলক মাকদ্দমা 1 ষুদিও উপরোক্ত মােকদ্দমা দুটি একই পক্ষদের মধ্যে, একই নালিশী জমি সংশ্রবে এবং বর্তমানে মোকদ্দযার মূল বিচার্য বিষয় উক্ত ঘোকদ্দমার ইস্যুর মধ্যে না থাকিলেও উক্ত ৭৩/৯৩নং দেওয়ানী মোকদ্দমার আলোচনার মধ্যে উক্ত ১২২৮নং দলিলটির বিষয়ে সিদ্ধান্ত থাকিলেও, উক্ত ৭৩/৯৩'নং মােকদ্দমার প্রকৃতি এবং বর্তমান মোকদ্দমার প্রকৃতি এক নহে ৷ যেহেতু উক্ত দুই যােকদ্দমার প্রকৃতি ভিন্ন সেই হেতু বিবাদীপক্ষ কর্তৃক আনীত res judicata সংক্রান্ত বিষয়টি বর্তমান মোকদ্দমার ক্ষেত্রে এঁযোজ্য নহে।

বর্তমান মোকদ্দমাঢি ইংরেজী ১ ২-৩-৬৯ ইং তারিখের রেজিষ্ট্রকৃত ১২২৮ নং দলিলটি জাল, জালিয়াতি কিনা এই মর্মে ঘোষণা এখানে এই বিষয় ছাড়া অন্য কোনবিচার্য বিষয়ের উপর আলোচনা করিবার অবকাশ নেই l”

Appellate Court below controverted above finding of the learned Assistant Judge in the following manner:

“বিজ্ঞ নিম্ন আদালতের উল্লেখিত অবজারভেশন টুকু সম্পূর্ণ ভাবেই আইনের পরিপন্থি ৷ কারণ উভয়পক্ষ কর্তৃক স্বীকৃত যে বিবাদীপক্ষের ১২-৩-৬৯ইং তারিখের ১২২৮নং রেজিষ্ট্রকৃত কবলাটি জাল মর্মে উল্লেখ করিয়াই বাদী রেসপনডেন্ট পক্ষ আরজির তফসিল বর্ণিত সম্পত্তি বাবদ স্বত্ত্ব ঘোষণা সহ দখল কায়েমের ওখাস দখলের প্রাত্নায় ৭৩/৯৩নং দেওয়ানী মোকদ্দমা দায়ের করিয়াছিলেন এবং সেই মামলায় বিজ্ঞ আদালত এই দলিলপত্র এবং বাদী রেসপনডেন্ট এর স্বত্ত্ব দখলের ভিত্তিতে বিস্তারিত আলোচনা করিয়াই ঐ দেওয়ানী ৭৩/৯৩'নং মােকদ্দমাটি খারিজ করিয়াছেন ৷ বিজ্ঞ নিম্ন আদালত ৭৩/৯৩'নং মোকদ্দমার প্রকৃতি এবং বর্তমান মোকদ্দমার প্রকৃতি এক নহে বলিয়া উল্লেখ করিয়াছেন ৷ কিন্তু বিজ্ঞ নিম্ন আদালত একটি বিষয় বুঝিতে ভুল করিয়াছেন তাহা হইল বাদী রেসপনডেন্ট পক্ষ ২টি মােকদ্দমাই দখিল করিয়াছেন সুনির্দিষ্ট প্রতিকার আইনের 8২ ধারার আওতায় ঘোষনামূলক ডিক্রিও প্রার্থনায় এবং বর্তমান মোকদ্দমায় বিবাদীপক্ষের দলিলটি তিনি জাল মর্মে ঘোষণার প্রার্থনা করিয়াছেন সেই দলিলটি জাল বলিয়া তিনি তাহার পূর্বে দাখিলকৃত মেং ৭৩/৯৩'নং মাকদ্দমার আরজীতে সুষ্পষ্টভাবে উল্লেখ করিয়াছিলেন  ফলে সন্দেহের কোন অবকাশ নাই যে, ১ ২-৩-৬৯ইং তারিখের রেজিষ্ট্রকৃত ১২২৮নং কবলা দলিলটি পুনরায় জাল বলিয়া দাবী করার বাদীপক্ষের দাখিলকৃত দেওয়ানী 8 ১/৯৯নং যেকাদ্দমাটি resjudicata 6দাষে বারিত l”

13. I have gone through the judgment passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Mohammadpur, Magura, in Title Suit No.73 of 1993 which is produced and marked as exhibit "Ka" in the present suit. It appears from the judgment that the present plaintiff filed Title Suit No.73 of 1993 for declaration of title and confirmation of possession for the Ka' schedule land and for eviction of houses and recovery of khas possession from the "kha" schedule land. On perusal of the judgment, it is apparent that in the plaint of that suit it was contended that the kabala no.1228 dated 12.03.1969 in the name of the defendant no.1 is forged. The kabala dated 15.12.1992 in the name of defendant no.2 is collusive and without jurisdiction. Defendant nos. 2-4 of the suit filed written statement denying contention of the plaint. After hearing the parties and assessing evidence on record, learned Senior Assistant Judge dismissed the suit on contest. Relevant portion of the judgment is quoted herein below: "The crux of this suit is the kabala dated 12.03.1969 bearing number 1228 and when this kabala takes birth then these defdts were not born and came into scence but as it is very much difficult to justify the genuineness of the said kabala but one thing is very much clear that the defendants are in absolute possession of the suit land which somehow substantiate the defendants claim." (sic)

14. After thorough and meticulous discussions, learned Senior Assistant Judge arrived at following finding: "In view of my foregoing discussions it is clear that the plaintiff has failed to prove his case of oral settlement and also possession. On the other hand plaintiff's witnesses by their evidence have proved the possession of the defendants. Besides that the D.W.2 man Uddin sikder and the DW.3 Suzaruddin Sheikh and the DW.4 Bipul Kumar Sarkar all have corroborated the defendants possession in the suit land. So I am not inclined to discuss the evidence all the DWs. at length In view of my aforesaid discussions and evidence on record of the plaintiff has failed to prove his title and possession for which all these issues have decided against the plaintiff and in favour of the contesting defendants." (sic) Section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure runs as follows: "No Court shall try any suit or issue in which the matter directly and substantially in issue has been directly and substantially in issue in a former suit between the same parties, or between parties under whom they or any of them claim, litigating under the same title, in a Court competent to try such subsequent suit or the suit in which such issue has been subsequently raised, and has been heard and finally decided by such Court. Explanation-I. The expression "former suit" shall denote a suit which has been decided prior to the suit in question whether or not it was instituted prior thereto. Explanation-II For the purposes of this section, the competence of a Court shall be determined irrespective of any provisions as to a right of appeal from the decision of such Court. Explanation-III The matter above referred to must in the former suit have been alleged by one party and either denied or admitted, expressly or impliedly, by the other. Explanation-IV- Any matter which might and ought to have been made ground of defence or attack in such former suit shall be deemed to have been a matter directly and substantially in issue in such suit Explanation-V Any relief claimed in the plaint, which is not expressly granted by the decree, shall, for the purposes of this section, be deemed to have been refused. Explanation-VI- Where persons litigate bona fide in respect of a public right or of a private right claimed in common for themselves and others, all persons interested in such right shall, for the purposes of this section, be deemed to claim under the persons so litigating." It is true that the issue of genuiness of registered kabala no.1228 dated 12.03.1969 was not an issue in the former suit i.e. in Title Suit No.73 of 1993 filed by the present plaintiff for declaration of title and confirmation of possession but as it is discussed above that the plaintiff of that suit i.e. the present plaintiff seriously assailed in that suit that the deed dated 12.03.1969 is forged and the defendant by filing written statement denied contention of the plaintiff. Court below after discussing the evidence on record dismissed the suit.

<u>15. By now, it is settled that any matter which might and ought to have been made a ground of attack or defence in the former suit shall be deemed to have been directly and substantially in issue in that suit. This is known as constructive res-judicata. For the application of the principle of res-judicata it is not necessary that the subject matter of both suits should be the same but that the matter in question is directly and substantially in issue in both the suits. It is also settled that res-judicata is not confined to the issues which the court is actually asked to decide but it covers issues or facts which are so clearly part of the subject matter of the litigation and so clearly have been raised that it would be an abuse of the process of the court to allow a new proceeding to be started in respect of them.</u>

<u>16. A matter may be directly and substantively in issue either actually or constructively. A matter is actually in issue when it is alleged by one party and denied or admitted by the other. It is constructively in issue when it might and ought to have been made a ground of attack or defence in the former suit, but has not been done. As a general rule, every ground of attack or defence with reference to title sued must be pleaded, if necessary in the alternative, for the plaintiff will not be allowed to make out a fresh case afterward.</u>

<u>17. It is apparent from record that the learned Additional District Judge thoroughly and meticulously discussed the issue and arrived at a finding that the suit is barred by resjudicata. The appellate court below also discussed thoroughly facts of the case and arrived at a finding that the suit is barred under order 2 rule II of the Code of Civil Procedure. It appears from the plaint of the suit that though the plaintiff prayed for declaration that registered kabala no.1228 dated 12.03.1969 is forged and not acted upon but did not seek declaration of title in the suit property. Without establishing his title in the property, the plaintiff is not entitled to get any other relief.</u>

18. Though the plaintiff claimed in his plaint that .20 acres of land orally gifted by Sourendra Mohon Bhattacharji and subsequently registered by his son Shaymaprashad Bhattacharji and the plaintiff is in possession of the suit but in his cross examination as PW.1 he stated that: স্কুল যে ২০শতক জমি দাবী করে উহাতে এখন কি আছে উহা বলিতে পারিব না।”

The above statement is not enough to prove claim of the plaintiff.

19. Considering facts and circumstances of the case and for the reasons stated above, I do not find any reason to interfere with the findings of learned Additional District Judge.

20. Accordingly, the rule is discharged without any order as to cost.

21. Judgment and decree dated 10.05.2000 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Magura, in Title Appeal No. 91 of 1999 reversing those of dated 29.06.1999 passed by the learned Additional Assistant Judge, Magura, in title Suit No. 41 of 1999 is maintained.

22. Order of stay granted at the time of issuance of rule is hereby vacated.

23. Send down lower courts record along with a copy of this judgment to the court concern at once.

End.
